European stocks were on track to edge higher at the open after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady as widely expected on Wednesday. The European Central Bank announces its next interest rate decision on Thursday.

News.title: Risk of Ebola spread in UK is low, experts stress
News.content:
Infectious disease experts have stressed the likelihood of Ebola spreading to the UK is low after the head of Africa’s health agency warned that the haemorrhagic fever could reach Britain.

The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the deadly virus that began in the volatile eastern region of the country. There have been 10,000 cases, including nearly 5,000 deaths, since the outbreak was first reported in May and it has now become the second largest Ebola epidemic in history.

In recent weeks the virus has spread to Kenya, where there have been nine cases including two deaths, and Nigeria. The case in Nigeria is concerning because the patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, the country’s capital, had no history of travel to the affected region of DRC. She has now been evacuated to Switzerland.

In comments reported by the Guardian Jean Kaseya, head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, described the outbreak as “unprecedented” as it was the first time that the disease had spread to three geographic regions of the continent. He warned that there was scope for further spread.

“We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”

On Wednesday the United States announced that travellers arriving by air would have to sign a statement affirming that they had not been in the DRC within the previous 21 days. Anyone found to provide false or misleading information would face imprisonment or a fine.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stressed that the risk to the UK is low. Dr Sam Collins, head of guidance, clinical and public health response at the agency, said the Ebola outbreak in DRC is serious but “the UK is well prepared to respond safely and effectively to the risk of imported cases arising here”.

UKHSA is monitoring travel routes from the affected countries and is providing information on symptoms.

The UKHSA said it is rare for Ebola to occur in returning travellers and the NHS has “well established procedures in place” for such a situation.

News.title: Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out
News.content:
It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

News.title: Burnham rules out calling early election
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has promised to offer households “breathing space” in his maiden Budget today.

The Chancellor insisted the economy has shown “resilience” in the face of the energy shock from the Iran war.

However, he admitted the conflict has pushed up the cost of living, “piling pressure on the families, on businesses, and on our public finances”.

Among the measures the Chancellor is expected to announce are plans to scrap standing charges on household gas bills – saving families up to £50 a year.

Mr Healey said: “We can’t stop these shocks that hit Britain, but we can make Britain more resilient when they do.

“So, this Budget is designed to give households breathing space from some of the everyday costs, provide targeted support for businesses and self-employed people, and to start the long-term action needed to get energy costs down for good.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey prepares to slash household gas bills by £50 | Chancellor to scrap standing charges on gas bills and curb Energy Secretary’s power

2) Minimum wage rise will drive up food prices, Healey warned | Manufacturers say they are already struggling to cover soaring production costs

What happened overnight

Ahead of the Budget, oil prices rose after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, which has renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East.

Brent crude was up 1.7pc to nearly $116 a barrel, maintaining inflationary pressure on the global economy. It traded around $70 before the start of the Iran war.

Meanwhile, Asia stocks rallied amid fresh enthusiasm about AI.

South Korea’s Kospi surged more than 6pc and was on track for its largest one-day gain since July, after chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold jump in quarterly profit and said it would return about $75 billion to shareholders this year.

The AI rally faces its next test when technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft report earnings after market close later today, with investors looking for evidence of returns that would justify the hefty cost of the AI build-out.

In Asia, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.7pc, with Japan’s Nikkei adding 1.1pc and ⁠China’s CSI300 blue-chip index climbing 0.7pc.

News.title: Government remains tight-lipped on aid spending in Autumn budget
News.content:
The government made no mention of plans to restore aid spending in the Autumn budget and is on track to miss its current aid commitment.

It had been rumoured that a Burnham government planned to reverse the overseas aid cuts made by Sir Keir Starmer, who reduced an already shrunken aid budget from 0.5 to 0.3 per cent of gross national income (GNI) in February 2025.

The current 0.3 per cent allocation is the lowest proportion of national income spent on aid since 1999.

It was expected the reversal would be drawn up as part of a wider shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) under Ed Miliband as foreign secretary, The Telegraph reported in September.

But there was no mention of any timeline for restoring Britain’s overseas development assistance to the legally enshrined 0.7 per cent of gross national income GNI target on Wednesday.

The UK is now also on track to miss its 0.3 per cent aid spending commitment, equivalent to £9.2 billion per year, following a failure to confirm any upwards adjustment to the UK aid budget to account for inflation.

The shortfall is estimated to fall at £410 million this year, an analysis from the Centre for Global Development (CGD) found.

Britain’s aid money is spent across the world in sectors like health, education, disaster relief, and helping to promote democracy.

Sports.title: Everton 3 Newcastle 1: Toffees set up Fleetwood tie as Toon sucker punched by Garner, Hackney and Barry strikes
Sports.content:
Next

DAVID MOYES will know he must be careful about what he wishes for, especially with the Cod Army waiting to hook another big’un.

But the Everton boss could at least celebrate the dynamic display that gave his side a last-eight clash against Fleetwood Town and dream a little of history.



For as pressure piled on opposite number Matthias Jaissle once more, Moyes will believe he’s on course for Wembley.

And if the Toffees get stuck in like they did against the Toon it’s difficult to imagine that the League Two conquerors of Prem champs Arsenal will be able to live with them.



Newcastle could have taken a firm grip on this tie early on but by the end Jaissle’s face was grim with stress and disappointment.

While Moyes might not admit it, he’s bound to be thinking that there is a route opening that could lead him and his players to the club’s first trophy since the FA Cup triumph of 1995.



Jack Grealish would have to make headlines and he did – but not for the right reasons.

He was left out of Moyes squad for what the club media announced on social media was for “a breach of club discipline.” – understood to have missed training without permission.

Moyes won’t have been happy given that he was already working with a threadbare squad.

What’s more, opposite number Jaissle went strong – no messing around with shadow squads following Sunday’s morale-boosting 2-0 win over Crystal Palace.



He made just one change, bringing in Jacob Ramsey for Joelinton having promised he would go “all-in” to try to help the Magpies towards a repeat of it’s 2025 triumph.

Moyes, meanwhile, replaced Grealish with Tyler Dibling and brought in £14.5million summer signing from Middlesbrough, Hayden Hackney.

Around 8,000 of the Toon Army were in the Hill Dickinson as part of a near-52,000-sell-out.

Among them was PM Andy Burnham and, like manager Moyes, the lifelong Blues fan will have been mighty relieved that Jordan Pickford kept out a close-range header from Harvey Barnes.

He ghosted onto a cross from Nico Gonzalez but didn’t quite get enough power on his near-post effort even if the England No1 kept his cool.



But soon after that 12th minute save he was raging as Newcastle, in barnstorming mode, turned the screw even more.

First he scrambled away a shot from Joe Willock before Vitalii Mykolenko put his body on the line to block a close-range smack from Murphy.

Then he produced a desperate stretch to push away a 30-yard strike from Fabian Schar before going ballistic with those in front of him who were being out-ran and out-fought.

Moyes side had suffered back-to-back defeats to the Gunners and Chelsea and through a pulsating opening 20 minutes they were suffering even more.

But there was welcome relief – although ultimate disappointment – as they started taking the game to their opponents.



Hackney looked like he was about to roll the ball into an empty net after Tyrique George’s shot deflected wildly to cause a scramble in the Toon box.

But Dan Burn, who returned after injury for that win over Palace, played a true captain’s part and was there to hack clear.

Another defensive giant, though one not quite so tall in James Tarkowski, then wore his skipper’s armband with pride as he produced a real crunching tackle to deny what looked like a certain opener from William Osula.

There hadn’t been a lot of quality in a cup tie both sides knew might be their only chance of gaining silverware in this campaign – and Everton were as “all-in” as their Geordie opponents.

And they hit Toon and hit them hard with a double shammy in the last 11 minutes of what had been a first half of true, old-fashioned cup thrills.



Both strikes finally added real class to the proceedings, too.

First Hackney captured the ball on Everton’s left flank, instantly dispatched into the middle, and there was Garner striding forward to rifle the ball into Lukas Hornicek’s net.

The six-foot-six-inch goalkeeper was left stranded by that 34th-minute class strike from the budding Three Lions midfielder.

Ditto that as Everton collected their second to leave him and all of the Toon contingent shell-shocked.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall drove straight down the middle and while he tumbled under a challenge the ball found its way to Thierno Barry,



The striker, not usually known for his precision, calmly controlled and guided the ball into the box and Hackney was there, free as a bird, to rise and side-foot his volley home.

In the 69th minute, he deservedly got his name on the score sheet too, sliding home after more impressive work from Dewsbury-Hall.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Burn headed home a late consolation and as sub Joelinton went to grab the ball out of the net, he and Tarkowski locked horns and a major scuffle broke out.

That pair, plus Pickford and Burn were booked along with Pickford and Burn for what, in reality, was just a silly case of handbags.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick acting as if its business as usual amid Man Utd sack threat – with Jason Wilcox far from safe either
Sports.content:
Next

TO LISTEN to Michael Carrick, you would think the circus surrounding Manchester United had packed up and left town.

The Red Devils’ under-fire boss carried himself in his press conference to preview the trip to Chelsea as if it were business as usual, apparently not living on a game-by-game basis, and his job was not on the line.



While debate rages about his future, Carrick, 45, desperately holds on to an illusion of calm, acting as though it were all quiet on the Old Trafford front.

The former United midfielder said he always expected the club hierarchy’s backing this week despite Sunday’s 3-0 thrashing by Bournemouth leaving the team 16th in the Premier League and only a point above the relegation zone.



But with that coming days just after the 4-1 Champions League humbling in Como, the rest of us were primed for his P45.

He now seems like an interim manager again, on a zero-hours contract.



For Carrick, this was a waking nightmare of deja vu.

Plonked in front of half a dozen cameras and twice as many journalists with Amazon’s lenses yards away, he was asked for the third time in a week about his job.

Couple that with more questions on his spiky relationship with rebellious captain Bruno Fernandes and how the pair have apparently made up.

Quizzed on the growing pressure, Carrick said: “I don’t really see it. I see the things that I need to see. I don’t look for it. It doesn’t really help in any way.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Clearly, midfielder Fernandes’ one-match exile is over after he called out Carrick’s tactics in Italy last Wednesday — and now the manager must deliver wins.

Sky Sports News is off the TV screens at United’s Carrington training HQ.

Instead, yesterday’s broadcasts featured Formula 1 highlights and BBC News — a timely distraction for Carrick given the relentless speculation surrounding his future following the home hammering by the Cherries.

Carrick appeared to embark on a farewell lap of Old Trafford at full-time, as the Stretford End cheered him before unleashing blood-letting boos at the players once their teary-eyed manager was out of sight down the tunnel.

The owners and board also brutally copped it throughout the dismal game.



Carrick admitted: “The reception drew mixed feelings. My responsibility is to the players. Outside is not for me to focus on.

“I know what help the group needs, guidance at certain times and dealing with things, that’s part of my direct role. We have held a meeting, we’ve spoken.

“The boys are hungry. We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games. But there is an intensity, an edge, a hunger to do better.”



We are yet to see any intensity from United and failure to beat Chelsea will stretch the team’s winless run to NINE matches and could plunge the crisis club into the relegation zone.

The Red Devils are two points above basement side Sunderland, level on points with Crystal Palace and just one point ahead of Nottingham Forest and Coventry.

Despite 13 years of chaos and seven different managers, United have somehow suffered their worst league start in 40 years, with their sole league victory coming against new boys Ipswich in August.

Overall, it has been six defeats in 12 games in all competitions, 22 goals shipped and no sign of another win since they beat Euro minnows Sabah 49 DAYS ago.

Co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Avram Glazer and Joel Glazer held a conference call on Monday with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox to weigh up their options as fans express their frustrations.



United are not yet sold on ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe, 48, or 39-year-old former Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann.

Boardroom figures are also mindful that the international break after home matches against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and Aston Villa five days later offers a natural, cleaner window for a new manager to take charge.

Public enemy No1 Wilcox’s future has also come under intense scrutiny.



One source close to United feels it is inevitable the former Leeds and Blackburn winger, 55, will eventually lose his job if a third managerial change in as many seasons occurs under his watch.

Externally, the drama has focused on recruitment — or lack of it, specifically at left-back and up front — United’s finances and massive debt levels, Carrick’s relative inexperience and, other than assistant boss Steve Holland, that of his coaches.

Carrick confirmed United’s only natural striker Benjamin Sesko would be out until New Year with a shin injury picked up last term.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In a bid to clear the air, Carrick called a squad and staff summit — with no directors invited — to ensure everyone was singing from the same hymn sheet.

A private meeting with out-of-sorts skipper Fernandes, 32, was said to be productive but Carrick urgently needs his reigning Prem Player of the Season to step up and deliver if he is to keep his job.

Sports.title: Inside Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s tattered sporting empire with just one success story as Man Utd lead Ineos disasters
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED were supposed to be the jewel in the Ineos sporting crown after Sir Jim Ratcliffe completed his share purchase at his boyhood club.

Instead, the empire appears tattered, with one stand-out exception.



Ineos’ three football clubs are currently assailed from all sides, while cycling success feels like a long time ago and his relationship with New Zealand’s All Blacks has long since disintegrated.

But the outfit that is going around in circles is sprinting ahead of the chasing pack, with a youthful Italian star at the wheel. SunSport looks at the state of Ineos play.



MANCHESTER UNITED

When Ratcliffe celebrated his successful £1.3bn bid to take a 27 per cent stake but day-to-day control of United in early 2024 he set out his vision.

Sitting in Ineos’ Knightsbridge office base, he promised: “The fans would run out of patience if it was a 10-year plan.



“To think that we’re going to be playing football as good as Manchester City played against Real Madrid last year by next season is not sensible.

“If we give people false expectations, then they will get disappointed. But it’s certainly a three-year plan to get there. The key thing is our trajectory, so that people can see that we’re making progress.”

More than two and a half years on, United are back in the Champions League but on their third full-time manager in addition to caretakers Ruud van Nistelrooy and Darren Fletcher.

And it looks only a matter of time before Michael Carrick is jettisoned as well – probably during the looming international break next month.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The frustration and anger aimed at United’s miserable performances – this is their worst start to a league season in 40 years – while fans are still furious over a ticketing clampdown that has drawn street protests.

Now Ineos are looking to sell up – with a sales pitch sent out to potential investors.

The reality is that it has not been a successful tenure.



Within six months of the takeover, Lausanne were relegated and have since become something of a yo-yo club despite moving to a new 13,000-capacity home.

CHELSEA have reportedly lined up a January move for defender Jacobo Ramon.

The defender played a starring role in Como’s victory over Manchester United in the Champions League.



Ramon, 21, has been with the Serie A outfit since the summer of 2025, when he made the move from Real Madrid.

The centre-back has gone from strength to strength in Lombardy as he helped the club qualify for the UCL last season.



The Daily Mail have reported that Ramon’s impressive performances have caught the eye of the Blues.

Ramon played under Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso when he was coaching in Madrid’s youth system.



The report has claimed that the West Londoners are not the only Premier League team interested in his services.

United and Arsenal have both been credited with interest in the Spain U21 international.

A potential transfer would be further complicated as Madrid retain a 50 per cent sell-on clause.

The LaLiga giants are also said to hold a buy-back clause on the defender – though the amount has not been specified.

The Blues opted to pursue Jeremy Jacquet but missed out on the Frenchman to Liverpool.

Ramon did make an error in Como’s 3-1 win over Torino in Serie A on Tuesday night.

But he made up for the error as he headed in the equaliser before goals from Nico Paz and Martin Baturina scored.



Manager Cesc Fabregas was encouraged watching the Spaniard show his ability to bounce back.

He said: “There were many chances, we were doing so much very well and didn’t deserve to be trailing.

“Maybe we wouldn’t have won last season, but we have more solutions now.

“That must not make us relax, but instead focus on what we still need to improve.

Sports.title: Sir Patrick Stewart last pictured watching beloved Huddersfield Town football team as club pays tribute to ‘hero’
Sports.content:
Next

SIR PATRICK Stewart was last pictured watching his beloved football club as the team paid tribute to “hero” supporter.

The Hollywood icon, best known for starring in Star Trek and X-Men, passed away aged 86 following a battle with Alzheimer’s.



The die-hard fan, from Yorkshire, can be seen beaming as he watched Huddersfield Town FC play against Crawley on November 9, 2024.

Sir Patrick may have been the most famous supporter of the West Yorkshire football club – who he has followed since he was seven years old.





Speaking to Sky Sports Patrick said: “I’ve been a fan for 70 years. I get the same rush when I walk up the steps of any stadium, no matter where it is.”

In a heartbreaking tribute, Huddersfield Town described Patrick as “a titan of his craft and a legend and hero to millions worldwide”.

“Fiercely proud of his Yorkshire roots, Sir Patrick was a Terrier in every sense, and we’re proud to have counted him as one of our own.”

Sir Patrick died in his home in Los Angeles surrounded by his wife Sunny following a short battle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, according to his spokesperson.



The actor’s illustrious career on stage and screen spanned over 60 years.

Born into a working-class family in Mirfield, West Riding of Yorkshire, Patrick left school at 15 to pursue his dream of becoming an actor.

He shot to fame in 1987 when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation”.



Though initially skeptical about the show’s success – famously telling reporters he had his bags packed in case the series was cancelled – the show went on to run for over 170 episodes.

The star conquered a second massive franchise as the telepathic mutant Professor Charles Xavier in the highly lucrative “X-Men” films.

By the end of his career he had been showered with awards including a Grammy and two Oliviers.

He was also knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 for services to drama.

Hollywood stars and heartbroken family members have poured out their love for the actor, praising his “invincible grace”.



An emotional statement said his final days were “surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all.

“We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”

His loved ones added that his “professional accomplishments” were matched by his “philanthropy and activism” for survivors of domestic violence, refugees, veterans’ mental health services and animals.



Co-star Hugh Jackman – who played Wolverine in X-Men – also shared a post in memory to his “tremendous friend”.

Writing on Instagram, he said: “We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days.”

Marvel Studios said they were “heartbroken” to learn of his loss as the acting giant was due to reprise his role as Professor Charles Xavier in the upcoming film, Avengers: Doomsday.

ESTEVAO could make a shock exit from Chelsea in the January transfer window.

The Brazilian has largely been ignored Xabi Alonso since his arrival as manager at Stamford Bridge in the summer.



Estevao, 19, has played just 163 minutes this season and was an unused substitute during the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool on Wednesday.

It would not come as a huge surprise if the winger asked for a move away from the Blues in the new year.



Estevao would not be short of options as he would still be a highly-rated prospect in the football world.

His debut season at Chelsea saw him score eight goals and assist four more in just 36 appearances.



Despite that impressive return, Estevao has not had the chance to replicate it under Alonso.

This is despite fans and stats suggesting that the Blues are a better team with the teenager in it.

Estevao is likely to have a queue of interested clubs should he be made available in January.

SunSport have picked five clubs that the Brazilian could ditch Chelsea for...



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Liverpool

Estevao was linked with an exit in the summer window, with Liverpool keen on his services.

However, the Reds opted to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain in a £123million transfer.

The Frenchman has yet to score for the Reds in domestic competition – though he has three in the Champions League.

Liverpool could return for Estevao to further boost their attacking options.

A slot in the forwards could open up should Cody Gakpo make an exit following his summer interest from Manchester City and Tottenham.



Paris Saint-Germain

The back-to-back Champions League winners are in the market for another attacker following the exit of Barcola.

The need for another option for manager Luis Enrique was ramped up after the injury to star man Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who is expected to miss the rest of the season.

Estevao would represent a possible option for the Parisians in order to fill the void.



The Brazilian would not have a guaranteed starting role and would need to compete with the Desire Doue, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts.

Barcelona

Barcelona could be another side interested in signing Estevao once the window opens.

The LaLiga giants have been long-term admirers of the Brazilian since before his move to England.

A move to Catalonia would see Estevao compete with Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon.

He would allow Yamal the opportunity to be rested in easier LaLiga fixtures and give Gordon additional competition for a starting berth.



Barca fans could be open to seeing the former Everton and Newcastle star be replaced after being unimpressed with his recent showings.

Palmeiras

Chelsea may not want to permanently part ways with Estevao, whose contract does not expire until 2033.

He could be a completely different player in that time, so a temporary move could be the best option for all parties.



Estevao could fancy a return to his homeland with former club Palmeiras.

The Sao Paulo-based side would likely love the chance to play their former star again.

A move back to Brazil could provide Estevao with the platform to rediscover his confidence.

AC Milan

The Italian giants could be another option for Estevao to join on loan for the remainder of the season.

AC Milan are unlikely to have the funds to finance a permanent deal but could be tempted into a loan.

Sports.title: 'Lack of talent' - Alonso doubles down on Albon criticism
Sports.content:
Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso has doubled down on his criticism of "low level" Formula 1 drivers who have a "lack of talent" following his collision with Williams' Alex Albon in Austin.

Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars.

Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin.

Post-race, Alonso stated the quality of the drivers in the bottom third of F1's grid is "very low" and he had not changed his stance in Thursday's media day ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix.

"I think it's simply a very low level of driving and lack of talent," he told Sky Sports F1.

"When you make repeated mistakes throughout the season and have crashes and 50 per cent of your race is in Lap 1, if I was the team principal I would not be happy but if they are happy, I'm OK with that.

"When I see Max [Verstappen], Lewis [Hamilton] starting at the back when they change the engine or whatever, Kimi in Monza, they still win the races. Lap 1 is not the end of the world when you have your confidence and the talent to wait for one or two more laps."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix

Alonso says he will not bring up the issue in Friday's drivers' meeting as "it's part of the game" and it is down to Aston Martin to start higher up the grid to "get out of that part of the field".

"Some teams cannot score points. It's the same for us this year. You go into the races knowing you need eight DNFs to score points, so it's more about driving the best race to the finish line," he added.

"Probably if you're not having a good season, being beaten by your team-mate, whatever is in your head it brings extra frustration but other drivers and teams should not pay for that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso criticised 'low quality bottom third drivers' following his collision with Alex Albon in Austin

'Not nice to hear that' - Albon reacts to Alonso comments

Albon was told about Alonso's comments in the FIA press conference and argued the grid is as strong as it has been "for a while".

"I'll double down with what I said as well. I have a huge respect for Fernando. I looked up to him a lot growing up as a kid," said the Williams driver.

"It's not nice to hear those comments in many ways. You're racing someone that you look up to, but at the same time, I don't agree. It's as simple as that.

"I think level is strong up and down the grid. I think 10, 15 years ago, the back half the grid wasn't the way it is now. We don't have pay drivers anymore. It is what it is. Hopefully, we don't cross corners or cross paths in the race this weekend!"

What is a pay driver in F1? A pay driver in Formula 1 is a driver who has a seat mainly due to personal financial backing through sponsors or other wealth, which can help the team

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Williams driver Alex Albon disagrees with Fernando Alonso's assertion that there's a 'lack of talent' in the lower third of the Formula 1 grid

However, Alonso had pointed out his comments would be the same at any point in his career since he made his F1 debut in 2001.

"It's the same over the years. When you are at the back of the grid, the cars are difficult to drive, more difficult to drive - they have less grip so mistakes are coming more often because you don't have an environment which is under control and the car is not welcoming you in a nice way, so you make more mistakes.

"But I don't feel all the incidents in Lap 1 and the touches, the front wings that fly around, all these things are not necessary, especially when you are fighting for nothing at the back of the grid and there is the cost cap, adding to this problem.

"There are teams that are happy with the cost cap and breaking things every race. They can pay for them."

Sports.title: Everton see off Newcastle to reach Carabao Cup quarter-final
Sports.content:
Everton are through to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup after seeing off Newcastle 3-1.

James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry were all on the scoresheet at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday night. Dan Burn netted a late consolation for Newcastle.

The Toffees will head to Fleetwood Town in the last eight in December, after the League Two side's epic win over Arsenal earlier in the week.

It provides Everton with a real opportunity of reaching a first cup semi-final since 2016.

Grealish dropped due to disciplanary breach Everton announced before the game that Jack Grealish had been dropped due to a disciplinary breach. It was reporter that the Man City loanee had missed a training session earlier in the week.

The hosts found the lead from nothing on 34 minutes. Tyrique George's pressure saw Amar Dedic lose the ball on the sidelines. Hackney then flicked the ball into Garner, who finessed a shot into the bottom corner.

On the stroke of half-time it was 2-0. Hackney turned scorer this time as he guided home from Barry's cross, to claim his first goal for the club.

And then it was Barry's time on 69 minutes, finishing up a clinical counter-attack with some fine movement and a cool finish after picking up Kieran Dewsbury-Hall's pass.

Burn headed in late on for Newcastle, but it was too little, too late.

The key moments from the Hill Dickinson Stadium

12: CHANCE! Gonzalez picks out the smart run of Barnes down the left. The winger ghosts in behind Rohl to head towards goal but he draws a save from Pickford instead.

34: GOAL! Garner applies some finesse on his finish to put Everton ahead. It comes from nothing. Dedic loses it near the corner flag, under pressure from George. Hackney finds Garner with a neat pass and the Everton midfielder curls home.

45: GOAL! HACKNEY GUIDES HOME HIS FIRST EVERTON GOAL! It all starts from a Newcastle opportunity. Barnes' effort takes a nick, and Pickford gathers before starting an Everton counter. Dewsbury-Hall leads the charge forward before being taken out. Advantage is played and Barry keeps going, taking the ball wide before digging out a cross for Hackney to see home.

69: GOAL! NEWCASTLE ARE SLICED OPEN BY EVERTON. Garner carries the ball up the field and feeds Dewsbury-Hall. He continues the charge down the left, pulling back a cross into the area. Barry has all the time in the world in the Newcastle box to compose himself and fire into the top corner.

89: GOAL! Burn heads in to give his side a consolation. Willock swings a ball into the area and Burn, high up the field, beats O'Brien to the ball. Burn is then booked, along with Joelinton and Tarkowski for some pushing and shoving after the goal.

Sports.title: Grealish dropped by Everton after breaching club discipline
Sports.content:
Everton said Jack Grealish was unavailable for their Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against Newcastle 'due to a breach of club discipline'.

Grealish, who is on loan from Manchester City, missed Saturday's defeat at Arsenal due to illness but had started Everton's previous three Premier League matches against Ipswich, Hull City and Chelsea.

He was dropped by manager David Moyes for their cup tie at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday night after reportedly missing a training session.

Sky Sports News reporter Keith Downie said: "My understanding is the reason he's not involved, and the reason he has been disciplined, is because he failed to show for a training session in the build-up to tonight's cup tie."

Everton vs Newcastle is live on Sky Sports+.

Jarrad Branthwaite also remained unavailable for a second successive game as he continues to follow concussion protocols.

Sports.title: Antonelli to miss Mexico media day with viral illness
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli will miss Thursday's media day at the Mexico City Grand Prix due to a viral illness ahead of the weekend when he will likely become Formula 1 world champion.

A top-nine finish in this Sunday's race will ensure Antonelli becomes the sport's youngest world champion at 20 years old - breaking Sebastian Vettel's record by three years.

Should Antonelli not score any points on Sunday, he will still be world champion if his Mercedes team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton don't win the race.

But the 20-year-old is having to recover from an illness ahead of Friday's practice sessions at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.

Mercedes said: "Kimi is feeling under the weather today as he recovers from a viral illness. As a precaution, the FIA have excused him from his mandatory media duties to give him the chance to rest head of the weekend.

"We expect him to be back tomorrow."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at our picks of the pivotal moments that defined the F1 season, as Kimi Antonelli looks to secure the 2026 World Drivers' Championship in Mexico

Antonelli has executed a superb 2026 in just his second Formula 1 campaign, all the more surprising after a difficult rookie season.

The Italian has won nine races this season and consistently had the upper hand on Russell.

Several F1 championships have been won without the champion finishing on the podium in that race, but Antonelli is keen to "finish on a high".

"The perfect way would be to finish off in style and enjoy the rest of the season," he told Sky Sports F1 after winning in Austin.

"First we focus and worry about finishing this [season] well and we will see."

Sports.title: Uefa close to selecting candidate to run against Infantino in Fifa election
Sports.content:
Uefa and its allies are close to identifying a candidate to run against Gianni Infantino in the Fifa election and could select the challenger as early as next week.

The clock is ticking on efforts to oppose Infantino in March, with candidates required to confirm they are standing by 18 November, but there is growing confidence those attempts are nearing a successful resolution. Discussions with potential nominees have gained momentum despite recent setbacks that included a U-turn by the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, who surprisingly endorsed Infantino’s push for a fourth term.

Should an opponent’s identity be confirmed, it will be presented to Uefa’s executive committee and in an online meeting of the confederation’s FA heads. There remains an appetite to leave any announcement until as close to the deadline as possible, largely to head off the possibility of a “dirty tricks” campaign by Fifa against the proposed candidate, but some sources believe the relevant meetings may be called in the next seven days.

Although Arsène Wenger has been among the high-profile names mooted, and is highly favoured as a potential unity candidate in some European football circles, the former Arsenal manager is not believed to have seriously entered the reckoning. Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global football development, could be found at the Fifa Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan this week extolling the virtues of his employer’s new tournament.

Anyone confirming their desire to stand will have to tackle severe doubts about the prospects of defeating Infantino, who has embarked on an international effort to recover his position in recent weeks after being heavily damaged by the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scandal. They would need to add a substantial number of votes from Asia, Concacaf and Africa to the European bloc, which itself may not be taken for granted in a secret ballot, to reach the 106 required.

There has been growing cynicism in some corners about the prospects of unseating Infantino in an election, one argument being that a more effective strategy would be a mass boycott or abstention from the vote in Rabat. A view exists that this would isolate Infantino, who has never hidden the fact that his organisation is dependent on Europe for vast amounts of its revenue. Now he finds it in a form of administrative paralysis. The 2029 men’s Club World Cup, currently without a host, is among the events stuck in a deep freeze with little progress being made on its shape or location.

View image in fullscreen Aleksander Ceferin is a strong critic of Gianni Infantino’s actions. Photograph: Mark Pain/Alamy

But there remains a determination to face down Infantino in March, with some close to the process pointing out that events may have turned further against the Fifa president by then. Infantino faces the spectre of Uefa’s application to four courts in the US for the release of documents pertaining to the failed FFE scheme, with a view to lodging a criminal complaint in Switzerland alleging financial mismanagement. Fifa has accused Uefa of “harassment” and “misinformation” and denied wrongdoing by Infantino.

A preliminary ruling is expected in the coming weeks, although the prospect of Fifa appealing against any decision that goes against it means the process may be extended. Should Uefa make significant progress with the case, any election or candidature process may come to feel inconsequential.

Fifa has until Monday, a deadline set by Uefa, to respond to 42 questions regarding its governance and decision making. Those include issues surrounding FFE, the Fifa peace prize and the suspension of Folarin Balogun’s ban at the World Cup. The Guardian understands Uefa is yet to receive any response. Infantino said last week that Fifa would “answer all the questions posed, to the extent that the process allows and to the best of our ability”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The US midterms, which will be held on Tuesday, may provide further hope for Infantino’s opponents. In July Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House judiciary committee, launched an investigation into links between Infantino, Fifa and the Trump administration. He asked Infantino to provide relevant documents and sit for a transcribed interview, although that is yet to take place. Should the Democrats flip the House, currently controlled by the Republicans, his quest may receive fresh impetus.

Regardless, the period before 18 November feels critical for Uefa and its president, Aleksander Ceferin. The Slovene has driven a hardline approach against Fifa’s leadership, which he restated in his “Emperor’s New Clothes” polemic against Infantino at the general assembly of European Football Clubs in Copenhagen last month. Fielding a viable candidate would go a long way towards underlining its credibility.

A repeat of Uefa’s climbdown on the eve of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, when it withdrew its threat to boycott the competition, would prove damaging. The extensive autumn charm offensive launched by Infantino has included visits to Latvia, Czechia and Azerbaijan.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership makes first UK move to remove Saturday 3pm broadcast blackout
Sports.content:
The Scottish Premiership has made the first move in what is expected to be a coordinated attempt from the UK’s domestic leagues to remove the Saturday afternoon broadcast blackout by inviting bids to televise all of its matches in the next rights cycle from 2029.

A tender document issued by the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) last week is understood to have given broadcasters an option to bid for live rights to all matches, including games kicking off at 3pm on Saturdays, the domestic broadcast of which is currently prohibited under Article 48 of Uefa’s statutes.

The Guardian revealed last year that the Premier League and English Football League were eager for the blackout to be lifted because they have concluded that selling more matches to broadcasters is the best way to raise revenues, a view that also appears to have taken hold in Scotland.

The SPFL’s invitation to tender, first reported by Sports Business, is understood to give bidders the flexibility to bid on the basis of the blocked hours governed by Article 48 not being in place.

A source with knowledge of the tender said it appeared increasingly unlikely that the four British Football Associations would apply blocked hours in their territories after 2029.

UK broadcasters are prevented from showing live football between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays when 50% of games in the top two divisions take place during that period, a provision that means 3pm kick-offs can be broadcast on FA Cup weekends and on weekend bank holidays over Christmas.

The UK is the last country in Europe to invoke Article 48, which allows associations to stipulate a period during which matches cannot be televised live in their territory.

While the English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish FAs are responsible for applying Article 48, they will be guided by the wishes of the clubs.

UK broadcasters can currently show up to 270 Premier League matches, 1,059 EFL games and 82 from the Scottish Premiership, amounting to 35% of fixtures across the season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Premier League chief executive, Richard Masters, said in August the subject of lifting Article 48 was a live discussion. “We’ve got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change,” he told TalkSport. “It’s not a decision for now. It’s a decision we’ve got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do. I’d say in about 18 months’ time we’ll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not.”

Sports.title: Carrick keeps Fernandes as captain and says he needs no assurances on United future
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has said he will not strip Bruno Fernandes of the Manchester United captaincy after dropping him for the defeat by Bournemouth and that he is not surprised to have kept his job as the head coach.

Carrick and Fernandes held talks this week after the Portuguese criticised the tactics in the loss to Como, resulting in the midfielder being an unused substitute on Sunday. Harry Maguire took the armband but will not retain it for Saturday’s game at Chelsea, with Carrick saying “there is no decision to be made” and praising Fernandes.

“He’s an important player for this group,” he said. “He has been and he will be. Between us, we’ve got to make a difference and we’ve got to push things in a good direction. He’s fully committed to this football club, he’s fully committed to making things better. It doesn’t change for me. He’s the one that’s kind of led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he’ll continue to do that.”

Carrick’s future remains unclear but he has been given a chance to turn around United’s form. The hierarchy held talks over whether to stick with Carrick at the start of the week after eight games without a win, including a wait of more than two months for a Premier League victory. There is keen interest in Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann as potential replacements.

“I don’t need any assurances from anyone,” Carrick said. “I totally get the position, I understand the job, I understand the responsibilities, I understand what comes with that.”

Asked whether he was surprised still to be in charge, Carrick said: “No, I am here to do my job. I am here to do the best for the team, and I am desperate to make us better and improve things, so I’m not surprised, no.”

The United supporters cheered Carrick off after the Bournemouth game, turning their anger on the players, who were booed at Old Trafford. “I care about what the supporters think,” Carrick said. “I care about what it feels like in the stadium, and them travelling for games, to come and see us and support us.

“I care about what we give them, and what we offer them, and what they see. I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings, I know what we need to do really to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me anything else.”

United will be without the striker Benjamin Sesko until the new year because of a shin injury but Carrick was boosted by Kobbie Mainoo’s return to training this week.

Sports.title: Max Dowman to miss three games after Arsenal’s red card appeal rejected
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s appeal against Max Dowman’s red card in their Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwood and the three-match suspension imposed has been rejected by an independent commission.

The 16-year-old Dowman was sent off for a kick out at Harrison Neal following a bruising tackle in the 85th minute of the game, which Fleetwood won on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Arsenal subsequently lodged an appeal, but the Football Association confirmed on Thursday an independent commission had dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Dowman.

As a result, Dowman will be suspended for Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool as well as their home game with Hull and trip to Newcastle either side of the international break.

The FA said the written reasons for the commission’s decision to dismiss the claims would be published in due course.

The Arsenal manager, Mikel Arteta, said after Tuesday’s match he had not spoken to Dowman about his dismissal, but added: “When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate, it was very clear.”

After Fleetwood’s keeper, Jay Lynch, saved Bruno Guimarães’ penalty, 19-year-old defender Conor Haughey stepped up to fire the hosts into the quarter-finals with one of the biggest upsets in the competition’s history. Fleetwood will host another Premier League giant, either Everton or Newcastle, in the last eight.

Arsenal fell behind to Aaron Loupalo-Bi’s 21st-minute strike in a disjointed first-half performance after Arteta made nine changes.

The captain, Martin Ødegaard, came on at half-time and Viktor Gyökeres quickly levelled, but Dowman was dismissed before Lynch starred in the shootout to secure a memorable victory.

Sports.title: Everton drop Jack Grealish from Carabao Cup tie over ‘breach of club discipline’
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish has been dropped from the Everton squad for tonight’s Carabao Cup tie against Newcastle over a breach of club discipline.

Everton took the unusual step of announcing that Grealish’s omission was for disciplinary reasons on social media, after listing David Moyes’s team for the fourth-round tie at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The club posted on X: “Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline.”

It is understood the 31-year-old missed training on Monday without permission.

Grealish returned to training at Everton’s Finch Farm complex after Monday’s absence but is expected to be fined for his unauthorised absence earlier in the week. The playmaker had missed Everton’s defeat at Arsenal on Saturday due to illness.

The England international rejoined Everton on a season’s loan from Manchester City this summer and had started in four successive games for Moyes’s side prior to Arsenal. Everton paid £12m in total to have Grealish on loan last season and are paying a similar sum for this campaign. He will become a free agent at the end of this season when his lucrative contract with City expires.

Sports.title: Chelsea’s fine finishing has them flying high – but how long can it last?
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick will arrive at Stamford Bridge on Saturday with the air of a dead man walking. Yet despite Manchester United being fifth-bottom of the Premier League and Chelsea fifth-top, the Blues have performed worse this season according to Opta’s expected points model.

Is there a glitch in the matrix? Has the fabled supercomputer clicked on a suspicious link? Even though the margin between their data is small, it feels unthinkable that Chelsea could be below United’s level.

That is until you review a few statistics. Xabi Alonso’s side held healthy expected goal margins in their wins over Fulham, Brighton and Everton, but were heavily outgunned against Arsenal and Brentford. The xG count went slightly against them versus Hull, Bournemouth and Tottenham, which is concerning when all three were at home in matches they would reasonably expect to win.

Opta’s data suggests Chelsea are the 12th-best team in the Premier League. They have risen to fifth by virtue of a hot finishing streak. Chelsea have scored 6.7 goals more than the quality of their chances imply they deserve, second only to Brighton (6.8), or above them if penalties are excluded. Chelsea scored five times from 10 shots against Bournemouth; while not without precedent, managing so many goals from so few efforts happens less than once a season in the Premier League.

Jordan Henderson has scored twice from five shots outside the box, after finding the net once for every 20 long-range efforts he attempted between 2014 and last season. Pedro Neto’s total of three league goals is two shy of his career best for a Premier League campaign. Morgan Rogers outscoring his expected goals figure is not unusual but he is ahead by 1.87 when he was up 3.15 across the whole of last season. This trio are unlikely to maintain such hot form across another 30 league games.

Adding in João Pedro gives Chelsea four of the 12 players who are above their non-penalty xG by at least 1.5 in the Premier League this season. The two league games the Brazilian missed are the two in which Chelsea failed to score, mustering a combined 1.3 expected goals across those matches (against Brentford and Tottenham). João Pedro’s return from injury cannot come soon enough for the club.

This is not least because he provides a good focal point for the frontline, even when he is not scoring. Data from Gradient Sports shows João Pedro has had possession in the opposition penalty area 5.7 times per 90 minutes this season, the most among centre-forwards with at least 400 minutes in the Premier League. Despite playing in wide areas, Estêvão Willian’s average for this metric is 5.8 since joining Chelsea. No single stat can justify a player’s inclusion but the teenager is being omitted when he offers something the team lack in João Pedro’s absence.

Keeping possession in the penalty area has become increasingly difficult for Chelsea, who have dwindled after a positive start. Third in the division for opposition box touches after four matches, they now sit eighth. While Premier League home teams are averaging 27 touches per match in the box, Chelsea had 17 in their previous two games at Stamford Bridge. Given their possession average is markedly lower than in any recent campaign, it could prove difficult to increase their penalty area activity.

Alonso has overseen three league matches in which Chelsea had a maximum 38% possession; he had four such games in almost three years at Leverkusen. This is not as game-state driven as you might assume. Chelsea had 40.8% possession at the point they went 3-1 up at Fulham, 34.6% thereafter. They raced into a 3-0 lead against Brighton despite attempting 28.4% of the total passes to that point.

This cannot be by design when Alonso’s Bundesliga-winning Leverkusen team topped the German possession standings with 61.8%. He acknowledged as much when quizzed on the issue before Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Anfield. “You want to have possession,” Alonso said. “Knowing the context, knowing what we are building, I think that we have room for improvement in that part. We need to play more confidently with the ball.”

History shows Champions League qualification is unlikely with Chelsea’s 46.5% possession. The miracle of Leicester’s title win provides the only instance from the past 12 seasons of a team finishing in the top four with a lower possession average. Beyond that, West Ham finishing sixth in 2020-21 is the best showing.

Things may improve once the tactical plan becomes embedded and the lineup settles. Alonso has deployed 3-4-3 and 4-2-3-1, neither for more than three consecutive league games. Only Tottenham have averaged more changes to their starting XI from game to game in the Premier League (and this with neither side having to rotate owing to European commitments). Chelsea have started three goalkeepers, summoning distant memories of 1996-97 when Craig Forrest, Kevin Hitchcock, Nick Colgan, Frode Grodås and Dmitri Kharine got starts between the sticks. It is little surprise the Blues have the second-worst rate in the division for conceding over their expected goal level.

Much is up in the air at Stamford Bridge, yet there is a weird sense of certainty about Manchester United. They are a poor team and Carrick will surely leave soon. Alonso is a long way from the exit door but many questions need answering about his side.

Sports.title: AC Milan and Inter reveal first pictures of new stadium as San Siro replacement unveiled after £543million naming rights deal
Sports.content:
Italian giants AC Milan and Inter have detailed first images of their proposed new stadium ahead of the demolishing of the San Siro. The two sides have long looked to move on from their iconic home, with plans to destroy it initially put on hold until things got back on track recently. The teams shared a preview video of the new ground, with the aim of it opening in the 2031-32 season. It is set to be called the Generali Stadium, with naming rights sold to the brand until 2052 for £543million. Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans. It is to feature an X-frame structure and double-curved roof, with the frame to emphasise two curves, with one dedicated to Inter fans and the other Milan supporters. The stadium will be two-tiered, and will also be built with the idea of hosting concerts, with more public spaces, green areas and leisure and retail areas to be included. Milan and Inter had initially planned on starting building in 2027, with plans to demolish the San Siro put into place as far back as 2019. A new symbol for Milano. A new home for future generations of fans. Generali Stadium 🏟️@GENERALI pic.twitter.com/c7D0827E7T — AC Milan (@acmilan) October 29, 2026 Inter and AC Milan have revealed images of their proposed new stadium ahead of the demolition of the San Siro The stadium will l also host concerts, though won't be ready until the 2031-32 season Two different outside views were shared - one with blue for Inter's games, and one red for AC Milan's games Construction won't begin until 2028, and the stadium is set to hold 71,500 fans in total Images shared of the proposed stadium show the ground in all its expected glory in the heart of Milan. One design showed a hypothetical game between Inter and AC Milan, with giant tifos of both sides shown in the ground. The proposal of a concert is also presented, with bright lights on show and thousands of fans in the stadium. There was initially no objection to the plans, but negotiations dragged on and concerns began to rise over the cultural impact of demolishing the ground, which was built more than 100 years ago. In 2023, it was ruled that the San Siro could not be demolished because it has 'cultural interest'. In 2025, however, the clubs bought the site to build a new ground, which made the decision to demolish the ground possible. In its initial form the stadium was completed in 1926 but the middle tier, along with the iconic spiral towers, was added in 1955. The San Siro was supposed to host the Champions League final this season, but was stripped of the right by UEFA after authorities in the Italian city could not offer guarantees that refurbishment work at the stadium and the surrounding area would not affect the match. The aim is to host matches at Euro 2032, which Italy will co-host with Turkey.

Sports.title: Man United consider shock Dominic Calvert-Lewin move as club launch search for new striker after Benjamin Sesko injury blow left them with NO fit centre-forward
Sports.content:
Manchester United are exploring the possibility of a move for Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the club looks to strengthen in attack in January. Daily Mail Sport understands a move is viewed as difficult given the fierce rivalry between the two clubs. Calvert-Lewin has revitalised his career at Leeds after joining on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, following an injury-plagued end to his time at Everton. The 29-year-old has scored 20 goals in 49 appearances for Leeds, including five in ten games at the start of this season. Calvert-Lewin scored against Man United when the two sides played out a 1-1 draw earlier this month. The forward’s form earned him an England recall during the last international window, ending a five-year absence from the national team set-up. Man United are exploring a possible move for Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin Calvert-Lewin netted against the Red Devils in a 1-1 draw between the sides earlier this month Man United are currently without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko on the sidelines Calvert-Lewin, who has started 38 times in his 43 Premier League appearances for Leeds, is currently contracted until 2028. Man United are currently operating without a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko having been ruled out until at least January with a shin injury. The 23-year-old was struggling with the issue at the beginning of the season and saw his game time carefully managed as the club attempted to nurse him back to full fitness but those efforts now appear to have been in vain. Sesko has not featured for the club since their defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on September 16, when he was substituted in the 66th minute. He missed all of pre-season with the complaint, which also plagued him last season and resurfaced against Liverpool in May, causing him to miss the final three Premier League games. The Slovenian, who pulled out of international duty last month, now looks set to be sidelined until the new year, dealing a major blow to United during a difficult run of form and leaving Michael Carrick without a recognised striker. WHEN LEEDS STARS JOIN MAN UNITED Eric Cantona - November 1992 Cantona's move to Man United was credited as one of Sir Alex Ferguson's most successful moves, with the Frenchman helping to transform his side into title winners. The maverick star had seen his relationship break down with Leeds boss Howard Wilkinson leading to speculation over a departure. Leeds chairman Bill Fotherby called his Man United counterpart Martin Edwards to enquire about signing Denis Irwin. After the suggestion was rebuffed by Edwards, Ferguson then asked about Cantona’s availability with a £1.2m deal then being struck. While initially seen as a risky move, Cantona helped inspire Man United to a first title in 26 years. The Frenchman was part of four title winning sides at Old Trafford and won two FA Cups. Rio Ferdinand - July 2002 Ferdinand became the most expensive British footballer in history when he completed a £30m move in 2002 after two seasons at Leeds. Ferdinand has claimed he sat in the office of Leeds chairman Peter Ridsdale for six hours to force through the transfer. The deal came amid growing concerns over Leeds financial situation, which was referenced by Sir Alex Ferguson when the transfer was completed. ‘A transfer like this has to be difficult. Leeds are a big club and our fiercest rivals, and he had four years left on his contract,’ Ferguson said. ‘We were hopeful because of Leeds' financial position. I think Peter Ridsdale has admitted that. Most importantly, Rio wanted to come here and this contributed to the deal.’ Ferdinand would go on to win six Premier League titles, the Champions League and two League Cups during his time with the Red Devils. Alan Smith - May 2004 Life-long Leeds fan Smith moved to Old Trafford in a deal worth £7million, with Danny Pugh going the opposite way. Smith opted to make the move following Leeds relegation to the Championship, which had left him in tears on the final day of the season. Smith's move angered Leeds fans having previously declared he would never play for Man United. The move, however, had helped Leeds amid the club's financial turmoil with Smith also waving a fee that was owed to him. Sir Alex Ferguson hailed Smith, stating 'I have never been more impressed with a young player, his desire to play for Manchester United is fantastic'. Smith career at Man United was heavily impacted by a broken leg and dislocated ankle he suffered in an FA Cup tie against Liverpool. He ultimately played 93 times for Man United, scoring 12 times, before moving to Newcastle. Karl Darlow - July 2026 Darlow is the most recent player to move between the two clubs, with the goalkeeper rejected a new deal at Leeds in favour of a move to Old Trafford. He had been Leeds first choice goalkeeper for much of last season but is now back-up to Senne Lammens at United. Darlow made his debut in Man United's Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton. When his summer move was confirmed, Leeds issued a 309-word statement but declined to name where Darlow had moved, instead stating he 'wished to explore a different challenge'. Right winger Bryan Mbeumo has been filling in at No9, starting their last five games there in all competitions, with Michael Carrick having lost faith in Dutchman Joshua Zirkzee. The decades-old rivalry between the clubs was highlighted in the summer when goalkeeper Karl Darlow became the first player to join Man United from Leeds since Alan Smith in 2004. Leeds refused to mention Man United in a statement confirming Darlow's departure at the end of his contract, with the club writing that he had 'wished to explore a different challenge'. Eric Cantona and Rio Ferdinand are among the most famous examples of star names to swap Leeds for the Red Devils. Daniel James moved from Man United to Leeds in a £25million transfer back in 2021, while Cameron Borthwick-Jackson was part of a rare loan deal between the sides in 2017 when Leeds were in the Championship.

Sports.title: What England learned from a disastrous tri-series in Pakistan: The big questions they need to answer and why Brendon McCullum has a tough task in bid to challenge for World Cup, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
England eventually won a game in the ODI tri-series in Pakistan, beating Sri Lanka by 55 runs in Lahore – a victory that came too late to reach Saturday’s final.

But what questions do they need to resolve before next month’s three-match series in Australia, asks Daily Mail Sport's cricket correspondent LAWRENCE BOOTH?

Who should open the batting?

Ben Duckett cemented his place by following Sunday’s 105 against Pakistan with a superb career-best 167 off 132 balls against Sri Lanka. Only Dawid Malan, Jonathan Trott and Joe Root have a higher ODI average for England than his 45 – and Duckett scores at a run a ball.

But who walks out with him at Perth on November 13? Jacob Bethell will be fit again after a knee injury, but Tom Banton has averaged 56 with a strike-rate of 108 since stepping in as opener for September’s home series against Sri Lanka, and over the past fortnight has put on 91, 74, four and 163 with Duckett, making himself difficult to drop.

Ben Duckett cemented his place by following Sunday’s 105 against Pakistan with a superb career-best 167 off 132 balls against Sri Lanka

What if Bethell goes in lower down?

With Jos Buttler still recovering from hamstring surgery, there will be room for Bethell at No 5 in Australia. But a fit Buttler walks into the first-choice XI, and the World Cup is only a year away. If England want to fit both him and Bethell into the middle order, Sam Curran can’t come in any higher than No 7 – the appropriate position, you might think, for someone with an ODI batting average of 23.

If Curran’s down at No7, how do England balance attack?

Not easily. Curran can’t be their third seamer on flat pitches, as his four wickets at 54 in this tournament confirmed. When England needed late breakthroughs in their two freakish defeats by Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi and Pakistan in Lahore, his variations were of little use.

But if he’s their fourth seamer, batting at No 7, that leaves room for only one frontline spinner. Since Ben Stokes’s retirement, England have lacked a seam-bowling all-rounder capable of batting in the top six – and Curran’s performances in Pakistan have been a reminder that they regularly feel a player short.

When England needed late breakthroughs in their two freakish defeats by Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi and Pakistan in Lahore, Curran's variations were of little use

Can England play Rashid and Dawson in the same side?

Only if they’re willing to limit themselves to three frontline seamers. But it’s not impossible, and it’s certainly tempting. Dawson collected a career-best four for 49 today/yesterday, and took the crucial wicket of Pavan Rathnayake. He was England’s leading wicket-taker in the series, with seven, and their tightest bowler, going at just five an over.

But Rashid has long been England’s white-ball banker, particularly in the middle overs, when they can look toothless. The selectors decided his leg-breaks would be less effective on Pakistani pitches than Dawson’s slow left-armers. But only Jimmy Anderson has more than Rashid’s 244 ODI wickets for England, and his ability to turn it both ways might have transformed the two-wicket defeat by Sri Lanka and the one-wicket defeat by Pakistan into a pair of wins.

England also know that the off-breaks of Will Jacks and Joe Root, plus Bethell’s slow left-armers, offer other spin options – though they have been stung in the past trying to turn that trio into a composite fifth bowler.

England also know that the off-breaks of Will Jacks and Joe Root, plus Bethell’s (above) slow left-armers, offer other spin options

What’s their first-choice seam attack?

Jofra Archer’s pace and hostility were missed in Pakistan, and he will take the new ball in Australia. Jamie Overton offered bounce and aggression in the middle overs, and went at only 5.26 an over.

But the rest all come with question marks. Gus Atkinson was less effective with the old ball than the new, Josh Tongue had an economy-rate of almost nine, and Sonny Baker cost nearly eight – but did take the important wicket of Janith Liyanage in Lahore. Henry Crocombe is still wet behind the ears.

Where does it all leave England?

Three defeats out of four have left them eighth in the ODI rankings, between Afghanistan and Bangladesh. Since World Cups are rarely won by a team outside the top two, they have a lot of work ahead if they are to ‘seriously challenge’ for next year’s trophy, as head coach Brendon McCullum put it. Against an Australian side sure to be weakened because of a punishing Test schedule, nothing but a series win will do.

Sports.title: How 'football geek' Kim Hellberg turned Middlesbrough into the 'PSG of the Championship' - thanks to 'Del Boy and Rodney', the next Harry Kane and the transfer strategy that's taken them to a new level
Sports.content:
I was sat in the press conference room at St Mary’s Stadium back in May when Kim Hellberg forced back tears as he talked about everything he’d sacrificed. All the time spent away from his family, all those nights when he called them to say he wouldn’t be coming home because he had more Southampton matches to watch. And despite them all, there the Middlesbrough manager still sat, beaten in the second leg of the Championship play-off semi-final by a manager who sent staff to spy on his training session and who was, for now, going to Wembley. ‘I have nothing to say to him,’ Hellberg had replied when asked if he had spoken to Southampton boss Tonda Eckert. Hellberg had already completed his TV and local radio interviews but informed club staff that he still had things, about sacrifices, that he wanted to say. In the end, of course, it was not over for Hellberg and Boro. Thanks to Daily Mail Sport’s stunning Spygate exclusive, Saints were eventually expelled and Boro went to Wembley in their place. By then, though, the chaos had taken its toll. Those who saw Hellberg in the build-up to the play-off final described him as exhausted and drained. As did his players, who were left in limbo as they tried, somehow, to remain fit and alert. Luke Ayling, the club’s captain, found out they were going to Wembley while he was bathing his young son just days before the final. Middlesbrough lost to Hull, and had to prepare for a 10th successive season in the Championship. They should have gone up automatically but blew it, having spent most of the season second in the table. All of that madness and heartbreak could, quite easily, have left Boro with too many scars and yet they host Charlton this weekend sitting top of the Championship, on a 10-game unbeaten run. Somehow, Boro have kicked on again and sources close to the dressing room believe they are better set than ever for a return to the top flight. Kim Hellberg has led Middlesbrough to the top of the Championship as they banish all memories of Spygate Aidan Morris celebrates scoring against Burnley last month - Boro are flying as they welcome Charlton on Saturday on a 10-game unbeaten run For a start, Spygate has barely been mentioned. There’s been no talk of it, according to club insiders, except to discuss the impending return to St Mary’s at the end of November, one which everyone expects to be poisonous. That has certainly not been helped by the FA’s decision to, effectively, let Eckert off scot free, and how much the Saints and their fans have appeared to revel in it. ‘Everyone in football knows it’s nonsense,’ said one source. Boro, meanwhile, have just got better. It helps when you play like Paris Saint-Germain. ‘People might laugh,’ said Hellberg, who twice made a point last week of claiming Boro’s style of play shows similarities to the French giants. Hellberg watched PSG’s clash with Barcelona in the Champions League and was drawn to the similar ‘massive spaces’ left in their midfield as they look to be brave in attack. That is how Hellberg wants his side to play, as risky as it sometimes looks to the casual observer, because it means creating a horde of good chances. They have the most xG (expected goals, which measures the quality of chances created) of any team in the league. Their 'expected goal difference', the gulf between the chances they create and concede, has rocketed since Hellberg took over from Rob Edwards almost a year ago. Now, they have the player they needed to take those chances in striker Will Lankshear, the Championship’s top scorer, who has recently been labelled the ‘next Harry Kane’. No pressure. Having been released by Arsenal, then gone through the Tottenham academy (via Sheffield United) before being sent out on loan to several clubs, there are plenty of parallels there, not least because Lankshear is proving himself to be one of the most lethal English strikers around. His 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland. Like Kane, he’s a superb technical finisher. There was some surprise when Tottenham agreed to sell him in the summer for an initial £8million that could rise to £20m. But with Roberto De Zerbi showing little interest in academy players, Lankshear knew he had to make a move to get game time. Spurs inserted a matching rights clause should anyone try to swoop in for him. Will Lankshear's 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland
