Sources close to the dressing room talk of a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers from elsewhere in the Championship, Europe, and Premier League, including Leeds, because he knew he would be given the minutes to flourish, in a team that creates heaps of chances and just needed someone to finish them off. ‘I’ve learnt as much as I have my whole life in one week under Kim,’ said Lankshear recently. So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders. Hellberg rested him for their recent game against Cardiff, only for the 21-year-old to come off the bench to score the equaliser. You suspect he won’t be making the same mistake again. Sources describe Hellberg as a ‘football geek’. He grew up, like many men in their 30s, playing Football Manager. When previewing Boro’s trip to Bolton last week, a thumping 5-1 win that sent them top, Hellberg said he hadn’t been there before but remembered playing against the likes of Jay-Jay Okocha and Kevin Nolan on the video game. One of his heroes, Frank Lampard, phoned him to offer some words of advice ahead of the play-off final. Hellberg celebrated the Bolton win by rewatching the game three times. He’d likely have watched it more if they lost. When he was asked by a Charlton reporter last season if he had ever been to the Valley, Hellberg revealed he had with his dad Stefan, also a football coach in Sweden, during tours of a few grounds in London when he was a young boy. Hellberg is described as a hands-on coach, one who likes to bombard his players with video clips about the minutiae of their game, and their opponents'. He’s hot on his data. Those who see him week in, week out, say he’s forever dropping stats into conversations and press conferences. His first role was in the part-time Swedish seventh tier, during which he worked as a gymnastics teacher, and in a kindergarten teaching three to six-year-olds. ‘They are more like the players than you think,’ said Hellberg. Sources talk of Lankshear as a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders As with many clubs on the rise – and on the slide – the foundations for that success, or failure, come from far above the grass. Just days after the Wembley heartache, Hellberg sat down with head of football Kieran Scott and head of recruitment Chris Jones to draw up their plans and key targets for the summer. Boro landed most of them. They beat lots of clubs to Lankshear, whom they had tracked for a while. They snapped up Ashley Phillips, also from Spurs, who was their top defensive target. And Radek Vitek, from Manchester United, their top goalkeeper target. The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’. Adilson Malanda, the French centre back, was described by one source as the ‘nearest we’ve had to Jonathan Woodgate since Jonathan Woodgate’. ‘We signed the quality that we didn’t have 12 months ago,’ said one club insider. ‘They are a level better. That’s the huge difference.’ This is what Boro have got really good at. Signing players to improve them, develop them, and sell them on at a huge profit. Scott and Jones, who describe themselves as ‘Del Boy and Rodney’ due to their constant need to sell the club to potential signings who might have glitzier offers, don’t have hordes of analysts but sit there themselves with data software SkillCorner and StatsBomb. And it’s working. A report by the CIES Football Observatory showed that Boro’s players have appreciated in value by nearly £150m over the last five years – the ninth-highest total in the country, ahead of Villa and Arsenal and just behind Chelsea. They consistently make a profit on their stars. They signed Morgan Rogers for £1m in 2023 only to sell him to Villa for up to £17m seven months later. When he joined Chelsea this summer for £117m, they banked another £21m as a world-record sell-on fee. Finn Azaz signed for £2m and was sold to Saints for £12m. Emmanuel Latte Lath, signed for £5m and flogged for £22.5m. Rav van den Berg, signed for less than £500k and sold for £11m. The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’ Morgan Rogers (centre) was bought for £2m, sold for £17m seven months later and earned Boro another £21m in sell-on fees when he moved to Chelsea this summer ‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together’ Academy players have brought in huge profits, too. Like Hayden Hackney, who joined Everton in the summer for £16.5m, Djed Spence, who headed for Spurs in a move worth up to £20m and Marcus Tavernier, who signed for Bournemouth for £12m. As Del Boy would say, lovely jubbly. The last time Boro lost in the play-off final, to Norwich in 2015, chairman and owner Steve Gibson gave a rousing speech to his troops to promise they would come back stronger, and they did. They went up automatically the following season. There is a similar feeling now around Teesside. Club insiders talk of the strongest bond between the club and the community since the days of Juninho and Fabrizio Ravanelli in the 90s. Their attendances, in what is the year of their 150th anniversary, are their highest since they were last in the Premier League. ‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together.’

Sports.title: Jack Grealish is DROPPED by Everton due to 'breach of club discipline' as midfielder misses Carabao Cup clash with Newcastle
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish is DROPPED by Everton due to 'breach of club discipline' as midfielder misses Carabao Cup clash with Newcastle

Jack Grealish has been disciplined by Everton after missing a training session without permission.

The Toffees winger, 31, has been left out of David Moyes's squad to play Newcastle in the Carabao Cup after the club punished him.

Grealish was said to be 'ill' when he missed Saturday's trip to Arsenal.

But now it is understood the Manchester City loanee has been reprimanded by Everton and was not part of the match day squad on Thursday night.

The club simply wrote on social media, accompanying the team news: 'Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of Club discipline.'

The midfielder has had a stop-start season so far, having failed to register a goal or assist in eight matches so far.

Jack Grealish was left out of Everton's squad for their game against Newcastle after missing a training session without permission

Grealish (pictured with partner Sasha Attwood) was absent after missing training prior to the game on Thursday - Instagram: sashaa__attwood

He returned to Merseyside on loan in the summer from Manchester City after being frozen out of their squad last season.

Last season, he played 22 games, including 20 in the Premier League, scoring two goals and picking up two assists.

He has been regularly included on the left of attack, but Tyler Dibling and Tyrique George were used out wide against Newcastle.

It comes after Grealish was praised by fans after donating £10,000 to the fundraising campaign of an Everton supporter suffering aggressive kidney cancer.

DJ Anton Powers – an Evertonian – is believed to have shared the efforts launched by the family of Leon, 35, on Wednesday night, with Grealish quickly responding to the call-out with a generous donation.

'What an absolute gent Jack Grealish is,' Powers wrote. 'I put up an Insta story up late last night about a heartbreaking situation for a big Everton fan.

'And Jack goes on to donate to his fund. What a top guy (blue heart, hands raised emojis).'

Fans flooded the comments of Powers' missive with their own praise for the former England star, with many recalling that he has made similar impressive gestures in the past.

'Believe he makes a lot of charity donations like this, gent of the game,' one user commented. 'More players should follow (hands raised emoji).'

'In fairness Grealish has shown over the years that he's class,' another wrote. 'Fair play (applause emoji).'

Sports.title: Chelsea's rivals eyeing unused Estevao - plus the reason Xabi Alonso is snubbing Brazilian, why other clubs believe Blues will win race for £90m Alex Scott and the Como wonderkid on radar: CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL
Sports.content:
Chelsea's rivals eyeing unused Estevao - plus the reason Xabi Alonso is snubbing Brazilian, why other clubs believe Blues will win race for £90m Alex Scott and the Como wonderkid on radar: CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL

Multiple Premier League and European rivals of Chelsea are watching the club's handling of Estevao Willian with intrigue after the Brazilian wonderkid again went unused under Xabi Alonso.

Despite Cole Palmer’s suspension and Joao Pedro’s injury, Estevao was overlooked during Wednesday’s Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool. The 19-year-old stayed sat on the bench at Anfield while four others were introduced during the 1-1 draw preceding the penalty shootout.

In Chelsea’s eight Premier League fixtures, he has been brought on as a late substitute six times and unused twice.

Estevao is tied down to a contract lasting into the 2030s with Chelsea, who consider him among their ‘untouchables’ and have looked at trying to arrange a new deal. But external sources have confided that his situation is piquing interest within Premier League and European circles.

It is understood Estevao's limited role under Alonso is not the result of a fall-out, and purely down to tactical and technical decisions. Chelsea’s manager has hinted that the physicality of the Premier League is a contributing factor while promising greater chances as the season progresses.

Alonso does not see Estevao as suited to a wing-back role, which involves a great deal of tracking back, but as a winger who can come inside, as Palmer does in the 3-4-2-1 system.

Estevao was an unused substitute during Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool and his lack of minutes is piquing the interest of rivals clubs in the Premier League and across Europe

In Chelsea’s eight Premier League fixtures, the Brazilian has been brought on as a late substitute six times and unused twice

Chelsea fans hope they will soon see more of Estevao in action – the away end at Anfield were singing his name on Wednesday while he went unused. But Palmer will be back available when Manchester United visit Stamford Bridge in the Premier League this Saturday lunchtime after serving his one-game ban.

Carlo Ancelotti has named him in his Brazil squad for their November friendlies against Japan and Singapore. Estevao has started as many matches for his country in their one international break as he has for Chelsea in all competitions this season.

Ancelotti said during the last break that he would overlook his lack of minutes with Chelsea because he considers it his duty to aid his development. The Sao Paulo native has six goals in 14 Brazil caps.

Como star on radar

Chelsea are continuing to keep tabs on Jacobo Ramon, the 21-year-old defender of Como who is impressing under Cesc Fabregas, though they are joined by others across England and Europe.

Arsenal and Manchester United have also been linked with Ramon. His situation is likewise complicated by Real Madrid retaining a 50 per cent sell-on clause in any deal for the Spain Under 21s centre back, as well as an unspecified buy-back clause.

Ramon played under Alonso way back in 2018-19, when the now-Chelsea manager began his coaching career within Madrid’s youth system.

Chelsea’s interest predates Alonso’s arrival and goes back to last January, when they had Ramon on a shortlist along with Jeremy Jacquet – then of Rennes, now of Liverpool – and Marcos Senesi – then of Bournemouth, now of Tottenham.

Chelsea focused on trying to sign Jacquet, but he chose Liverpool, signing a pre-agreement to join them in the summer for £60million. He came on as a substitute in Wednesday’s Carabao Cup clash, replacing Virgil van Dijk.

Chelsea are continuing to keep tabs on 21-year-old Como defender Jacobo Ramon (left), but face competition from various rivals

Chelsea leading race for £90m Scott

Sources at rival clubs believe Chelsea will end up winning the race to Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, with it possible that an agreement could be reached before the January window.

The word is a fee of around £90m would be expected to be enough, despite Bournemouth saying they want £100m-plus.

In a way, the improving results of Marco Rose’s side are helping expedite Scott's exit, as they insist any winter sale would be blocked if their Premier League position were precarious. Scott is injured and Bournemouth have won five consecutive games in all competitions without him.

While Liverpool have looked at Scott, they are not said to have shown as much interest as Chelsea, and there are some suspicions that Bournemouth would like a bidding war for a 23-year-old midfielder who has indicated his interest in moving on.

Monaco’s Lamine Camara, who Chelsea came close to signing for half the price of Scott at £47m in the summer, also has his fans at Liverpool.

Chelsea's rivals believe the Blues will win the race to sign Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott

A bad omen for Blues?

Five years ago this week…

October 24, 2021: Manchester United lose 5-0 at home to Liverpool.

October 25-26: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer appears on the brink of losing his job.

October 27: Solskjaer surprisingly avoids the sack.

October 30: United head to London and win 3-0 away at Tottenham.

Chelsea are aiming to avoid history repeating itself when Michael Carrick's side visit Stamford Bridge this Saturday after a week in which United were beaten by Bournemouth but the boss avoided the axe.

Chelsea are expecting United captain Bruno Fernandes to return to their starting line-up after his clear-the-air talks with Carrick.

Lavia hits the full 90

Romeo Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes in a competitive match for Chelsea against Liverpool, which can only be good for his confidence levels.

Alonso identified that as an issue in pre-season, when he allowed the 22-year-old midfielder to complete the match in a friendly win over AC Milan. Chelsea’s manager told those of us on the tour that he wanted to give Lavia that moment because he believed he had a ‘mental block’ about it after his injury history.

Romeo Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes in a competitive match for Chelsea against Liverpool on Wednesday night

Post-career protection

This week, a group of Chelsea first-teamers and promising academy players got together in a meeting room at Cobham for a talk from a specialist brought in to discuss career-ending insurance.

While a dry topic, it is an important consideration for footballers in this unpredictable game.

Speaking of injuries, Chelsea have had an unfortunate run of muscle issues of late, with Maxence Lacroix struggling to walk off the pitch at Anfield after picking up a hamstring problem.

Fancy a job at Chelsea?

Chelsea are searching for a physical performance coach to join their first-team support staff. Within the job listing, they say they want someone who can ‘lead on GK specific physical development’.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham's father Mark called up to play for England's OVER-50s in clash with Ireland - after smashing more than 700 goals during journeyman non-league career
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham's father Mark called up to play for England's OVER-50s in clash with Ireland - after smashing more than 700 goals during journeyman non-league career

Jude Bellingham's father Mark has received a call up to England Veterans Over 50s squad to face Republic of Ireland this weekend.

A talented non-league striker in his heyday, Bellingham netted over 700 goals across at least 20 different clubs, including Leamington, Stourbridge and Sutton Coldfield Town.

He even earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career, which ended in 2017.

The father of Real Madrid and England superstar Jude, 23, and Borussia Dortmund and England Under-23 midfielder Jobe, Mark is now set to dust off his shooting boots and become the third member of the Bellingham family to don the Three Lions shirt.

England Veterans Over 50s are the reigning Seniors World Cup champions, having clinched their ninth title in Thailand earlier this year.

Gareth Barry, the former Manchester City and Everton midfielder, lined up for the side alongside Lee Hendrie, also formerly of Aston Villa, although both of those names are absent for the upcoming match in Berkshire on Sunday, November 1.

The father of Real Madrid superstar Jude, 23, and Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe, Mark is now set to dust off his shooting boots (Source: judebellingham/Instagram)

A former West Midlands Police officer, Bellingham earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career. Pictured above with Jude (Source: CJPhillips1982/X)

When not playing football of his own, Bellingham is regularly seen attending his two sons' matches.

A Southend United supporter, Mark introduced Jude to football, with the England star's first live matches coming alongside his father at Roots Hall.

Speaking about his father in a recent interview, Jude said: 'We talk about footballing heroes, and my dad was like my first.

'When you go and watch him play every week in non-league, you know it's not the Premier League or anything, but seeing the way that he played and the atmosphere, it made me fall in love with football so he was probably my first hero.

'After the first few times of going, I'd start to pay a bit more attention to the games and stuff, the atmosphere and he's scoring goals so you see him celebrating and stuff like that - you want that to be me.

'Growing up, he'd always give me tips on what I could do and now it gets to a certain age and it sort of flips and that's brilliant because we have that sort of relationship like father and son and then as I got older, like coach and player.'

Mark helped set up Stourbridge Juniors, Jude’s first club, and was a sergeant before fully focusing on his sons’ careers.

He became their agent and negotiated Jude’s £88.5m transfer to Real Madrid from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, and dealt with Dortmund again when Jobe moved there from Sunderland in 2025.

View this post on Instagram

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup together this past summer

While in Germany, Mark reportedly held an emotional discussion with Dortmund sporting director Sebastian Kehl after being left unhappy by Jobe's substitution at half-time during his Bundesliga debut.

German publication BILD added at the time that Mark sought a meeting with manager Niko Kovac directly - and 'made no secret of his opinion.' The club proceeded to ban all family members from the dressing room following the incident.

Mark’s influence as an agent is said to have stretched to Jude’s media duties when with England. Notably, the player has gone out of his way to speak more at this most recent World Cup, but at previous tournaments he had avoided speaking beyond his obligations despite his increasing influence within the squad.

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico this past summer.

Sports.title: Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card is REJECTED: Gunners star, 16, to serve ban after sending off in Fleetwood defeat - which left Mikel Arteta fuming - as club legend sends warning
Sports.content:
Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card is REJECTED: Gunners star, 16, to serve ban after sending off in Fleetwood defeat - which left Mikel Arteta fuming - as club legend sends warning

The FA have upheld Max Dowman’s three-match ban after the teenager was sent off in Arsenal’s shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

Arsenal appealed the red card after Dowman was sent off in the 86th minute of Tuesday’s defeat for kicking out in retaliation to a scissor challenge by Harrison Neal, who was shown a yellow card.

But the 16-year-old will now miss Arsenal’s Premier League matches against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle after the FA stuck with the on-field decision one day after the Premier League champions lodged their appeal.

As the teenager left the field, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta gave him a scathing look and uttered a few words to the young attacker, understood to be: ‘Get to the changing room, Max’.

Dowman has turned out four times this season and his suspension comes as a blow after injuries to Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke.

His dismissal split opinion with Arsenal legend Paul Merson among those who jumped to his defence on the Sky Sports broadcast on Tuesday evening.

Arsenal have failed in their appeal to have Max Dowman's three-match ban overturned

Dowman was dismissed for his reaction to a strong challenge from Fleetwood's Harrison Neal

Fellow Arsenal legend Ray Parlour however, has urged Dowman to learn from his mistakes following his midweek dismissal.

It was Dowman's second red card this month, having also been sent off while representing England's Under 19s.

And Parlour - part of the Invincibles side which went unbeaten in winning the Premier League in 2004 - said: ‘Well, I thought he (Dowman) was a little bit unlucky, if I'm being honest. He was tangled with the legs, but he's a young man, he's going to make mistakes.

‘He's got to learn from it, that's all. I'm sure Mikel pulled him to the side. He's 16 years old remember, he's still a kid. He's trying to set all sorts of records at the moment, and then he's got sent off as a 16-year-old.’

On whether he thought Neal’s tackle was dangerous, he said: ‘Well it's a challenge that happened all the time in my era, but obviously the rules have changed.

‘He’s gone for the ball but it’s a bit reckless. I thought Max was a little bit unlucky in what the scenario was, legs all tangled up in this way, but he reacted a little bit.

‘Usually, a referee just says, “OK, maybe a yellow card maximum” and that's it, done.’

Arsenal legend Ray Parlour believes the Gunners youngster was 'a little unlucky' to be sent off

Speaking at the premiere of the film ‘We Go Again’, the former midfielder also tipped Arteta to build a dynasty at Arsenal in a similar vein to Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden tenure at Manchester City.

‘Absolutely, he's got a great opportunity now to really, really dominate like Man City have done under Pep (Guardiola),’ he said.

‘He's got a great young squad of players. Everybody's going in the right direction, everybody knows they have to set their standards and he’s a very demanding manager which you've got to be with an elite team.

‘He’s done a brilliant job and people have given him time. Obviously, everybody's backed him including the owners.

‘We see with other managers, they come and go at clubs. Once you've got a good manager, you've got to try and stick with him. It’s great news that Mikel has signed a new contract, and obviously, players now will be signing new contracts as well. Hopefully they can stick together.’



Parlour was speaking at the launch of Oakley Meta’s new film ‘We Go Again’ to highlight their partnership with Arsenal.

Sports.title: Patrick Stewart snubbed Cristiano Ronaldo to fulfil wife's Lionel Messi wish
Sports.content:
Patrick Stewart snubbed Cristiano Ronaldo to fulfil wife's Lionel Messi wish

After Patrick Stewart passed away at the age of 86, many may remember his anecdote when he met Lionel Messi at a glitzy award's ceremony

View 2 Images Patrick Stewart has died aged 86 (Image: Getty Images)

Patrick Stewart looked straight past Cristiano Ronaldo so he and his wife could grab a picture with Lionel Messi. The legendary Star Trek and X-Men actor has sadly passed away at the age of 86 years old after a short battle with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.

‌



‌



Tributes have been made to the star, who died at his Los Angeles home. There are many tales about the iconic British actor, but one that stands out is his brief meeting with Messi.

‌



In 2017, at the Best FIFA Football Awards Show in London, Stewart was invited to present the FIFA Fair Play award on stage, while accompanied by ex-Chelsea defender Marcel Desailly and actor Idris Elba. After the show, Stewart was determined to meet Messi so his wife Sunny Ozell could have a picture with him.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

Not only did Stewart have to drag his other half through endless waves of security to get to the football great, he even walked past Cristiano Ronaldo. Looking back at the amusing story while appearing on stage, four days after the show, he said: "It was really, really hard because there was security like you've never seen.

"It might've been the Royal Family because there was Messi, and Cristiano Ronaldo and Maradona, and you couldn't get to them. I was sitting at the front row but right at the end, all these guys were on the other end.

‌



"I decided when the show was over, I'm going to make a run for it. They were saying 'Thank you everybody, what a great night, thank you.' I turned to my wife and I said 'You follow me and stay close'.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"I shot along the front row and the edge of the stage going 'Excuse me, excuse me' and going 'I'm Patrick Stewart, I'm Patrick Stewart' thinking it might help. I arrived and they were like 'Oh yeah, okay' and I saw Cristiano Ronaldo look up and go 'Oh it's this guy' and I couldn't see Leo, he wasn't there.

"He had actually turned around and bent down over his seat, and he's quite short, and so he just vanished behind everybody. I stood behind him and then he stood up and turned around and we were face to face. This is emotional to me. He just breathed into my face and I said 'Senor Messi. Por favor. Mi esposa'."

‌



Messi kindly obliged and posed for a picture with Stewart's other half. While this exchange was happening, Messi's partner Antonela Roccuzzo realised who her iconic husband was talking to.

View 2 Images Stewart presented the FIFA Fair Play Award before the meeting (Image: Photo by Alexander Hassenstein - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Stewart added: "They shook hands and then I said 'Can I please take a photograph of the two of you together?' I took the photo, not a selfie, I took a photo of Lionel Messi and my wife side by side and then his wife said 'And I want a photograph with you!'"

Stewart and Roccuzzo then joined Ozell and Messi for, what quickly became, one of the most iconic photos of the evening. Amusingly, in one of their photos, Ronaldo was clearly seen behind them on stage receiving his reward.

Article continues below

The photograph from the exchange is one which will certainly be reminisced upon as the world comes to terms with Stewart's passing.

Manchester United are reportedly exploring the possibility of signing a new centre-forward in January following Benjamin Sesko's injury

View Image Dominic Calvert-Lewin is on Man Utd's radar

Manchester United are reportedly considering the acquisition of a new centre-forward in January following Benjamin Sesko's injury, with Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin identified as a possible option. Sesko hasn't appeared for United since their Carabao Cup fixture against Brighton on September 16, after experiencing discomfort in his shin following the match.

Man Utd target Premier League star for January transfer after suffering huge injury blow

Manchester United are set to be without Benjamin Sesko until at least January due to injury, leaving the Red Devils short up front, and a striker is on their shortlist

View 2 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin recently scored against Manchester United (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

Manchester United are weighing up a surprise move for Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the January transfer window. Calvert-Lewin, 29, is enjoying his second season at Leeds and scored one of his five goals this season against the Red Devils in this month's 1-1 draw at Elland Road.

‌



‌



The England international bagged 15 in his first campaign after leaving Everton on a free transfer and has proven his fitness with Daniel Farke's side. Leeds are already keen to offer him a new contract, with his current deal due to expire in 2028, but United are now circling.

‌



According to The Athletic, Calvert-Lewin is under consideration at Old Trafford as they target a striker. It follows this week's news that Benjamin Sesko, who led the line for the Red Devils last term, will be out until at least January because of a shin injury.

Sesko is one of only four United players to have scored a Premier League goal this season, despite his minimal game time. "Unfortunately, Ben looks like he's going to be out for a period of time," Carrick confirmed on Thursday.

Sports.title: Arsenal learn Max Dowman red card appeal verdict after controversial Fleetwood red card
Sports.content:
Arsenal learn Max Dowman red card appeal verdict after controversial Fleetwood red card

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman was sent off after kicking out at Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal during the Gunners' defeat in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Tuesday

View 2 Images Max Dowman was given a straight red card against Fleetwood (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Arsenal's appeal to overturn Max Dowman's red card against Fleetwood has been rejected, the FA have confirmed. Dowman, 16, will now serve a three-game suspension for violent conduct.

‌



‌



The winger reacted to a strong tackle from Harrison Neal by kicking out at the Fleetwood midfielder, and he was shown a straight red card by referee Michael Salisbury in the closing stages of Tuesday's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie. Fleetwood went on to win the game on penalties, booking their place in the quarter-finals for the first time in League Two club's history.

‌



Arsenal launched their appeal on Wednesday but their case has been dismissed. A statement from the FA read: "An independent Regulatory Commission has dismissed claims of both wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment for Max Dowman.

‌



"The Arsenal player was sent off during their EFL Cup game against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday 27 October and will be suspended for three matches. The Regulatory Commission's written reasons for its decisions will be published in due course."

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Dowman will miss the Gunners' upcoming Premier League matches against Liverpool, Hull and Newcastle. The ban means that he won't be available for a top-flight fixture until November 29 when Arsenal host Manchester City.

Mikel Arteta gave Dowman a talking-to as the 16-year-old walked off the pitch at Fleetwood before seeing a replay of the incident. Asked about what he said to Dowman, Arteta told BBC Radio 5 Live that it was 'something that we discussed already before the match.'

‌



The Arsenal manager went on to say: "It's difficult to see on the cameras like that. So I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation."

Dowman's absence leaves Arsenal short of wide players going into Sunday's game away to Liverpool. Noni Madueke, Bukayo Saka and Christos Tzolis are already sidelined.

‌



Should Max Dowman's red card have been overturned? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Arsenal will be without Max Dowman for three games (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Also missing against Fleetwood were Riccardo Calafiori and Declan Rice. "Calafiori was out, Noni was out with an ankle, and Declan was feeling a problem the other day (against Everton), which is why I had to substitute him," Arteta explained post-match.

The Gunners boss added regarding the defeat: "When we create the volume of shots and chances we did, you have to score three, four or five. You capitalise on it. If you don't, there are no margins, and that's the reality. Then you have to wait and get through the round on penalties, and we didn't do that.

Article continues below

"The probability was low with the way the game was panning out, but it's football and still with low probability, there is always a chance you could be out of the cup."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms Bruno Fernandes captaincy decision after Man Utd crunch talks
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms Bruno Fernandes captaincy decision after Man Utd crunch talks

Bruno Fernandes was dropped to the bench for Manchester United's clash with Bournemouth last Sunday after criticising Michael Carrick's tactics, plunging his future as captain into jeopardy

View 2 Images Michael Carrick held talks with Bruno Fernandes at Carrington on Tuesday (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has confirmed that Bruno Fernandes is 'fully committed' and will remain captain of Manchester United. The decision follows clear-the-air talks between the pair at United's training ground, Carrington, on Tuesday.

‌



‌



Fernandes' future as captain became uncertain after he publicly questioned Carrick's tactics in the Red Devils' 4-1 defeat away to Como last week. Carrick subsequently dropped Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth in what he described as a 'football decision'.

‌



Speaking ahead of United's trip to Chelsea on Saturday, Carrick was asked whether the 32-year-old Portuguese would continue to wear the armband, which was passed to Harry Maguire against Bournemouth. "There's no decision to be made on that," the United manager replied.

‌



"He's the captain of our football club. There are different personalities, different characteristics, different ways to lead. It all comes down to what happens on the football pitch and whether you win or not in the end.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"He cares deeply about this football club and the team and he's desperate to do well. We'll lead that together."

Carrick added: "It was a decision for the game. That's it. Bruno is fully committed to this football club. I've got no issues with that, we move forward."

‌



Fernandes' role wasn't the biggest talking point during Carrick's press conference on Thursday. His own future has been in jeopardy, with United having won just one of their opening eight Premier League games.

Defeat at Chelsea coupled with two other results going against the Red Devils could see them drop into the relegation zone. Despite the intense speculation, Carrick insists that he doesn't need assurances from the club's board over his position.

‌



"I don't need assurances from anyone," the former United midfielder said. "I totally get the position, I get the job, the responsibility, I get what comes with that. I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard."

Should Bruno Fernandes have been stripped of the captaincy? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes will continue to be Manchester United's captain (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Carrick went on to say: "I don't see [the criticism]. I only see the things I need to see. I don't look for it. It doesn't help. I've said it before, I care about what the supporters think.

‌



"I care about how it feels in the stadium and them travelling to games - I care about what we give them and what they see. I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else. I know this job and I know what we need to be better. I don't need anyone else to tell me."

On whether he was surprised to still be in a job, Carrick responded: "No. I'm here to do my job. I'm here to do the best for the team. I'm desperate to make things better and improve things. I'm not surprised, no."

Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star's girlfriend in lucky escape on train behind fatal Spain crash with 69 dead
Sports.content:
Ex-Chelsea star's girlfriend in lucky escape on train behind fatal Spain crash with 69 dead

The partner of a former Chelsea star has revealed her shock after narrowly escaping a fatal train crash in Spain that killed at least 69 people

View 3 Images Marc Cucurella's partner has had a lucky escape

The partner of former Chelsea footballer Marc Cucurella has revealed her shock after travelling on the train directly behind one involved in a fatal collision in Toledo, Spain, which killed at least 69 people.

‌



‌



Claudia Rodriguez, who has three children with the Real Madrid defender, was travelling to Malaga when two trains collided around 40 miles south of Madrid on Wednesday. She later took to social media to express her distress and offer her condolences to the victims' families.

‌



"I was on my way to Malaga on the train behind it; I'm in shock. My heart goes out to the victims' families and friends," she wrote, alongside a post sharing helplines set up to support passengers and their loved ones.

‌



The crash, one of the deadliest railway disasters of the 21st century, occurred on the high-speed line between Madrid and Seville. An AVE train collided with a stationary Iryo service, with both trains travelling from Madrid's Atocha station towards Santa Justa in Seville.

Eyewitnesses describe horrors of Spanish train crash that where at least 68 dead READ MORE :

Spanish Cup matches postponed after tragic train crash leaves at least 64 dead READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Almost 550 people were on board the two trains when the collision happened at 8.54am local time. At the time of writing, at least 69 people had been confirmed dead, while more than 100 others were injured. A total of 50 people remain in hospital hospital, including 15 in a serious condition.

‌



Following the collision, two carriages plunged down an embankment, while a section of rail pierced one of the carriages and could be seen protruding from the wreckage.

Early reports suggested the automated signalling system had failed, leaving the train operating under human control. Government sources indicated that human error involving an operator at the railway infrastructure manager Administrador de Infraestructuras Ferroviarias (ADIF) was a possible cause of the disaster.

‌



View 3 Images At least 69 people were killed in the crash (Image: UME HANDOUT/EPA/Shutterstock)

Several hours after the collision, Rodriguez reassured her followers that she was safe and explained that her train had not been damaged. It had been travelling a considerable distance behind the train involved in the crash, meaning she escaped the worst of the tragedy.

‌



"Guys, I'm fine. My train wasn't affected at all, as there was a long way between my train and the train that was involved in the accident," she posted.

She added that the experience had left her shaken by how easily the circumstances could have been different.

‌



"It really unsettled me to think that if it had happened later, it would have happened to my train, but, please, it's nothing compared to what the people who were actually on it must have gone through," she said.

View 3 Images Claudia was a regular at Stamford Bridge during Cucurella's four-year spell at Chelsea (Image: Claudia Rodríguez / Instagram)

‌



Cucurella also shared a message of support for those affected by the disaster, offering his condolences to the victims and their loved ones.

"A huge hug to everyone affected by the accident in Toledo and to their families. Stay strong, and all my love at this difficult time," wrote the Spain World Cup winner.

‌



As a mark of respect, all 24 Copa del Rey first-round matches scheduled for October 28 were postponed. Spanish football clubs, including Real Madrid and Barcelona, also expressed their condolences to the victims and their families.

Cucurella and Rodriguez have been together since 2018, although they are not married. They have three children together.

Article continues below

The defender enjoyed a successful five-year spell in the Premier League, spending the bulk of that time at Chelsea before joining Real Madrid in a £50million deal in June. He went on to feature in Spain's World Cup-winning side a few weeks later.

Sports.title: Gary Neville launches fresh Glazers rant as he demands Man Utd sale - 'Enough is enough'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville launches fresh Glazers rant as he demands Man Utd sale - 'Enough is enough'

Gary Neville has opened fire on the Glazers are demanded they sell up at Manchester United with the American owners presiding over consistent failure at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Gary Neville has continued to call out the Glazers in recent years (Image: Sky Sports Premier League/YouTube)

Gary Neville has again called for the Glazers to sell up at Manchester United as he doubled down on the astronomical debt they've amassed and their refusal to take responsibility for their shortcomings.

‌



‌



For two decades the Glazer family has sat at the top of the club and the flaws in their ownership were masked for a period by the success enjoyed under Sir Alex Ferguson, but since his retirement the Red Devils have endured a steep decline.

‌



A lack of achievement on the pitch has shone a light on the issues in the boardroom and Neville, a former captain of the club, has continued to speak out against the American owners, who are rarely if ever seen at the club.

‌



For long periods they delegated to other figures, who became hugely unpopular among fans, and in recent years sold a stake to INEOS, who are now copping it from the supporters. But Neville maintains that the overall issue remains with the Glazers.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



He said on Stick to Football: "There's £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion) of debt in that football club, they're hamstrung in some ways. They've spent an absolute fortune on players, just under Man City in the last 15 years. £1.4bn ($1.86bn) on players, they're second in the spending, but a lot of it's the never-never.

"They have to sell now, they have to sell, I'm sorry the time has come. They have subcontracted the football department out to INEOS, they are trying to run the football department, they have had three years of struggling and it looks like this year is going to be a struggle.

‌



"The Glazer family over in America, in Tampa, they're very popular over there, they go to every game, apparently, I hear, they go to all the NFL games, they've hardly been to Old Trafford in 20-odd years."

View 2 Images The Glazers have copped huge criticism since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement (Image: Getty)

‌



Neville went on to lament their failure to invest in Old Trafford, which has fallen way behind the elite stadiums in the world today. Plans are being made for a new venue, but the former player questioned where the apparent £2bn to fund it is going to come from.

He concluded: "You've got a failure of 13, 14 years on the football side, you've subbed it out to somebody else, which is ridiculous, and not took responsibility. It is now at a point where they have to sell. Enough is enough, they have to sell the whole the club. The fans have had enough. They have to go now."

‌



Neville has previously confessed to a sense of regret at not speaking out against the Glazers when he was a player at the club, but has said: "I worked on the theory at the time that we could have worse owners. They were quite passive.

"But when Sir Alex Ferguson left, it's then I started to realise they were only successful because of Sir Alex Ferguson. They haven't been able to develop a successful sporting project without him."

Sports.title: Carlos Tevez 'wanted to kill' Gary Neville after acrimonious Man Utd exit
Sports.content:
Carlos Tevez 'wanted to kill' Gary Neville after acrimonious Man Utd exit

Carlos Tevez admits Gary Neville's comments surrounding his Manchester United exit rattled him and he was determined to go after his ex-teammate when they came up against each other

View 2 Images Carlos Tevez was determined to go after Gary Neville once they were on opposing sides

Carlos Tevez has confessed he wanted to go after Gary Neville once he was at Manchester City following comments made by his former captain.

‌



‌



Tevez made a seismic move in 2009 when he decided to go from Manchester United to their local rivals, who had just been backed by their Abu Dhabi millions and were looking to challenge the established order.

‌



City's capture of Tevez was huge given the quality he had and the success he'd enjoyed at Old Trafford, where he won several Premier League titles and the Champions League.

‌



A row over a new contract saw Tevez head for pastures new, and he didn't go far, with Neville accusing Tevez of disrespecting Sir Alex Ferguson. But the Argentine maintained that Neville commented without fully understanding the situation - which left a sour taste.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Ferdinand stated on his YouTube channel: “When I played against you, you wanted to kill Gary Neville.” Tevez smirked and said: “Gary, he said that I didn’t respect Ferguson. He didn’t understand me. He didn’t understand the situation.”

Neville's frustration remains and he accused Tevez of downing tools on Sky Sports several years ago, which led to a live feud between him and Kia Joorabchian, who was Tevez's agent at the time and wanted to defend his player.

‌



The legendary United right-back has also said on his switch: "I couldn't understand how he would want to engineer a move to your closest rivals. City were building a project at the time but they weren't anywhere near where we were. I couldn't understand it, the lack of loyalty. You come to United you embed yourself in the team and you wed yourself to the club. You can't go and play for them, if we still want you, you can't play for them."

View 2 Images The Argentine signed for Man City when they were building towards a title charge (Image: PA Archive/Press Association Images)

‌



Tevez's anger stemmed from an apparent promise from the Ferguson, who maintained United would sign him once his two-year loan ended, but that never came to pass.

The former striker, who scored 84 times in the Premier League for three different clubs, said: “I think that Ferguson had, from the day we talked, up to six months to keep his word. And he didn’t. On the contrary, he started leaving me on the bench."

Article continues below

Tevez would score three times in a two-legged cup semi-final against United in his debut year for City, but ended up on the losing side. Despite a public fallout with Roberto Mancini and months away from the club, he would return and contribute to their Premier League success of 2012.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.
