Sports.title: Fans “pay a bit less attention” to Formula 1 as calendar gets longer – Sainz | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr suspects the growing size of the Formula 1 calendar may not be helping to make the sport more popular.

F1 has increased the number of rounds to 24, though only 23 are scheduled to happen this year due to the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. The number could fall further if either of the final two rounds are cancelled.

If the final rounds go ahead as planned, F1 will hold nine events in just eleven weeks. Sainz says he would have enjoyed more regular races when he was younger but suspects it may have become a turn-off for some fans.

“I think if I were a fan, I would love it because the more F1 I can watch on TV, the better,” he said. “I remember when I was a kid and there were only 16 races in the calendar, or 18. I used to miss Formula 1 [because it was not on] for a lot of weekends.

“But we also need to consider as a sport if that’s something that maybe is also counterproductive. Sometimes you need to miss the sport to get people engaged. When you get so many races in a row, people or the sport can maybe feel a bit like a league, like the Premier League rather than the Champions League. So maybe you pay a bit less attention to the matches or to the races in this case.

“So, it’s more a philosophy for the sport to consider whether you want to keep having so many races in a row.”

However Sainz, a director of the Grand Prix Drivers’ Association, is also concerned about the effect F1’s long calendar has on the teams’ staff.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“More important than that, I think as the GPDA, we’ve been told more or less that 24 races, 25 races is the limit of the championship that they’re willing to go for. I don’t know if that will be the case, the more offers there are to keep increasing venues. But I think that is the limit.

“I think it’s more about the members of the team that are going to spend only three or four days at home, or five days at home every month. And it’s the people in the teams that get the tougher end rather than the drivers. I think we are in a more privileged position in that sense.

“So, let’s see. I have the motivation to do however many races we need to do. I have the will to race. I love racing. But it is true that this end of the triple header, with three triple headers in a row, is going to be tough for the body, tough for the people, tough for the mind.”

Sports.title: F1 newcomers Tsolov, Mini and Slater among nine drivers to run in practice on Friday | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Nine teams will give practice outings to inexperienced drivers at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

Three of them – Red Bull junior driver Nikola Tsolov, Alpine’s Gabriele Mini and Audi’s Freddie Slater – will make their debuts in an official F1 test session. Tsolov will drive for Red Bull’s second F1 team, Racing Bulls.

Teams must give four opportunities to inexperienced drivers – two in each of their cars – in first practice sessions over the course of the year.

Among the others driving this weekend is Luke Browning. Williams has entered him for a fifth session this year after he completed no laps when he appeared for them at the Circuit de Catalunya. Colton Herta will also appear in a session for the fifth time this year at Cadillac.

Also in action this weekend are Leonardo Fornaroli and Jak Crawford, making their fourth appearances for McLaren and Aston Martin respectively. McLaren recently confirmed Fornaroli, the 2025 Formula 2 champion, will drive for its new WEC Hypercar team.

Ayumu Iwasa will also make his fourth appearance this year, and third for Red Bull. He has also previously driven for Racing Bulls. Ryo Hirakawa will appear for the third time in a Haas this season.

More than half the teams will have completed their obligation to run drivers on four occasions after next week’s Brazilian Grand Prix. Unlike in previous years, none of the remaining rounds are sprint events, meaning they theoretically have more opportunities to run their junior drivers. But with doubt continuing to hang over whether the final races in the Middle East will go ahead, teams appear to be ensuring they do not fail to fulfil their practice quotas should they be cancelled.

Sports.title: New contract to keep Perez racing for Cadillac until at least 2029 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac has announced a new contract with Sergio Perez, days before he starts his 300th grand prix at home in Mexico.

Perez will remain at the team until at least 2029 under his new, long-term deal.

He joined the F1 newcomers last year ahead of their debut this season.

“Building a competitive team in F1 is a long-term journey, and securing Checo’s talent and leadership gives us the continuity and commitment we need to build on the strong foundation established in our first year,” said CEO Dan Towriss. “Together, we are focused on the next phase of our journey, pushing the team forward and making progress up the grid.”

Cadillac is yet to confirm the identity of Perez’s team mate for next year. The team are yet to score a point, Perez having achieved a best finish of 14th, current team mate Valtteri Bottas 13th.

“Building a Formula 1 team from the ground up takes time, relentless work and patience, but the progress we are making together is incredibly rewarding,” said Perez. “There is still a lot of work ahead of us and I am fully committed for the next three years.”

Perez has experienced disappointment with multi-year contracts before. In 2019 he agreed a three-year deal to stay at Lawrence Stroll’s Racing Point team, before it became Aston Martin. However Stroll dropped Perez at the end of the following season and replaced him with Sebastian Vettel.

During his fourth year at Red Bull the team extended his contract by two years, then dropped him at the end of the season. He sat out the 2025 campaign before returning to F1 with Cadillac.

Sports.title: Richard Schaefer Oversells Canelo Alvarez’s Christian Mbilli Choice
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez looks to have picked the softer option in Christian Mbilli, though nobody expects an easy night at the office. Mbilli gives Canelo clear lanes to time counters, letting him steal rounds on the scorecards even if he gets outworked. Osleys Iglesias, on the other hand, represents a far more unforgiving matchup.

Promoter Richard Schaefer repeatedly praised Canelo at Thursday’s final press conference for picking Mbilli to give fans the best fight possible. That narrative ignored how slim the pool really was. With WBA titlist Jaime Munguia practically off the table due to gym loyalty, plus a vacant WBO belt, Canelo really only had Mbilli or IBF champion Iglesias to consider.

“Because I do not believe in shortcuts. I have been a champion for many years. I just want to fight the best,” Canelo said when asked about the decision.

Even if Mbilli throws a hundred punches a round, Canelo knows how judges score fights. A crisp, explosive counter shot that snaps an opponent’s head back often wins rounds over flurry work that lands to the body, head, or gloves. Against Mbilli, Canelo has a clear path to win rounds on the cards.

Iglesias is an entirely different problem, and arguably a far more punishing one. The Cuban is a rangy, hard-hitting southpaw who controls real estate with a stiff jab and detonates with a lead right hook. Canelo struggling against disciplined boxers with length and movement is well established.

Following Iglesias around the ring while absorbing straight lefts, right hooks, and jabs would be grueling, with very few clean openings to fire back. Iglesias brings real knockout danger without needing to smother himself on the inside to get it. Iglesias brings the bigger punch, but he also possesses the technical skill to dominate without hunting for a knockout.

Canelo risks trailing, missing, and soaking up damage without landing enough in return to keep pace. Reaching the final bell would still leave him battered. That is a projection, yet the Cuban’s length, precision, and power make it a very real danger.

Mbilli brings heat of his own. His swarm could pin Canelo against the ropes for long stretches. The difference is that Mbilli’s relentless forward motion keeps him squarely in range for Canelo’s signature counter rights and body hooks.

That gives Canelo a realistic path to victory. Mbilli can throw and land three as many punches, but judges often reward Canelo’s cleaner, harder single shots. Activity does not guarantee points, and Mbilli will offer plenty of targets for flashier work.

Canelo would get far fewer looks against Iglesias. He would need to evade the jab, close the gap, and connect before Iglesias moves away or fires back with something harder.

“I just need to be myself, and that is how I am going to win this fight,” Mbilli stated.

He could be right. Mbilli’s furious engine could easily overwhelm the veteran if Canelo cannot punch with enough authority to slow him down. Calling him the better option is far from guaranteeing a Canelo win.

Canelo never admitted to dodging Iglesias over stylistic concerns, and this remains a personal breakdown of the matchup. Still, Schaefer’s spin invites a reality check. Between the two champions on the table, Canelo selected the opponent who gives him room to land and a much clearer route to a victory on the cards.

It still could be controversial if Canelo wins a decision against Mbilli, but at least he would see the final bell, and his face wouldn’t be as beat up as it would be against Iglesias.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley’s Canelo Massacre Pick Ignores Reality
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley expects Canelo Alvarez to completely destroy Christian Mbilli, but that forecast fits the fighter Canelo used to be, not the one we see in the ring today. While his counterpunching remains lethal, blowing out an energetic pressure fighter requires relentless, high-gear output that recent outings just do not support.

Bradley argues that veteran savvy and sharp timing will punish Mbilli’s defensive flaws. That prediction hinges on Canelo avoiding the ropes and dictating action in the center of the ring.

“Canelo by massacre. Canelo by massacre. That’s what I got. He might even stop him,” Bradley said on Into the Storm. “Canelo is not gonna throw more punches than Mbilli, but his punches gonna be way more accurate, way more sound, way more placed than Mbilli.”

Bradley points to a glaring habit in Mbilli’s approach. When Mbilli bites on feints, he tends to dip his head and stare at the canvas, opening himself up to clean hooks and uppercuts. The expectation is that Canelo will time those flaws, threading counters through the incoming storm to force a late stoppage.

Still, even peak Canelo rarely battered elite competition into submission the way Bradley imagines. Older versions of Shane Mosley and Miguel Cotto went the full twelve. Gennadiy Golovkin lasted thirty-six rounds with him across three meetings, including the trilogy finale when Golovkin was forty. Different styles produce different results, but boxing history shows that defensive openings do not immediately guarantee a blowout.

Bradley fought in that very same era, so his viewpoint might lean on respect for his peer group. That does not discount his technical breakdown, but it does raise questions about whether his prediction relies on an outdated version of the Mexican star.

Seeing an opening is completely different from exploiting it through twelve fast-paced rounds. Canelo might spot the exact counter he wants, yet lack the stamina to deliver it over and over. A single crisp shot might turn heads, but it will not magically halt the next wave of pressure if Canelo cannot command real estate.

“As long as Canelo keep his back up off the ropes and keep the fight in the center of the ring,” Bradley added, suggesting Canelo should handle the assignment smoothly.

The eye test over the past few years undercuts any idea that Canelo is going to command the center of the ring against a relentless motor like Mbilli. Ever since the Jermell Charlo fight, Canelo’s legs have steadily abandoned him. What used to be deliberate ring generalship has turned into an older fighter looking for a place to lean.

Once the clock hits round six, his default setting is backing straight into the ropes, shelling up behind the high guard, and letting the ropes do the work of keeping him upright.

Against Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga, William Scull, and Terence Crawford, that exact pattern played out. Canelo cannot sustain footwork to dictate geography anymore, and he certainly lacks the conditioning to maintain the work rate required to keep an aggressive dog off his chest. His stamina dictates that he fights in brief, explosive bursts, spending the remaining two minutes of every round resting and waiting to time a single big counter.

That strategy works when hand-picking opponents who either freeze under the lights or lack the punch volume and inside craft to make him pay for taking rounds off. Munguia had the volume but zero defensive awareness or punching power; Berlanga was hesitant and limited; Scull had nowhere near the offensive pop or pedigree to capitalize. They were tailor-made style matchups designed to let Canelo coast on reputation and single heavy shots.

Mbilli is the complete opposite of a hand-picked rest stop. He does not care about getting countered; he never stops throwing, and he thrives precisely where Canelo now camps out: on the inside, chest-to-chest, hammering away at the ribs and arms.

If Canelo’s only plan is to retreat to the ropes and look for single uppercuts while Mbilli fires non-stop for twelve rounds, relying on the judges to favor low-volume potshots is going to be a very dangerous game.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Reveals Shakur Stevenson Vanished After Ring Stunt
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson gathered all the buzz for a potential O’Shaquie Foster bout without stepping into the ring. By stepping through the ropes following Foster’s win over Raymond Ford in May, Stevenson ignited major public anticipation. Yet Foster reveals his team pushed for the bout, waited, and met total silence.

That recent past demands a sharper look at Stevenson’s latest words. Foster just took down Emanuel Navarrete, and Stevenson quickly voiced fresh interest. Boxing enthusiasts ought to pause before celebrating, keeping Foster’s prior experience in mind.

“We kept asking. We didn’t hear nothing. We didn’t hear nothing,” Foster said on the Ariel Helwani show. “We held out for a little bit. We didn’t hear nothing. Tyrone didn’t hear nothing.”

Foster explained that talks never progressed to discussing weight classes. He expressed total readiness to step up to lightweight or junior welterweight, clearing away a major hurdle for a 130-pound titleholder looking upward.

“We didn’t even get that far, but I didn’t care,” Foster noted. “Like, I honestly didn’t care whether it was 135, 140. Either one. It didn’t matter to me.”

It looked like pure clout chasing from Shakur, plain and simple. Walking into another man’s spotlight right after a hard-earned victory creates the illusion that you want the fight next. Fans get excited, the broadcast cameras lock onto you, and you get all the free publicity without taking an ounce of risk. Then, the second Foster’s camp actually reached out to make the fight happen, Shakur vanished into thin air. Total silence.

Once Foster beat Navarrete, Stevenson offered public compliments along with a fresh challenge.

“Hell of a fighter. He will never give me my credit, but I’ll be real tonight. He showed his level,” Stevenson stated in a social post read on air. “That’s a challenge that would get me out of bed. Let’s do it whenever he’s ready. I’ll be here after his undisputed run.”

That is what makes Stevenson’s latest comment after Foster beat Navarrete look so empty. Saying he will fight Foster “whenever he’s ready” completely flips the reality of what happened. Foster was ready months ago, even offering to jump up in weight to make it effortless for Stevenson. Shakur was the one who went missing.

For now, Foster’s sights remain locked on unifying all four belts at 130 pounds. Chasing undisputed status puts Foster in control rather than hanging on Shakur’s schedule. Foster can hunt the remaining belt while Stevenson figures out whether his online comments translate into real business.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Gives PBC More Years Without Becoming A Star
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is locking in more of his prime with PBC, even though his run with the outfit has not turned him into a household name. He has collected belts in three divisions. Casual fans still have little reason to tune in, and facing Michal Cieslak on December 5 will not change that.

Benavidez turns thirty next year. He burned through his twenties chasing Canelo Alvarez. Then he cleared out of light heavyweight without ever facing Dmitry Bivol or Artur Beterbiev. Now he sits at cruiserweight, stacking belts while marquee opponents remain out of reach.

“I’ve always wanted to stay with PBC. I feel like what we’ve built, obviously PBC is PBC before I got there, but the work I’ve put in for this promotional company, I’m not going to get that anywhere else,” Benavidez told FightHubTV. “I feel comfortable with Luis De Cubas. I feel comfortable with Al Haymon. This is my family. I’m one of the pillars that helps PBC stand.”

He sounds like someone trapped by sunk costs. Pouring years into a promotional stable is no reason to surrender the rest of his career. If mainstream fame is the actual target, he needs to look honestly at what loyalty has given him.

He has put on solid bouts. Caleb Plant provided genuine heat. Demetrius Andrade came undefeated. David Morrell was a dangerous test. Gilberto Ramirez offered the chance to pick up cruiserweight hardware. The resume is legitimate.

The box office numbers tell a different story. Reports put the Morrell clash at 150,000 to 160,000 pay-per-view buys. The Andrade fight reportedly landed around 60,000 buys. Those figures are not official numbers, but they prove he has not developed into an elite pay-per-view draw.

Canelo was the matchup that could have launched him into superstardom. It never happened, even with both fighters under the PBC umbrella. Canelo walked his own road, while Benavidez paid the bill in wasted time. Sharing a promotional banner provided zero leverage to force the biggest draw into the ring.

Bivol chose his own path too, giving up the WBC belt rather than facing Benavidez in 2025. Promoters cannot force anyone to sign. Yet Benavidez is the one creeping toward thirty without those career-defining names on his record.

Cieslak brings another strap to the table, but offers zero buzz for American fans. Winning might give Benavidez three cruiserweight titles, yet leave him completely invisible to general sports culture. That is the exact loop he must break.

Launching DB Promotions once his deal with Sampson Lewkowicz wraps up gives him real leverage. Sticking with PBC feels familiar, but familiarity seems to be his main motivation for staying put.

Benavidez has shown he can win titles with this team. He has not shown he can become a crossover sensation with them. Betting the remainder of his peak on this same routine is risky. He needs Jai Opetaia or another opponent people will actually pay to watch. Cieslak is just another belt while the real clock keeps ticking.

Sports.title: Canelo vs. Mbilli: Updated Start Time, Ring Walks and DAZN PPV Price
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez challenges Christian M’Billi for the WBC super middleweight title on Saturday, October 31, at ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The nine-fight card streams live on DAZN PPV and is included with DAZN Ultimate.

What Time Does Canelo vs M’Billi Start?

Opening-card coverage begins at 10 a.m. ET / 7 a.m. PT / 2 p.m. UK. The PPV card starts at 1:47 p.m. ET / 10:47 a.m. PT / 5:47 p.m. UK.

Canelo and M’Billi are expected to make their ring walks at approximately 4:55 p.m. ET / 1:55 p.m. PT / 8:55 p.m. UK. The main event is scheduled for 5 p.m. ET / 2 p.m. PT / 9 p.m. UK and will not start before then.

How to Watch on DAZN

The standalone DAZN PPV costs $79.99 in the United States. Eligible DAZN Ultimate subscribers can watch without a separate PPV purchase. The event is not available in Mexico or China.

Canelo vs M’Billi Fight Card and Times

The listed bout times are estimates and can move depending on the length of earlier fights.

Opening card

10:44 a.m. ET / 2:44 p.m. UK: Carlos Emiliano Rojo vs Flavius Biea

Canelo returns for his first fight since Terence Crawford beat him in September 2025. M’Billi makes his first defence of the full WBC title after a split draw with Lester Martinez.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Documentary Launches on Netflix Ahead of Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
Netflix releases TYSON FURY on November 27, tracing the heavyweight’s rise through boxing and examining his personal struggles before he faces Anthony Joshua on December 11.

Lucy Wilcox directs the feature-length documentary. Fury, his wife Paris and father John give interviews alongside previously unseen footage from his life and career.

Tyson Fury’s Career and Family Life

The film follows Fury from childhood into the heavyweight ranks, revisiting the victories and setbacks that shaped his career. His family contributes its accounts of the experiences behind those performances.

Mental health, addiction and the loss of a child are among the subjects covered. The documentary also examines Fury’s views on masculinity, his family relationships and the support he has relied on throughout his career.

Paris and John bring their perspectives to a film that explores the personal pressures accompanying Fury’s success in the ring.

Fury vs Joshua: December 11 Date and Netflix Broadcast

Fury and Joshua step into opposite corners on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. Netflix will broadcast their first professional meeting globally to all members at no additional cost.

The remaining bouts have yet to be announced.

At their September 30 press conference, Fury spoke about the years spent waiting to get Joshua into the ring.

“I’m looking forward to the challenge. It’s been 10 years in the making,” Fury said.

“The rise has been phenomenal from both fighters. We’ve both had our ups and downs. Finally, we arrive at this moment.”

Fury also praised his British rival: “He’s been a role model and a poster boy for British boxing for years.”

Joshua welcomed the occasion and said their exchanges would drive him through extra rounds in the gym.

“I feel fresh. I feel very excited about this opportunity to work again,” Joshua said.

Sports.title: Jake Paul Ends Retirement Doubts With December 24 Dubai Fight
Sports.content:
MVP chief Nakisa Bidarian addresses questions over Paul’s boxing future following the Anthony Joshua injury, with a Christmas Eve comeback confirmed.

Jake Paul will fight again after the broken jaw he suffered against Anthony Joshua raised doubts about his boxing future. MVP has confirmed a December 24, 2026, comeback in Dubai, and promoter Nakisa Bidarian says Paul’s decision answers those who questioned his desire to return.

The opponent remains unconfirmed.

Bidarian put the injury and its aftermath at the centre of his comments about Paul’s first fight back.

“Twelve months ago he suffered a double broken jaw against a two-time heavyweight world champion and since then many have doubted his desire or need to return to boxing,” the MVP co-founder and CEO said.

“Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport.”

Paul Answers With a Christmas Eve Comeback

Paul heads into his return with a 12-2 record and seven knockouts. His December 2025 meeting with Joshua preceded the year-long absence that will end when he headlines MVP’s card in the United Arab Emirates.

He has committed to another fight.

“I’m hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I’m returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey,” Paul said.

The comeback will also take Paul into a new location for his professional career. He has never contested a professional bout in Dubai, which will host the event through MVP’s cooperation agreement with the Dubai Sports Council and Dubai’s Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP has not yet named the opponent, venue or broadcaster. The promotion plans to release further details over the coming weeks, with no weight division or scheduled distance specified in the October 29 announcement.

Paul began his professional career in 2020. His headline appearances have since included Mike Tyson in November 2024 and Joshua the following December, with the latter leaving him facing a lengthy spell outside the ring.

Bidarian described the decision to resume fighting as evidence of Paul’s commitment to boxing. Paul, meanwhile, closed his comeback statement with a prediction for whoever signs to face him.

“Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody’s getting knocked out.”

Sports.title: David Benavidez Ready To Put Oleksandr Usyk First
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is risking his shot at Oleksandr Usyk by messing around with Jai Opetaia or Artur Beterbiev beforehand. Jumping straight up to heavyweight makes total sense, especially since he already sounds open to flipping the script.

Talking about skipping straight to Usyk sounds a whole lot less like fearless ambition and a whole lot more like self-preservation.

Benavidez knows that the road running through Jai Opetaia and Artur Beterbiev is not a tune-up run. It is an absolute danger. If he actually believed he could steamroll both men, he would happily take their scalps, build an undeniable mountain of momentum, and walk into a showdown with Usyk as a massive multi-division attraction.

Bypassing them exposes the reality: he knows the risk of getting derailed before cashing that mega check is sky-high.

“If they want me to go up … I don’t give a f***,” Benavidez stated in the interview. “I want to fight. I want to fight the best people. And if I got to go up there and fight for the lineal belt with no belts, I’ll do that … I just want to fight the best in the world. I want my respect, and I’m going to get it one way or another,” said Benavidez to Fight Hub TV about moving up to heavyweight to face Usyk.

That sounds like someone ready to sign for Usyk the moment pen meets paper. He never locked himself into clearing out Opetaia or Beterbiev before taking that leap.

If he takes an L against either one, the Usyk lottery ticket instantly turns to dust. Usyk is not going to look twice at a defeated Benavidez trying to pick up the pieces, not when he can command massive money elsewhere.

Opetaia has the exact southpaw movement, discipline, and sharp counterpunching to turn Benavidez into a frustrated stalker swinging at fresh air while eating clean leather all night. Beterbiev brings brutal inside violence and technical craft that makes trading in the pocket pure trouble.

Both matchups carry a high probability of stripping Benavidez of his spotless record and shredding his market value.

Benavidez already wasted years chasing Canelo Alvarez, only to come away empty-handed. Now that he is finally free from that waste of time, he ought to recognize the danger of waiting around for the stars to align.

Usyk is clearly the legacy crown he wants.

“Usyk has more accolades than Canelo, in my opinion,” Benavidez noted. “Once I beat him, there’s no denying me my spot in the history of boxing.”

Admitting he would train “like I’m scared for my life” shows he respects the mountain in front of him. Taking Usyk immediately carries risk, but it locks down the biggest prize while Benavidez’s zero remains intact.

Ghana News.title: Ghana targets $1.2bn investment and 150,000 jobs under new textile policy
Ghana News.content:
Ghana is targeting about $1.2 billion in investment and 150,000 direct and indirect jobs over the next decade under a new textile and garment policy approved by Cabinet.

The policy, which is expected to be formally launched by the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, also seeks to expand the country's textile and garment industry from an estimated $400 million to about $2 billion.

It further aims to revive domestic cotton production across 50,000 hectares as part of efforts to strengthen local raw material supply and support the growth of the industry.

The targets were announced by the Trade Ministry’s Director of Research, George Amoah, at the launch of the second phase of the International Labour Organization’s (ILO) Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work programme.

Mr Amoah described the textile and garment industry as a significant source of employment, with the potential to create decent jobs and help address unemployment.

He cited estimates indicating that the global garment sector employs about 94 million people, with women accounting for between 60 and 80 per cent of the workforce.

However, he said investment in factories and equipment alone would not be enough to achieve the sector’s growth ambitions.

“We need a skilled workforce, efficient production systems, strong management, compliance with standards and workplaces where people can perform at their best,” he said.

At the same event, ILO Programmes Manager Bismark Ghartey outlined some of the achievements of the first phase of the Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work programme.

He said the programme supported the development of Ghana’s first productivity statistics, providing a national evidence base for discussions on productivity, employment, wages and policy.

Mr Ghartey also cited developments in the shea sector, where the programme supported the establishment of the Shea Employers Association and the Ghana Shea Workers Union.

The two organisations subsequently signed what he described as the sector’s first collective bargaining agreement in 2026.

He said the agreement provided a framework for employers and workers to address shared concerns through dialogue.

ILO Global Programmes Manager for the Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work, Stephan Ulrich, said the second phase would build on the initial programme by coordinating productivity improvements at the policy, labour and enterprise levels.

He stressed the need for deliberate pathways to help workers transition into more decent employment, noting that economic growth does not automatically translate into job creation.

The programme is funded by the Swiss government through the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs.

Switzerland’s Deputy Head of Mission and Head of Cooperation to Ghana, Janine Walz, called for a coordinated approach to job creation, stressing that improvements in productivity and employment require collaboration across businesses and institutions.

The Productivity Ecosystems for Decent Work programme adopts an integrated approach to improving productivity and working conditions at enterprise, sectoral and national levels.

It seeks to address structural factors contributing to low productivity and high informality rather than focusing only on their effects.

The proposed textile and garment policy is expected to form part of broader efforts to attract investment, strengthen local production and improve employment opportunities in the sector.

Ghana News.title: UPSA Graduates 1,314 Students at 18th Congregation
Ghana News.content:
The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), on Wednesday held the third session of its 18th Congregation at the Kofi Ohene Konadu Auditorium, where 1,314 students from the Faculty of Management Studies graduated. Various awards were presented to students who excelled.

The cohort comprised 1,009 undergraduate degree recipients and 305 diploma recipients. They form part of the 5,120 students expected to graduate across the University’s 18th Congregation sessions.

In his report, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor John Kwaku Mensah Mawutor, urged the new graduates to uphold integrity and accountability while pursuing continuous learning to remain relevant in a changing professional environment. “Let integrity and accountability guide you as you step into the next chapter of your lives,” he said.

He encouraged the graduates to harness emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), responsibly while exercising independent judgement.

He further urged them to remain curious, adaptable and committed to developing their knowledge and skills, and to build professional reputations grounded in competence, integrity and service.

The Special Guest of Honour, Managing Director of Appointed Time Limited, Jacqueline Afful, urged the graduates to pair desire with discipline, direction and character in order to succeed in the world of work.

She said graduation marks the end of a long journey that began with excitement upon receiving admission letters, particularly for those who got their desired courses.

According to her, one of the most powerful forces in human life is desire, and every graduate has a dream they desire to achieve, but the critical question is how many are willing to go through the process to achieve it.

On corporate sustainability in Ghana, Mrs. Afful said one of the fears of most organisations is how to transcend generations, a challenge she linked to the attitude of young graduates towards hard work.

Recounting an experience in her company, she said 10 National Service Personnel who served in 2025, when asked about their career aspirations and which department they would like to join if retained, all chose Human Resources, including those who studied Marketing.

When asked why they were not interested in marketing, a field they studied and served in, she said they responded that marketers suffer too much because of constant pressure over targets during management and performance reviews. “At this time, we all want to do HR," she quoted them as saying, adding that the company eventually had to let go of the graduates.

Mrs. Afful said the incident illustrates a simple truth: "In this world, it is those who want to go the extra mile, those who want to do the hard work, who can achieve success. “She told the graduates that while they have earned their degrees and some have already started their national service or dream jobs, the degree may not necessarily be the path of their future growth. She noted that it is normal to change career paths, as long as one is still driven by desire, but cautioned that desire must have discipline and direction.

She reminded them that the world is big enough for everyone and that UPSA has equipped them to either seek employment or come together to form their own organisations.

She warned that there will be financial difficulties and stiff competition, but urged them to be determined to do more and go the extra mile. “Go out there and be champions of your profession,” she charged the graduates.

Ghana News.title: Ten missing manhood cases false; Police vehicle vandalised at Breman
Ghana News.content:
The Asankragwa Divisional Police Command has dismissed 10 reported cases of alleged missing manhood in its operational area as false, following medical examinations that confirmed the complainants’ genitalia were intact and medically normal.

The Divisional Police Commander, Chief Superintendent (C/Supt) Vitus Napen, made the disclosure at a press briefing in Asankragwa.

The briefing was attended by the District Police Commander, Superintendent James Ankan, and the Divisional Crime Officer, Mr John Kwakye.

C/Supt Napen said the Division recorded the first case at Wassa Dunkwa on October 17, 2026, and has since recorded 10 similar cases.

He said Wassa Dunkwa recorded six cases, Asankragwa two cases, Aboi Nkwanta one case and Breman one case.

According to him, the complainants alleged that their genitalia had disappeared after coming into physical contact with other persons.

C/Supt Napen said all complainants were referred for medical examination, which established that their genitalia were intact and medically normal.

He added that preliminary investigations suggested that panic, anxiety and misinformation had contributed to the spread of the allegations.

The Divisional Commander cautioned the public against raising false alarms over alleged missing genitalia, warning that such actions could attract legal consequences.

He said persons found culpable could be prosecuted for offences related to the publication of false news and deceiving a public officer.

Touching on an incident at Breman, C/Supt Napen said a mob attacked and vandalised a police patrol vehicle when officers arrived to rescue a suspect accused of causing the disappearance of a man’s genitalia.

He said the mob smashed the rear windscreen of the vehicle in an attempt to lynch the suspect.

C/Supt Napen condemned the incident, describing it as criminal, and warned that anyone who attacked security personnel or destroyed state property would be arrested and prosecuted.

He urged the public to desist from taking the law into their own hands and to allow the Police to investigate such allegations.

The Divisional Commander appealed to chiefs, opinion leaders and assembly members in the Wassa Amenfi West Municipality to intensify public education and encourage residents to report suspected criminal activities to the Police.

He said no arrests had been made in connection with the vandalism as of the time of the briefing, adding that investigations were ongoing.

Ghana News.title: 47 university students attend first Unmute Yo’Self public speaking event in Accra
Ghana News.content:
Forty-seven university students have participated in the first edition of Unmute Yo’Self, a free public speaking and confidence-building event aimed at helping young people communicate their ideas more effectively.

The event was held on Friday, October 23, 2026, at the Accra AI Community Center in Ridge, Accra.

Organised by the Sincerely Accra Podcast in collaboration with The Gold Coast Report (GCR), the programme was sponsored by Malta Guinness and Ashesi University. Participants included students from first year through to their final year.

The initiative was designed to address the challenges young people face in expressing themselves confidently in classrooms, job interviews and professional settings.

Organisers said the programme provides a supportive space for students to practise communication skills and develop the confidence to share their ideas.

Co-creators of the Sincerely Accra Podcast, Joseph Nti and Kwame Asante Ofori, led sessions on public speaking and the responsible use of social media.

Mr Nti, the podcast’s host, and Mr Ofori, its producer, guided participants on managing nervousness and structuring presentations around a clear opening, central message, supporting example, and conclusion.

Guest speaker Nadia Daniel-Wilson addressed the topic “Using AI Without Surrendering Your Creativity,” encouraging students to use artificial intelligence tools to support their work without losing their individual voice and judgement.

A panel of creative entrepreneurs also shared their experiences of building careers in the creative industry and turning their skills into income.

The panel featured Shaunn Armah, a founder, creator and storyteller; Kabiru Seidu, co-founder and Director of Design and Strategy at The Big Fat African Development; and Seli Dzogbenuku, a writer, creative entrepreneur and podcast host.

The discussions focused on their journeys into content creation, the opportunities available in the creative sector and the practical steps involved

Ghana News.title: Philippine police obtain warrant to search Thomas Markle’s devices
Ghana News.content:
Philippine police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from the former home of Thomas Markle, father of the Duchess of Sussex.

Earlier this month, it was reported that hundreds of images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Thomas Markle Sr., 82, had been found at the property in the Philippines.

Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr., handed police four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives, and old videotapes, last week. However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.

Thomas Markle Sr., now in the US, has strongly denied his son's allegations, describing them as "sick lies".

Cebu Regional Prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC that Thomas Markle Jr was "adamant" that the case should be investigated, and that he felt his father "has to answer for it".

Last week, the Sun on Sunday reported that Thomas Markle Sr's ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless, had sent a letter to the Metropolitan Police about the 2019 allegations, which the Duke and Duchess of Sussex received at the time.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's two half-siblings. She divorced Thomas Markle Sr. in 1975, before he married the Duchess' mother.

Ghana News.title: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17bn deal it says will expand customer options
Ghana News.content:
DoorDash will acquire grocery delivery firm Instacart in a $17bn (£12.8bn) deal, creating a behemoth that will bring more meals, quick-need purchases and big weekly shops directly to customers.

DoorDash said the deal, expected to be final in about a year, will expand customer options and let more sellers use the companies' services.

Instacart shoppers will be able to buy from 150,000 stores, up from 100,000, while DoorDash will expand beyond restaurants into retail, the firms said.

"Together, we can accelerate innovation across the grocery industry and make online grocery more seamless and affordable for the millions of households we serve," Instacart's chief executive said.

"Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more," CEO Chris Rogers also said.

For DoorDash, the acquisition will allow it to use Instacart's grocery selection and substitution expertise, the company's co-founder and chief executive, Tony Xu, said.

"Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online. Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you'd choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts," Xu said.

He added that "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day".

The deal, expected to be done by the end of 2027 or first six months of 2028, is DoorDash's biggest acquisition to date, and could help it take on delivery giants like Amazon.

Morningstar analyst Martin Szumski told Reuters that the growth area in food delivery was shifting.

"Restaurant delivery is maturing, and growth now lies in more frequent, higher-value orders: weekly grocery shops, convenience items, and retail," he said.

In the agreement, DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a value of $65 a share, which would be a 26% premium on the closing price of Instacart stock on 22 October - the price before news of the potential merger first emerged. The deal will be at least 75% cash, DoorDash said.

DoorDash plans to keep Instacart's brand, app, and technology products. The delivery services will keep operating as independent companies until the deal is concluded.

The merger may raise antitrust issues with government regulators, Reuters also reported.

New York City's commission on consumer and worker protections, which last month reached a $131.5m settlement with DoorDash over allegations of underpaying workers, said in a statement: "This proposed merger continues a troubling trend of mega-corporations consolidating."

"Whether or not this merger proceeds, we will fully enforce delivery workers' rights," it added.

Ghana News.title: Trade Ministry launches pharmaceutical policy to double local medicine production
Ghana News.content:
The government has launched the Cabinet-approved Ghana Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Policy, seeking to double domestic medicine production, create skilled jobs and position the country as a leading pharmaceutical manufacturing hub in West Africa.

The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, announced the policy at its launch in Accra on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

She said the policy was designed to address Ghana’s dependence on imported medicines, which currently account for about 70% of the country’s medicine supply.

Under the policy, Ghana aims to increase the share of locally manufactured medicines in the domestic market from 30 per cent to 60 per cent, as an intermediate step towards President John Mahama’s target of achieving 70 per cent local pharmaceutical self-sufficiency.

“Medicines are not ordinary goods. A country that cannot produce its own essential medicines leaves its health, economy, and sovereignty vulnerable,” Mrs Ofosu-Adjare said.

She explained that the policy would provide a coordinated framework to align investment, regulation, public procurement, skills development and regional trade in support of local pharmaceutical manufacturers.

The Minister outlined six key pillars underpinning the policy, including improving the quality of locally manufactured medicines to meet international standards, expanding market access for domestic producers and providing affordable, long-term financing.

The government also plans to support local manufacturers to obtain World Health Organisation Good Manufacturing Practice certification and prequalification, while using public procurement and the National Health Insurance Scheme to prioritise quality medicines produced in Ghana.

On financing, Mrs Ofosu-Adjare said the policy would promote partnerships with Development Bank Ghana, Ghana EXIM Bank and GIPA to improve access to long-term funding for pharmaceutical businesses.

The policy also seeks to move the industry beyond packaging into the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients, excipients and vaccines.

Other priorities include strengthening collaboration between academia and industry, equipping clinical pharmacists with skills for pharmaceutical manufacturing, and expanding exports through the African Continental Free Trade Area and the Economic Community of West African States.

The launch brought together representatives from key institutions involved in the policy’s implementation, including the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Finance, Food and Drugs Authority, National Vaccine Institute, Development Bank Ghana, GIZ, the World Health Organisation and the European Union.

The government expects the policy to strengthen local manufacturing capacity, reduce dependence on imported medicines and create opportunities for Ghanaian pharmaceutical businesses to expand into regional markets.

Ghana News.title: Ghana woos Polish investors with access to African markets
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has urged Polish and other European businesses to invest in the country, citing its democratic stability, access to African markets and improving economic conditions as key advantages.

The Deputy Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Sampson Ahi, made the call during a panel discussion on “What Investors Need to Know from Both Governments” at the TOP CHARITY ChangeMAKERS Africa Business Mixer in Accra.

He said Ghana’s stable democratic environment, respect for the rule of law and growing middle class made it an attractive destination for investors seeking to expand their operations.

Mr Ahi also highlighted Ghana’s role as host of the Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), describing it as a strategic advantage for businesses seeking access to the wider African market.

The AfCFTA provides a framework for trade across 54 African countries, representing a potential market of approximately 1.4 billion people.

He encouraged Polish and other European businesses to explore investment opportunities in Ghana, particularly as the government pursues efforts to strengthen the country’s industrial base, create jobs and deepen international trade relations.

The Deputy Minister said greater investment would support Ghana’s economic ambitions while creating opportunities for stronger commercial partnerships between Ghanaian and European businesses.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Palestinians face growing bans from Al-Aqsa as Israel tightens control
World.content:
For more than two years, Sheikh Ekrima Sabri has been barred from occupied East Jerusalem’s Al-Aqsa Mosque, unable to pray or deliver sermons at the holy site.

And with his latest exclusion order extending the ban until April 2027, the Palestinian preacher – the head of the Higher Islamic Council in Jerusalem – is among those facing Israeli restrictions at the site – the third holiest in Islam and a Palestinian national symbol.

Sabri has faced repeated exclusion orders since August 2024. The latest order, issued on October 20, prevents Sabri from praying or delivering sermons at Al-Aqsa until April 2027.

At the same time, far-right Jewish religious activists have increasingly been allowed to pray at the site under Israeli police protection, going against a longstanding status quo and opposition from ultra-Orthodox Jewish religious authorities.

The restrictions began after Israeli police detained Sabri in August 2024 over a sermon in which he mourned the Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh, who was assassinated by Israel.

Sabri, one of the most prominent Palestinians in East Jerusalem, has faced repeated Israeli interrogations.

Palestinians say this is part of a campaign against them at Al-Aqsa. The Wadi Hilweh Information Center, a Palestinian human rights monitoring group, says Israeli authorities have issued more than 1,000 exclusion orders barring Palestinians from Al-Aqsa Mosque and the Old City since the beginning of 2026, including against religious figures and Islamic Waqf employees.



The centre reported an increase in exclusion orders ahead of Jewish holidays, documenting more than 40 issued over five days in early September.

Sabri told Al Jazeera that the latest extension was the fifth time Israeli authorities have issued an exclusion order against him.

He described the decision as unjust, illegal, inhumane and uncivilised, saying it was intended to silence those speaking out about Al-Aqsa.

Sabri said that he would continue defending Al-Aqsa despite the restrictions, describing the mosque as an integral part of his Islamic faith.

“These measures are aimed at diminishing the Palestinian presence at the mosque, while simultaneously allowing settlers to carry out incursions in large numbers,” Sabri said. “Such actions represent an aggressive policy targeting the Al-Aqsa Mosque and the Islamic presence within it.”

Prohibited activities

Ibrahim al-Natsheh was released by Israeli police earlier this month after spending a week in detention after he was arrested while attending funeral prayers for his cousin at Al-Aqsa Mosque.

He told Al Jazeera that officers took him to a police room and handed him a six-month exclusion order barring him from East Jerusalem’s Old City. He said no specific charge was brought against him.

According to al-Natsheh, the order warns that he could face arrest and further penalties, including a fine or imprisonment, if he enters the prohibited area.

Al-Natsheh said he has received so many exclusion orders that he has lost count. He said the restrictions began about nine years ago, following an Israeli crackdown on Islamic study circles at the mosque.

Palestinian students, teachers and activists associated with the activities have faced arrests and exclusion orders.

“The orders banning us from the mosque provide no specific reason; they simply cite ‘disturbing the peace’, even though we are there solely to pray,” al-Natsheh told Al Jazeera. “Ahead of the Jewish holidays, they sent a message to me and a group of other worshippers, warning us not to approach the mosque or else we will be arrested.”

Even when he is not subject to a formal exclusion order, al-Natsheh said, Israeli police have prevented him from entering Al-Aqsa. He also alleged that officers have repeatedly arrested him at Al-Aqsa’s gates and severely beaten him while in detention.

“The path to the mosque has become incredibly difficult; it is swarming with soldiers and settlers,” he said. “We are denied the ability to reach it with any ease, and if we try, we face arrest and beatings with batons. It is deeply painful to witness what is happening to Al-Aqsa now.”



Al Jazeera has reached out to Israeli authorities for comment, but has yet to receive a response.

Diminishing Waqf role

Al-Aqsa Mosque has seen an escalation in Israeli restrictions and violations throughout 2026.

After the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran on February 28, Israeli authorities closed Al-Aqsa to most worshippers for 40 days, reopening the compound on April 9.

Meanwhile, according to the Palestinian Authority’s Jerusalem Governorate, almost 28,000 visits by Israeli settlers were recorded at Al-Aqsa between July and September.

Ma’rouf al-Rifai, an adviser to the Jerusalem Governorate, told Al Jazeera that during recent Jewish holidays, Israeli restrictions on Muslim worshippers had intensified.

These measures included closing the mosque for periods of time, preventing noon prayers on at least one occasion, and restricting access for residents of the Old City during visits to the site by Israeli settlers and Jewish religious activists.

Al-Rifai said the Islamic Waqf Department faces mounting constraints on its role in managing the mosque’s affairs.

He said Israeli police have prevented Waqf officials from accompanying Jewish groups when they entered the site, curtailed the authority of mosque guards, and arrested or barred several employees from the compound.

As a result, he said, fewer than 15 guards are now on duty during the morning shift, compared with approximately 50 previously.

He pointed out that the closure of the mosque for 40 days during the war with Iran took place without consulting the Waqf or providing prior notification, which he said demonstrated the Waqf’s diminishing role in the mosque’s administration.

“Settler incursions have undergone a shift over the past three years; they now include Jewish prayers and religious rituals, the raising of Israeli flags, and attempts to bring in sacrificial offerings,” al-Rifai said.

These changes have undermined longstanding arrangements at the compound, under which the Waqf manages Muslim religious affairs while Israeli police oversee security and access.

According to al-Rifai, Israeli authorities have prevented the Waqf from carrying out restoration work at the Bab al-Rahma prayer hall and restricted maintenance of the compound’s trees and gardens. He said the committee responsible for restoration work at Al-Aqsa has been unable to carry out its duties for years.

He warned of efforts to alter the status quo at Al-Aqsa Mosque, pointing to several proposals and developments, including demands to allow Jewish visitors into the compound on Saturdays, plans advanced by Israeli politicians to divide access to parts of the site between Muslims and Jews, and an Israeli police recruitment drive for volunteers tasked with escorting Israeli incursions at the site.

Al-Rifai said these developments represented a further erosion of the Waqf’s authority and warned that they could eventually transform the arrangements governing worship and access at the holy site.
