World.title: Palestinians injured, arrested in Israeli raids across West Bank
World.content:
This comes as more than 3,300 Palestinians are forced from homes in Hebron in Israeli military offensive.

Israeli forces and settlers have escalated pogroms and raids across the occupied West Bank, attacking and injuring Palestinians, restricting their movement, carrying out arrests and demolishing homes.

This comes as a military offensive and siege on the Hebron governorate entered its seventh day – an operation that has displaced or besieged hundreds of Palestinian families and kept tens of thousands of students out of classrooms.

In the Qalandiya refugee camp just north of occupied East Jerusalem, Israeli forces carried out a raid that triggered clashes on Thursday. Two children were wounded, the Palestine Red Crescent Society said.

It said its teams treated a 15-year-old boy who was shot with live ammunition in both legs, and a child, aged 12, who was injured by live-bullet fragments. Both were taken to hospital.

In a separate incident, Israeli soldiers and settlers beat disabled Palestinian Mohammad Ahmad Ayesh Thawabta in the village of al-Maniya, southeast of Bethlehem, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

In the northern West Bank, Israeli forces detained 13 Palestinians, including three brothers, in raids before dawn on Thursday, the Palestinian Prisoners Media Office and local sources said. Most of the raids were in the Nablus governorate, where soldiers searched homes and harassed families.

Hebron offensive

In Hebron, Israeli forces continued raids and closures that began last week after two Israeli soldiers were killed in a gun attack. Both Palestinian suspects were also killed.



Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said on Thursday that 537 families, comprising 3,361 people, have been forced from their homes, Wafa reported.

They include 232 infants, 326 older people, 147 pregnant or breastfeeding women and 213 people with chronic illnesses. Municipal figures put the total number affected, including those under siege, at about 5,000 people from 780 families.

Dudin said the offensive has disrupted education for about 262,000 students across 589 schools in the governorate this week, forcing schools to move to remote learning. Officials estimated daily economic losses at 10 million to 12 million shekels ($3.2m to $3.9m).

The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society said Israeli forces detained 110 Palestinians in the governorate from Friday to Wednesday. Soldiers beat two men in Dura and Wad al-Saman and arrested two brothers while they were ploughing their land east of Yatta, it said. Israeli forces also raided homes in Taffuh and Halhul, and settlers attacked vehicles at the city’s closed northern entrance, it added.

Memorials demolished

In nearby Masafer Yatta, armed settlers attacked US journalist Jasper Nathaniel and two activists in the village of Umm al-Khair on Wednesday. Russian activist Adele Shoko said on X that the settlers beat and threatened them and stole their equipment and Nathaniel was pepper-sprayed and arrested.

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said Israeli forces are still operating in Hebron, blocking access and imposing tight restrictions on movement across the governorate.

They are “disrupting Palestinians’ access to livelihoods, education and healthcare. Most displaced families are staying with relatives,” OCHA said, calling for the prevention of further forced displacements and demolitions.

Israeli forces also demolished memorials to Palestinians in several parts of the Hebron governorate on Thursday. In Dura, south of Hebron city, soldiers fired a heavy barrage of tear gas before bulldozing a mural bearing the images of several of the town’s dead, including Bajis Abu Atwan, who was killed in the 1970s.

The targeting of memorials “appears to be a new pattern recently adopted by Israeli forces across all West Bank governorates – though at a higher rate here in Hebron”, Al Jazeera’s Muntasir Nassar said, reporting from Dura.

Israeli military and settler attacks across the West Bank have intensified since Israel’s war on Gaza began in October 2023.

World.title: Does Russia offer African countries an equal partnership?
World.content:
President Vladimir Putin hosts African leaders at a summit in Moscow.

The Russian president, speaking at the third Russia-Africa Summit being held in Moscow, has told African leaders that his country is a better partner than the West.

Vladimir Putin says Russian companies operate in Africa on an equal footing, accusing Western countries of still focusing on exploiting the continent’s resources.

Some African nations have turned to Russia for security assistance in recent years. Trade and economic ties are also growing.

And Russia has highlighted the importance of what it calls a “multipolar world” – while it seeks support from the Global South to counter Western pressure over its war in Ukraine.

So, what are Russia and African countries getting out of this gathering?

Presenter: Dareen Abughaida

Guests:

Beverly Ochieng – Associate director at Control Risks, specialising in Francophone Africa and the Sahel

Andrey Kortunov – Russian foreign affairs analyst and the former director general of the Russian International Affairs Council

Sanusha Naidu – Foreign policy analyst and senior research associate at the Institute for Global Dialogue

World.title: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete
World.content:
Opposition explores options to form coalition as no party secures the 61 seats required for parliamentary majority.

Share Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete on social media

Vote counting is complete in Israel’s elections with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition winning a majority in parliament, Israeli media have said.

As the provisional results were being published on Thursday, opposition politicians met to explore options for a coalition.

With more than 99 percent of Tuesday’s ballots tallied, Netanyahu’s bloc held 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats, Israeli outlet Haaretz reported. The Arab list parties, meanwhile, held a combined 19 seats, it added.

Both Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition parties fell short of securing the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.

The final results of the Knesset elections will be certified and announced by Wednesday. Until that date, the results are subject to change.

Tuesday’s elections – the first since the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza – were widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s premiership.

Coalition options

On Thursday, Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party, met former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together party, to discuss ways to form a new government “as quickly as possible”, according to a statement reported by Israel’s Ynet News outlet.

Eisenkot also met Democrats party chairman Yair Golan, the only member of the opposition alliance to support forming a coalition with parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, while all other political groups have rejected any such union.



Golan met separately with Mansour Abbas, who leads the United Arab list, or Ra’am, which is projected to win seven of the 19 Arab party seats.

“This is a time for action. Our responsibility is not to miss the opportunity for change and the salvation of Israel,” Golan said in a post on X after his meeting with Abbas.

Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh noted that “Eisenkot has an uphill battle ahead of him.”

The former military leader-turned-politician has pledged “not to ally himself or get into a partnership with the Palestinian Israeli parties”, Odeh said, reporting from the occupied West Bank because Al Jazeera is banned from Israel.

But given the fact that no political bloc has a majority, the Eisenkot-led opposition bloc cannot form a governing coalition without the support of Arab-led parties, she added.

Netanyahu ‘using state institutions for his personal needs’

Meanwhile, Netanyahu’s Likud party has continued to amplify unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance – claims that have been rejected.

The head of the Central Elections Committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought to him in a letter to the Shin Bet security agency. Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims, but given their serious nature, he asked the agency to investigate.

Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of working to delegitimise the election results with his allegations.

In a video posted on his X account, Eisenkot said: “The days of Netanyahu using state institutions against Israeli interests for his personal needs are over,” adding that no “spin” can change voters rejecting his government at the polls.

“Benjamin Netanyahu is not satisfied with the results, no matter how much he has been saying that he won,” political analyst Xavier Abu Eid told Al Jazeera.

He added that while it seems unlikely the opposition could take advantage by overcoming differences with the Arab-led groups, there could be an understanding to replace the current speaker of the Knesset, who is close to Netanyahu.

“If there is a new speaker in the Knesset, … Netanyahu loses an important ally,” Abu Eid said, adding that this might give an opening for the opposition to “actually start passing legislation” against him.

Odeh said the next steps would involve negotiations between political groups after the Central Elections Committee announces and certifies the election results by Wednesday.

World.title: Man targeted Muslims, Africans and North Africans, French prosecutors say
World.content:
Prosecutor Olivier Christen said suspect admitted that he chose the location because it was ‘a hotbed for Islamists’.

A man in France charged with murder and attempted murder has admitted he targeted individuals “who appeared to be Muslim, African, or North African”, prosecutors have said.

France’s anti-terrorism prosecutor’s office confirmed on Thursday that the 39-year-old, identified as Kevin T, had been formally charged in connection with a “terrorist” enterprise. Prosecutor Olivier Christen said Kevin admitted he chose the location because it was “a hotbed for Islamists”.

Before changing his position on Thursday, Kevin had disputed the racist nature of the attack.

One person was killed and seven others were injured last Friday when a man fired at people from his car as he drove through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere, west of Paris. He was arrested later that day. A child was among the victims, most of whom had foreign heritage.

The prosecutor said Kevin had stated that he felt “no regret” but that he did not intend to “kill children”. However, he added that he “might have been mistaken due to their size”.

Pengo Bossio Wangi, a 26-year-old French citizen with Congolese heritage, was killed in the attack.

During a search of Kevin’s home, authorities found “weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer”, officials said.

Police also found a copy of Adolf Hitler’s book Mein Kampf, along with a Quran, a Bible and stickers celebrating Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally party. Kevin T had displayed a “very high level of preparation” ahead of the attack, according to prosecutor Christen.



He explained that in September, Kevin acquired “several weapon components designed to enhance the tactical effectiveness of a Sten submachine gun, as well as a police armband and handcuffs”.

The suspect said he was neither a member of nor a sympathiser with any political party, Christen added.

World.title: Cornell begins no confidence vote over handling of alleged gang rape
World.content:
Faculty vote will continue until next Friday and could send message that school’s president has lost their confidence.

Cornell University has begun a no-confidence vote for the school’s leadership after an alleged gang rape prompted public outcry over sexual assault on college campuses and scrutiny over the university’s handling of the case.

Faculty members started the no-confidence vote on Thursday that is expected to continue until November 6. The initiative is non-binding, but could send a message that president Michael Kotlikoff has lost the confidence of the school’s faculty.

“Hundreds of students, staff, faculty and alumni approached the sponsors of this resolution to emphasize to us that the Jane Doe case is but a tip of the iceberg,” said Paul Ortiz, the lead faculty sponsor of the resolution.

A lawsuit filed last month alleges that a female student, identified as Jane Doe, was drugged and gang raped by seven male students at a fraternity house in 2024.

The case has raised questions about whether the university acted with sufficient urgency or downplayed the alleged abuse in order to protect its reputation. The university initially shut down the fraternity and suspended the male students, two of whom were later expelled.

Faculty considered on Wednesday whether to postpone a vote of no confidence, with some urging patience and others arguing that the vote was a necessary response to institutional reluctance to take the issue seriously.

The Associated Press news agency reported that the debate took place after a group of 20 female science and engineering faculty members called on Kotlikoff to resign in a letter to trustees.



“What our community needed was clear leadership; instead, it faced a leadership vacuum,” the letter stated.

Kotlikoff sought to address the fallout in a statement earlier this month in which he listed a number of preliminary responses.

“I am deeply sorry for the harm Jane Doe suffered in 2024, and appalled that this act of sexual violence occurred within our Cornell community,” he said.

Two of the men accused of taking part in the alleged rape of Jane Doe have asked for New York Attorney General Letitia James to be removed from her role overseeing the renewed criminal probe into the case over social media posts from the attorney general expressing support for the accuser prior to her appointment.

A judge on Thursday appeared sceptical of one of the challenges, which James’ office has said are “without merit”.

World.title: Israel’s opposition may not be able to form a government, but it still could control Parliament.
World.content:
For decades, Israel’s Arab parties have been relegated to the margins of Israeli political life, often sitting on the sidelines while Jewish parties assembled a governing coalition in Parliament and picked a prime minister.

Heading into Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned his supporters that the Arabs were “trying to steal the election,” though electoral officials said there were no reports of widespread irregularities. He repeatedly invoked the specter of Arab voters to galvanize his right-wing base, vowing to keep them out of power.

Mr. Netanyahu’s leading rival, Gadi Eisenkot, largely declined to answer whether he would partner with Arab parties if necessary to topple the Netanyahu government, though he said none met his conditions as potential allies.

But record turnout by supporters of the Arab parties looks to deliver them their largest vote totals in generations, possibly since Israel’s establishment 78 years ago.

Now, the Arab minority represents a political reality that cannot be ignored.

Turnout in the Arab community, which represents about 20 percent of Israeli citizens, appears to have translated into a stunning windfall of parliamentary seats — potentially as many as 19 combined between the two leading parties, Raam and the Joint List alliance. The Arab parties have 10 seats in the outgoing Parliament.

Israel’s future could turn in part on whether Mr. Eisenkot decides to take the political risks of partnering with them. Without their support, Mr. Eisenkot and his alliance will almost certainly fall short of the 61-seat majority required in the 120-seat Parliament to form a new government and end Mr. Netanyahu’s hold on power. Mr. Netanyahu’s alliance also looks to fall short of 61 seats.

Many Israeli Jews have long objected to building a governing coalition that relies on Arab party backing for a majority. Some say a Jewish state should be ruled exclusively by Jews. Some cite national security reasons, questioning whether Arab leaders who see themselves as part of the wider Palestinian people can be entrusted with crucial matters of state.

Those objections became even more acute after the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel and the subsequent rightward shift in Israeli politics. Both Raam and some members of the Joint List condemned the assault, although they have also been highly critical of how Israel has conducted its war against Hamas in Gaza.

The Arab parties for many years were themselves reluctant to join governments that oversaw the Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza. And turnout among Arab citizens has traditionally been lower than Jewish turnout, reflecting doubts about their ability to influence national decision-making.

Raam, a socially conservative party with roots in Islamist politics, has achieved some acceptance in Israel’s mainstream by putting less emphasis on the cause of Palestinian statehood. But the Joint List, an alliance of three smaller parties that includes a joint Jewish-Arab leftist faction and a Palestinian nationalist faction, is seen as more antagonistic toward Zionism.

Initial election results show that the Joint List will be the significantly larger of the two in Parliament.

“Netanyahu knows that without the Arab parties, there’s no majority to unseat him. That’s why he incites against us,” said Yousef Jabareen, the leader of the Joint List alliance in an interview. “The opposition should reject that incitement.”

He added: “The ball is now in Eisenkot’s court. Whoever wants to remove Netanyahu and change his policies — we are ready to cooperate to topple his government.”

Political analysts say the Joint List would be more likely to support Eisenkot from outside the governing coalition, for instance by agreeing to block any no-confidence votes. There is some precedent for this: In the 1990s, then Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin relied on Arab lawmakers to prevent the collapse of his own minority government.

Arab citizens, some of whom identify themselves as Palestinians with Israeli passports, experience a tension that can cut to the heart of daily life. Unlike Palestinians in the West Bank — who live under Israeli military rule — they have the right to vote, and some have held high office, including on the country’s Supreme Court.

But they largely live in separate cities and towns from Jewish Israelis and retain tight familial and historical bonds with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza. Many view themselves as second-class citizens in the Jewish state, saying they face discrimination in housing as well as neglect in receiving public services.

Before this year, the largest electoral success recorded by Arab parties was in 2020, when they secured 15 seats. And the first — and so far, only — time an independent Arab party joined the Israeli governing coalition was in 2021, when Mansour Abbas, the leader of Raam, joined Mr. Netanyahu’s rivals to unseat him in favor of a short-lived government.

Mr. Abbas has since worked to make his party more acceptable to Israeli Jews. He has recognized Israel’s Jewish character as a fact of life and publicly considered integrating Arabs into the country’s mandatory national service, in particular community service.

In a bold move during the election campaign, he named Jewish lawmaker Yoav Segalovitz — a former senior police officer and centrist Zionist — as the number two on the Raam candidate list.

But if exit polls and initial results are correct, Raam’s support would not be enough to give Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc a parliamentary majority. He would also have to rely on the Joint List to topple Mr. Netanyahu. While political analysts say that Mr. Eisenkot might be willing to bring Raam onboard, he would struggle to keep his bloc with him if he made common cause with the Joint List, even if he wanted to, because this could provoke too much political blowback from many Jewish voters.

“There’s a shift in Arab politics, an attempt to get closer to the Jewish Zionist mainstream. It’s just that the other side is not willing to do so,” said Thair Abu Rass, an expert on Israel’s Arab politics. “There’s no partner on the Jewish side to create an alternative reality.”

World.title: The crash comes months after a fatal accident involving the same train operators.
World.content:
Pinned

A high-speed passenger train rear-ended another in Spain on Wednesday morning near the central city of Toledo, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens more, officials said, in one of the deadliest train crashes in Spanish history.

The accident happened after traffic control operators told a high-speed train to continue its journey when another train was stopped farther along the tracks, Spain’s transportation minister, Óscar Puente, said. He called the operators’ instruction “inexplicable.”

The deadly crash was the second this year involving the same two rail operators; the first, in January, killed 46 people. The latest accident, and its timing months after the previous crash, was likely to deepen doubts about the security of Spain’s once-vaunted rail system.

In Spanish news reports, passengers described an awful impact that tossed people from a dining car, broke limbs and piled passengers atop one another. People crawled out of windows and others were carried by fellow passengers into a nearby field on makeshift stretchers. Local workers, who had heard the crash, rushed to help and guide survivors to safety.

The crash came about a month ahead of national election in Spain, and it had the potential to become an issue in an already bitter campaign about the competence of the left-wing government of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

Spain’s rail authority, the Adif, said the trains involved were a “Renfe train and another from the Iryo company,” both covering the route between Madrid, the capital, and the southern city of Seville. Renfe is the national rail provider.

Mr. Sánchez visited the scene of the crash, saying that Spanish rail’s security systems clearly needed to be reinforced. “If there has been negligence, it will come to light,” he said. “If there have been failures in the safety system, we will respond with the utmost firmness.” He declared three days of official mourning.

The conservative opposition leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, voiced his own concern.

“I am very concerned about the information we are receiving regarding another train accident,” he wrote on social media soon after the crash. “The priority now is to assist the victims and support their families. My full support goes to the emergency teams working on the ground.” His Popular Party canceled all its campaign events around the country.

Here’s what else to know:

Survivor speaks: A passenger on one of the trains described a routine trip, a sudden jolt and an effort to tend to the dead and injured. Read more ›

An earlier deadly crash: In January, a northbound Iryo train derailed, two of its cars falling onto the opposite track, and a southbound Renfe train slammed into the carriages seconds later. An official report on what caused that lethal accident has not been released, but preliminary investigations pointed to a broken rail as the likely cause.

A detailed account: In a news conference, Spain’s transportation minister described the events that he said preceded Wednesday’s crash. Read more ›

José Bautista contributed reporting from the scene of the crash.

World.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election
World.content:
The main Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders have denounced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleging foreign interference following the election which saw his coalition lose its majority.

Netanyahu's Likud accused Israel's Arab-led parties of "stealing" the election. Home security agency Shin Bet is investigating whether they received illegal funding from Qatar and Turkey.

Qatar's foreign ministry denied the "ridiculous and dangerous" allegations and accused Israeli politicians of conducting a disinformation campaign against Doha.

Final results confirmed that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the Jewish opposition had won a majority in parliament.

The two Arab party lists - The Joint List and the Ra'am - defied expectations to win a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers, with Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats and his rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc securing 48.

On Thursday Likud alleged that voters had been "bribed" to vote for Arab parties, after the head of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate "serious suspicions" of foreign interference.

Both Arab parties strongly rejected the claim, with the Arab-majority Joint List alliance saying it was baseless.

The row is being seen by Netanyahu's critics as an attempt to delegitimise the Arab parties, thereby making it politically impossible for Eisenkot to join forces with them - which is currently his bloc's only route to power.

World.title: Audio reveals exchanges between Spain train operators and drivers moments before deadly crash
World.content:
Leaked audio recordings that were published in Spanish media have revealed conversations between train drivers and a control centre just minutes before a deadly crash on Wednesday morning, that has killed 69 people.

Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train near Urda.

Three audio recordings between Madrid's control centre and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another train had stalled on the track, about 25km (15 miles) ahead.

Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez has said that authorities will "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy".

Dozens of people were injured, with survivors recounting harrowing scenes people crying and bleeding, passengers trapped in their seats, missing limbs and smoke billowing throughout the carriages, one of which caught fire.

On Thursday, Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited some of the injured passengers in a hospital in Toledo.

He later expressed condolences to the victims' relatives, pledging that the investigation would determine why the crash happened, and what measures would be taken for this not to happen again.

World.title: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next
World.content:
The Ukrainian city of Kherson has known its first two days of quiet after many years, as a US-brokered temporary ceasefire has allowed residents rare moments of respite from the constant Russian aerial attacks that plague the front line region.

Videos posted on social media showed people strolling down streets covered in anti-drone nets and gathering in the city's squares - ordinary activities that usually mean keeping one eye on the sky and one ear out for incoming drones.

"Ever since the ceasefire was announced, there's been total silence," said Olga, 42, speaking by phone from Kherson. "We are all, of course, overjoyed."

"I don't even know what to call it," she added, her smile coming through in her voice. "It's as if everything has finally come to an end."

Since Tuesday, Kherson has "literally come back to life," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said.

"People are calmly going out, walking, enjoying the autumn sun. What for some is ordinary everyday life, for residents of the Kherson region today is the greatest desire."

The temporary pause in hostilities - due to end on Sunday - is the result of efforts by US First Lady Melania Trump to broker a safe passage out of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which lies on the other side of the Dnipro river from Kherson.

For several days, Russian forces have been working to clear the road of mines, ahead of a planned evacuation of Oleshky's civilians on Friday.

But there are fears that, alongside carrying out the well-publicised "humanitarian operation" â which some American journalists will be invited to witness â the Russians are using the truce to bolster their forces in the area ahead of a renewed onslaught of Kherson from next week.

"They are... using this lull to strengthen their positions, bring in more military supplies, weapons, ammunition, and drones, and carry out some redeployment of their forces," an anonymous source working in local government told the BBC.

World.title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
World.content:
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.

Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.

Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.

Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.

In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to the railway operator chief, Oleksandr Pertsovsky.

"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform" when the drone struck, he said.

Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said the incident was a tragedy, adding that a drone hit an electric civilian train.

Pictures from the Ukrainian rescue services show a large hole in a platform that is strewn with blurred-out bodies, near a blast-damaged train with smashed windows.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said "the Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."

He called for further US, European and G7 sanctions on Russia and repeated his criticism of a controversial deal that was struck earlier this month between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which eased some sanctions on Moscow, allowing the US to import Russian diesel.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, two girls aged 15 were killed in a Russian missile attack on the centre of Chernihiv city, in the north of the country, regional head Vyacheslav Chaus said. At least 25 others, including four children, were injured, he added.

A day of mourning has been declared for Chernihiv and Dnipro on Friday.

In the city of Kremenchuk, in the central Poltava region, three people were killed and 28 injured in a Russian drone attack that hit residential buildings and a school, regional head Vitaliy Diakivnych said.

World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
World.content:
Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".

However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."

Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.

In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".

The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.

An analysis of election data conducted by BBC Brazil and BBC Verify has also found that only around 34,000 people voted during the extended hours - far lower than the 4.4 million votes that separated Lula from Bolsonaro.

In his letter, Bolsonaro also addresses his departure from Brazil - which caused confusion after he disappeared for more than 24 hours.

It later emerged that he had gone across the land border to Argentina, and from there flew on to Florida, following a brief refuelling stop in Ecuador.

World.title: Philippine police obtain warrant to search Thomas Markle's devices
World.content:
Philippine police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from the former home of Thomas Markle, father of the Duchess of Sussex.

Earlier this month, it was reported that hundreds of images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Thomas Markle Sr, 82, had been found at the property in the Philippines.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes, were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week. However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.

Thomas Markle Sr, who is now in the US, has strongly denied the allegations made by his son, describing them as "sick lies".

Cebu Regional Prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC that Thomas Markle Jr was "adamant" that the case should be investigated, and that he felt his father "has to answer for it".

Last week, the Sun on Sunday reported that Thomas Markle Sr's ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless, had sent a letter to the Metropolitan Police about the 2019 allegations, which was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's two half-siblings. She divorced Thomas Markle Sr. in 1975, before he married the duchess's mother.

World.title: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
World.content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has laid out her vision for what an "associate membership" status for Canada to the EU would look like as officials gather in Montreal to discuss closer ties.

It is "a partnership that comes close to membership than anything we have done before," she said on Thursday's remarks at the two-day Canada-EU summit.

She added it is a type of relationship that would be open "only to our closest partners outside of Europe who are ready to open a new frontier together."

It includes close alignment on governance and policies, and partnering in research and innovation.

For decades, Canada-EU summits took place without much fanfare - but that's not the case for this year's meeting in the Canadian city.

Thursday and Friday's summit is being closely watched for details on how Canada and the European bloc deepen their ties.

Von der Leyen first proposed "opening the door" to Canada last month for what she called an "associate membership" - a status that does not currently exist.

The overture came after Prime Minister Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg, telling EU lawmakers that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".

Carney and many EU member states welcome closer ties, but not all are on board with what to call this new relationship.

Some, like Germany, are questioning the "associate member" term, fearing that Canada is getting preferential treatment ahead of other nations who also want in.

According to reports by multiple news outlets, Germany and other nations successfully lobbied to remove mention of the title in a draft statement ahead of the summit, opting instead for softer language that references an "ever closer association".

Germany's ambassador to Canada, Matthias LÃ¼ttenberg, told CTV News on Tuesday that some member states were "a little surprised" by von der Leyen's announcement last month.

While there is broad support for closer ties, the concept of "associate membership" is something that is not clearly understood as it pertains to Canada, he said.

"Germany has been using the term of associate membership for something completely different, which is the relationship of the EU to Ukraine and potentially Moldova", he said, both of which have been trying to join the bloc for many years.

Despite some opposition, von der Leyen has continued to use the term has not addressed the disagreement over the term.

World.title: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
World.content:
At least two people have been killed and five injured after a rock formation collapsed at a tourist site in Turkey's historical region of Cappadocia, local media is reporting.

One of the rock spires, which are known as fairy chimneys, reportedly disintegrated at the popular open-air museum in the central town of GÃ¶reme.

NevÅehir provincial Governor HÃ¼seyin KÃ¶k said the victims' bodies had been recovered from under the rubble, but the justice minister warned there could be "other potential victims" still trapped.

The cause of Thursday's incident was not immediately known, however local media reported the collapse could have been triggered by heavy rain.

Turkish media reported that the collapse happened near the entrance to the museum - a Unesco World Heritage site - at about 15:15 local time (12:15 GMT).

In a later post on social media, Justice Minister AkÄ±n GÃ¼rlek said that "according to initial assessments, two individuals have lost their lives in the incident, and five others have been injured".

He added that a search and rescue operation was continuing at the site.

The Cappadocia region attracts tourists from around the world, who want to see the ancient fairy chimneys - tall, cone-shaped rock formations that are created by volcanic activity.

World.title: Mbah presents manifesto performance, says Enugu has regained confidence
World.content:
Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, has rendered an account of his manifesto performance to the people of Enugu State, saying his administration had made substantial progress in restoring Enugu’s position as a place where people want to live, work, invest and visit.

Mbah recalled that he presented his manifesto at the same venue in October 2022 ahead of the 2023 governorship election, saying the Manifesto Performance Update was in keeping faith with the Citizens Charter (Executive Order 001), which he executed upon his inauguration on 29 May 2023.

Speaking at the event themed “Our Commitment to Ndi Enugu: The Journey So Far,” which took place at the Peter Mbah Law Auditorium at Godfrey Okoye University, Enugu, on Thursday, Mbah recalled the state of affairs at the time he assumed office and outlined his government’s achievements, development priorities and long-term economic ambitions.

“Think back to May 2023, when we first assumed office. Think about the condition of our state, the difficulties we faced, and the expectations we had.

“There was a time when Monday was no longer an ordinary working day in Enugu. Shops remained closed. Roads were deserted. Parents were afraid to send their children to school. People who depended on their daily earnings had to surrender an entire day’s income because others had decided they should remain indoors. That was the reality we inherited.

“Our roads were in poor condition. Public services had deteriorated. Many schools were struggling to provide the kind of education our children deserved. Our health facilities needed substantial investment. And Enugu, a city that had once been the natural centre of commercial, political and cultural life across the region, was gradually losing that position.

“Businesses were looking elsewhere. Major events were moving to other cities. Our airport had barely two incoming flights a day,” he stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He, however, said his administration had guided the state to significant progress, highlighting achievements in health, education, tourism, agriculture, transportation and other sectors, and their connections to his 2023 campaign promise to eradicate poverty and grow the state’s economy from $4.4 billion to $30 billion.

“Today, people are going about their business with a freedom that had been denied to them for far too long.

“A trader can plan a full working week. Children can attend school. Businesses can receive customers, move goods and keep their employees working. That security gave us a foundation upon which other changes could begin,” he said.

“That is how economic development begins to reach into households and communities.

“The changes are visible, and the scale of our ambition is becoming clearer. We should take pride in what has been achieved, while recognising how much remains to be done,” he maintained.

He urged the people to seize the opportunity of the moment by rallying around him to continue with the task of building a prosperous future for the state.

“This is one moment in the long history of Enugu. This is a moment of extraordinary possibility for our people. And I believe this is the moment we must seize. The work we have begun needs the commitment of all of us.

“I ask you to bring your ideas, your skills, your enterprise and your experience into the life of our state. Take an interest in what is happening in your community. Help us identify problems and develop practical solutions.

“We have the opportunity to leave something of lasting value to those who come after us: a state with stronger institutions, a more productive economy, better opportunities for its children and communities whose people can take pride in what they have achieved together. That is the Enugu I want us to build,” he concluded.

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Godfrey Okoye University, Professor Christian Anieke, recalled that Mbah had presented his manifesto at the same venue in 2022, ahead of the 2023 governorship election, which he subsequently won.

Anieke commended the governor for returning to the university to render an account of his stewardship nearly four years into his administration.

He urged other political leaders entrusted with public office to emulate the practice of returning to the people to explain their performance and account for their promises.

The vice-chancellor said the accomplishments of the Mbah administration were evident and verifiable, arguing that many of the projects and interventions were visible to residents.

The event drew the attendance of a cross-section of the society, including members of the academia, students, civil society organisations, business owners, professional bodies, and media, among others.

World.title: 2027: Peter Obi rolls out plans for Nigeria, challenges Tinubu on borrowing
World.content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has outlined his plans for Nigeria if elected president in the forthcoming general election.

Mr Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, spoke on Thursday evening during the NDC’s Town hall meeting at Amadeo Event Centre in Enugu.

Plans on electricity, insecurity

Mr Obi vowed to solve Nigeria’s electricity crisis by ensuring the generation, transmission and distribution of at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected president in 2027.

The former governor identified electricity as a major priority of his administration if elected, stressing that reliable power supply was necessary to revive industries, create jobs and stimulate economic activities in the country.

“As I promised, we will generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity, because we want industrial work,” he said.

For context, Nigeria’s total available electricity generation is approximately 5,403.3 megawatts, according to September 2026 data from the Transmission Company of Nigeria’s National Control Centre.

The NDC candidate also pledged to address Nigeria’s worsening insecurity, assuring that his administration would take decisive action against the issue in the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“As president of Nigeria, I will unite Nigeria. As president of Nigeria, I will secure Nigeria. We will deal with security,” he assured.

Education, corruption and health

Mr Obi equally pledged to declare emergencies in education and the fight against corruption.

He said he would also ensure access to primary healthcare in every ward across the country.

The former governor argued that Nigeria needs a leader with the competence, capacity, compassion, commitment and character to address its economic and security challenges and restore public confidence in the country’s governance.

“Today, our country is suffering. Today, people are hungry. Today, our children do not have employment. Today, Nigeria is not secure,” he said.

The NDC candidate asked Nigerians to elect a president who can unite the country, secure lives and property, and create an environment for economic growth.

“As president of Nigeria, I will unite Nigeria. As president of Nigeria, I will secure Nigeria. We will deal with insecurity,” he vowed.

Mr Obi further contended that public funds must be deployed for the benefit of citizens, and promised to ensure greater transparency and accountability in government expenditure and borrowing.

“People must stop stealing public money. Public money must be used for public good. That is why I am making my commitment. We will be accountable, we will be open,” he said.

The former governor assured that, under his administration, Nigerians would be informed about the purpose of government borrowing and how borrowed funds were utilised.

The NDC candidate stressed that he would treat education and healthcare seriously to ensure children have access to schooling and that every ward in the country has primary healthcare services.

Obi challenges Tinubu to account for borrowing

President Bola Tinubu recently submitted a letter to the National Assembly requesting a new loan.

The president’s letter sought approval to process external loans worth $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643 under the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.

But at the town hall meeting, Mr Obi challenged Mr Tinubu to campaign across the country and provide details on his administration’s performance since 2023, including how he used the loans he took.

The former governor contended that Nigerians deserve to hear directly from politicians seeking their votes and to evaluate their records and policy proposals before making electoral choices.

The NDC candidate also faulted the president’s foreign travels, demanding explanations on government expenditure.

“We are asking him, please spend at least 36 days and go round Nigeria and tell them what you have been doing for the past three years,” he said.

Mr Obi maintained that presidential candidates should engage Nigerians across the country rather than remain in Abuja and solicit support from voters without sufficient public engagement.

“He must go round Nigeria and tell them what he used nearly $100 billion he borrowed for,” he said.

‘Corruption, criminality and disunity affecting development’

Earlier at the town hall meeting, political economist Pat Utomi urged Nigerians to push for a change in the country’s leadership.

Mr Utomi, a professor, stressed that corruption, criminality and disunity had undermined Nigeria’s development aspirations.

The economist expressed hope that Mr Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, would save Nigeria if elected.

“We come before you to say to you that we have done our research and I know that a combination of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said.

The professor recalled that he celebrated his 60th birthday at the same venue on 6 February and then appealed to Nigerians to make the next year’s anniversary memorable by voting for Messrs Obi and Kwankwaso.

“All that is left is for all of us to ensure that the people come out massively, vote, defend their votes, and a new Nigeria will begin,” he said.

World.title: IOM unveils 25-year migration plan for Nigeria
World.content:
The International Organisation for Migration (IOM) has unveiled a framework to guide Nigeria’s migration policies over the next 25 years, as the United Nations agency marked its silver jubilee in the country.

According to a statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Thursday by the organisation’s National Communications Officer Elijah Elaigwu, the framework, called Migration Vision @25, was unveiled in Abuja.

The event was attended by Borno State Governor Babagana Zulum, the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Bernard Doro, and other government officials and development partners. Vice President Kashim Shettima sent a congratulatory message.

Mr Shettima stated that Nigeria could harness migration to promote economic growth by investing in skills development and creating opportunities for young people at home and abroad.

“Migration is not only a challenge to be managed; it is an opportunity to be harnessed,” he said.

He also called for greater engagement with Nigerians in the diaspora, citing their skills, investments, innovations and international networks as assets for national development.

According to the IOM, the new framework seeks to position Nigeria as a leading African hub for safe and productive migration and a competitive source of skills and talent.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It is built around three pillars: mobility, opportunity and resilience. Its priorities include protecting migrants, expanding regular migration routes, supporting returning migrants to rebuild their lives and finding lasting solutions for communities affected by displacement.

Displacement and migration policy

The initiative comes as Nigeria continues to face widespread displacement caused by conflict, insecurity and climate-related disasters.

Data published by the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) on 1 October put Nigeria’s internally displaced population at 3,679,757. The country also had 141,688 refugees and asylum-seekers, bringing the total number of forcibly displaced people to more than 3.8 million.

Nigeria adopted a National Migration Policy in 2015 to address issues including irregular migration, border management, labour migration, migrants’ rights and diaspora engagement.

Contributing, Mr Doro stated that a revised National Migration Policy and its implementation plan had been approved on 19 August.

The minister explained that the revised policy provides for clearer responsibilities, measurable outcomes and improved migration data to support planning and reintegration.

The statement said environmental degradation and economic pressures were also increasing the vulnerability of affected communities. It noted that irregular migration could expose people to exploitation and other protection risks.

The relationship between the revised national policy and Migration Vision @25, including how the new framework will build on existing commitments, was not detailed in the agency’s announcement.

IOM’s interventions

The IOM noted that it had provided humanitarian assistance to more than 2.5 million people since 2014 and supported nearly 500,000 displaced people with shelter.

It also helped more than 737,000 people access safe drinking water and facilitated the safe and voluntary return of over 72,000 Nigerian migrants.

Through its economic recovery programmes, the agency said it had created or restored more than 75,000 jobs through skills development and start-up support. It had also strengthened more than 2,150 small businesses and trained over 12,700 people in skills linked to market demand.

The agency stated that it had supported six major national migration policies and frameworks in collaboration with the Nigerian government and helped strengthen border management systems at 33 locations across the country.

Looking ahead

The IOM’s Regional Director for West and Central Africa, Sylvia Ekra, said Nigeria could help shape migration across the region by investing in skills, expanding safe migration routes and strengthening cooperation between countries.

The agency’s Chief of Mission in Nigeria, Sharon Dimanche, stated that the anniversary was an opportunity to recognise the resilience of Nigerians and the impact of the organisation’s work.

“Twenty-five years ago, IOM began its journey in Nigeria with just two staff members working from a small office in Lagos,” she said.

Ms Dimanche noted that the agency hoped to help create a future in which fewer people were forced into vulnerable situations, and more had opportunities to thrive.

World.title: APC youth support group urges unity, warns against divisions ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
A support group, the All Progressives Congress (APC) National Young Stakeholders Forum, has urged members of the party’s youth wing to respect internal processes and refrain from actions capable of deepening divisions ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The call comes days after the party’s National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, faced public scrutiny over a video he posted and later deleted showing seven new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado sport utility vehicles (SUVs) reportedly allocated to youth leaders for campaign activities. The development drew reactions amid questions about the resources being deployed for political mobilisation.

The wife of the president, Remi Tinubu, had also disclosed the provision of utility vehicles for APC youth leaders, alongside campaign materials and footwear.

At a press conference in Abuja on Thursday, Shehu Attah, the forum’s National Publicity Secretary, declared the group’s support for Mr Israel and urged party youths to focus on mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election rather than engage in internal disputes.

According to him, the internal disagreements should be resolved through established party channels rather than factional manoeuvres or attempts to establish parallel centres of authority.

Mr Attah said the party’s youth wing must close ranks and focus on mobilising support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election rather than engage in internal disputes.

“We call on all young people in the APC to close ranks and unite behind the National Youth Leader. The need to de-escalate tensions, respect the party’s internal processes, and refrain from actions that could deepen divisions cannot be overemphasised as we head into the thick of the campaign season,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The focus should be on uniting to deliver Mr President’s re-election, not internal warfare!”

The forum warned that political ambitions and personal disagreements should not be allowed to undermine recognised party structures, particularly the office of the National Youth Leader.

Mr Attah said disagreements were inevitable in a large political organisation such as the APC but argued that the party’s ability to manage them through established procedures was essential to maintaining internal cohesion.

He urged members to refer disputes to the appropriate party authorities, warning against statements or actions that could create uncertainty over the legitimacy of the youth leadership.

The forum did not identify the individuals or groups it accused of attempting to undermine Mr Israel’s office.

Forum backs Israel’s leadership

The group passed a vote of confidence in Mr Israel, describing his office as an important link between the party’s leadership and its young members.

Mr Attah said the youth leader had introduced initiatives to engage and equip young party members, including the APC Youth House, the Nest Resource Centre and the Renewed Hope Conversations programme in tertiary institutions.

He also claimed that more than 100 party youths and youth leaders had benefited from overseas training and capacity-building programmes over the past two years.

READ ALSO: APC reacts to court judgement sacking Uzodimma as senatorial candidate

The forum further commended Mr Israel for facilitating campaign mobilisation vehicles for selected youth leaders, as well as the earlier distribution of buses to other party members.

Mr Attah said the initiatives had helped improve morale within the youth wing and demonstrated efforts to address demands for better recognition and rewards for party members.

He said attempts to weaken the youth leadership through factional disputes could discourage young Nigerians seeking inclusion and opportunities within the party.

The forum called on all contending interests to respect the APC’s internal processes and allow its recognised structures to function without undue interference as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Lagos govt threatens to seal illegal boreholes, prosecute operators
World.content:
The Lagos State Government has warned borehole operators to obtain the necessary permits or risk having their facilities sealed and facing prosecution.

The Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission (LASWARCO) said drilling boreholes and extracting groundwater without authorisation could contaminate underground water, cause land subsidence and threaten the state’s water resources.

The warning comes amid concerns over groundwater pollution in Lekki.

In August 2025, the Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services and Water Resources, Mahmood Adegbite, warned that residents in the area could be consuming contaminated water because of inadequate wastewater treatment.

Mr Adegbite, who spoke at a stakeholders’ meeting, called for proper wastewater treatment to prevent further contamination and reduce the risk of waterborne diseases, according to Radio Nigeria Lagos.

Lagos began regulating borehole drilling and groundwater extraction in 2022 to curb pollution and manage its underground water resources.

The then Executive Secretary of LASWARCO, Funke Adepoju, stated that the regulation covered groundwater abstraction, consumption, supply and distribution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In its latest statement posted on Facebook on Thursday, LASWARCO noted that the Lagos State Environmental Management and Protection Law, 2017, empowered it to regulate borehole drilling, groundwater extraction and water supply services.

The commission’s Executive Secretary, Oluwabukola Adeyemo, said anyone intending to drill a borehole or extract groundwater must first obtain the required permits.

“Drilling or abstracting groundwater without LASWARCO authorisation is illegal and punishable under the Law,” Ms Adeyemo said.

She stated that the commission would seal facilities operating without the required authorisation and prosecute offenders.

Ms Adeyemo urged residents and community leaders to report illegal borehole drilling and unauthorised groundwater extraction.

Complaints can be made through LASWARCO’s hotline on 0816 878 2223 or at Block 19, third floor, Lagos State Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja.

World.title: There is no other Stella for Ebola, By Azu Ishiekwene
World.content:
The most expensive thing in Nigeria is not petrol, not food or medicines, not even cement. It is memory loss – an epidemic that has obviously been escalated by screen addiction from its initial default mode of poor record-keeping and absence of institutional diligence.

Nigeria has met Ebola again. Not with the terror of 2014 – which has all but been forgotten – when a Liberian-American named Patrick Sawyer walked into Lagos carrying a virus and a stubborn disregard for other people’s lives.

This time, it’s with a quieter, more bureaucratic alarm – an imported case in Abuja, not from the West but from the east coast of Africa. A 42-year-old woman reportedly arrived from Uganda, developed symptoms four days later, sought care at a private hospital, and tested positive for the Bundibugyo (Ugandan) strain on 20 October.

Ebola, this Time

The good news is that the patient has been evacuated, is in isolation and is receiving care. The bad news is that Nigerians have a special talent for treating preparedness like aso-ebi: impressive on D-day and impossible to find at the next occasion.

Twelve years ago, Ebola taught Nigeria a lesson written in the blood of health workers. It also gave us Dr. Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, the physician whose refusal to let a highly infectious patient leave helped stop an epidemic before it became a national catastrophe. She paid with her life. Nigeria does not need another such invoice.

The current case reads like a travel itinerary. According to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), the patient returned to Abuja from Uganda through Addis Ababa on 3 October. She developed symptoms on 7 October, was admitted to a private health facility on 11 October, and the NCDC was notified on 19 October. Laboratory confirmation came on 20 October.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Follow the Timeline

That timeline deserves attention. There were 17 days between the index case arriving in Abuja and confirmation, and 12 days between symptom onset and notification. In infectious-disease terms, that is not a gap. It is a corridor.

Ebola is not malaria. It does not announce itself with a neon sign. Early symptoms such as fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, and sore throat can masquerade as ordinary ailments that Nigerians treat with paracetamol, prayer, pepper soup, and the national motto: “It is well.”

By 25 October, the NCDC said 53 contacts had been identified and were being monitored. On 26 October, the patient and her husband were medically evacuated to Switzerland, where she is receiving specialised care.

Once Upon a Sawyer

On 20 July, 2014, Sawyer, a Liberian government official, flew from Monrovia to Lagos via Lomé. He was infected with the Zaire strain of Ebola, the deadliest of the species. He collapsed at the airport and was taken to First Consultants Medical Centre in Obalende, where Dr Adadevoh and some of her colleagues took the bullet that could have turned Lagos into an Ebola graveyard.

Sawyer, by several accounts, wanted to leave the hospital. He reportedly resisted isolation. In a country where “the customer is always right” has been elevated to a theology, Adadevoh did something – she disagreed with the customer.

She and her team kept him in the hospital, alerted the authorities, and began the difficult work of containment. Sawyer died on 24 July, 2014. Adadevoh tested positive for the virus on 4 August, while caring for him and died on 19 August, 2014, aged 57.

The Toll

Nigeria eventually recorded 20 Ebola cases and eight deaths in that outbreak. It was declared Ebola-free on 20 October, 2014, barely three months after Sawyer’s arrival. The world called it a success. Nigerians called it a miracle. Both descriptions were true, but neither should obscure the cost: eight people died, including heroic health workers, because one man’s illness met one doctor’s courage.

There is a temptation to reduce Adadevoh’s story to inspiration. Nigerians love inspiration; it is cheaper than infrastructure.

But inspiration is not a substitute for systems. Adadevoh’s heroism was effective because it was eventually supported by contact tracing, laboratory capacity, isolation, communication, and coordination.

The Ebola Emergency Operations Centre, established during that response, became a model praised internationally. It showed that Nigeria could organise when it chose to. Nigeria showed that capacity again with COVID-19 when even first-world countries were confounded.

Forgetfulness Meets Tragedy

That is where forgetfulness meets tragedy. Nigeria does not lack competence. It lacks consistency. We can mobilise brilliantly for a crisis, then dismantle the machinery once the cameras leave. We build emergency operations centres with the urgency of a man whose house is on fire, only to let them gather dust until the next fire.

The 2026 case is a test of institutional memory. Do we still have the laboratories, the trained personnel, the isolation capacity, the surveillance network, the community trust and the political will that carried us through 2014 and COVID-19?

The fact that the NCDC was notified on 19 October, eight days after admission, suggests the system eventually worked. Every day of delay expands the contact list, deepens anxiety and increases the burden on already stretched health workers.

What’s Different?

In 2014, Nigerians received text messages recommending bathing with salt water at dawn. Grown men and women, including some who could operate complex businesses and quote economic statistics, obediently scrubbed themselves with salt. It did not kill Ebola. It did, however, reportedly cause injuries and deaths from excessive salt consumption.

The lesson was simple: panic is also a public-health hazard. Fear makes people hide symptoms, avoid hospitals, blame outsiders and embrace dangerous remedies.

If Dr Adadevoh could speak today, she would probably not ask for statues. She would ask practical questions: Where are the isolation beds, gloves, gowns, face shields? Are oxygen supplies available, not “available on request,” which in Nigerian English means unavailable? Are health workers trained and insured? Is there a functioning referral system from private clinics to public isolation centres? Are contact tracers properly equipped? Is there a single, credible source of information rather than twelve competing WhatsApp broadcasts?

Emergency Love

Nigeria’s political class loves emergencies. An emergency provides photo-ops, special committees, presidential directives and the dizzying grammar of “stakeholders.” One more thing: emergencies are also pipelines for big money, and cash out. Prevention, by contrast, is boring. It involves maintenance, training, data, procurement and accountability.

Perhaps it is instructive that Ebola has visited Nigeria in campaign season, when politicians remember that power resides with voters and move from town to city to village telling deadly lies like the Ebola virus. It will be easier to trace political lies in this season, when politicians are at their mobile best, than to trace a virus.

In Memory of Adadevoh

But the truest memorial to Adadevoh is not a plaque. It is a health system in which no doctor has to choose between personal safety and public duty. It is a country where a suspected case is reported within hours, not days. It is an isolation centre that works before the emergency, not one hastily converted from a conference hall after the first alarm.

Adadevoh stepped on a virus on our behalf. Twelve years later, Ebola has returned with a different strain, a different city and a different patient. The virus has changed its address. The question is whether Nigeria has changed its habits.

Azu Ishiekwene is Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book,Writing for Media and Monetising It.

World.title: ‘No retiree will be forgotten’ — Tinubu promises pension reforms
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to implement a long-delayed minimum pension guarantee and expand healthcare support for retirees, saying his administration is determined to ensure that Nigerians who served the country are not abandoned after retirement.

Mr Tinubu made the commitment on Thursday at the National Pension Conference and Awards, held at Transcorp Hilton, Abuja, as part of the maiden National Pension Week 2026.

Represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, the president said pension security was a national obligation and that his administration was determined to improve the welfare of retirees.

“A pension is not a favour granted by Government. It is a wage earned, deferred and held in trust. It is a promise. And this Administration has resolved that the promise will be kept,” he said.

He said his administration was working to address outstanding pension obligations and improve retirees’ welfare through measures intended to strengthen the Contributory Pension Scheme.

The measures include implementing the Minimum Pension Guarantee under the Pension Reform Act 2014 and expanding PenCare, a healthcare support programme for eligible retirees.

“Since enactment, that promise has never been honoured. Under President Tinubu, it will be,” Mr Akume said, conveying the president’s commitment to implementing the minimum guarantee.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The president also reiterated his administration’s commitment to the N758 billion Federal Government Pension Bond, which was approved to settle outstanding accrued pension rights and strengthen the Pension Protection Fund.

“That was not an accounting exercise. It was an act of restitution to Nigerians who served their country and were made to wait for what they had earned,” Mr Akume said on behalf of the president.

The president said pension security should be treated as a government responsibility rather than a discretionary benefit for retired workers.

“Above all, no Nigerian who has served this nation will be forgotten in retirement. Nigeria will keep faith with those who kept faith with Nigeria.”

Minimum pension guarantee, healthcare support

The proposed Minimum Pension Guarantee is intended to provide a safety net for eligible retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme whose retirement income is inadequate.

Although the Pension Reform Act 2014 provides for the guarantee, the minimum amount payable and the detailed implementation arrangements will depend on the relevant guidelines from the National Pension Commission (PenCom).

The president also highlighted PenCare, a healthcare support programme intended to improve access to essential medical services for low-income retirees.

The initiative is designed to extend retirement support beyond pension payments by helping eligible beneficiaries access healthcare services.

PenCom has begun rolling out PenCare, with an initial phase targeting 30,000 retirees. The programme is funded jointly by the commission and participating pension fund operators.

According to the president, the initiative reflected a broader approach to retirement welfare, judging the pension system not only by the savings contributors accumulate but also by the security and dignity those savings provide in retirement.

He urged relevant institutions to ensure that the measures produced tangible improvements in pensioners’ lives.

Pension assets rise, but concerns persist

The Director-General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, said Nigeria’s pension assets rose from N20.79 trillion in July 2024 to N31.8 trillion in August 2026.

The N11.01 trillion increase represents about a 53 per cent growth over the period.

However, she said the expansion of pension assets had not translated into adequate retirement income for many contributors, particularly private-sector workers.

“Almost 70 per cent of private sector employees earn below the national minimum wage in retirement. More than 55 per cent of all retirees whose pensions fall below the minimum wage come from the private sector,” she said.

Ms Oloworaran attributed the problem partly to employers calculating pension contributions on limited portions of workers’ earnings rather than their full remuneration.

She said the statutory combined pension contribution of 18 per cent comprises 10 per cent from employers and eight per cent from employees, warning that inadequate pensionable earnings could weaken retirement benefits.

“Our private sector workers are retiring into poverty. This must change,” she said.

The PenCom chief urged private employers to contribute to the Pension Protection Fund alongside the Federal Government and pension industry operators.

She also challenged pension fund administrators to generate returns that exceed inflation, which continues to erode the purchasing power of retirement savings.

“Beating inflation is not an aspiration. It is your job,” she said.

Ms Oloworaran disclosed that the commission had secured commitments from pension industry operators to establish three million additional funded, active Retirement Savings Accounts within the next year. The target is intended to extend coverage to workers currently excluded from formal pension arrangements.

She also announced that President Tinubu would launch the Pension Security Initiative on 10 November, incorporating PenCare and the minimum pension guarantee.

The commission further directed pension fund administrators and custodians to complete their recapitalisation by 30 June 2027.

“Every pension fund administrator and custodian must complete recapitalisation by 30th June 2027. We are not changing our minds,” she said.

Highlighting recent improvements, Ms Oloworaran said some federal retirees had received pension increases ranging from 67 to 120 per cent, while certain Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund pensioners recorded increases exceeding 1,000 per cent.

She added that retired professors could now receive pensions equivalent to their final salaries, while some retirement benefits were being processed within 48 hours.

The commission also announced an exit benefit scheme for retirees from treasury-funded federal ministries, departments and agencies, with symbolic cheques presented at the event.

Tinubu warns against risky investments

President Tinubu warned pension fund administrators and custodians against exposing workers’ retirement savings to reckless investments, insisting that the pursuit of higher returns or national development must not compromise contributors’ financial security.

He said pension assets must be managed with transparency, accountability and strict risk-management standards.

Although pension savings could support infrastructure development and economic growth, he said investment decisions must prioritise the interests of the workers whose contributions make up the funds.

“National development must never come at the expense of pensioners. Every investment must stand on its own merits, pass rigorous tests of risk and return, and serve the best interests of contributors,” he said.

The president warned that inflation was weakening the purchasing power of retirement savings, making it necessary for pension operators to deliver sustainable returns without compromising capital preservation.

“Preservation without growth is a slow erosion. Retirement savings that fail to keep pace with inflation quietly betray the very people who saved them,” he said.

He urged pension fund administrators and custodians to strengthen their investment expertise, diversify portfolios responsibly, reduce operating costs and improve accountability.

According to him, the pension industry’s performance should be measured by the financial security it delivers to retirees rather than the volume of assets under management.

The president also called on PenCom to enforce pension regulations firmly and fairly, while urging public and private-sector employers to remit pension contributions fully and promptly.

He described the deduction of workers’ pension contributions without transferring the money to their Retirement Savings Accounts as a breach of trust.

The president further called on state governments, organised labour and other stakeholders to expand pension coverage, including among traders, artisans, farmers, transport operators and other self-employed Nigerians.

He said the government would promote the Personal Pension Plan and new distribution channels to make retirement savings more accessible to people outside conventional salaried employment.

“Pensions for All must mean exactly that: all,” he said.

He urged stakeholders to ensure the summit produced measurable commitments, including increased enrolment, faster benefit payments, improved investment performance and clearer disclosure of pension fund activities.

National Assembly reviews pension laws

Meanwhile, the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Pensions, Jallo Mohammed, said the National Assembly was reviewing the Pension Reform Act 2014 and other pension-related legislation.

He said proposed amendments, including legislation concerning intelligence and military pensions, were progressing through legislative consideration ahead of public hearings.

Mr Mohammed also disclosed ongoing engagement with NNPC Pension Fund Limited over compliance with PenCom directives following years of regulatory concerns.

He pledged continued legislative oversight to improve pension administration, strengthen regulatory compliance and protect contributors’ retirement savings.

“Our shared objective must be to build a pension industry that not only protects the savings of today’s workers, but also guarantees greater financial security and dignity for future generations of retirees,” he said.

Background

Nigeria’s Contributory Pension Scheme was established under the Pension Reform Act 2004 and subsequently governed by the Pension Reform Act 2014. The framework requires employers and employees in covered employment to contribute towards retirement savings, with pension fund operators managing the accumulated funds under regulatory oversight.

The scheme was introduced to address weaknesses associated with previous pension arrangements, including delays in benefit payments and the accumulation of unfunded liabilities.

However, some retirees have continued to face inadequate pension payments, delays in receiving accrued rights and difficulties meeting healthcare costs after leaving employment.

In October, PenCom announced that the Federal Government’s pension intervention had been used to clear inherited accrued pension liabilities dating back to 2007, with the commission reporting that 957,045 beneficiaries had been covered.

The commission has also identified the Minimum Pension Guarantee and PenCare as measures intended to improve the financial security and welfare of retirees.

President Tinubu said the success of the reforms should ultimately be measured by their effect on pensioners’ lives.

“The true measure of our success will not be how much money the system holds. It will be how much security, and how much dignity, it delivers,” he said.

World.title: GYMFEST: Organisers hail increased participation, target international breakthrough
World.content:
The third edition of GYMFEST Championship will hold in Lagos on 7 November, with 278 young gymnasts expected to showcase their skills as organisers intensify efforts to develop grassroots talent and improve Nigeria’s prospects in international gymnastics.

The event, organised by Tee Tumblers Gymnastics Club (TTGC) in collaboration with the Society of the Performing Arts in Nigeria (SPAN), will take place at The Dome, 1 Freedom Way, Lekki Phase 1, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.

Yoyin Akpose, co-convener of the championship and founder of Tee Tumblers Gymnastics Club, said participation had increased from fewer than 100 children at the inaugural edition to 278 registered participants this year.

“At some point, we have to tell some schools, please wait until next year. We don’t have the capacity for any more this year, but it’s encouraging to see that parents are interested now and the community keeps growing,” she said at a press conference in Lagos.

Mrs Akpose said the competition was established to provide children with opportunities to showcase their abilities, develop their skills and gain experience in competitive gymnastics.
