She expressed confidence that sustained grassroots development could help Nigeria produce gymnasts capable of competing internationally.

“I know, we do have the talent, so that’s why I have the drive and the motivation to keep pushing because I feel like I know we will get there,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Organisers seek international breakthrough

Mrs Akpose said her determination to promote gymnastics was reinforced by watching an international competition last week, where she was disappointed by the limited representation from Nigeria and West Africa.

She said the experience strengthened her resolve to create opportunities for young Nigerians to develop their abilities and compete at the highest level.

Gymnastics remains a developing sport in Nigeria, and GYMFEST seeks to encourage more schools and clubs to participate while increasing awareness of its competitive and developmental benefits.

Oluremi Jemitola, chief operating officer of SPAN, said the championship was established through the vision of the organisation’s founder and chairperson, Sarah Boulos, to promote healthier, more confident communities through movement, creativity and the performing arts.

She said the partnership between SPAN and Tee Tumblers, which began three years ago, had strengthened the competition’s technical capacity and contributed to its growth.

“Today, we are proud to say that, together, we have built and continue to grow what we aspire to be Nigeria’s biggest gymnastics competition,” Mrs Jemitola said.

She added that the organisers hoped to establish GYMFEST as Africa’s leading gymnastics festival and competition, with global recognition as a long-term ambition.

According to her, the championship goes beyond sporting performances by helping children develop confidence, discipline, teamwork and perseverance. It also provides an opportunity for parents to celebrate their children’s progress and coaches to receive recognition for their contributions.

Lagos Commission backs grassroots development

Oluyomi Olusanmi, director of school sports at the Lagos State Sports Commission, commended the organisers for providing opportunities for children to participate in organised sporting activities.

Representing the commission at the press conference, Ms Olusanmi said the initiative aligned with Lagos State’s development agenda, particularly its focus on youth engagement and children’s overall development.

She explained that sports helped develop children’s cognitive, affective and psychomotor skills, contributing to their intellectual, social and physical growth.

Ms Olusanmi added that participation in sports could provide career opportunities and help address social challenges, including truancy, juvenile delinquency and negative peer pressure.

She said the championship supported the commission’s vision of making Lagos a leading sports destination in Africa.

The organisers said their partnership with the commission would help expand gymnastics participation beyond Lagos and contribute to the sport’s development across Nigeria.

Sponsors support championship

The organisers acknowledged the support of ProvidusUnity Bank, the diamond partner, alongside Banksome Group, Leadway Assurance, YD Company, Studio24, Indomie and Gratia Chin Chin.

They said the partners had contributed financially and supported efforts to ensure the event’s success.

The festival will also feature the GYMFEST Souk, where vendors will sell food, pastries, clothing, gymnastics attire and other products. A children’s play area catering to different age groups will provide additional activities for families.

The organisers said the championship would allow participants to demonstrate skills developed through months of training while encouraging more children to embrace gymnastics.

World.title: 2027: Utomi, Ohaa, Yesufu urge Nigerians to mobilise support for Obi
World.content:
Peter Obi

Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027.

The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters.

Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges.

He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity.

According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change.

“We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said.

Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means.

In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance.

He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones.

According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development.

“My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said.

Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians.

He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections.

Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process.

She said the election was not merely about Obi’s presidential ambition but about the collective responsibility of Nigerians to rescue the country from its numerous challenges.

According to her, the election is not about Obi but about every one of us, as the mistake we made in 1999 must be corrected.

“The class of 1999 has destroyed this country. The class of 2027 must fix this country.

“We must take this election as our own election. Mr Peter Obi and his running mate have one business, and that is to be on the ballot paper.You and I must do the remaining work to ensure victory,” she said.

Yesufu challenged every supporter to mobilise at least 20 eligible voters for Obi, stressing that political change required collective action rather than depending solely on candidates.

The activist also urged Nigerians to demonstrate courage and determination in protecting their votes during the elections, saying that Nigerians must reject political intimidation and insist on credible elections that reflect the will of the people.

Earlier, the NDC Chairman in Enugu State, Mr Ibuchukwu Obetta, welcomed Obi, Kwankwaso and other party leaders to the state, describing their visit as a significant moment in the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections.

Obetta said the visit had renewed the confidence of party members and strengthened their determination to work for a Nigeria founded on integrity, accountability, competence, justice and inclusive development.

(NAN)

World.title: I’ll work closely with Kwankwaso if elected, Obi reassures
World.content:
The NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, (BBC)

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has reiterated willingness to work closely with his vice-presidential candidate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to move the country forward.

Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during a town hall meeting in Enugu, where he engaged supporters and stakeholders on the country’s challenges and his vision for national development.

The former Anambra State governor said they would work together to tackle insecurity and restore safety across Nigeria if elected president in 2027.

He said that securing lives and property would be a priority of his administration, promising to confront the security challenges threatening communities and livelihoods across the country.

The presidential candidate regretted that the current administration had failed to protect the lives and property of Nigerians, which he maintained was the primary responsibility.

Obi assured voters in the South East to vote for him because of his competence and ability to tackle challenges facing the nation.

He challenged other presidential candidates to meet and discuss their plans, and warned the people not to be deceived by rhetoric and propaganda.

On education, Obi said he would declare a state of emergency on education to enable his administration to tackle the issue of out-of-school children head-on, hinting that Nigerian children deserved quality education.

In his remarks, the vice-presidential candidate of NDC, Kwankwaso, advised that nobody should be deceived by ethnicity, saying, “It’s obvious that Nigerians are going through numerous difficulties”.

Kwankwaso lamented that people were facing challenges like insecurity, unemployment, poverty, hunger and so many other challenges.

He explained that the only solution to achieve a new Nigeria was unity, diligence, perseverance and willingness.

He urged Nigerians to come out en masse to cast, protect and follow up on their votes until results were announced, noting that it was not a one-man show but a collective responsibility.

Also, Sen Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly, described Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso, as the “best presidential ticket” to lead Nigeria.

Umeh expressed confidence that the South-East would rally behind Obi in the 2027 presidential election, urging the people to remain resolute and resist attempts to intimidate or discourage them from pursuing their political choice.

He also commended the resilience of supporters who, according to him, ensured that the meeting held despite reported attempts to frustrate the gathering.

The senator further praised Kwankwaso for his efforts to build support in Northern Nigeria, expressing optimism that the Obi-led ticket could attract votes across the country.

Umeh urged the people of the South-East to use their votes to make a strong political statement in 2027, declaring his support for Obi’s presidential ambition and calling on the region to unite behind the project.

(NAN)

World.title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
World.content:
San Siro

Inter and AC Milan unveiled their new “Generali Stadium” Thursday, which will replace the iconic San Siro stadium from the 2031/32 season.

It will be shaped “low in the body, and it rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said during a press conference in Milan.

The design aims to bring spectators as close to the pitch as possible, with the stands behind the goals set at a steep 37-degree incline, said David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project.

“The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling,” he said.

“It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling, and everything that we needed to do here was to carry it into the (new) building”.

Manica said the design team “started with proximity”.

“We brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass,” he said.

They also paid great attention to acoustics: the roof covers the stands, leaving only the pitch exposed, and is designed to “amplify the roar” of the fans, Manica said.

“This building is steeper than many other new buildings are built today, and that’s intentional, because it allows us to bring those seats up and over the field as much as possible, and create that sense of intimacy and atmosphere,” he said.

The stadium, sponsored by the Italian insurance giant Generali, will also be capable of hosting American football games, rugby matches and concerts.

“I want the crowd to come to the new stadium and to feel that excitement that they felt before, and to feel the building, living and breathing with them as it does currently,” Manica said.

AC Milan and Inter paid 197 million euros ($219 million) to acquire the current stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they intend to build their new, shared home.

The project for the new San Siro — which will have a capacity of 71,500 seats, compared to the current 75,000 — will cost the two clubs 1.2 billion euros.

Construction is set to begin in 2028.

Foster and Manica previously worked together on London’s Wembley Stadium.

Milan’s current stadium — one of the most iconic in European football and often likened to a “concrete cathedral” — is the largest in Italy.

But the venue, which opened in 1926, no longer meets the needs of spectators or the clubs, despite undergoing several renovations over the decades.

San Siro, also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, will be largely demolished once construction work on the new stadium nears completion.

World.title: 2027: INEC grants provisional clearance to Pantami, Gwarzo – Source
World.content:
Pantami

By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe

There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections.

The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night.

In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night.

INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections.

The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome.

The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29.

Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again.

His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time.

Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027.

The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates.

World.title: ‘Star Trek’, ‘X-Men’ star Patrick Stewart dies at 86
World.content:
(FILES) English actor Sir Patrick Stewart poses during a photo call at Dubai International Film Festival in Dubai on December 8, 2017. Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through “Star Trek” and the “X-Men” franchises has died, an official statement said on October 29. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said. (Photo by PATRICK BAZ / AFP)

Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at the age of 86, an official statement said Thursday.

“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said.

The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before crossing the Atlantic to enjoy an acclaimed career on the US stage and screen.

His best known Hollywood roles were as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films.

“His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said.

“He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.”

AFP

World.title: Troops neutralise two high-profile ISWAP leaders, others in Borno
World.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

The troops of Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have killed 15 Boko Haram terrorists, including two (2) prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira in Kerenoa, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State.

This is as the Theatre Commander of OPHK, Major General Ibikunle Ajose on Thursday commissioned the newly constructed three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri.

The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s one year in office, which also reflects his commitment to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness.

In a press statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni on Thursday said: “Troops of OPHK continued to record operational successes through sustained intelligence-led offensive operations aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities and dismantling their networks across the theatre.

“In a further operation, OPHK air assets, at about 9:20 pm on 28 October 2026, conducted an armed reconnaissance and air interdiction mission in the Kerenoa Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, resulting in the neutralisation of 15 terrorists and the destruction of an IED hideout.

“The mission followed intelligence reports on terrorist activities in the area. During the operation, the air assets tracked two terrorists on a motorcycle to a makeshift structure beneath a tree. Further surveillance revealed additional movements around the location, indicating the presence of other terrorists. Consequently, the location was engaged with precision strikes.

“Following the strikes, Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) indicated that 15 terrorists were neutralised, while structures at the location were destroyed. Additionally, a secondary fire observed after the engagement suggested that the targeted structure may have been used for the storage of terrorist IED logistics hub.

“It has been confirmed that 2 prominent ISWAP Qayids, Abu Musanna and Hassan Abu Huraira were amongst those neutralised while several other fighters were severely wounded, including the Wali (ISWAP Governor) of the area who is reported to be critically injured.

“The operation forms part of OPHK’s sustained intelligence-led air offensive aimed at degrading terrorist capabilities, disrupting their hideouts and dismantling logistics networks across the theatre. The Joint Task Force continues to conduct coordinated operations against terrorist elements in the North East to achieve its Operational mandate of restoring total and long-lasting peace in the region,” Goni stated.

Meanwhile, the Nigerian Army has reaffirmed its commitment to personnel welfare with the commissioning of three blocks of 12-family Corporals and Below Quarters (CBQ) at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri. The commissioning reflects the commitment of the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu NAM, to improving troops’ living conditions, strengthening morale and enhancing operational effectiveness. The commissioning forms part of activities to commemorate the COAS one year in office.

The COAS was represented at the ceremony by the Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force (North East) Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), Major General Ibikunle Ajose, on Thursday, 29 October 2026, at Maimalari Cantonment, Maiduguri.

Delivering the COAS’ remarks, Major General Ajose stated that decent accommodation and a conducive living environment were essential to sustaining troops’ morale, discipline and effectiveness.

He emphasised that operational excellence on the battlefield must be supported by adequate welfare provisions and a strong administrative foundation at home.

He described investments in accommodation as investments in human capital and a practical demonstration of the Nigerian Army’s appreciation of personnel’s sacrifices and contributions to national security.

The COAS expressed profound appreciation to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, for his continued support to the Nigerian Army, particularly in force development and personnel welfare. He also acknowledged the contributions of relevant departments and directorates, contractors, project supervisors and other stakeholders whose efforts supported the execution of the projects, noting that sustained institutional support remains vital to the Army’s transformation and operational effectiveness.

The COAS charged beneficiary personnel and their commanders to maintain a strong culture of discipline, accountability and proper maintenance to preserve the facilities for long-term use. The commissioning reinforces the Nigerian Army’s Soldiers First Concept, which places the welfare, wellbeing and professional development of personnel at the centre of its institutional priorities and recognises their importance to sustained morale, operational readiness and effective service to the nation.

Beyond the quarters commissioned, several other projects are ongoing at Maimalari Cantonment to improve living and working conditions. These include additional Corporals and Below Quarters, the drilling of two boreholes, construction of a 50-bed ward for 7 Division Medical Services and Hospital, a new Headquarters 7 Division complex, Senior Officers’ Quarters and the renovation of existing family accommodation.

These interventions reflect broader efforts to strengthen military infrastructure and provide personnel and their families with improved housing, healthcare and essential facilities.

In his welcome address, the Acting General Officer Commanding 7 Division and Commander Sector 1 OPHK, Brigadier General Solomon Diwa, described the commissioning as another significant milestone in the Army’s welfare initiatives. He noted that Corporals and Below constitute a vital component of the Army’s fighting strength and perform indispensable roles at the tactical level. He stressed that providing them with decent accommodation demonstrates the Army’s recognition of their service and sacrifices while reinforcing the connection between personnel welfare, high morale and combat readiness. Similarly, the Acting GOC urged occupants to uphold high standards of cleanliness, take ownership of the quarters and ensure their responsible use.

In his project description, the Commander, 47 Engineer Brigade, Brigadier General Abubakar Saleh, disclosed that the renovation was awarded to Messrs Ammah Contractors Limited by the Office of the Chief of Army Staff, Directorate of Procurement. He explained that following a site assessment, six blocks of six-family Corporals and Below Quarters, comprising 36 two-bedroom flats, were selected for renovation as suitable alternatives to the originally designated structures. He noted that the buildings were previously in a severely dilapidated condition, with leaking roofs, structural cracks and damaged floors. The renovation involved extensive structural rehabilitation, including the introduction of columns and beams, repairs to damaged floor slabs and masonry, replacement of roofing sheets, doors and windows, and complete electrical and plumbing installations.

He added that 47 Engineer Brigade supervised the project under the guidance of Headquarters 7 Division to ensure compliance with approved specifications and quality standards.

While delivering the vote of thanks on behalf of the beneficiaries, Warrant Officer Ogunmodede Sunday expressed his sincere appreciation to the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, NAM, for prioritising personnel welfare through the Soldiers First Concept. He also thanked the Theatre Commander for his leadership and for representing the COAS at the occasion. He noted that the renovated quarters and other ongoing infrastructure projects demonstrate the Nigerian Army’s commitment to improving personnel welfare and living conditions. He pledged that the beneficiaries would maintain the facilities responsibly and reciprocate the gesture through discipline, professionalism and dedication to duty.

He concluded by appreciating the project supervisors, contractors and everyone who contributed to the success of the project, while praying for God’s continued protection of troops, blessings upon their families and lasting peace and security for Nigeria.

World.title: Just In: Tinubu lands in Saudi Arabia for Umrah
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday evening arrived in Saudi Arabia, landing at the King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah.

He was received by Nigeria’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Saudi head of royal protocol Ahmad bin Thafir.

The President is scheduled to perform Umrah, also known as the lesser hajj, and is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the religious exercise.

Thursday’s trip marks the second time Tinubu has travelled to Makkah to perform Umrah since assuming office on May 29, 2023.

President Tinubu visited the holy city in November 2023, shortly after attending the Saudi-African Summit in Riyadh, where he also prayed for divine guidance in leading Nigeria.

The latest trip is part of a series of foreign engagements undertaken by Tinubu since becoming president. He has visited more than 30 countries in over 50 unique and recurring trips.

World.title: Germany’s Zverev becomes tennis world No. 1
World.content:
Germany’s Alexander Zverev poses after his match against Netherland’s Tallon Griekspoor (not pictured) at the Erste Bank Open 2026 ATP 500 tennis tournament in Vienna, Austria, on October 29, 2026. Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on October 29, 2026 as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open. The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital. (Photo by HELMUT FOHRINGER / APA / AFP) / Austria OUT

Alexander Zverev accelerated his ascension to number one in the world rankings for the first time in his career on Thursday as he beat Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 to reach the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open.

The 29-year-old German was already assured of finishing the season top of the ATP rankings but, in the absence of current incumbent Jannik Sinner, two-time Grand Slam champion Zverev will now take that crown in next week’s updated standings after winning his opening two matches in the Austrian capital.

Long seen as tennis’ nearly-man, Zverev has enjoyed a stellar 2026, breaking his major duck by picking up the titles at the French and US Opens.

Now he has broken further ground by becoming only the 30th man to claim top spot since the rankings were first published in 1973.

He will be aged 29 years and 196 days when Monday’s new rankings are published, making him the second-oldest first-time number one after Australian John Newcombe.

Due to a knee injury Italy’s Sinner decided to end his season at the start of October, opening the way for Zverev to dethrone him.

And the big-serving Hamburg native ensured he did just that ahead of the season-ending ATP Finals next month by seeing off Martin Landaluce and Griekspoor in his opening two matches in Vienna.

Zverev needed to save four match points against Spain’s Landaluce in his first-round match on Tuesday, but was much more comfortable as he defeated Griekspoor in straight sets to write his name into the history books.

He raced out of the blocks on Thursday, breaking the 30-year-old Dutchman in the very first game and then confidently serving his way into a one-set lead.

The second frame went to 5-5 before Zverev pounced on Griekspoor’s serve to get his nose in front.

The match met an unexpected stoppage as Zverev brought up match point when a smash off the German’s racquet caused part of the electronic board behind Griekspoor to malfunction.

But once the umpire covered the problematic panel up with a towel, Zverev then sealed his new ranking with an unreturnable serve.

World.title: FG Inaugurates Committee to Review National Security Strategy 2026
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Federal Government on Thursday inaugurated a 33 member committee to review the 2019 National Security Strategy and develop a new framework for addressing emerging security threats.

Speaking at the inauguration ceremony in Abuja, the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, urged the committee members to produce a comprehensive, realistic and actionable document that reflects the country’s changing security environment.

Represented by the committee chairman, Major General Sarkin Bello (Rtd.), the NSA said Nigeria’s domestic, regional and global security landscapes had changed significantly since the last review in 2019, necessitating a reassessment of the country’s security priorities.

“Our national security landscape is undergoing rapid and profound transformations. Since the last review of our strategy in 2019, the domestic, regional and global security environments have changed dramatically in intensity,” he said.

Ribadu identified terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, cyber threats, misinformation, economic challenges, food insecurity and environmental problems as some of the threats the new strategy must address.

Against this backdrop, he said the National Security Strategy 2026 would provide an overarching framework for coordinating national security, resilience and sustainable development.

“The National Security Strategy 2026 will serve as an overarching compass for coordinating national security, resilience and sustainable development for Nigeria. It must reflect our current realities, anticipate future disruptions and directly support the realisation of our national objectives amid the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly in the areas of human security, economic transformation and national cohesion,” Ribadu said.

He further urged committee members to engage relevant institutions and stakeholders in developing a strategy that could be effectively implemented.

“Engage robustly with our resource institutions and strategic stakeholders to produce a comprehensive, realistic and actionable document. Nigeria demands a strategy that is realistic and implementable,” he said.

To facilitate the process, Ribadu said the Office of the National Security Adviser would provide the necessary administrative, technical and logistical support to ensure the successful completion of the assignment.

In his acceptance remarks, the committee’s deputy chairman, Major General Emeka Onumajuru (Rtd.), highlighted the evolving nature of security threats, stressing the need for a comprehensive strategic realignment.

He noted that conventional security challenges, including terrorism, insurgency and banditry, had become increasingly intertwined with non-kinetic threats such as cyber vulnerabilities, economic challenges, food insecurity and climate change.

Emphasising the need for a forward-looking approach, Onumajuru said the new strategy must go beyond reactive measures to address the country’s complex security challenges.

“To address these complexities, our nation requires an overarching framework that moves beyond reactive measures. The National Security Strategy 2026 must be an inclusive, forward-looking and highly actionable blueprint,” he said.

He added that the committee would consult resource institutions, private-sector representatives and traditional leaders to ensure that the strategy reflected a broad range of national security concerns.

Major General Onumajuru also disclosed that the committee had four weeks to submit its final draft to the NSA, describing the timeline as demanding.

“Our timeline is quite unyielding. We have exactly four weeks from today to submit our final draft copies to the National Security Adviser. So, it demands immediate, focused momentum,” he said.

The committee is chaired by Major General Bello (Rtd.) and comprises representatives of government ministries, the Armed Forces, intelligence agencies, law enforcement bodies, civil society organisations and academia.

Other institutions represented on the committee include the Defence Headquarters, the Nigerian Army, Navy and Air Force, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services, the National Intelligence Agency, the Defence Intelligence Agency and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission.

World.title: First Lady Unveils N110m Empowerment Scheme For Elderly, PWDs In All 109 Senatorial Districts
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, on Thursday unveiled her pet project, the Renewed Hope Initiative’s (RHI’s) N110 million empowerment package for elderly citizens and persons with disabilities in all the 109 senatorial districts nationwide.

She has, therefore, urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidates to oversee its implementation and ensure the funds reach vulnerable Nigerians.

The initiative, comprises two programs, each with a N55 million allocation, targeting 250 beneficiaries apiece.

Under the RHI Economic Empowerment Program for Persons with Disabilities, 250 beneficiaries are expected to receive N200,000 each per senatorial district.

The RHI Elderly Support Scheme will follow the same funding structure, with 250 elderly beneficiaries receiving N200,000 each per senatorial district.

Mrs Tinubu announced this at a stakeholders’ meeting attended by the APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda; Senate President, Godswill Akpabio; other APC members of the Senate, members of the RHI Governing Board and APC senatorial candidates.

The First Lady said the decision to work through the senatorial candidates followed consultations with political leaders on how best to deliver the intervention to beneficiaries, improve coordination and ensure that the program achieves its intended purpose.

According to her, the initiative was designed to leverage the candidates’ familiarity with their constituencies to identify vulnerable people and facilitate the distribution of the assistance.

She cautioned that the program must not be restricted to APC members.

“We don’t say give it only to party members, but give it to your voters,” she emphasized to the candidates to ensure that deserving people in their districts benefit from the intervention.

Mrs Tinubu said the intervention reflects her longstanding commitment to the welfare of vulnerable Nigerians, drawing on her experience in public service and empowerment initiatives during her 12 years in the Senate.

“The vulnerable in society are the people we are supposed to care for”.

She explained that the RHI had previously supported persons with disabilities but was expanding its empowerment efforts to give them renewed assistance, while also stating that the intervention for elderly citizens has entered it fourth edition.

Mrs Tinubu said she had considered various approaches to delivering the funds, including working through state coordinators and traditional rulers, before consultations with political leaders led to the adoption of the senatorial district model.

The First Lady said the arrangement would also help raise awareness of the RHI’s programs and ensure that communities across the country are reached more effectively.

In his remarks, Senate President, Godswill Akpabio commended the First Lady for bringing together serving and incoming senators to coordinate the intervention, describing the meeting as an opportunity to strengthen the delivery of programs aimed at improving the lives of vulnerable Nigerians.

He said President Bola Tinubu had given his nod to the arrangement, adding that the initiative is intended to extend assistance beyond party boundaries.

Akpabio urged the candidates to treat the responsibility as a public trust and ensure that the support reached the elderly and persons with disabilities in their various constituencies.

The Senate President cited the First Lady’s commitment to women, children and elderly citizens, noting that her Renewed Hope Initiative had provided support to displaced communities, vulnerable households and women across the country in the last three years.

He also encouraged the candidates to work with other APC political office-seekers in their districts to broaden the program’s reach.

Also speaking, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt Hon Tajudeen Abbas, commended the First Lady for her various empowerment programs and interventions across the country, saying the Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI) has reached 31 state with its monthly Food Outreach Program.

Abass described the engagement as historic and praised Mrs Tinubu’s commitment to the welfare of women and vulnerable Nigerians.

“On behalf of the House of Representatives, I want to say a big thank you to our mama for all the good things she is doing”.

The Speaker said the decision to involve senatorial candidates in distributing assistance to elderly citizens and persons with disabilities would help them connect with their constituents better and ensure that the support reaches the intended beneficiaries.

He urged the candidates to justify the confidence reposed in them by the First Lady and the party and deliver on the assignment.

The House Speaker also wished the candidates success in the forthcoming elections, assuring them of continued support and engagement ahead of the polls scheduled for January 16, 2027.

On his part, APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, commended the First Lady’s interventions, saying the RHI had reached vulnerable communities in states across the federation through food support, cash assistance and economic empowerment programs.

He urged the senatorial candidates to involve party structures and other relevant stakeholders in implementing the program, while ensuring that beneficiaries were selected without discrimination on the basis of ethnicity, religion or political affiliation.

Yilwatda said the initiative would strengthen social cohesion and improve the party’s engagement with communities, urging the candidates to deliver on the responsibility entrusted to them.

For 250 beneficiaries of the Elderly Support Scheme, the initiative has provided a sum of 50 million per senatorial district with a similar fund provided for the financial support program for Persons with Disabilities

The meeting brought together the APC leadership, serving and incoming senators and members of the RHI Board of Trustees to coordinate the planned interventions for vulnerable Nigerians.

RHI Financial Support program for Persons with disabilities is a major highlight of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities which comes up on December 3 while the Elderly Support Scheme is scheduled for December 17, 2026.

World.title: Sunbeth’s N150bn Commercial Paper Offer Oversubscribed by 46.7%
World.content:
* Investors subscribe N220bn as cocoa trader strengthens procurement and processing expansion plans

Sunbeth Global Concept Limited has secured subscriptions exceeding N220 billion for its N150 billion commercial paper offer, surpassing its target by more than N70 billion and recording an oversubscription of over 46.7 per cent.

The strong investor response underscores confidence in the company’s business strategy and growth prospects as it expands its cocoa sourcing, trading and processing operations.

Sunbeth said proceeds from the issuance would be used to support cocoa procurement for the new season, as well as meet its trading and working capital requirements.

The successful offer comes amid the company’s efforts to strengthen its position in the cocoa value chain through an expanded sourcing network, increased trading capacity and investments in local processing.

A key component of the strategy is a planned cocoa processing plant in Nigeria with a capacity of 70,000 metric tonnes. The facility is expected to support the company’s ambition to deepen local value addition and supply cocoa products to customers in domestic, regional and international markets.

Commenting on the outcome of the issuance, Sunbeth’s Chief Financial Officer, Adeyemi Aduwo, said the level of subscriptions reflected investors’ confidence in the company and its growth strategy.

“The strong response reflects investors’ confidence in Sunbeth and our growth strategy. We thank our investors and transaction partners for their support. This funding strengthens our cocoa procurement capacity as we continue building an integrated business spanning sourcing, trading and processing,” Aduwo said.

The commercial paper proceeds are expected to provide additional funding flexibility for seasonal cocoa purchases, a critical requirement in the company’s trading operations, while supporting its broader expansion objectives.

Sunbeth also acknowledged the contributions of Chapel Hill Denham, the lead arranger, alongside the participating dealers, advisers and professional partners involved in the transaction.

The partners included AVA Capital Plc, Cordros Advisory Services Limited, Coronation Merchant Bank Limited, FSL Advisory Limited, Meristem Capital Limited, Norrenberger Advisory Partners Limited, PAC Capital Limited, Rand Merchant Bank, CFG Manyard, Absa Nigeria, Zedcrest and KPMG. The New Practice served as legal counsel to the transaction.

The successful issuance provides Sunbeth with additional resources to strengthen its procurement capacity at the start of the new cocoa season while advancing its plans to build a more integrated business.

The company said it remained focused on expanding its global customer base, strengthening its sourcing network and developing its processing capacity, supported by disciplined financial management.

With the planned processing investment complementing its existing sourcing and trading activities, Sunbeth is positioning itself to capture greater value from Nigeria’s cocoa sector and participate more actively in regional and international cocoa markets.

World.title: Jobberman Launches ‘Her Next Move’ Campaign to Advance Female Inclusion Through Free Skills Training
World.content:
Jobberman Nigeria, Nigeria’s leading career development and recruitment solutions company, has launched ‘Her Next Move’, a campaign designed to empower young Nigerian women with practical skills and confidence to pursue career opportunities and participate more fully in the workforce.

Through free online training, the initiative supports women aged 18 to 35 as they prepare to enter the workplace, advance into better roles or explore freelance and gig work.

Built around the message ‘Your Future. Your Skills. Your Move’, the campaign places female inclusion at the centre of career development, encouraging women to take an active role in shaping their professional futures. It connects the ambition to progress with an accessible starting point: learning skills that can help women prepare for their next opportunity.

‘Her Next Move’ recognises that career progress looks different for every woman. For a graduate, it may mean preparing for a first job. For a woman already working, it may involve developing the skills to take on greater responsibility or pursue a new role. For another, it may mean understanding how to navigate freelance work and participate in the global gig economy. The campaign brings these aspirations together through a shared emphasis on learning, preparation and action.

This Initiative by Jobberman in partnership with Mastercard Foundation promotes two courses: Jobberman Soft Skills Training and Becoming a Successful Global Gig Worker. Both courses are free, with a free certificate upon successful completion.

Jobberman Soft Skills Training focuses on workplace readiness, helping participants build the professional skills needed to navigate work and prepare for career progression. Becoming a Successful Global Gig Worker introduces participants to the demands and opportunities of freelance and gig work, supporting women interested in exploring career paths beyond traditional employment.

By making the training and certification available at no cost, ‘Her Next Move’ reduces the financial barrier to participation and encourages more young women to invest in their professional development. Its focus extends from raising awareness of learning opportunities to helping participants follow through and complete their chosen course.

To bring the campaign to life, Jobberman is working with young creators who are sharing personal stories about ambition, career transitions and the role of learning in their journeys. Through videos, social media posts and follow-up conversations, the creators encourage young women to reflect on their own goals and identify the practical steps they can take towards them.

These stories are intended to make career development relatable, connecting everyday aspirations with opportunities to learn. Across the campaign, the question “What is your next move?” invites women to define progress for themselves and begin preparing for it.

‘Her Next Move’ reinforces Jobberman’s and Mastercard Foundation’s commitment to supporting career development and expanding access to learning for young Nigerian women. By combining free skills training with relatable storytelling and encouragement to take action, the campaign seeks to help more women feel prepared to pursue their ambitions.

World.title: Abuja Job & Career Fair 2026 Connects Talents With Employers, Advances Inclusive Access to Employment
World.content:
The Fair brings together government, employers and development partners to expand employment opportunities, strengthen workforce readiness and promote inclusive hiring.

The Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment (FMLE), with the support of the Mastercard Foundation in partnership with Jobberman Nigeria and the GIZ SEDEC Cluster, has convened the Abuja Job & Career Fair 2026 to strengthen connections between talents and employers, improve workforce readiness and expand access to employment opportunities.

Held under the theme ‘Opportunities, Connections and Impact,’ the Fair features employer engagements, career counselling, CV reviews and training sessions on employability and skills development, with a focus on expanding access for women, persons with disabilities and other underserved groups.

“The Abuja Job & Career Fair is about more than bringing talents and employers into one space. It is about creating connections that lead to employment and giving participants a clearer pathway to dignified and fulfilling work,” said the Country Head of Programmes at Jobberman Nigeria, Olamide Adeyeye.

She noted that physical career fairs remain vital, as many young people still face barriers to online opportunities, adding that more than 150,000 people secured jobs through job fairs, career events and job centres in the past year.

Opening the Fair, the Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr. Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi, pledged to expand access to jobs through public job centres and the National Electronic Labour Exchange (NELEX), the ministry’s digital job-matching platform.

He identified skills mismatches and weak links between job seekers and employers as key challenges and urged employers to look beyond academic qualifications.

Delivering a goodwill message on behalf of Dr Markus Wagner, Country Director, GIZ Nigeria and ECOWAS, Oladoyin Olawaiye noted that GIZ and the ministry have established 11 job centres across five states under the Skills Development for Youth Programme, serving over 65,000 people, more than half of them women.

For participant Victory Izevbizua, the Fair delivered on both fronts. She came hoping to meet employers in Customer Service and Data Analytics and met several, but her highlight was a Jobberman career counselling session, where a counsellor reviewed her CV and gave her clear, actionable advice on tailoring it for different roles.

“The job seekers I have met here are innovative, willing to work and enthusiastic about what they do. With talents like these, we believe we can change the narrative of healthcare in Nigeria,” said Anomiri Chidozie-Pascal, Founder and CEO of Big Panda Medicare (PandaCare), which is recruiting for administrative, public health, data analysis, social media and digital marketing roles.

The Fair is supported by the Mastercard Foundation, through its Young Africa Works Programme, and international development partners, including the European Union (EU), the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), the Swiss Development Cooperation (SDC) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark.

World.title: Mission To Breed And Replicate Umo Enos
World.content:
By Anietie Usen

Ndifreke Akpekong is a cassava farmer in Eket, Akwa Ibom State. Four years ago in 2022, he was operating as a struggling farmer in a local community in the hinterland of his LGA.

The only trouble was that Akpekong was dealing with severe capital limitations that prevented him from expanding his cassava farming. This restriction kept profit margins thin and limited his scope of operations.

But his story changed after he received a grant of N500,000 from IBOM IGNITE, an NGO set up by Pastor Umo Eno, six years before he became the Governor.

With the half-a-million Naira grant, according to reports in THE GATHERING, Akpekong “successfully cultivated a 0.7-hectare cassava plantation and directly expanded his local economic footprint by employing over 15 persons both directly and indirectly within the community”.

Udofia Emmanuel, a metal fabricator and another beneficiary of IBOM IGNITE told his story to journalists covering the 2025 edition of the programme. “I was struggling to meet customer demands because I lacked the specialized gear. Winning the ₦250,000 grant completely changed my trajectory. I was able to acquire a brand-new specialized machine for my metal fabrication yard. Not only did it increase my capacity, but I have also been able to hire two additional staff to join my business.”

So are the stories of Ruth Bassey, founder of Enriched Bakery, Uyo; Tochukwu Lorenzo, fine artist and interior decorator; Uyo; Mary Ekpo, fashion and apparel designer, Eket; Blessing Udofot, fashion designer inEket; Pastor Church Mfon Monday, a manufacturer of cosmetics and household products in Etim Ekpo; Ikemesit Awak, a producer of cleaning products and liquid soap; to mention a few.

Before the grant of N500,000, Bassey, a chemical engineering graduate was trying to break into the bakery business. She was constrained by low-capacity of domestic baking tools, which restricted her market reach and daily output.

After the grant, she said she “upgraded her workflow by acquiring a commercial mixer and an additional industrial oven”. She also initiated her formal NAFDAC product registration and scaled up her operations to hire five permanent staff.

For Pastor Monday, another graduate of the University of Uyo, “the IBOM IGNITE grant in addition to my savings helped me to purchase a brand new 30KVA; four cylinder sound proof diesel generating plant, to expand my soap production factory from manual method to a fully automated soap factory…”

Tochukwu Lorenzo, a creative artist and decorator got a grant of N500,000. Before the grant, he was relying on sporadic, raw commissions without the machinery or high-grade supplies needed to tender for corporate interior design projects.

After the grant, Lorenzo secured commercial studio gears, allowing him to transition his artistic talent into a formal business structure capable of handling large-scale commercial decoration contracts across Uyo and Eket.

It is virtually the same story for more than 10,000 trainees who have successfully gone through the IBOM IGNITE programme since inception in 2017.

Over the years, beneficiaries of the IBOM IGNITE Conference have shared overwhelming testimonials, describing the programme as the critical turning point for their businesses.

Beyond the financial seed funding, past participants consistently highlight the mindset shift, practical financial prudence, and the ability to structurally design a business vision as the most valuable takeaways that helped them transition from ideas to surviving local enterprises.

IBOM IGNITE is one programme that reflects the deepest desires of Governor Eno to, in his words, ‘produce after its own kind’, a Biblical phrase that establishes the biological and spiritual law that every living thing reproduces offspring matching its exact species or nature.

As the NGO is taking stock of its last six years, all is set also for the take off of the IBOM IGNITE CONFERENCE 2026, scheduled for October 27 and 28, 2026, at Ibom Hall, IBB Avenue, Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.

Launched as a private, faith-based, youth-focused empowerment platform by Pastor Eno way back in 2017, six years before he became the Governor of Akwa Ibom State, the annual capacity building and entrepreneurial empowerment programme draws from the Eno example and background as a self-made entrepreneur, who built the Royalty Group and a fortune from a small 5-room hotel in Eket.

Since then, the IBOM IGNITE Conference has evolved from a local faith-based youth initiative into one of the most influential state-backed youth entrepreneurship and leadership movements in Nigeria’s South-South region.

The maiden conference took place in Eket, Akwa Ibom State, drawing around 2,000 young leaders and featuring prominent local business mentors. Over the years, the annual conference shifted to the capital city of Uyo.

Following Pastor Eno’s election as Governor, the platform seamlessly aligned with his Administration’s ARISE Agenda, cementing its role as a premier gateway for human capital development and startup financing in Akwa Ibom State.

This year’s stanza of the programme is featuring a blend of administrative leaders, spiritual mentors, and seasoned strategy consultants; including Pastor Eno himself, a highly successful entrepreneur who is bringing to the table practical business experience together with his hands-on background and track record in governance.

Other resource persons include Apostle Joshua Selman, the highly influential founder of Eternity Network International (ENI) and host of Koinonia. He is globally recognized for his teachings on principles of personal development, mindset shifts, and leadership strategy; Sir Charles Sebastian Udoh, a seasoned media, communications, and brand management executive who has served as a state commissioner, bringing public relations expertise to the panel and Ime Uwah, the Senior Special Assistant on Entrepreneurial Development to Governor Eno.

Hanson Johnson, a prominent digital ecosystem builder and country director behind local tech hubs, focusing heavily on fueling software development and youth digital empowerment across the South-South region; as well as

Dr. Maxwell Ubah, an elite corporate strategist, leadership expert, and CEO of Strategy House Limited, who specialises in restructuring businesses and training executives.

They will all focus on the theme: “REINVENT: Rethink, Reimagine, Redesign, Become”. The target is 1,500 young leaders, entrepreneurs, and innovators, selected on merit through a public, digital application pipeline that operated on a strict, first-come-first-served basis.

Applicants were filtered into two distinct streams based on their intent: those registering strictly as general conference attendees to participate in leadership training, and those applying for the IBOM IGNITE Entrepreneurship and Innovation Grant.

For participants seeking a portion of the ₦50 Million funding pool, an additional layer of selection was implemented. Out of the registered pool, 470 applicants were selected to advance to a mandatory physical screening and live pitching assessment held at the IBOM-LED Complex on October 24, 2026. The final winners in both the Startup and Existing Business categories will be unveiled live during the wrap-up event of the IBOM IGNITE Conference on October 28, 2026.

According to Governor Eno the initiative maintains an over 60% success rate, verified by trackable testimonials of beneficiaries who used early seeds to build functional, surviving businesses.

Across its distinct annual cycles, the program has collectively trained, upskilled, and mentored over 10,000 Akwa Ibom youths in corporate leadership, digital innovation, agribusiness, and financial prudence.

By drawing down global industry leaders, tech CEOs, and national visionaries (like Apostle Joshua Selman and Obafemi Banigbe), it bridges the gap between grassroots local entrepreneurs and national economic pipelines.

Beyond the financial seed funding, past participants consistently highlight the mindset shift, practical financial prudence, and the ability to structurally design a business vision as the most valuable takeaways that helped them transition from ideas to surviving local enterprises.

Ikemesit Awak who emerged as the standout winner last year in the highly competitive Business Startup Category and walked away with a ₦2 Million startup capital grant after delivering a masterful pitch, said her business fortunes and trajectory are now irreversible.

“This grant helped me achieve one of my major business goals, which was to increase my business revenue and achieve consistent daily sales…Overall, the grant has been instrumental in supporting my business growth, improving my marketing efforts, and increasing my revenue”, Awak said.

Her journey is widely cited by the organizers as a prime example of female youth empowerment under the platform.

The very first batch of beneficiaries from the 2017 maiden conference held at the Rehoboth Arena in Eket, started micro-ventures with small seed grants and have successfully sustained their businesses for nearly a decade, serving as the foundational proof-of-concept that convinced the State government to adopt and expand the platform.

Beneficiaries frequently state that learning to build a “Vision Board” under local business mentors like Mrs. Ekaette Umoh, the DG of

Ibom-LED completely transformed how they handle day-to-day operations and scaling.

Past winners express deep gratitude for the capital injections. “In a challenging economic landscape,like ours, the grants provided me with the essential safety net that prevented my startup from folding in the first year”, Akpekong said.

“It was an eye-opener for me… I discovered that the mind of an entrepreneur must be a problem solving mind, risk taking, value adding and an investment conscious mindset… You have to move from talent to skill and intentional networking”, Ekpo said.

For Blessing Akpan, an Agricultural entrepreneur, her take home and key to building a thriving enterprise is: “Never underestimate the potential contributions of anyone, as they may hold the key to realizing your dreams” .

Governor Eno’s campaign promises regarding skill acquisition, capacity building, and entrepreneurial development were anchored heavily in his official governance blueprint, The ARISE Agenda. Drawing from his personal background as a successful businessman, his campaign focused on shifting the mindsets of Akwa Ibom youths from “job seekers” to “job creators”.

Governor Eno is a man who went from a small-scale entrepreneur to a conglomerate powerhouse. Now, he’s passing the torch. Through massive capacity-building programs, both at the governmental and Non-Governmental levels, Akwa Ibom is training the business giants of tomorrow.

Said Obafemi Banigbe, CEO of EMTS/9mobile, who was the Keynote Speaker last year: “When I look at this State, I see possibilities. To the young people here: you are not just leaders of tomorrow, you are leaders of today. Don’t dim your spark, ignite it”.

*Anietie Usen writes from Uyo

World.title: Oloworaran: PenCom to Roll Out Healthcare Support for Retirees November
World.content:
James Emejo in Abuja

Director General, National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms Omolola Oloworaran, Wednesday revealed that the commission will unveil a healthcare programme for retirees next month.

The move is part of efforts to reduce medical expenses that erode pension income and undermine the financial security of senior citizens.

She spoke at the Senior Citizens Fair, with the theme, “Pension for All: Building a Secure Future Together,”

in Abuja, held as part of activities marking National Pension Week 2026.

She said the PenCare initiative was undergoing a pilot phase ahead of its nationwide implementation, with the programme designed to improve retirees’ access to healthcare and address concerns over the rising cost of medical services.

The initiative is expected to help pensioners manage healthcare expenses after retirement, when limited and often fixed incomes leave many vulnerable to rising living costs and unexpected medical bills.

Oloworaran said the commission was committed to integrating healthcare into retirement protection, stressing that Nigerians who had spent years in public and private service deserved to live with dignity without struggling to afford essential medical treatment.

She explained that the formal inauguration, initially scheduled to hold today had been postponed due to scheduling constraints.

The health iniatiative seeks to address a critical dimension of retirement security, as healthcare expenses can quickly consume pension payments and leave retirees with fewer resources for food, housing and other basic needs.

Beyond healthcare access, the PenCom DG identified disparities in pension payments among retirees in similar circumstances as another concern requiring urgent attention from the relevant authorities.

She said the commission would continue to strengthen the policies, laws and regulations governing pension administration to protect beneficiaries and improve retirement outcomes.

Oloworaran also urged retirees to provide feedback on their experiences with the pension system, noting that such engagement would help the commission identify service gaps and develop more responsive policies.

She reaffirmed PenCom’s commitment to working with labour unions and other stakeholders to resolve pension-related concerns and improve service delivery.

Speaking at the event, PenCom’s Commissioner for Finance, Dr. Charles Efe-Emukowhate, said healthcare support would help retirees preserve more of their pension income for other essential expenses.

He commended President Bola Tinubu for approving the settlement of ₦758 billion in inherited pension liabilities, describing the move as a significant commitment towards addressing outstanding pension obligations.

Emukowhate also assured pensioners that the commission would sustain regulatory oversight of the pension industry, protect retirement savings and ensure that beneficiaries received their entitlements as and when due.

He, however, warned retirees against fraudsters offering unrealistic investment returns, particularly schemes promising to double their savings.

He advised pensioners to verify unsolicited investment proposals with PenCom or their Pension Fund Administrators before committing their funds, warning that retirees could lose their savings to fraudulent operators.

Meanwhile, Consultant Geriatrician and Founder of JBS Gerontology Centre, Dr. Olutoyin Akande-Ajala, urged retirees to adopt healthy ageing practices to preserve their independence and quality of life.

Speaking virtually at the fair, she explained that healthy ageing did not necessarily mean living without illness but managing medical conditions effectively while retaining the ability to perform everyday activities.

She advised older persons to exercise regularly, eat balanced diets, undergo routine medical examinations, monitor their blood pressure and blood sugar levels, and adhere to prescribed medications.

Akande-Ajala also urged retirees to seek prompt medical attention for persistent symptoms, including recurrent falls, unexplained weight loss, worsening memory and prolonged fatigue, rather than dismissing them as inevitable consequences of ageing.

She emphasised the importance of maintaining social relationships, engaging in mentally stimulating activities and seeking appropriate support for depression, loneliness and significant memory changes.

The geriatrician further urged families to respect older persons’ independence and involve them in decisions affecting their health and welfare.

The Senior Citizens Fair brought together retirees, pension beneficiaries, pension professionals and other stakeholders to discuss healthcare access, financial security and strategies for improving retirement outcomes.

The event featured wellness activities, health screenings and pension information sessions, including information on PenCare and the process of registering for health insurance.

The fair formed part of PenCom’s broader efforts to promote retirement security and improve the welfare of pensioners.

World.title: Adesokan: 92% of Taxpayers Pay Zero or Lower Taxes Under New Act
World.content:
*Declares 21 states have adopted harmonised tax, levy legislation as authorities seek to dismantle multiple charges amid 27% rise in revenue

*FG, states plan joint audits to cut compliance costs, disruption to businesses, seeks to end roadside tax collection, others

James Emejo in Abuja

Executive Secretary, Joint Revenue Board (JRB), Mr. Olusegun Adesokan, has said disclosed that the implementation of the new tax regime has yielded early fruits with a 27 per cent increase in tax revenue from 23 states in the First Half of the year (H1 2026) compared to the corresponding period of 2025.

He said the performance reflected a shift towards bringing more high-income earners into the tax net while reducing the burden on lower-income taxpayers.

The JRB boss spoke during an engagement with journalists in Abuja.

He said the reform was also beginning to improve revenue administration through the harmonisation of taxes and levies, the introduction of a National Tax Identification system and closer coordination among federal and state tax authorities.

Adesokan said 21 states had adopted the harmonised taxes and levies legislation as of October 27, with the National Economic Council (NEC) identifying the initiative as one of its priorities for implementation within a 90-day action plan.

The figures provide an early indication of the reform’s potential to improve domestic revenue mobilisation without imposing additional tax burdens on low-income households and businesses.

However, the board acknowledged that multiple taxation, unauthorised collections and confusion over legitimate government charges remain widespread challenges.

21 states move to harmonise levies

Adesokan said the harmonisation initiative was designed to consolidate numerous taxes, levies and charges imposed by subnational authorities into nine broad categories, reducing duplication and making compliance more predictable for businesses and individuals.

He said the board developed the framework in collaboration with the Presidential Committee on Fiscal Policy and Tax Reforms and had circulated it to states for adoption.

He acknowledged that unauthorised roadside collections remained a problem, including demands by individuals and groups claiming to represent government authorities.

He said the JRB was working with the police and state revenue authorities on a coordinated enforcement mechanism to address the practice.

According to him, the board also planned to intensify efforts to eliminate illegal collections affecting transport operators and traders, although Adesokan did not give a definitive commencement date for the proposed enforcement measures.

He urged businesses to verify suspicious demands with the relevant tax authorities and ensure that payments were made into authorised government accounts rather than accounts belonging to private consultants or collectors.

The listed the states to include Kebbi, Niger, Kaduna, Plateau, Ekiti, Benue, Zamfara, Enugu, Kogi, Abia and Kwara.

Others are Nasarawa, Anambra, Gombe, Akwa Ibom, Adamawa, Bayelsa, Delta, Yobe, Ondo and Borno.

Low-income earners get tax relief

Furthermore, Adesokan said data obtained from 23 states showed that an average of 92 per cent of income earners covered by the assessment now paid lower or zero personal income tax under the new framework.

He said the changes were intended to leave more money in the hands of lower-income earners while ensuring that individuals with greater financial capacity contributed a fairer share.

Under the revised personal income tax structure, the first N800,000 of annual taxable income is taxed at zero per cent, while higher income bands attract progressively higher rates, reaching 25 per cent for the top band.

Adesokan stressed that the reform was guided by the principle of taxing prosperity rather than poverty, adding that the government had not introduced new taxes through the framework.

He acknowledged concerns about traders and small businesses who continued to complain about tax demands despite the exemptions provided under the new rules.

According to him, inadequate public awareness and the persistence of unauthorised collectors had contributed to the confusion.

He said the board would continue its public education campaign to clarify which taxpayers were exempt from personal income tax and distinguish legitimate taxes from other authorised charges.

However, the 92 per cent figure relates to the personal income tax assessment presented by the board and does not qualify as an exemption from every form of taxation, including applicable consumption taxes.

National tax ID to curb multiple taxation

Adesokan said the National Tax Identification system was another major component of the reform, providing a common means of identifying taxpayers across federal and state jurisdictions.

The system is expected to link existing taxpayer records and enable authorities to verify tax compliance without requiring individuals and businesses to repeatedly establish their status in different states.

He said the arrangement would reduce administrative bottlenecks, particularly for individuals conducting business or property transactions outside their state of residence.

He stated that JRB was also promoting uniform tax administration guidelines and information-sharing arrangements to improve transparency and voluntary compliance.

Joint audits planned for businesses

In a further measure to reduce the cost of compliance, Adesokan said the JRB was preparing to facilitate joint tax audits involving NRS and state internal revenue services.

He said the arrangement would enable relevant authorities to coordinate their examinations of businesses rather than visiting the same companies separately at different times.

Under the proposed approach, state authorities could examine personal income tax compliance, including employers’ obligations, while the federal revenue service would address the company’s relevant federal tax obligations.

Adesokan said coordinated audits would reduce disruption to business operations, paperwork and the time companies spend responding to separate tax assessments.

He added that the JRB’s mandate was to coordinate and harmonise revenue administration rather than collect taxes directly.

Implementation challenges remain

Meanwhile, despite the early progress, there were concerns about continued roadside collections, conflicting demands from federal and state tax authorities, and the limited visibility of public benefits from taxes paid.

Adesokan said the board was working to improve collaboration between revenue agencies, including through joint audits and more consistent administration of tax laws.

He also acknowledged complaints about levies imposed on pensioners and residents in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), adding that the relevant legal provisions would be examined.

The JRB chief maintained that the ultimate test of the reform would not be the volume of taxes collected alone, but whether businesses could expand, create jobs and contribute to economic growth without being weighed down by multiple and unpredictable charges.

No more roadblocks, cash collection

Adesokan added that JRB at its 158th meeting banned the sales of stickers and emblems nationwide.

He said, “This means motorists will no longer be subjected to the purchase of irrelevant documents before transporting goods from one part of the country to another. Thereby reducing the cost of farm produce.”

He explained that the prohibition was supported by the model Harmonised Taxes & Levies Law and the Presumptive Tax Regulations, 2026.

World.title: ‘My girl!’: Sacha praises girlfriend Sarah Langa amid ‘cheating’ rumours
World.content:
Springbok and Stormers star Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has publicly claimed his girlfriend, Sarah Langa, amid rumours he “cheated” on her with Cape Town model, Robyn Mia Peters.

The famous flyhalf has trended on the X platform after an image of him with the woman went viral.

Neither Sacha nor Sarah – who have a nine-year age gap – has addressed the speculation.



SACHA FEINBERG-MNGOMEZULU GUSHES OVER GIRLFRIEND, SARAH LANGA

On her Instagram account, Sarah Langa has continued to post content, ignoring social media rumours claiming her partner, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, was unfaithful.

Under several sponsored posts, the 24-year-old Springbok has appeared to do “damage control”.

“My girl”, he commented under one post of her modelling for a fashion house. “My star”, he commented under another.



While neither Sarah Langa nor Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu have responded to the “cheating” rumours, the former has erased any connection to her younger partner.

Although they still follow each other on IG, Sarah has deleted an image from her feed in which she called Sacha the “love of my life”.

She’s also deleted a TikTok video of her unboxing a designer handbag reportedly gifted to her by Sacha.



CHEATING?

This week, an image of Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu cosying up to Cape Town model Robyn Mia Peters set tongues wagging.

A look at Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and his new girlfriend Robyn Mia Peters. pic.twitter.com/SNIIBK1b2M — Musa Khawula (@Musa_Khawula) October 28, 2026

It’s unclear where and when the image was taken.



However, social media users were convinced that the 24-year-old had been unfaithful to his 33-year-old girlfriend, Sarah Langa.

On her Instagram account, which she has since disabled, Robyn laughed off the commentary with a meme.

World.title: Actress Carina Nel on ‘paralysing’ breast cancer diagnosis
World.content:
Carina Nel has opened up about hr breast cancer diagnosis. Images via YouTube screenshot

Former 7de Laan actress Carina Nel – known for playing medical doctor Alexa Welman – has opened up about receiving a “paralysing” breast cancer diagnosis following a routine check-up.

The mother-of-two, who shared her journey during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment and is in good spirits.

CARINA NEL ON BREAST CANCER DIAGNOSIS

Speaking to SABC’s Expresso show, Carina Nel revealed that a routine check-up in April, after suffering from exhaustion, set off alarm bells.



Five days later, she had been formally diagnosed with breast cancer.

Carina shared that she had no history of breast cancer in her family, and at 38 years old, she was shocked at her diagnosis.

“The five days before I received my daignosis was probably the worst days in this whole journey. It was filled with paralysing fear, where you can’t think, you can’t breathe, you can’t move…

“No one can really understand what it feels like, or what you’re going through until you’re in that situation”.

Carina added that her Christian faith had encouraged her to keep going, and fighting.

She continued: “I remember being overwhelmed with this calmness”.



‘GO GET IT CHECKED’

Like Carina Nel, rugby referee Aimee Barrett-Theron has also gone public with her battle with breast cancer.

The 39-year-old – a qualified biokineticist specialising in sports performance and rehabilitation – shared her diagnosis in July, stating that she would step away from the pitch to undergo treatment.

She has used her platform to encourage women to get screened for breast cancer.

She said in a video interview with the URC: “Early detection is so important when it comes to breast cancer. I was very lucky to find mine in the early stages. I think it literally saved my very active career and potentially my life.

“I chose to share it publicly, and what I found is a lot of people have said that they’re guilty of not doing the self-checks and not going for their scans.

“And, you know, life is busy or they’re worried about the outcome.

“But hopefully, by standing up for this and raising a bit of awareness around it, people are more proactive, and they take action to look after themselves.”
