World.title: Accusations over De la Espriella’s narco ties “lack conclusive or solid evidence,” says Colombia’s justice minister
World.content:
Colombia’s Justice Minister, Ivan Cancino, downplayed the evidence of ties between President Abelardo de la Espriella and drug traffickers that was displayed in Congress by opposition Senator Ivan Cepeda.

In a video, Cancino said that “political oversight is a fundamental tool of our democracy. However, it cannot become an arena for launching accusations without proving and substantiating them.”

The justice minister admitted that the pieces of evidence provided to Congress “may seem serious,” but “lack conclusive or solid evidence, as well as any support that could jeopardize the innocence and the presumption of innocence of our president.”

It is not just about displaying organizational charts, deeds from over a decade ago, and business transactions to construct a narrative that supports neither judicial decisions nor the documentary, testimonial, circumstantial, or expert backing required for these types of accusations. Ivan Cancino

Cancino accused the opposition of remaining “silent regarding the grave scandals involving corruption, drug trafficking, and even alleged sexual abuse, as well as fiscal irresponsibility and possible links to criminal organizations that surrounded the previous government. ”

The justice minister was forced to come out after Cepeda showed Congress evidence of De la Espriella’s business ties with multiple convicted drug traffickers and announced criminal complaints against the president.

De la Espriella’s law firm rose to prominence during the demobilization of paramilitary organization AUC with whom he created a foundation that sought to justify the paramilitary violence that terrorized much of Colombia in the 1990’s and 2000s.

Once the ties between the AUC and elected politicians became known, the president ended up defending many of the “parapoliticians” in court.

According to Cepeda, De la Espriella plays a key role in a “revolving door” system that could end up benefiting the very drug traffickers and corrupt politicians that have paid the president for his legal defense in the past.

World.title: Colombia’s opposition announces criminal charges against De la Espriella over ties to drug traffickers
World.content:
Colombia’s opposition leader, senator Ian Cepeda, accused President Abelardo de la Espriella of leading an agrarian counter-reform designed to benefit land-owning clans and convicted drug traffickers.

During a congressional debate, Cepeda claimed that De la Espriella put allies of drug traffickers and paramilitaries in charge of key state institutions responsible for land distribution and asset forfeiture.

The president and his appointees are part of a revolving door system of people who, before being appointed to government positions, defended the interests of drug traffickers and paramilitaries associated with De la Espriella and his businesses, according to the opposition leader.

For example, the president put Diana Patrica Bravo, a former prosecutor and partner at his law firm De la Espriella Lawyers, in charge of The Society of Special Assets (SAE), which controls assets that were seized from drug traffickers.

The leader of the leftist Historic Pact party showed financial statements of one of De la Espriella’s companies, Dominio De la Espriella, that would prove that in between 38% and 40% of its capital deposits came from the family and corporate network of Hugues Rodríguez, a.k.a. Comandante Barbie, a former paramilitary financier who was charged with drug trafficking in the US.

The SAE would control more than 130 properties of Comandante Barbie.

De la Espriella family construction firm, Cosenza S.A.S., made property purchases in the city of Monteria directly with individuals under investigation for money laundering and illicit enrichment, according to Cepeda.

The president’s ex-wife, Yoly Beatriz Illidge, was appointed Superintendent of Notaries, making her “directly responsible for inspecting and monitoring all land entries and records issued by restitution judges throughout the country,” according to Cepeda.

De la Espriella is an associate of drug traffickers, owns assets purchased from drug traffickers, and defends drug traffickers from within the national government. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Last but not least, Agriculture Minister Indalecio Dangond “arrived at this post to execute an agrarian counter-reform at the service of paramilitary land-grabbers, foreign capital, and agro-industrial partners” while blocking investments for small farmers and displacement victims, the opposition leader stated.

Cepeda vowed that he would give the dossier to the United States Department of Justcie and to “Congressmen of the Democratic Party, given that mister De la Espriella is a US citizen.”

The opposition leader additionally promised to file criminal charges against the president and his agriculture minister in Colombia.

World.title: Colombia’s government claims Petro exploited 48 women as president
World.content:
The administration chief of Colombia’s President Abelardo De la Espriella told Congress that former President Gustavo Petro hired at least 48 women who were “trapped and exploited” for presidential parties.

During a hearing, DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios claimed that Petro had 48 women “working in the Presidency, who were unfortunately exploited through temporary work contracts.”

We’re going to prove this to the Colombian people: how, unfortunately, the Casa de Nariño was set up, organized, and designed not for governing, but for partying there every day, bringing women there and engaging in behavior we should not be engaging in—behavior that sets a bad example. DAPRE director Carlos Andres Rios

“Forty-eight women are already speaking with us about how, through a contract and an OPS, they were trapped and exploited in order to be with President Petro,” said Rios.

Former DAPRE director Angie Rodriguez, who was sacked by Petro in July, doubled down on her successor’s allegations and asked the former president to prove that the president managed a network of women, including child transvestites.

Were there transvestite children there? Answer me, Mr. President. Were there transvestite children there? I am asking you a question, and I have every right to ask it. Were there? And if there weren’t, uh… prove that what I am saying is a lie. Angie Rodriguez

Last but not least, far-right magazine Semana published an interview with a woman identified as Deicy Jimenez, who claimed she as hired by Petro after meeting him on an adult website.

Jimenez even told Semana’s former presidential candidate Vicky Davila she trafficked drugs for the former president when he was senator.

VD: What happened on the day you say you transported drugs for Petro? DJ: Yes, I was traveling, and he asked me as a favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Were you outside of Bogotá? DJ: Yes. VD: How do you recall that favor Petro asked of you? DJ: He asked me as the favor to bring him some drugs. VD: Did you buy them? DJ: Yes, I bought them somewhere. He gave me money. VD: Did he give it to you in cash or deposit it for you? DJ: In cash. VD: How much money? DJ: Three million pesos. VD: What kind of drugs did you buy? DJ: Cocaine. VD: Where did you buy it? DJ: I bought it from some people. I can’t say (publicly) their names or the location. VD: Is it a gang? DJ: Yes. VD: Did he know you were going to buy the drugs from that gang? DJ: Yes. VD: At that time, was he a senator or the president? DJ: A senator. VD: How did you bring that drug in? DJ: I brought it through the airport. VD: You mean, on a plane? DJ: Yeah. VD: Did you get on a plane with Petro’s drugs? DJ: Yes. VD: How were the drugs packaged? DJ: In bags. VD: Like individual doses? DJ: Yes. VD: And where did you hide the drugs? DJ: In my suitcase.

In a response, Petro denied having hired women for sex and claimed that the far-right attack were the result of authorities’ failure to sustain corruption allegations.

World.title: “Brazil and Colombia need each other,” says De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella recognized the election victory of his Brazilian counterpart Luiz Ignacio Lula, who defeated far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday.

In a post on social media platform X, the Colombian President said that “in the Colombian presidential campaign, President Lula openly supported Ivan Cepeda, and I won. In the Brazilian campaign, I supported Bolsonaro, and Lula won.”

“Neither does Lula decide for Colombians, nor do I decide for Brazilians. THE PEOPLE DECIDE! And when the people speak at the polls, their will is respected because it is sacred,” the president added.

Lula and I have major and profound political and ideological differences, but we agree on one fundamental point: Brazil and Colombia need each other. No other consideration can take precedence over the interests of our nations. Colombia and Brazil are sister nations, facing enormous shared challenges and opportunities.

President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella stressed that “we have much to do and much work to carry out for the benefit of our peoples” an ought to “fight against narco-terrorism and illegal mining, the protection of the Amazon, and the well-being of our citizens.”

Lula was the first leftist candidate and critic of US President Donald Trump to win an election, triggering celebrations among leftists throughout the continent.

De la Espriella, a US citizen, has been among the most fanatic among Trump supporter in trying to align his domestic policies to US foreign policy.

World.title: De la Espriella sacks interior minister after Congress bungles Colombia’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia President Abelardo de la Espriella sacked Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara hours after Congress found a procedural flaw in the passed 2027 budget, which makes the law invalid.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella briefly thanked Lara and announced he would be replaced by the ambassador to the Organization of American States, Alejandro Ordoñez.

The news surprised the interior minister, who suddenly left a congressional debate on a law to facilitate the demobilization of illegal armed groups after receiving a message on his phone.

Lara was apparently held responsible for the blunder of Congress, whose two houses approved the 2027 budget but with conflicting versions of an article on financial risk-coverage mechanisms for the Ministry of Finance.

By the time the error was detected, the budget debate had passed its October 20 deadline, forcing De la Espriella to issue a decree that would convert an older version of the budget bill into law.

The interior minister was the administration’s primary political liaison responsible for managing legislative procedure and whip operations in Congress.

Lara’s job was already under pressure after he failed to convince Congress to cede its presidency to the president’s candidate.

While Ordoñez returns from Washington, Justice Minister Ivan Cancino will assume the role of interior minister.

The incoming interior minister is an ultra conservative Catholic with ties to the Society of St. Pius X, which considers the modernizing reforms of the Catholic Church heresies and errors, and was declared in a schism with the church in June.

In Colombian politics and particularly among the opposition, Ordoñez is mainly remembered as the inspector general who illegally removed former President Gustavo Petro from his post as mayor of Bogota in 2013.

Petro was ultimately reinstated and would become president of the country in 2022.

World.title: Colombia’s Congress approves De la Espriella’s 2027 budget
World.content:
Colombia’s Congress agreed to increase the government’s 2027 budget despite promises by President Abelardo de la Espriella to reduce public spending.

Next year’s budget will be COP634.9 trillion, almost $204 billion, which is 16% more than last year’s budget and 10% higher than the proposal made by former President Gustavo Petro.

According to Finance Minister Miguel Gomez, the budget seeks to bring the State’s finances in line with reality.

The budget was approved in both the Senate and the House of Representatives with the support of De la Espriella’s government coalition.

The Historic Pact, the only leftist opposition party, rejected the budget and boycotted the vote.

On behalf of the national government, I would like to thank you all for your work over the past few months in passing the budget. I would also like to thank the opposition for the strength with which they defended their views. The message that Congress has sent today regarding the government’s economic policy is very important. It is the first step toward putting the country’s economy back on track toward growth, fiscal responsibility, and addressing the nation’s needs. Finance Minister Miguel Gomez

The budget seeks to reimpose the neoliberal model that had been abandoned by Petro and reduce public debt.

According to Green Party representative Jaime Raul Salamanca, who opposed the budget, funding for free higher education was cut in half from COP800 billion ($254 million) to COP400 billion (127 million).

“This cut raises concerns about its potential impact on the continuity and scope of this policy, which has enabled thousands of young people to enroll in public institutions of higher education,” said Salamanca.

The budget also cut the budget for the war crimes tribunal JEP, which could endanger the future of the peace process with the FARC and is opposed by the government.

World.title: De la Espriella announces “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism”
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella announced an “open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism” as part of his “cultural counterrevolution.”

During a visit to the Culture Ministry, De la Espriella described wokeism as “an ideological paradigm that aims to transform moral, cultural, and social foundations in the West, perverting values, family tradition, and national identity.”

According to the president, Culture Minister Paola Holguin was a general in the “cultural counterrevolution.”

Culture has an enormous capacity to shape society, and that is why the State has a moral, inescapable, and political duty to prevent cultural spaces from being taken over by social communism, which is atheist and an enemy to the fundamental values upon which the nation of Colombia is built. This is where that cultural counterrevolution will begin. President Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella said that Holguin, the daughter of a reported money launderer, would lead the “Culture War” against the “extreme left,” which has “permeated all parts of society, particularly the cultural and academic spheres.”

I want to be clear about this: we are going to wage an open, resolute, and patriotic struggle against wokeism, which is nothing more than an ideological movement that aims to transform the moral, cultural, and social foundations of the West, corrupting values, family tradition, and national identity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Earlier in the day, the National Museum removed all references to members of the exterminated Patriotic Union party, slain guerrilla leader and presidential candidate Carlos Pizarro, and the struggle for the rights of Colombia’s LGBT+ community.

References to Colombia’s former guerrilla movements was “terrorism apology, which is “exactly what we have come to confront” in an attempt to “recover pride for Colombian culture.”

Atheists, the Pizarro family and gay rights activists rejected the president’s attempts to remove them from mainstream culture.

World.title: Colombia’s first lady promises transparency over earthquake donations
World.content:
Colombia’s first lady, Ana Lucia Pineda, vowed to reveal how much money she collected and spent in response to the August 10 earthquake that affected hundreds of thousands of people.

Amid mounting public pressure about where the money had gone, Pineda went on the morning program of public television channel Nuestro Caribe to promise that her foundation, Luz y Sonrisas, will take its finances public on Friday.

Carrying a white folder, the wife of President Abelardo de la Espriella stressed that “in the foundation’s accounts rest all, absolutely all of the monies from the donations we received during the ‘Colombia One Single Heart’ campaign” that was announced on August 12.

“A lie is not going to tear down the truth of who I am or what I represent, or how my children recognize me,” said Pineda.

Luz y Sonrisas was one of three NGO’s that were promoted by the De la Espriella government to collect contributions for victims of the earthquake.

Pineda’s foundation was the only one that could receive contributions from abroad.

Earlier in the week, news program Noticias Uno revealed that her foundation that was founded on July 7 lacked the tax exemption that would allow it to accept donations, a process that usually takes months.

In a press statement, tax office DIAN subsequently said that it had granted the tax exemption to the first lady and that she could legally accept financial contributions.

Pineda did not say how much money she had received, but said that she stopped supporting the initial relief efforts “because the humanitarian aid was sufficient, it was huge.”

The first lady vowed she had saved the donations for the reconstruction phase “because I have also taken the initiative to build and return to the victims a house that is durable for the families who lost everything.”

World.title: “I am the right person”: Delcy Rodríguez casts herself as guarantor of Venezuela’s transition
World.content:
“I am the right person”: Delcy Rodríguez casts herself as guarantor of Venezuela’s transition

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 17:42 UTC Full article

“There will be elections, all those our Constitution requires, organised by a renewed electoral authority and with the world as witness,” Rodríguez said in an address to the nation

Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez on Thursday presented herself as the guarantor of democratic change in the country and promised elections organised by a “renewed” electoral authority, though she set no date. “This process can only be led by someone who knows the inner workings of the Venezuelan state deeply. I know this state and I am the right person to carry this process forward,” she said.

“There will be elections, all those our Constitution requires, organised by a renewed electoral authority and with the world as witness,” Rodríguez said in an address to the nation, recalling that she has served as deputy foreign minister, foreign minister, minister and vice-president. She championed a “political, economic, cultural, spiritual, democratic, orderly and verifiable” transformation and said her government has a roadmap. “Venezuela’s political horizon is not measured by a date on the calendar but by a sequence of objectives we must achieve,” including legal reform, guarantees of participation for all political forces and “elections that are a solution and not a source of irreconcilable conflict”. “An announcement like this is worth not what it promises but what it delivers,” she added.

Rodríguez also announced a national consultation to reform criminal justice, with technical assistance from the European Union, and said she had requested the cooperation of the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights. The National Assembly last week presented a reform that the Supreme Court declared constitutional, and Rodríguez called for it to be debated in a broad consultation with all sectors.

The address came four days after opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after nearly ten months abroad, and shortly before her first press conference since her return. Rodríguez had called her arrival a “show”. Rodríguez has governed as acting president since January, after Nicolás Maduro’s removal from power in a US military operation. Her government has been negotiating with the opposition since August a roadmap that includes renewing the Supreme Court and the National Electoral Council and holding regional elections before the presidential vote, a sequence Machado rejects. The US State Department has said that under that roadmap Rodríguez should leave the presidency vacant in 2027.

On Tuesday, President Donald Trump suggested that Venezuela become the “51st state” of the United States and elect a governor instead of a president, an idea Rodríguez has rejected in the past.

World.title: The IMF urges Argentina to “stay the course” despite doubts over growth and country risk
World.content:
The IMF urges Argentina to “stay the course” despite doubts over growth and country risk

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 16:26 UTC Full article

On Tuesday, IMF staff and the Argentine authorities reached agreement on the third review of the Extended Fund Facility programme, which would allow a disbursement of about US$900 million

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday urged Argentina’s government to stick with its economic programme as the best way to reduce country risk, and set out four measures to turn the gains of stabilisation into growth and jobs, at a time when the press is warning of a possible technical recession.

“Our best advice for Argentina to continue reducing its country risk is to continue with its strong policy implementation, that is, to keep implementing the programme as it has been doing,” IMF spokeswoman Julie Kozack told her press briefing in Washington. She added that accumulating net international reserves and strengthening the external position are “really fundamental” to that end. “Our overall message on Argentina is really to stay the course with strong policies while broadening the benefits,” she said.

Asked about the possibility of the economy recording two consecutive quarters of contraction, Kozack said the Fund and the government agreed on “the importance of expanding the gains of stabilisation into stronger growth and job creation”. She listed four agreed measures: deepening capital and mortgage markets to widen access to financing; improving labour market flexibility to support private-sector employment; advancing recently awarded infrastructure concessions; and facilitating strategic investment under the Incentive Regime for Large Investments (RIGI), where approved projects already exceed US$76 billion, according to the Fund.

On Tuesday, IMF staff and the Argentine authorities reached agreement on the third review of the Extended Fund Facility programme, which would allow a disbursement of about US$900 million. Kozack said the board could consider it in early December. The Fund said the programme “continues to deliver impressive results, despite a more complex global environment”: net reserves exceeded the June target by about US$4 billion, the Central Bank bought nearly US$16 billion this year and the Treasury raised more than US$5 billion in local markets. The government, backed by official creditors, also secured US$3.2 billion in guaranteed international bank financing and is working on a further US$1 billion before year-end.

The agreement keeps the target of a primary surplus of 1.4% of GDP for 2026 and a similar effort in 2027, along with the exchange rate band regime. In October, the IMF cut its 2026 growth forecast for Argentina from 3.5% to 2.1%.

World.title: Falklands unveil 2026-2030 Islands Plan, with a sovereign wealth fund for energy revenues
World.content:
Falklands unveil 2026-2030 Islands Plan, with a sovereign wealth fund for energy revenues

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 14:49 UTC Full article

Under the first priority, the Plan aims to create the conditions for the economy to grow and diversify “while also ensuring effective regulation of industries”

The Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly on Thursday published the Islands Plan 2026-2030, the programme of government for the current Assembly, which provides for a sovereign wealth fund so that energy sector revenues benefit future generations and acknowledges that the government faces some of the largest projects in its history, with a capital programme of more than £300 million. Executive Council formally adopted the Plan on October 27.

The document, signed by the eight Members of the Legislative Assembly — Stacy Bragger, Lewis Clifton, Dean Dent, Jack Ford, Michael Goss, Dot Gould, Cheryl Roberts and Roger Spink — is built around a single vision: “a strong, secure and sustainable future for the Falkland Islands”. From it flow three priorities: providing strategic and proactive stewardship for the long-term prosperity of the Islands, building a sustainable and diversified economy for the future, and enabling a healthy, capable and prosperous community “with a strong sense of identity”.

An unprecedented capital programme

In the foreword, Members note that the Assembly has inherited “a substantial programme of work”: a capital programme of more than £300 million covering a new port, energy projects, improved waste management, housing and the development of land for release. These, together with the future of telecommunications and “the regulation of a developing hydrocarbons industry”, are “among the largest undertakings the Falkland Islands Government has ever embarked upon”.

The authors acknowledge the limits facing a small government. Each project “demands significant time, money, and expertise, and there is a limit to how much a government of our size can carry at once, and to what we can afford while living within our means”. Members have therefore chosen not to set a fixed four-year delivery plan: priorities will be set on a rolling 12-month basis “so that timeframes stay realistic and resources go where they are needed most”.

First-year priorities

For the first twelve months, the Assembly sets six priorities: progressing the Sovereign Wealth Fund for energy sector revenues; speeding up the release of housing plots and the building of government homes; delivering the next phase of the wind farm; introducing modernised anti-discrimination legislation; updating education law, including support for children with additional needs; and reviewing the Permanent Residence Permit system.

A tracking document setting out actions, owners and milestones will be brought to Executive Council, and a public version will be published “so the community can follow progress and hold the Assembly to account”.

Economy, energy and resilience

Under the first priority, the Plan aims to create the conditions for the economy to grow and diversify “while also ensuring effective regulation of industries”, review the National Infrastructure Plan and ensure delivery of the new port, energy projects, waste management and the healthcare and education estates. It also includes strengthening “national resilience” against evolving risks through intelligence-led risk management, modern technology, cross-government coordination and “international partnerships”, and a new framework for telecommunications.

On the economy, the government pledges to help local businesses meet the demands “of the new energy sector and other emerging sectors”, to work with partners on additional flight connectivity, and to review the Tourism Development Strategy, the tax system, aspects of the immigration system and health and social care provision. It also plans an inward investment strategy setting out “a clear framework for acceptable international investment” and national branding for the Islands’ economic, tourism and public diplomacy activities.

Identity and a voice in the world

The third priority covers housing, equalities, education and health, and mechanisms to monitor the social and economic effects of growth. It includes developing a set of “Falkland Islands Values” to communicate “our British values and our unique identity as Falkland Islanders, at home and abroad”, and a commitment to make “the voice of the Falkland Islands heard around the world” through public diplomacy and support for national sports teams, promoting “our right to self-determination”.

“By taking these bold steps, we are securing the right of Falkland Islanders to determine their own future,” the foreword concludes. The back cover reproduces a plaque bearing the words of then British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher on April 3, 1982: “They are few in number but they have the right to live in peace, to choose their own way of life and to determine their own allegiance.”

The Plan is published as development of the Sea Lion oil field north of the archipelago advances, the revenues from which would feed the future sovereign wealth fund. Argentina, which claims sovereignty over the islands, has imposed sanctions on companies linked to the project and asked the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea to halt it; the hearing will take place in Hamburg on November 10 and 11. The document does not mention Argentina.

Islands Plan 2026-2030 by MercoPress

World.title: Christine Lagarde to step down early as European Central Bank president in February
World.content:
Christine Lagarde to step down early as European Central Bank president in February

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 14:32 UTC Full article

Lagarde informed the ECB’s Governing Council and European Council President António Costa of her decision; the European Council is responsible for appointing her successor

European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde will leave her post on February 7, 2027, almost nine months before her term is due to end in late October that year, the Frankfurt-based institution announced on Thursday.

Lagarde informed the ECB’s Governing Council and European Council President António Costa of her decision; the European Council is responsible for appointing her successor. The European Union launched the selection process the same day. “To ensure a smooth transition of the ECB’s next leadership, the process for appointing her successor will start today,” Costa wrote on social media.

The Financial Times reported in February that Lagarde intended to leave before France’s presidential election in April 2027, which the ECB denied at the time. According to a source quoted by the newspaper, she wanted to make it easier for French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to agree on who will lead one of the EU’s most important institutions.

Lagarde, a former French finance minister, became ECB president in November 2019 after heading the International Monetary Fund from 2011.

World.title: UK Government aims to spend 3% of GDP on defense by 2030, Chancellor says, but not everyone's convinced
World.content:
UK Government aims to spend 3% of GDP on defense by 2030, Chancellor says, but not everyone's convinced

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 08:42 UTC Full article

Former Defense Secretary Dan Jarvis sets out Defense Investment Plan to MPs

The UK Government will aim to spend 3% of economic output on defense by 2030, and will plot a course for the target at next year's spending review, Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey has said. Work is underway to reach the target – and Britain's promise to NATO to spend 3.5% of GDP on defense by 2035 – in a “fiscally sustainable way”, the Chancellor said, indicating that raising defense spending further could in part come from making cuts elsewhere.

Mr. Healey's target of 3% by 2030 would fulfil a threshold he thought would be missed under Sir Keir Starmer's premiership, which sparked his resignation as defense secretary in June this year.

The announcement was welcomed by Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte, Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and the author of the Strategic Defense Review (SDR), Lord Robertson of Port Ellen.

Meanwhile, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch criticized his announcement as a “plan to have a plan”.

As he delivered his first Budget, the Chancellor told the Commons: “This year, our defense budget is £14bn higher than it was in the Conservatives’ last year of government.

”At the spending review next year, I confirm that I will set out the details of how we will meet our Nato commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defense by 2035, with a target date for 3% in 2030.And today I am getting work underway to get there in a fiscally sustainable way.“

Reaching the 3% target by the end of the decade is estimated by the Office for Budget Responsibility to cost an extra £17.3bn in 2029-30.

And Mr Healey hinted that reaching the commitment could come at the cost of spending elsewhere, telling MPs: ”That will include looking hard at public spending, as I have done to fund the Defense Investment Plan (DIP) today.But I am also determined to use more innovative financing, alongside the private sector and our international allies.“

Defense will rise to a 2.7% share of the economy by 2027 Mr Healey also committed at the Budget to ”fully funding“ a £4.7bn black hole in the Defense Investment Plan, left over by Sir Keir Starmer. The £4.7bn shortfall will be funded ”through reprioritization of capital budgets“, according to the published Budget document.

Departments across Government will be asked to reduce their capital budgets by 1% between 2027-28 and 2029-30 to raise some £3bn. The remaining £1.7bn shortfall will be made up from an “unallocated contingency in the Treasury’s capital reserve”.

The DIP, one of Sir Keir's final major announcements as prime minister, promised an extra £15bn of funding for the UK defense sector but only committed £10.3bn to it, leaving the rest for Mr. Healey to find. The extra cash means that government spending on defense will rise to a 2.7% share of the economy by 2027.

Responding to the Budget, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said Mr Healey had not met his pledge and was making troops unsafe.

Mrs Badenoch said: ”He should have set out a plan for 3% today. So, now he is the man who is increasing risk to personnel on operations; he is the man who is making our country less safe; he has failed his own test. This is on him and no-one will ever forget. If he had any decency he would resign again today.“

She added: ”What he's done is he’s given himself a bit of breathing space until next year. Instead, what we have is a plan to have a plan. I bet (Vladimir) Putin's really scared now.“

Budget reaction in the defense world One of the SDR authors and former Nato secretary general Lord Robertson of Port Ellen said: ”John Healey is acting in the national interest – and has done exactly what he said was needed for defense in his resignation letter, by setting a head-mark for 3% in 2030.

“I am strongly in favor of innovative ways of financing defense – and this is a credible route to get more into UK defense. Today’s announcements strengthen UK leadership in NATO once again.”

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey pressed the Government to push for a “European rearmament bank” which he said would “bring our allies together behind a shared vision of defence investment to protect our continent from Putin”.

Former defense secretary and Scots Guards officer Sir Ben Wallace was quick to criticize the Budget, highlighting the way he said it would affect people like Mr Healey's own son, who is a member of the Army Reserve.

Sir Ben posted on X: ”The MOD faces a real term cut to day-to-day spending of nearly 0.5% (RDEL) in 27/28.That's money we spend on training, ammunition, maintenance and operations. So the Chancellor's son in the reserves will have even less training and ammo.“

His comments were echoed by Afghanistan veteran Mike Martin, who said: ”The Chancellor has handed another year to Putin by deferring decisions to increase defense spending in today's Budget.

“The Government says we should prepare for war with Russia in three years, but is totally comfortable wasting one of those years standing still as it defers increasing defense spending until the next Spending Review.

”By then it will be 18 months since the Chancellor resigned as defense secretary over the Government's failure to reach 3% of GDP.”

Mr Healey also announced plans that will see the Government work with private and international finance. A defense finance taskforce is being set up ahead of next year’s spending review. (Forces.net by Sian Grzeszczyk Melbourne).

World.title: IMF expects Brazil to become the 8th largest economy in the 2027 ranking
World.content:
IMF expects Brazil to become the 8th largest economy in the 2027 ranking

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 08:33 UTC Full article

Brazil in 2026 figures as the tenth largest global economy

Brazil is expected to return to eighth place in the global GDP ranking for 2027, overtaking Russia and Italy, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and its World Economic Outlook report, released this month.

IMF points out that Brazil’s GDP, which measures the value of goods and services produced in the country, is expected to reach US$2.80 trillion next year. This year Brazil is expected to finish in tenth place. A trillion in 12 zeros.

Likewise for 2027, United States is expected to remain the world’s largest economy, followed by China, Germany, India, UK. Follows the IMF top ranking for next year,

1. United States: US$ 34.44 trillion

2. China: US$ 22.94 trillion

3. Germany: US$ 5.66 trillion

4. India: US$ 4.52 trillion

5. United Kingdom: US$ 4.49 trillion

6. Japan: US$ 4.47 trillion

7. France: US$ 3.65 trillion

8. Brazil: US$ 2.80 trillion

9. Italy: US$ 2.77 trillion

10. Russia: US$ 2.68 trillion

11. Canada US$ 2.63 trillion

According to the IMF’s projections, Brazil is expected to maintain that position through 2031, the final year covered by the forecast. Brazil’s highest position in the global GDP rankings was seventh, a ranking it held in 1995 and from 2010 through 2014.

The rising star. One of the highlights of the IMF’s forecast is India, which is expected to jump from sixth to fourth place, overtaking the United Kingdom and Japan. By 2031, India is projected to move into third place, ahead of Germany.

The United States and China are expected to retain the top two positions, in that order, through 2031.

World.title: Bolsonaro’s exit via Argentina further strains relations between Milei and Lula
World.content:
Bolsonaro’s exit via Argentina further strains relations between Milei and Lula

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 01:30 UTC Full article

Presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier said the government had “taken note of the result” of the Brazilian election but ruled out an official statement

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s transit through Argentina, after he left Brazil despite a court ban and flew to Miami from Puerto Iguazú following his election defeat, has opened a new front in the strained relationship between the governments of Javier Milei and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, while the Casa Rosada maintains its refusal to congratulate the Brazilian president on his re-election.

Argentina’s National Migration Directorate confirmed that Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters entered the country via the Tancredo Neves international bridge in Misiones province at 10.50 p.m. on Tuesday, with valid documents and “without any legal impediment”. About 40 minutes later they boarded a private plane belonging to Argentine company Baires Fly, which stopped in Guayaquil before reaching Miami. Brazilian Supreme Court Judge Alexandre de Moraes had ordered the senator to surrender his passports and barred him from leaving the country as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering. Bolsonaro will lose his parliamentary immunity in January when his term ends.

Presidential spokesman Adrián Ravier said the government had “taken note of the result” of the Brazilian election but ruled out an official statement, arguing that Lula did not congratulate Milei when he was elected in 2023. According to the newspaper Ámbito, Lula congratulated “the elected authorities” at the time, without naming Milei.

Bolsonaro’s departure fuelled suspicion in Argentina. According to La Nación, presidential adviser Santiago Caputo was in Misiones when the plane took off; the government has not commented on that report. Sources in the Misiones provincial government distanced themselves and said that if there had been an irregular operation by the migration agency or the Airport Security Police, it was up to the national government to explain. Opposition lawmakers filed a formal request for information in the Chamber of Deputies. In the letter he released from Miami, Bolsonaro thanked Milei for “his courage, his sense of justice and legality”, without specifying what he meant.

Bilateral relations are at one of their lowest points. Milei backed Bolsonaro during the campaign and called Lula a “thief” and a “jailbird”, prompting Brazil to recall its ambassador in Buenos Aires for consultations in July. Brazil is Argentina’s main trading partner.

The episode coincided with another Argentine government decision pointing in the opposite direction: the ruling party amended the sovereignty defence bill to narrow sanctions on companies linked to hydrocarbon exploitation in the Falklands, following objections raised by the United States.

World.title: “True president”, then “leader”: Bolsonaro’s letter from the United States
World.content:
“True president”, then “leader”: Bolsonaro’s letter from the United States

29th Thursday, October 2026 - 01:17 UTC Full article

In the letter, Bolsonaro says he did not flee but refused to submit to “political persecution” and judicial harassment

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who arrived in Miami on Wednesday after leaving Brazil despite a court ban, released a letter in which he presented himself as “the true president-elect of Brazil”, alleged “electoral fraud” without evidence and thanked Argentine President Javier Milei for his “courage”. About 30 minutes later the text was changed and Bolsonaro described himself instead as Brazil’s “leader”.

“I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the true president-elect of Brazil. First of all, I want to thank President Milei for his courage, his sense of justice and legality, and President Trump and the wonderful American people for welcoming me,” the first version read, shared by commentator Paulo Figueiredo and by the senator’s allies. According to the newspaper O Estado de S. Paulo, the text went through three versions. The first carried the coat of arms of the “Estados Unidos do Brazil”, which fell out of use in 1968, and was later corrected.

In the letter, Bolsonaro says he did not flee but refused to submit to “political persecution” and judicial harassment, and accuses Supreme Court Judge Cristiano Zanin, whom he calls “Lula’s former lawyer”, of making possible “a mathematical impossibility” by extending voting hours: that Lula gained more than ten million votes between the first and second rounds. The president went from 53.9 million votes on October 4 to 64.2 million on Sunday, in an election in which both campaigns focused on mobilising the roughly 33 million voters who abstained in the first round. The head of the Superior Electoral Court, Kassio Nunes Marques, appointed by the senator’s father, said on Monday that the extension did not alter the result.

Bolsonaro says he will lead the opposition from the United States and compares his departure with those of Charles de Gaulle, Rui Barbosa, José Martí, Juan Guaidó, Edmundo González and María Corina Machado. The State Department has granted visas to him and his family. President Donald Trump said on Monday that the Brazilian election “looked like another rigged election”.

Argentina’s National Migration Directorate confirmed that Bolsonaro entered the country via the Tancredo Neves bridge at Puerto Iguazú on Tuesday night, with valid documents and “without any legal impediment”, before flying to Miami on a private plane. The letter does not specify what the thanks to Milei refers to, and the Argentine government, which has also not congratulated Lula on his re-election, had not commented on it. Bolsonaro is under investigation at the Supreme Court for alleged money laundering, which he denies.

World.title: After a surprisingly strong start, Chipotle plans more restaurants in Nuevo León and Mexico City
World.content:
Chipotle, the U.S. fast-casual food chain inspired by Mexican and Tex-Mex food, plans to open more restaurants in Mexico after its first branch in the country exceeded expectations.

Mexico’s first Chipotle restaurant opened in July 2026 in the border state of Nuevo León, in the high-end municipality of San Pedro Garza García, part of the greater Monterrey area.

Alsea, a Mexican company that operates the U.S. brand, said it plans to open between three and four additional locations in Nuevo León during the first quarter of 2027, while also preparing for its entry into Mexico City that same year.

According to Alsea CEO Christian Gurría, the public’s positive response to the first restaurant exceeded the “honeymoon effect” associated with the initial excitement surrounding an opening.

“Now that our operation is consolidating and the flow of customers is stabilizing, we remain above [expectations],” Gurría said during a call with analysts cited by Bloomberg Línea.

Chipotle arrived in the country after other Tex-Mex food chains tried—and failed—to establish a market there, including U.S. fast-food mainstay Taco Bell, which attempted to expand into Mexico in the 1990s and the 2000s.

Gurría attributed the favorable reception of Chipotle to a combination of price, quality, and portion size. According to Bloomberg Línea, the bowls, burritos, and salads on the Mexican menu cost between 150 and 200 pesos (US $7.98 and $10.64).

The expansion of Chipotle is part of the renewal of Alsea’s portfolio in Mexico, which also includes preparations for the arrival of Raising Cane’s, a U.S. chain specializing in breaded chicken tenders. According to Gurría, the brand’s first branch is set to open in the first quarter of 2027.

Beyond Mexico, Alsea operates and develops restaurant and coffee shop chains in other parts of Latin America and Europe. Its portfolio includes brands such as Starbucks, Domino’s Pizza, Burger King, Vips, Chili’s, Italianni’s, P. F. Chang’s, and The Cheesecake Factory.

According to Alsea’s latest financial report cited by specialized media Merca 2.0, Starbucks remains one of its largest-scale operations with 1,983 coffee shops across 12 countries, including 976 located in Mexico.

The company operates more than 4,800 units across 12 countries, and trades on the Mexican Stock Exchange.

With reports from Bloomberg Línea and Merca 2.0

World.title: Mexico City Grand Prix: Everything to know for the year’s premier motor sports event
World.content:
Formula 1 — the world’s most popular motorsport series — is in Mexico City this week for the 21st race of its 2026 season.

Widely viewed as one of the most vibrant, high-energy and uniquely festive spectacles on the F1 calendar, the Mexico City Grand Prix is expected to attract 400,000 fans to the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez this weekend.

For most in Mexico, Guadalajara native Sergio “Checo” Pérez is the star attraction of this year’s F1 event and will be competing in his 10th Mexico City GP. Checo — who missed last year’s race after being released by Red Bull following the 2024 season — will be racing for Cadillac, a constructor in its first year of competition.

Helping make his return to his home country extra special, Cadillac announced on Wednesday that it had signed Checo to a contract extension, keeping the six-time Grand Prix winner with the team through the 2029 season.

Checo has another reason to celebrate. Sunday’s race will be his 300th F1 race, making him the seventh driver in history to reach that number. As if getting to achieve that milestone at home is not enough, Checo also made a special appearance in the capital on Wednesday.

Driving a modified Formula 2 car, Pérez rumbled along the Paseo de la Reforma avenue in front of an estimated 100,000 onlookers. He burned rubber while performing donuts near the Diana roundabout, then stopped at the Angel of Independence Monument to acknowledge the fans.

“I know some of you have been here since last ​night. I really appreciate it,” Checo told the crowd. “You guys are one of the main reasons I ​came back.”

The what, when and where of the F-1 weekend

For those planning on attending the F-1 race, the Hermanos Rodríguez circuit is inside the Ciudad Deportiva de la Magdalena Mixhuca public park located at the eastern terminus of the Viaducto Río de la Piedad (Viaducto Miguel Alemán). It can also be reached by Metrobus (Line 2) and Metro (Line 9).

Tickets are available via the Official Mexico GP Website, the Formula 1 Official Ticket Portal or through verified secondary resale markets like StubHub.

As for the event, drivers will take two practice runs on Friday, while the third practice run and qualifying take place Saturday.

The Mexico City GP, featuring 71 laps of the 4.3-kilometer (2.6-mile) track, begins at 2 p.m. Sunday.

Of note, Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli, 20, could become the youngest champion in series history by finishing in the top nine.

Also competing is five-time Mexico City GP winner Max Verstappen (2017, 2018, 2021, 2022, 2023). Sergio Pérez was Verstappen’s teammate from 2021 through 2024.

With reports from The Associated Press, Reuters, The Straits Times and Grand Prix 247

World.title: MND Local CDMX: Rent reforms, a viral Tesla crash and possible Cowboys game
World.content:
Mexico City is tackling a range of issues this week, from housing affordability and suspected dog poisonings to a dramatic car crash caught on camera. Meanwhile, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has teased a future NFL game in the capital, adding to the growing buzz around U.S. sports in Mexico.

Let’s get into it.

Morena’s housing bill aims to curb rent hikes and gentrification

The ruling Morena party and Mayor Clara Brugada put forth a framework on Oct. 22, aimed at stabilizing Mexico City’s ongoing housing rental affordability crisis.

Dubbed the Law on Tenant Relations and Fair, Reasonable and Affordable Rents, the reforms include capping rent increases, prohibiting excessive requirements to obtain a rental, creating an official government office tasked with handling tenant-landlord relations, and building more affordable housing.

In a news release, the administration said the bill is aimed at “curbing gentrification and guaranteeing the right to housing.”

According to the mayor’s office, roughly 2 million people rent their homes in the capital, representing a 54% increase over the past 15 years. Rent, meanwhile, “frequently exceeds 30% of the family income,” a benchmark set by the United Nations in 2020, with prices in some high-demand areas skyrocketing between 100% and 200% over the past decade.

Mexico City’s government already passed a 2024 law capping rent increases relative to inflation. However, the new legislation goes a step further, barring landlords from raising a property’s rent when it changes from one tenant to another. There is an exception for landlords who undertake significant renovations to a property.

Other reforms included in the legislation

A Bill of Rights protecting renters from excessive rental requirements and discrimination. A Tenant Relations Ombudsman tasked with providing free legal advice and resolving disputes. A Digital Registry of Contracts and a one-year lease requirement. A Social Support Office for Evictions, tasked with ensuring the eviction process is “peaceful and respects human dignity.” An affordable housing project that aims to build 80,000 new units alongside 120,000 improvement and expansion projects in low-income neighborhoods. A Public Housing Observatory tasked with monitoring land prices and rental prices across Mexico City’s 16 boroughs.

According to the International Business Times, Morena is gathering signatures for the bill, which it will present to the Mexico City Congress as a show of public support. The proposal is currently being considered by the joint Housing and Administration and Justice committees.

Authorities investigate suspected dog poisonings at Parque España

We reported on this in Mexico News Daily’s regular coverage. However, some stories are so important, we felt it prudent to reiterate here: Authorities are investigating suspected dog poisonings at Parque España in the capital’s Condesa neighborhood.

Simply put, if you or someone you know is a pet parent in the capital (cat walkers, we see you too), please be aware and spread the word.

In a news release published Oct. 27, the Attorney General’s Office of Mexico City announced it is launching an investigation and preventative measures after several dogs became fatally ill while spending time in the park, which features a popular off-leash dog area.

According to the AG’s office, the Citizen Security Ministry (SSC) was called to a nearby veterinary clinic that was treating the dogs. The SSC subsequently canvassed the park and found a blue pill wrapped in a piece of sausage. The pill, which is currently being investigated, has not been definitively linked to the suspected poisonings.

The case is being treated as potential animal abuse and cruelty. While the park is still open, the dog run and children’s areas were closed for cleanup.

“Citizens are urged to report any situation that could put the integrity of animals at risk to 911 or to the SSC Secretary’s Contact Unit, at telephone 55 5208 9898,” the Attorney General’s Office wrote in its news release, “as well as through the accounts @SSC_CDMX and @UCS_GCDMX.”

Tesla crash in affluent Mexico City neighborhood goes viral

A viral video of a shocking car crash in western Mexico City is making the rounds, roughly a week after the incident.

According to video obtained by U.S. media outlet TMZ, a Tesla careens off the road in Cuajimalpa, smashes through a gate and part of another structure before launching off a side patio and ultimately landing somewhere off-screen.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by TMZ (@tmztv)

A time stamp on the footage, taken from what appears to be a home surveillance video, dates the incident to Oct. 19. The incident occurred in Cuajimalpa’s affluent Lomas del Chamizal neighborhood.

International Business Times reports that the cause of the crash, as well as the condition of those involved, is unknown.

Dallas Cowboys tease future game in Mexico City

With the NFL’s first Mexico City series game of the season less than a month away, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones suggested his team could soon be coming to the capital.

During a post-game interview with ESPN’s John Sutcliffe on Monday, Oct. 26, Jones was asked, on a scale of one to 10, about the likelihood of the Cowboys playing at Mexico City’s Estadio Azteca (also known as Estadio Banorte).

“One,” Jones said several times before catching his mistake and changing his answer to an emphatic 10. “We’re coming,” he added.

Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott doubled down on the enthusiasm, telling Sutcliffe a game in Mexico City would be “exciting.”

“I know the atmosphere would be electric,” Prescott said. “Viva Mexico!”

U.S. sports have had something of a moment in Mexico as of late.

Ticket demand for the Nov. 22 Week 11 match-up between the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings was extraordinary, with some 840,000 fans registering to get a highly coveted seat, as Mexico News Daily previously reported.

Meanwhile, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver suggested last week that Mexico City could be considered for a future league expansion, telling the Pat McAfee Show, “It’s a shorter flight from New York to Mexico than from New York to Los Angeles, so you can see why we’d be interested.”

Drew Pittock serves as Mexico News Daily’s features director. He is based in Mexico City. Have an idea for a feature story or unique event in CDMX? Send an email to drew.pittock@mexiconewsdaily.com.

World.title: Mexico in Numbers: How does Mexico’s education system compare to other countries?
World.content:
Last week, we published Part 2 of the MND Mexico Well-being Series, which focused on eight education indicators, including expenditure on education as a percentage of GDP, average class sizes in primary and secondary schools and Mexico’s scores in the 2025 PISA tests.

This “Mexico in Numbers” article is a condensed version of that report — a concise presentation of the key data, complemented by visual features.

As we have previously noted, the MND Mexico Well-being Series — a collection of articles on a range of topics related to well-being — draws on the most recent internationally comparable data, as well as data from the past decade, to assess the state of well-being in Mexico today, and to see what has changed in Mexico during the eight years that the ruling Morena party has been in office.

Without further ado, let’s take a look at the key data from Part 2 of the series.

* The data in this article comes from the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Education at a Glance 2026 report and the OECD’s PISA 2025 Results report.

Early childhood education enrollment rates

Just 4% of two-year-olds in Mexico were enrolled in early childhood education programs meeting International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED) criteria in 2024, compared with an OECD average of 50%, placing Mexico last among 30 countries assessed.

Enrollment among children aged 3 to primary-school entry was 75%, versus an OECD average of 90%, ranking Mexico 42nd of 46 countries.

Both rates declined from 2015, when they stood at 5% and 79%, respectively, widening Mexico’s gaps with the OECD averages.

Expenditure on education as a percentage of GDP

Mexico’s government spent the equivalent of 2.9% of GDP on education in 2023, below the OECD average of 4.2%, ranking it 39th of 42 countries, or fourth-lowest.

Mexico’s spending on education fell from 4.4% of GDP in 2015 — when it matched the OECD average — a decline of 1.5 percentage points.

Educational attainment rates

In 2025, 40% of Mexicans aged 25–34 lacked an upper secondary qualification, down from 55% in 2015 but still well above the OECD average of 12%, leaving Mexico fourth-worst among 47 countries.

Tertiary attainment among the same age group rose from around 21% to 29% over the decade.

In 2025, 28% of young men and 30% of young women held tertiary qualifications — 12 and 24 percentage points below the respective OECD averages — ranking Mexico 39th of 45 countries for both sexes.

Teacher qualifications

In 2024, 82% of preschool teachers, 92% of primary teachers and 87% of lower secondary teachers in Mexico met national minimum educational attainment requirements. Mexico exceeded the OECD average only at primary level, by four percentage points, while trailing it by five points at preschool level and two points at lower secondary level.

All three rates declined between 2017 and 2024, falling by five, five and six percentage points, respectively.

Average class sizes in primary and lower secondary education

Mexico’s primary school classes averaged 23 students in 2024, while lower secondary classes averaged 25 — both two students above the respective OECD averages. Mexico’s classes were larger than those in 30 of 38 countries assessed at primary level and 27 of 38 at lower secondary level.

Since 2015, average primary class sizes increased by one student, while lower secondary class sizes fell by three.

PISA scores

Mexican 15-year-olds scored below OECD averages in all four areas assessed in PISA 2025: reading (408 points), science (414), mathematics (388) and computational problem solving (453), with gaps ranging from 47 to 75 points.

Mexico ranked equal 52nd of 90 countries and jurisdictions in reading, equal 63rd of 91 in science and equal 64th of 90 in mathematics.

Since 2015, Mexico’s average reading score fell by 15 points, its math score declined 20 points and its science score dropped two points. Nevertheless, the gaps between Mexico’s scores and OECD averages narrowed as OECD scores declined more sharply between 2015 and 2025.

Students’ exposure to bullying

In 2025, 19.5% of Mexican students aged 15 and 16 reported being bullied at school at least a few times a month, just below the OECD average of 19.6%. Mexico had the 38th-lowest bullying rate among 88 countries and jurisdictions.

Mexico’s bullying rate declined from 20.2% in 2015 — a fall of 0.7 percentage points — allowing it to move from above to slightly below the OECD average.

NEET rate

In 2025, 19% of Mexicans aged 18–24 were neither employed nor in education or training (NEET), five percentage points above the OECD average of 14%, giving Mexico the joint ninth-highest rate among 41 countries. The rate was 29% for young women, compared with 10% for young men.

Mexico’s overall NEET rate fell from 23% in 2015, narrowing its gap with the OECD average from seven to five percentage points.
