World.title: Poland and UK sign Warsaw Defence Plan to “deter Russian threats”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland and the United Kingdom have signed the Warsaw Defence Plan, an agreement to enhance their cooperation on security. The aim, says the British Ministry of Defence, is to “deter Russian threats”. The plan, which follows on from the two countries signing a strategic defence partnership earlier this year, will include joint development and production of defence technologies and military exercises in the Baltic Sea. The UK and Poland share a deep and historical defence partnership. Today, Defence Secretary @WesStreeting signed the Warsaw Defence Plan to bring our two nations’ Armed Forces and industries closer together and help ensure collective security in Europe. 🇬🇧🤝🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/IP98D1Qs1L — Ministry of Defence 🇬🇧 (@DefenceHQ) October 27, 2026 “Poland is one of the UK’s closest allies – from flying together in the Battle of Britain, to breaking the Enigma code, they have been a vital partner for our defence for nearly a century,” said British defence secretary Wes Streeting on a visit to Warsaw. “The new Warsaw Defence Plan honours this cooperation and sets out how we will continue to work together today, building a stronger Europe in a stronger NATO,” he added. His Polish counterpart, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, declared that “the Polish-British alliance has never been as strong as it is now”. Both he and Streeting also emphasised the importance of working together to support Ukraine. Among the aims listed for the plan are collaboration in the development and manufacture of next-generation air-defence missiles, as well as drones and counter-drone technologies. Earlier this year, Poland and the UK, along with Germany, France and Italy, agreed to jointly develop and procure air-defence systems, including missiles and drones. The Warsaw Defence Plan also pledges to “increase defensive maritime activity in the Baltic Sea through exercises and regional coordination, helping British and Polish forces protect vital lines of communication in the sea”. The two countries will also seek to build upon existing cooperation between their defence industries, including Poland’s purchase of CAMM-ER surface-to-air missiles and 100 launchers from MBDA and last year’s strategic partnership on ammunition production between Poland’s PGZ and Britain’s BAE Systems. Poland and the UK have signed a major new defence and security treaty. The agreement includes plans to jointly develop a new air-defence missile, hold large-scale military exercises, and cooperate on countering Russian hybrid attacks https://t.co/cXeYT2u1lw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 27, 2026 This week’s agreement builds upon the Northolt Treaty signed by Poland and the UK in May this year, under which the two countries agreed to cooperate more closely on security. Last year, Poland signed a similar agreement upgrading relations with France. That followed a strategic partnership agreement with Sweden the previous year. In April this year, Poland signed new comprehensive strategic partnership agreements with South Korea and Japan. This year, it has also deepened security ties with Canada and Norway. In November, Poland will host the first military exercises organised by the so-called Coalition of the Willing. Thousands of personnel from the UK, Poland, France and Germany will test operational readiness for a multinational force to secure a potential future Ukraine peace deal. World.title: US chooses Poland to host service facility for Patriot missiles
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The United States has chosen Poland to host a new centre for servicing and maintaining missiles used in Patriot air defence systems, in a decision described as “historic” by both Washington and Warsaw. It was chosen ahead of bids from four other European countries. The new centre, the first of its kind ot be located outside the US itself, will “dramatically shorten turnaround times and further secure critical supply lines”, said the US Department of War, announcing the decision on Tuesday. Undersecretary of War Michael P. Duffey added that the choice of a country on NATO’s eastern front “sends a clear message [that] the Alliance is united, serious about deterrence, and ready to back our words with action”. Poland Selected to Host Historic PAC-3 Missile Maintenance Facility, Strengthening Allied Burden-Sharing and Transatlantic Security – U.S. Department of War – Release | @DeptofWar https://t.co/2caqADRRx8 — US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) October 27, 2026 The decision was welcomed by Polish leaders, with defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz saying that it shows “Poland is a trusted ally and holds an extremely important place on the map of global security”. His deputy minister, Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, said that Poland was chosen ahead of rival bids from Germany, the Netherlands and Norway to host the facility. However, US ambassador to Poland Thomas Rose indicated that Sweden, not Norway, was the fourth candidate. Kosiniak-Kamysz and Sobkowiak-Czarnecka both pointed to the role President Karol Nawrocki had played in securing the deal. On many issues, the government is in conflict with the opposition-aligned president, but the two sides worked together on the Patriot bid. Historyczna decyzja! Centrum serwisowania pocisków PAC-3 do systemów Patriot powstanie w Polsce! 🇵🇱 O europejską lokalizację tej inwestycji rywalizowały cztery państwa, obok Polski – Niemcy, Holandia i Norwegia. Już na etapie składania wniosków polska oferta została oceniona… pic.twitter.com/wUgFhzlzUk — Magdalena Sobkowiak (@magdasobkowiak) October 27, 2026 Nawrocki, a conservative, is a close ally of his US counterpart, Donald Trump. The Polish president’s national security advisor, Bartosz Grodecki, claimed that it was “thanks to a conversation between” the two presidents that the new Patriot servicing centre was being established in Poland. The head of Nawrocki’s foreign policy office, Marcin Przydacz, meanwhile, thanked Washington for choosing Poland to host the new centre. “The Polish-American alliance and the good atmosphere in relations once again yield results,” he declared. “We can see what positive effects the President’s activity brings for Poland.” Poland is one of a number of European countries that operate Patriot air defence systems. Others include Germany, Greece, the Netherlands, Romania, Sweden and Ukraine. The new centre will service the PAC-3 missiles used in Patriot batteries. The competition to host the facility was announced in July, with the selection made by the US government in conjunction with American defence giant Lockheed Martin, the producer of missiles. In its press release, the Pentagon emphasised that, although Poland would host the new centre, its work would “be underpinned by robust, transatlantic industrial cooperation, with critical supply chain integration led by Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden”. Sweden will deploy Patriot air defence systems and around 100 accompanying military personnel to Poland later this year to protect the NATO logistics hub in the city of Rzeszów, which is the main conduit for aid to Ukraine https://t.co/cq9p7OVO7E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 6, 2026 Global demand for Patriot systems has risen significantly, with the United States expending at least 1,500 interceptors in its war with Iran, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Patriot systems have also been crucial in Ukraine’s defence against Russian ballistic missile attacks, although Ukraine’s supply of missiles is now almost entirely exhausted. After Trump recently suggested that he would authorise Ukraine to produce its own missiles, Poland offered to host any such factory, to ensure its security. However, today’s announcement concerns a site for maintaining and servicing, rather than producing, the missiles. Poland has proposed that, if the United States grants Ukraine permission to produce its own missiles for Patriot air-defence systems, the facility could be located on Polish territory to ensure its security https://t.co/jaQng5wtGg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 28, 2026 The decision cements Poland’s position as one of Washington’s most important security partners in Europe. War secretary Pete Hegseth has praised Poland as a “model ally”, noting that it has for years met NATO’s defence spending targets, unlike many other member states. Poland has also been a significant customer for US defence firms. Between 2021 and 2025, Poland was NATO’s biggest arms importer, with 44% of the equipment it purchased coming from American suppliers. Last year, Poland signed a $2 billion deal for the US to provide logistical support and training for Patriot systems. This year, it was announced that Polish state defence group PGZ would become the first European producer of American Barracuda-500M cruise missiles. Poland will become the first country in Europe to produce cruise missiles developed by US defence firm Anduril Industries The agreement will "transform the continent's defence industry", claims Anduril https://t.co/LPJnwOLfp2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 7, 2026 Warsaw is also currently lobbying for a new permanent US military base to be established in Poland, with the government and the president once again putting aside their differences to promote the idea. Last month, Nawrocki claimed that the proposed base, which he said would be called “Fort Trump”, was “confirmed”. However, Washington has not publicly announced any final decision. World.title: Germany’s economy minister hails Poland as “example of great success”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Germany’s economy minister, Katherina Reiche, has praised Poland as an “example of great success”, saying that it offers a model for other countries. Speaking at the fourth Polish-German Economic Forum in Warsaw, which she opened on Monday alongside Polish finance minister Andrzej Domański, Reiche highlighted the deepening trade ties between the two countries. She noted that bilateral trade last year exceeded €180 billion for the first time, up from €25 billion in 2000, reports Deutsche Welle. Germany has been Poland’s biggest trading partner for decades, although recent data suggest that China, for the first time in history, overtook Germany as Poland’s largest source of imports in July this year. Germany has also long been a major investor in Poland. But Reiche welcomed growing recent investments by Polish companies in Germany, which she said was helping to create jobs. Earlier this year, for example, Poland’s largest manufacturer of trains and trams, Pesa, announced the acquisition of German rival HeiterBlick as part of its efforts to expand its operations across Europe. Reiche noted that around 1,000 Polish companies have invested in Germany, while about 1,600 German companies have invested in Poland, reports Reuters. Poland’s largest manufacturer of trains and trams, Pesa, has announced the acquisition of German rival HeiterBlick as it seeks to expand its operations across Europe https://t.co/N1wE1aYL5m — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 12, 2026 Among leading German firms with a presence in Poland are carmakers Mercedes-Benz, which recently invested around €1 billion to build its first electric-only van plant there, which produces its Crafer vans at a plant near the city of Poznań. Reiche also pointed to Poland’s stellar economic performance since joining the European Union in 2004, noting that its GDP has grown by an annual average of 3.8% over that period – twice the EU-wide average. Poland’s economy is on the verge of becoming the 20th largest in the world, with the country hoping to become part of the G20. Meanwhile, Domański used his remarks at the Polish-German Economic Forum to warn Europe against repeating past mistakes as it confronts a rapidly changing geopolitical landscape. He said the continent faced a “unique” historical moment. “The world is changing faster than ever, and we are facing new geopolitical, strategic, and technological challenges.” Europe would need a strong economy and new sources of growth to meet those challenges, he added, warning against what he called “economic naivety” and urging Europe – and Germany in particular – not to return to its previous approach to Russia. “I would like to state this very clearly: Europe must learn from the past. Under no circumstances can there be a return to the previous approach toward Russia. Poland will never agree to that,” Domański said, noting that this position applied in particular to renewed use of Russian energy imports. “We will only be resilient once we are truly independent of external, unstable suppliers of raw materials,” he added, emphasising that Poland and Germany must “work together to modernise the European energy market, focus on technological change and bear security in mind”. Discussions focused on protecting and strengthening European industry’s competitiveness and economic security amid geopolitical challenges. “Today, we are facing the consequences of the fact that, in the past, competitiveness was often relegated to second, third or fourth place. Competitiveness took a back seat to other priorities, with the result that European industry now faces serious challenges,” said Domański. He proposed making competitiveness a core EU policy priority, cutting red tape, strengthening the single market, lowering energy costs, investing in strategic technologies such as AI, and tightening trade protections against unfair foreign competition. World.title: Witness testifies Polish president discussed “making money bringing girls” to hotel where they worked 20 years ago
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A former colleague of Polish President Karol Nawrocki from when he worked as a security guard in a hotel two decades ago testified in court that he told her it was possible to “make some extra money by bringing in girls”. She says she saw him escort a woman onto the premises. The testimony was given after the president himself sued the owner of a website that, just before last year’s presidential election, published claims that Nawrocki had been involved in procuring prostitutes while working at the luxury Grand Hotel in the town of Sopot. The court case began in September but, until now, hearings have been held behind closed doors. However, the judge decided that today’s session would be open to the public, with two former colleagues of Nawrocki giving evidence. The president himself is due to appear before the court in January. 🗣️ "Moją automatyczną oceną było, że to prostytutka i alfons." Nowe zeznania w procesie Karola Nawrockiego z wydawcą Onetu. Przed sądem stanęła była współpracowniczka prezydenta z sopockiego Grand Hotelu. pic.twitter.com/Cn6KyMSjcv — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 27, 2026 In May last year, less than a week before the second round of the election, in which Nawrocki was standing in a run-off against rival Rafał Trzaskowski, Onet, a leading news website, published an article titled “Karol Nawrocki and the secrets of the Grand Hotel”. It claimed, based on information provided by unnamed former colleagues of the future president, that he had “participated in bringing prostitutes for guests of the Grand Hotel in Sopot while working there as a security guard” almost 20 years earlier. Onet said that its interlocutors wished to remain anonymous for their own safety, but had expressed their willingness to testify in court if required. The revelations caused a major scandal, but were vigorously denied by Nawrocki, a conservative candidate aligned with the right-wing opposition, who called them a “pack of lies”. He then went on to narrowly defeat Trzaskowski in the election. Conservative presidential candidate @NawrockiKn says he will sue news website @onetpl for claims it published today that he procured prostitutes for clients at a luxury hotel when working there as a security guard. He called the report "a bunch of lies" https://t.co/WZ4rZWfFT1 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 26, 2025 Nawrocki then sued Ringier Axel Springer Polska (RASP), the Polish subsidiary of a German-Swiss media house that owns Onet, demanding an apology. RASP stood by Onet, saying that its reporting was “factual”. At today’s hearing, one of Onet’s sources, Natasza Geldon, who worked at the hotel in 2006 and 2007, was questioned. She said that, one evening, she had noticed Nawrocki leading a man and a woman into the hotel, before then taking only the woman into a lift and returning alone. This had struck her as unusual, because staff were not supposed to escort guests into the hotel, “let alone take them upstairs”, said Geldon, quoted by broadcaster TVP. “When Karol came back downstairs, I asked him what was going on,” continued the witness. “He said it was possible to make some extra money by bringing girls in, and asked if I wanted to join in.” Geldon refused the offer, telling the court that, “as a young girl, 19 years old, I had the impression that a pimp had been coming in with a prostitute”. However, when asked to confirm if she had seen prostitutes in the hotel, Geldon said: “I don’t know. It’s hard to say. It was just that one incident.” A second witness, Łukasz Franczak, described as a longtime friend of Nawrocki who worked alongside him in security at the Grand Hotel, also gave evidence on Tuesday after being called by Nawrocki’s legal team. He testified that there had been prostitutes in the hotel. However, he added that he had not heard of any organised operation to supply them to guests; nor had he witnessed Nawrocki procuring prostitutes or discussing payment for them, reported Onet from the hearing. Franczak’s testimony was welcomed by Nawrocki’s former national security advisor, Sławomir Cenckiewicz, who said that it showed that those making claims against the president have no evidence of his involvement in any wrongdoing. Oni się wszyscy teraz nakręcają jak szaleni, nie czytając tego co sami piszą na własnej stronie… No i dowiedzieli się dzisiaj, że w hotelach bywają prostytutki 🙂 A ja to wszystko czytam na bieżąco, a tam słynny Łukasz z Gdańska, ulubiony świadek-historyk Antka Dudka, i… https://t.co/9sKGZT4PpD — Sławomir Cenckiewicz (@Cenckiewicz) October 27, 2026 RASP’s lawyers have called for Nawrocki himself to testify in the case. The president’s legal team wanted him to provide his testimony in writing, according to Onet. But on Tuesday, judge Aleksandra Orzechowska ordered Nawrocki to give testimony directly – either in person or remotely – at the next hearing, which is scheduled for 18 January 2027, reports broadcaster TVN. World.title: Guitar Legend Carlos Santana to Return to Czech Republic in 2027
World.content:
Legendary guitarist Carlos Santana will return to the Czech Republic on July 22, 2027, for an outdoor concert in the Castle Gardens of Slavkov u Brna, near Brno.

The ten-time Grammy Award winner will perform as part of his Planet of Free Will Global Tour 2027, bringing more than five decades of music to the Czech audience.

Known for blending rock, blues, jazz and Latin rhythms, Santana has built a distinctive sound that has influenced generations of musicians and listeners.



His performance at the 1969 Woodstock festival helped establish him as an international star, while early albums such as Santana*(1969) and Abraxas (1970) produced classics including “Evil Ways,” “Black Magic Woman” and “Oye Como Va.”

Santana reached another career milestone with the 1999 album Supernatural, which featured collaborations with artists including Rob Thomas. The record became a global hit, spawning the singles “Smooth” and “Maria Maria” and winning nine Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year.

Over his career, Santana has received ten Grammy Awards and three Latin Grammy Awards. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998, received the Kennedy Center Honors and was ranked 11th on *Rolling Stone* magazine’s list of the 100 greatest guitarists of all time.

Despite his long career, Santana continues to release new music and perform internationally. His live shows are known for extended guitar solos, Latin-inspired rhythms and a mix of classic hits and newer material.

Tickets will cost CZK 2,000, plus booking fees.

General ticket sales start on October 30, 2026, at noon, through Ticketmaster and Ticketportal.

World.title: Prague Metronome Lets People Donate to Charity for Just 50 CZK
World.content:
Prague’s Metronome is taking on a charitable role through a new initiative that allows people to pay for a minute of illumination while supporting one of six nonprofit organizations.

The project, called Puls města (City Pulse), was launched by real estate company PSN, which operates the landmark on Letná Hill. Donations start at 50 Czech crowns, and participants can choose which organization they want to support.



The new initiative connects its lighting system with fundraising, allowing members of the public to contribute through the project’s website.

Six Colors, Six Charitable Causes

Each participating organization is represented by a different color. Red supports the Tereza Maxová Foundation for Children, while light blue represents the Kapka naděje (Drop of Hope) Endowment Fund.

Yellow is associated with Díky, že můžem, an initiative focused on civic engagement and democratic values. Pink represents Pink Crocodile, dark blue supports the AutTalk Endowment Fund, founded by Kateřina Sokolová, and green is dedicated to the Fund for Endangered Children.

Visitors can select a cause and make a contribution directly through the project’s website.

Donations Start at 50 CZK

Contributions range from 50 to 9,999 CZK. Regardless of the amount donated, each payment purchases exactly one minute of illumination. A larger contribution therefore does not extend the lighting time.

The website also displays the amount raised for each organization, allowing donors to follow the campaign’s progress. A virtual queue shows when each participant’s turn is scheduled, with the expected time provided after payment.

World.title: Prague’s Golden Eye to Host Japanese Brunch With Live Chef Demonstrations
World.content:
Prague’s Golden Eye bar at Fairmont Hotel is hosting a Japanese-inspired brunch combining traditional ceremonies, live sushi preparation, premium food and signature cocktails.

The afternoon will begin with Kagami Biraki, a traditional Japanese sake barrel-opening ceremony often associated with celebrations and new beginnings.



Guests will then be able to watch a live tuna carving, one of the event’s main attractions.

The programme will also include omakase bites, with chefs preparing sushi at a live station. Guests can pair the food with signature cocktails and a curated selection of wines throughout the afternoon.

A live DJ will provide the soundtrack, adding music to the Japanese-inspired dining experience.

The event is designed exclusively for adults, with tickets priced at CZK 7,900 per person. Full prepayment is required to secure a booking.

Reservations can be made through Golden Eye’s online booking page.

World.title: Hip-Hop Star Xzibit Coming to Prague’s Roxy on November 17
World.content:
West Coast rap legend Xzibit will perform at Prague’s ROXY on November 17, bringing his show featuring tracks from his latest album and some of his best-known hits.

Presented by Gotobeat and Enjoy Events, the show will feature music from *Kingmaker*, alongside career highlights including “X,” “Multiply,” “Paparazzi” and “What’s the Difference.”



Xzibit returns with new album Kingmaker

A major name in West Coast hip-hop since the 1990s, Xzibit built his reputation through his distinctive deep voice, forceful delivery and collaborations with some of the genre’s biggest artists.

His albums Restless, Man vs. Machine and Weapons of Mass Destruction helped establish him as one of the defining rappers of his generation. His work with Dr. Dre, Eminem, Snoop Dogg and Ice Cube further cemented his place in hip-hop, while his television career brought him to a wider audience as the host of MTV’s Pimp My Ride.

Released on May 16, 2025, Kingmaker marked Xzibit’s first solo studio album since 2012.

The 20-track record brings together established names and newer voices, with guest appearances from Dr. Dre, Ice Cube, Busta Rhymes, Ty Dolla $ign, Royce da 5’9”, Redman and B-Real.

The album combines the sound that made Xzibit famous with a more contemporary production style, reflecting on his decades in the music industry while introducing his work to a new generation of listeners.

World.title: From Takumi to Gonta, a New Chapter for Japanese Food in Prague
World.content:
For those craving a taste of Japan without leaving Prague, Takumi offers a chance to explore Japanese cuisine in the heart of the city.

Located behind Quadrio, near the moving head sculpture of Franz Kafka, the restaurant recently celebrated its first anniversary this September.

We spoke with co-owner Euntaek Kim about the restaurant’s history, his journey to Prague, and his latest project, Gonta, a Japanese tonkatsu restaurant.



From Korea to Prague

The Takumi franchise was founded in Düsseldorf, Germany, in 2007 by Haruhiko Saeki and Kenjiro Komatsubara. Kim and his business partner, Viet Hung Phung, later partnered with the founders to bring Takumi Ramen to Prague, opening their first branch on Senovážné náměstí in 2019.

Kim’s connection to the restaurant business began long before that. Before he moved to Prague, his uncle owned several Hanil restaurants in Vienna and planned to expand into the Czech market. This led Kim’s family to move to Prague in 2000, when he was just 12 years old.

Later, Kim and his sister took over the Hanil restaurant their parents had run. He eventually sold it to a Korean chef he had worked with for several years.

Over time, Prague became much more than a place to do business.

“Prague has become like my second home. After having lived here for almost 26 years, I feel connected to its culture as well as my own Korean culture. In business settings and everyday life, I always try to find a balance between both,” Kim says.

His decision to open a Japanese restaurant was driven by what he saw as a gap in Prague’s dining scene.

“I felt like something was missing in Prague. Previously, Asian cuisine was close to nonexistent here. I wanted to make a change,” he explains.

Since moving to Prague, Kim has noticed growing interest in Asian food and culture among local residents, reflecting the city’s changing culinary landscape.

Introducing Gonta, a Japanese Tonkatsu Restaurant

Kim’s latest project, Gonta, brings another Japanese specialty to Prague. Located at Jungmannova 750/34, near Můstek metro station, the restaurant focuses on tonkatsu, a Japanese dish made with breaded, deep-fried pork cutlets, typically served with rice and a tangy sauce.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Gonta Prague (@tonkatsugonta.prague)

“When people think about Japanese cuisine, most people tend to think of sushi or ramen. Tonkatsu is a delicious dish that has not yet reached Prague. I craved it a lot,” Kim says, explaining what inspired him to launch Gonta.

The restaurant is scheduled to open in October 2026, adding another option to Prague’s growing selection of Japanese dining spots.

World.title: Why October 28 Is a National Holiday in the Czech Republic
World.content:
October 28th is Czechoslovak Independence Day, marking the establishment of Czechoslovakia in 1918.

Although Czechoslovakia peacefully split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia in 1993, October 28 remains one of the most important dates in Czech history.

It commemorates the struggle for independence and the emergence of modern Czech statehood. It should not be confused with Czech Statehood Day, celebrated on September 28.



Why Czechoslovakia Declared Independence in 1918

Before 1918, the Czech lands and present-day Slovakia were part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

Bohemia, Moravia and part of Silesia belonged to the Austrian half of the monarchy, while Slovakia was part of Hungary. For decades, Czech and Slovak political leaders had sought greater autonomy and the right to determine their own future.

World War I, which began in 1914, weakened the empire and intensified nationalist movements. Food shortages, economic difficulties and growing public discontent increased support for an independent state.

Politicians working abroad played a crucial role in the independence movement. Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk, Edvard Beneš and Milan Rastislav Štefánik coordinated diplomatic efforts to win support from the Allied powers. France, Great Britain and the United States recognised the Czechoslovak National Council as a provisional government in 1918.

Czechoslovak legions also fought on several fronts during the war, including in France, Italy and Russia, helping draw international attention to the independence movement.

How Independence Was Declared

On October 18, 1918, Masaryk issued the Declaration of Independence of Czechoslovakia in the United States, known as the Washington Declaration. It outlined the ambition to establish a democratic state based on the right of the Czechs and Slovaks to self-determination.

The decisive events took place in Prague on October 28, as news spread that Austria-Hungary had agreed to armistice terms. Many people interpreted the reports as a sign that the empire was collapsing and gathered in public squares to celebrate.

The Czech National Committee took control and issued the first law establishing an independent Czechoslovak state. October 28 subsequently became the official date of its founding.

Who Founded the New State?

Masaryk became Czechoslovakia’s first president after independence. A philosopher, educator and politician, he had spent years persuading foreign governments to support the creation of a new state.

Beneš was instrumental in diplomatic negotiations and later served as foreign minister and president. Štefánik, a Slovak politician, astronomer and military officer, helped organise the Czechoslovak legions and strengthen cooperation between the Czech and Slovak independence movements.

Politicians working in Prague, including Alois Rašín, Karel Kramář and Antonín Švehla, also helped organise the transfer of power.

What Happened After 1918?

During the interwar period, Czechoslovakia became a parliamentary republic with one of Central Europe’s most developed industrial economies. However, tensions between its different national communities presented ongoing challenges.

In 1938, the Munich Agreement led to the loss of the Sudetenland. Nazi Germany occupied the Czech lands in March 1939, while Slovakia became a separate state aligned with Berlin. Czechoslovakia was restored after World War II but later came under communist rule.

The Velvet Revolution ended communist rule in 1989. On January 1, 1993, Czechoslovakia peacefully split into two independent countries.

World.title: Where to Celebrate Halloween in Prague: 6 Events for Children and Adults
World.content:
Prague will mark Halloween 2026 with events for children and adults, ranging from pumpkin carving and lantern parades to costume competitions and late-night club parties.

Here are some of the events planned across Prague, including admission prices where available.

Blackout Halloween Rave at SaSaZu

Blackout Events will hold its first Halloween rave on Tuesday, October 27, at SaSaZu, bringing hard techno, Halloween costumes and stage productions to the Prague club.

The lineup includes WYNTER at 9 p.m., HOOOR at 10:30 p.m., A.N.I. at midnight, NOTMYTYPE at 1:30 a.m. and KLAR at 3 a.m. The event is scheduled to finish at 4 a.m.

An afterparty will follow at Club Mecca in Holešovice from 3 a.m. The event is restricted to visitors aged 18 and over. Organizers say further program details will be published on Blackout Events’ Instagram account.

Halloween at Hybernia Theatre

Hybernia Theatre, near Náměstí Republiky, is also listed as a venue for a Halloween electronic music event. The program is set to combine electronic music, Halloween decorations and the historic theatre’s interior.

Italian DJ SPADA is announced as a special guest. Admission is listed at CZK 499, although the event date should be confirmed with the organizer before publication.

Spooks at Žluté lázně

Žluté lázně in Podolí will host a Halloween afternoon on Saturday, October 31, from 1 p.m. to 7 p.m.

Children can follow a spooky trail featuring a spiderweb tunnel, a mysterious castle and a series of challenges. The program will also include pumpkin carving, face painting and dancing.

The organizers will announce the winner of the best-costume competition at 6:10 p.m. Admission costs CZK 150, while children wearing costumes can enter for free. Pumpkins for carving will be available for CZK 100.

Halloween Among Dinosaurs at DinoPark Harfa

DinoPark on the rooftop of Galerie Harfa will offer Halloween activities on Saturday, October 31, including a trail where children can complete tasks among the dinosaurs.

The afternoon program will feature Stegoušek Kvído, a walking dinosaur character who will lead two lantern parades, at 4 p.m. and 5 p.m. Visitors should bring their own lanterns.

DinoPark will be open from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Children in Halloween costumes can enter for CZK 50.

Pumpkin Carving at the Public Transport Museum

The Public Transport Museum in Střešovice will combine Halloween activities with a look at Prague’s historic trams and buses on Saturday, October 31.

Visitors can carve pumpkins and explore the museum’s collection of historic vehicles. Those arriving in costume will receive a gift.

At 4:45 p.m., the carved pumpkins will be lit in the museum courtyard. The museum will be open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Bloody Sexy Halloween Returns to SaSaZu

Bloody Sexy Halloween will return to SaSaZu on Friday, October 30, and Saturday, October 31, for two nights of music, performances and themed productions.

Founded in 2009, the event has become one of the region’s established Halloween parties, attracting more than 4,000 visitors in previous editions, according to the organizers.

One of the weekend’s main attractions is the Bloody Sexy Costume Contest. Participants can register at SaSaZu between 9 p.m. and midnight. Costumes are judged on creativity, originality and presentation, with the winner selected by audience applause at midnight and awarded CZK 40,000.

World.title: Thirty Seconds to Mars to Play Prague in 2027 With Special Album Tour
World.content:
Thirty Seconds to Mars will return to Prague on May 18, 2027, for a concert at the O2 arena.

The Jared and Shannon Leto-led band will revisit two of its best-known albums, A Beautiful Lie and This Is War, as part of a special world tour.

The American rock band will perform without an opening act, with the show expected to last approximately two hours. Tickets start at CZK 1,500, excluding ticketing fees, and VIP packages will also be available.



The concert is part of the band’s A Beautiful Lie vs This Is War tour, which focuses on two records that helped establish Thirty Seconds to Mars as a major name in alternative rock.

Tickets will be available through Ticketmaster and Ticketportal from October 30, 2026, at 10 a.m. Fan club members will have access to a presale beginning October 27 at 10 a.m. Live Nation, Spotify and O2 presales will follow on October 29 at 10 a.m.

Two albums that defined the band’s sound

Released in 2005, A Beautiful Lie marked a turning point in the band’s career, bringing its music to a much wider international audience. The album features some of Thirty Seconds to Mars’ best-known songs, including The Kill, From Yesterday and the title track.

The follow-up, This Is War, arrived in 2009 and expanded that sound. Tracks such as Kings and Queens, This Is War and Closer to the Edge became signature songs, helping the band reach a broader audience.

From alternative rock to global tours

Led by brothers Jared Leto, the band’s vocalist, and Shannon Leto, its drummer, the group continued to develop its sound on Love, Lust, Faith and Dreams in 2013 and America in 2018. The latter included the singles Walk on Water and Rescue Me.

In 2023, the band released its sixth studio album, It’s the End of the World but It’s a Beautiful Day, exploring a different musical direction while maintaining its focus on melody and emotional themes.

The band has also received several MTV awards and a Billboard Music Award. Its touring history includes a Guinness World Records recognition for the longest concert tour.

The 2027 tour will take Thirty Seconds to Mars across Europe, the United Kingdom, South Africa and other destinations. Its Prague stop will bring the band’s anniversary celebrations and catalogue of established hits to the Czech capital for a show centred on two of its most influential albums.

World.title: Ryanair expands in Budapest – but what could come next for the rest of Hungary?
World.content:
Ryanair is adding a 12th aircraft to its Budapest base and operating 54 routes this winter. But could lower airport charges help bring more flights to other parts of Hungary?

Ryanair is expanding its operations in Budapest with a record winter schedule, but the airline believes Hungary could attract considerably more passengers if airport costs became more competitive. At a press conference in the capital, the airline’s chief marketing officer also faced questions about its approach to regional airports and the possibility of exploring more of Hungary beyond Budapest.

Ray Brown of Magyar Minute attended the event at Hotel Vision Budapest, where he heard details of Ryanair’s latest expansion before sitting down with Dara Brady for a one-to-one conversation. With support from Daily News Hungary, Brown also explored what the airline’s plans could mean for travellers and the country’s wider aviation market.

Ryanair adds a 12th aircraft to its Budapest base

Ryanair’s winter 2026 schedule includes 54 routes from Budapest, supported by the addition of a 12th based aircraft. The airline says its annual passenger traffic in Hungary stands at around six million.

According to the company’s announcement, its Hungarian operations support more than 4,800 jobs, including 360 pilot and cabin crew positions. These figures cover employment supported by the airline’s activities, rather than exclusively new jobs created by the latest expansion.

However, Ryanair argues that Hungary could handle substantially more air traffic if its operating environment became more attractive.

If you missed it: Ryanair expands Budapest base, but warns Hungarian government

Why airport charges matter to Ryanair’s plans

A central theme of the conversation was the cost of operating flights from Hungary. Ryanair has called for lower airport charges, arguing that more competitive costs could help the country attract additional passengers and support further growth.

The airline estimates that Hungary could handle more than ten million passengers annually under a more competitive cost structure. That would mean roughly four million additional passengers compared with its current traffic levels.

This is a potential growth scenario put forward by Ryanair, not a commitment to introduce a specific number of new routes. The airline’s argument is that lower costs could make additional capacity commercially viable.

The background to Ryanair’s tax dispute

The discussion also touched on Ryanair’s legal dispute with Hungarian authorities over the airline’s handling of the special aviation contribution introduced in 2022.

Ryanair challenged a HUF 300 million consumer-protection fine, worth approximately EUR 750,000 at the time. Hungary’s Supreme Court, the Kúria, ruled in the airline’s favour in the case concerning the disputed passenger information.

However, the scope of the ruling is important. The court did not examine whether the contractual clause Ryanair used to pass the tax on to passengers was lawful. Its decision therefore should not be interpreted as a general ruling that the tax itself or the airline’s contractual arrangements were illegal.

Hungary abolished the aviation contribution separately, with the change taking effect in January 2025. Airport charges are a distinct operating cost and remain central to Ryanair’s calls for a more competitive aviation market.

Stay up-to-date with Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Could Ryanair expand beyond Budapest?

For travellers, one of the most interesting questions is whether the airline sees opportunities outside the capital. Brown raised the issue of regional airports during his conversation with Brady.

No new regional service was announced during the discussion. Nevertheless, the question highlights a broader issue for Hungary’s tourism sector: whether more competitive aviation costs could help spread international travel opportunities beyond Budapest.

Regional connections could offer visitors a more direct way to reach destinations elsewhere in the country, while potentially bringing additional tourism revenue to areas beyond the capital. For now, however, any such expansion remains a possibility rather than a confirmed part of Ryanair’s plans.

Where would you spend 48 hours in Hungary without Budapest?

The conversation ends with a question for travellers: if you had just 48 hours to explore Hungary but had to leave Budapest off your itinerary, where would you go?

From historic towns and wine regions to lakeside destinations and countryside escapes, Hungary offers plenty of alternatives for visitors willing to venture beyond the capital. Whether airlines can make those destinations easier to reach is another question – and one that could become increasingly relevant if Hungary’s regional aviation market grows.

Watch the Magyar Minute video for Brown’s conversation with Dara Brady and a closer look at Ryanair’s plans for Hungary.

World.title: 18+: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian railway station kills 14, including train passengers
World.content:
A Russian drone strike hit a railway station in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro on Thursday, killing 14 people and injuring another 14, including an 11-year-old boy who is among six people in serious condition.

The attack struck a platform where a civilian passenger train travelling between Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia was waiting, Ukrainian authorities said. Emergency services, police and medical teams rushed to the scene to help the victims and document the aftermath, Ukrainska Pravda reported.

According to Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration, 13 of the injured people have been taken to hospital. All six seriously injured victims suffered multiple shrapnel wounds. A 40-year-old man had both legs amputated, while doctors are fighting to save the lives of other victims.

Four drones launched in attack on Dnipropetrovsk region

The Ukrainian Air Force said Russian forces launched four jet-powered drones against the Dnipropetrovsk region at around 11 AM on Thursday. Ukrainian air defences shot down three of them, while the fourth struck the railway station in Dnipro.

The attack hit the platform where train No. 866, operating between Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia, was standing. Borys Filatov, the city’s mayor, confirmed that a civilian passenger train had been struck.

“Dnipro has suffered a tragedy. A drone hit a civilian commuter train. Many people have been killed. Many have been injured,” Filatov said.

Ukrzaliznytsia, Ukraine’s state railway operator, confirmed the strike and said an air-raid warning had been issued before the attack. However, a significant number of people were still on the platform when the drone hit.

Filatov urged people not to describe such attacks merely as damage to infrastructure, saying: “This is a genocidal war. Have the guts to say things as they are.”

Russian attacks increasingly target Ukraine’s railways

The number of Russian attacks on Ukrainian railway infrastructure is growing. According to Ukrzaliznytsia, around 1,700 railway facilities have been hit since the beginning of 2026. The attacks have damaged 120 passenger carriages, 304 locomotives and 43 railway stations.

During the same period, 50 railway employees have been killed while on duty, the company said, according to Telex.

Ukraine has tightened railway safety measures in response to the attacks. Passengers are required to leave trains when air-raid alerts are issued, adding significant delays to journeys.

The Dnipro–Odesa route has experienced delays of between five and 12 hours, according to Russian independent news outlet Meduza.

Police officers, rescue workers and medical teams remain involved in the response to Thursday’s attack, as authorities assess the damage and assist those affected.

World.title: Hungary and US sign two cooperation deals on energy infrastructure and law enforcement
World.content:
Hungary and the United States have signed two cooperation agreements covering regional oil and natural gas infrastructure and law enforcement against crimes committed by radical organisations, Foreign Minister Anita Orbán announced on Thursday following talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington.

In a post on Facebook, Orbán said the first agreement, called the Trump Peace Pipelines Framework, would strengthen cooperation on developing regional natural gas and oil infrastructure.

The second agreement aims to reinforce law enforcement cooperation and information-sharing between the two countries in connection with crimes committed by radical organisations, further deepening bilateral work in domestic affairs and public security.

Anita Orbán and Marco Rubio. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Anita

If you missed it: Could Viktor Orbán become UN Secretary-General? Trump administration reportedly wants him to

Rubio highlights fight against far-left terrorism

Rubio also commented on the agreements, saying the two governments were aligned in their efforts to tackle what he described as a resurgence of far-left terrorism.

“We are aligned in taking steps together in our governments to confront this resurgence of far-left terrorism, which is something that has been ignored for far too long,” the US secretary of state said, referring to a subject he had also discussed earlier this year.

His remarks underline the US administration’s emphasis on joint action against politically motivated violence, while the Hungarian foreign minister’s announcement focused on the agreements’ energy and law enforcement provisions.

SECRETARY RUBIO on AGREEMENTS WITH HUNGARY: We are aligned in taking steps together in our governments to confront this resurgence of far-left terrorism, which is something that has been ignored for far too long and something I spoke about earlier this year. https://t.co/whGEpDZk1X — Department of State (@StateDept) October 29, 2026

Stay up-to-date with Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Talks held behind closed doors in Washington

Orbán met Rubio at 4 PM Hungarian time on Thursday. The meeting was held behind closed doors, with the press excluded. US Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs Allison M. Hooker and Under Secretary of State for Arms Control and International Security Thomas G. DiNanno also attended.

The meeting had originally been scheduled for Tuesday but was postponed until later in the week. The two sides had already agreed to hold the talks at a later date.

Rubio visited Budapest in February, when he met Viktor Orbán, Hungary’s prime minister at the time, and expressed the US administration’s support for him.

Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar later invited Rubio to attend the 23 October commemorations in Hungary, but the US secretary of state ultimately did not attend the event.

World.title: Viktor Orbán reported to police over controversial speech about ‘handing out appropriate tools’
World.content:
Hungary’s National Bureau of Investigation has confirmed receiving a criminal complaint against former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán over remarks about distributing ‘appropriate tools’ for resistance. Authorities are now examining the complaint, but it’s unclear whether a criminal investigation will follow.

Hungary’s National Bureau of Investigation (NNI) has confirmed that a criminal complaint has been filed against former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán over controversial remarks he made at a gathering of the Digital Civic Circles (Digitális Polgári Körök, DPK) in Lakitelek earlier this month.

According to Hungarian broadcaster ATV, the authorities are currently examining the contents of the complaint as part of a preliminary procedure to supplement it. It is not yet known whether a formal criminal investigation will be launched or what suspected offence, if any, it would concern.

Orbán’s comments triggered a strong reaction from Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who accused his predecessor of referring to an armed uprising and the violent overthrow of Hungary’s constitutional order.

If you missed it: Vučić allegedly considered a coup after election defeat – Did Orbán help stop him?

What did Orbán say at the Lakitelek event?

At the DPK gathering in Lakitelek on 18 October, Orbán was asked about the ‘national resistance’ he had previously called for against the Tisza-led government.

The former prime minister responded that the country was not yet in a suitable state for such resistance, but his own camp was ready.

“Our country is not yet in a state suitable for this. We already are. We could hand out the appropriate tools here, whoever gets what, blunter or sharper – that is not the question,” Orbán said.

The remarks drew attention because of the reference to distributing tools of varying sharpness. Magyar subsequently argued that the comments amounted to a reference to armed rebellion and the violent alteration of the constitutional order.

Stay up-to-date with Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Magyar accuses Orbán of referring to armed rebellion

Magyar reacted to the remarks on social media on the same day, citing provisions of Hungary’s Criminal Code concerning crimes against the constitutional order.

He pointed to legislation under which acts directly aimed at violently changing Hungary’s constitutional order, or threatening to do so, can carry prison sentences of five to 20 years or even life imprisonment. Preparatory acts intended to facilitate such a crime can also be punishable by one to five years in prison.

Orbán had previously called for ‘national resistance’ and a fight against the Tisza government at political events in Tusnádfürdő over the summer and at the Kötcse gathering in September. He claimed that Hungary was facing a new form of colonialisation under the new administration.

Police confirm complaint after fresh media inquiry

ATV first contacted the National Police Headquarters (ORFK) on 21 October to ask whether a complaint had been filed over Orbán’s comments. At that point, the authorities said no proceedings had been initiated in the matter by the time they responded.

The broadcaster sent a further inquiry earlier this week to establish whether the situation had changed.

In its latest response, the National Bureau of Investigation confirmed that the complaint had arrived at the office and that its contents were being examined as part of a procedure to supplement the complaint.

World.title: Budapest to Prague in just 3 hours? Magyar announces push for V4 high-speed railway after talks with Babiš
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar and his Czech counterpart Andrej Babiš have pledged closer cooperation on energy, migration and transport, while Magyar delivered a sharp response to speculation about Viktor Orbán becoming the next UN secretary-general.

Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar described himself as an “easygoing guy” after holding the first-ever joint Czech-Hungarian government meeting in Prague on Thursday. Speaking alongside Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš, Magyar stressed that the two countries wanted to focus on practical cooperation rather than their political differences.

The talks covered energy security, migration, European Union affairs and plans for a high-speed railway connecting the Visegrád Four (V4) countries. Magyar also took the opportunity to criticise his predecessor, Viktor Orbán, over reports that the former Hungarian prime minister could be considered for the post of UN secretary-general.

Photo: MTI

‘I’m an easygoing guy’, Magyar says

Asked about his approach to cooperation with Babiš, Magyar said he was interested in Hungarian interests rather than ideological debates.

“I’m an easygoing guy. I’m interested in the interests of Hungarians,” he said, adding that he wanted to discuss concrete issues with international partners instead of focusing on subjects that divide them.

Babiš, who previously enjoyed a close relationship with Orbán, said he represented the interests of his own country and respected the choices made by other nations. He praised Magyar’s strong electoral mandate, saying he envied the Hungarian prime minister for winning such a decisive victory without needing coalition partners.

Magyar welcomed the renewed momentum behind the V4, which brings together Hungary, Czechia, Poland and Slovakia. He said cooperation between the four countries could strengthen their position in the European Council, particularly on energy and migration.

Magyar mocks prospect of Orbán leading the UN

One of the most striking exchanges came when CNN asked Magyar how he would react if US President Donald Trump backed Orbán for the UN secretary-general position.

“If someone wants to destroy the UN, take an Orbán – that would be a good start,” Magyar said.

He acknowledged that the international organisation had shortcomings but rejected the idea that it was a criminal organisation. He also referred to alleged criminal cases involving former members of Orbán’s government as part of his criticism.

The comments followed reports that Orbán’s candidacy had been discussed in US political circles. However, no confirmed appointment or selection has been announced, and the process for choosing the next secretary-general remains ongoing.

High-speed railway could connect Budapest and Prague in three hours

Transport and energy cooperation also featured prominently in the talks. Magyar said the two governments wanted to turn broad commitments into concrete projects, including encouraging energy companies to invest in each other’s countries.

The leaders also discussed a proposed high-speed railway linking the V4 capitals. Magyar said the route could eventually cut travel time between Budapest and Prague to around three hours, while a Budapest–Warsaw journey could take approximately five hours.

The project could cost more than €10 billion, and the four countries want to secure substantial funding from the EU’s next seven-year budget. Hungary and Czechia also signed a memorandum on transport cooperation, including railway investment.

Prague. Source: Pixabay

Hungary hopes to end daily €1 million EU fine

Magyar also confirmed that the Hungarian budget contains no allocation for the daily €1 million EU penalty imposed over the country’s migration policy.

He said he hoped Hungary could secure an exemption before the end of the year. Babiš also criticised the fine, calling it absurd that Hungary should pay for protecting its borders against illegal migration.

The Czech government is expected to visit Budapest in the spring for the next bilateral government meeting, with both leaders expressing confidence that closer cooperation could deliver tangible benefits for their countries.

World.title: Spar turns to Brussels again: ‘Euphoria about Hungary’s new government proved unfounded’
World.content:
The Austrian parent company of supermarket chain Spar has urged the European Commission to intervene, accusing Hungary of systematically discriminating against foreign retailers despite hopes of a fresh start under the new government.

Spar’s Austrian parent company has renewed its call for the European Commission to take action against Hungary over the retail sector’s special tax, which the government has no plans to abolish. The company’s leadership has expressed disappointment with the new administration, arguing that recent changes have failed to address what it sees as unfair treatment of foreign supermarket chains.

According to Austrian newspaper Die Presse, Hans Reisch, head of Spar’s Austrian parent company, has written to the European Commission again, urging it to intervene in the dispute. He reportedly described the government’s retail policy changes so far as a smokescreen and said he had little confidence that the sector-specific tax would be scrapped any time soon.

Spar calls for EU infringement proceedings

Reisch claims that foreign retail chains continue to face systematic discrimination in Hungary and argues that the government is unwilling to establish a level playing field for domestic and international businesses.

The company believes the European Commission should therefore launch infringement proceedings against Hungary over its retail taxation policy.

The dispute centres on the special retail tax, which will remain in place under the government’s plans for the 2027 budget. The highest tax band, applying to the portion of the tax base exceeding HUF 50 billion (approximately €125 million), will continue to carry a rate of 4.5%.

‘Euphoria about the Magyar government proved unfounded’

Peter Manhartsberger, a director at Spar’s Austrian parent company, voiced his frustration in an interview with Die Presse.

“Unfortunately, the euphoria surrounding the Magyar government proved unfounded,” he said.

Manhartsberger also pointed to the government’s plans to abolish the mandatory retail margin cap while retaining the special tax. In his view, the tax represents a considerably greater financial burden for the company.

Stay up-to-date with Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Dispute costs Spar €130 million a year

According to Manhartsberger, the two measures together cost Spar around €130 million annually. Of this amount, approximately €90 million is attributable to the special retail tax, while the margin cap accounts for a further €40 million.

The figures illustrate the scale of the financial dispute between the supermarket group and the Hungarian government. With the special tax set to remain in place in 2027, Spar’s Austrian parent company is once again turning to Brussels in an effort to secure a change in policy.

World.title: Portuguese man brutally assaults Hungarian partner’s stepfather in their home
World.content:
A Portuguese man who travelled to Hungary to visit his partner following the birth of their child is facing prison after allegedly beating her stepfather so severely that the victim required life-saving surgery.

Came to witness the dawn of life, almost took one

According to the indictment, the defendant, a Portuguese national living in the Netherlands, came to Hungary to see his partner, who had temporarily returned to her home country for the birth of their child. She was living in a village in Borsod County with her mother and stepfather.

During the visit, the defendant and the older man began drinking together in the kitchen. They communicated through gestures as they didn’t speak each other’s language, but the situation eventually deteriorated into a loud argument. The Portuguese man allegedly slapped his partner’s stepfather, and the two began fighting before the victim was pulled to the ground.

The Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén County Chief Prosecutor’s Office has brought charges of attempted murder over the incident, which took place in October 2024. Prosecutors say the victim’s survival was down to chance, as the assault carried a genuine risk of life-threatening injuries.

The attacker even smashed a car window with a shovel

The confrontation briefly subsided when the victim and the woman’s mother went outside and got into a car. However, the defendant followed them. He allegedly threw a sack of corn at the vehicle’s windscreen before threatening, through gestures, to cut the older man’s throat.

The victim got out of the car and attempted to keep the Portuguese man at a distance using a shovel with a handle approximately 1.5 metres long. The defendant wrested the tool from his hands and used it to smash the car’s rear window.

The woman’s stepfather then tried to flee, but the defendant caught up with him in the yard. Prosecutors allege that he punched the victim repeatedly in the head with considerable force. After the man fell to the ground, the attacker continued kicking and stamping on him, including striking him in the ribs.

Stay up-to-date with Hungary Weekly Briefing: subscribe on Substack!

Only the police could stop him, prosecutors seek prison sentence

The assault only stopped when police arrived after being alerted by family members. The victim was taken to hospital by ambulance, where he underwent emergency surgery followed by further surgical treatment. Prosecutors say there was a realistic possibility that he could have suffered life-threatening injuries, and that his death was prevented only by chance.

The Portuguese man has no previous criminal record. Nevertheless, prosecutors have requested a prison sentence and a ban on holding public office. They have also asked the court to rule that he should not be eligible for parole. The case will now proceed through the Hungarian judicial system.
