World.title: Iraq’s Development Road to provide million job opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The designs for the Development Road project have reached their final stages and will be fully completed before the end of 2026, according to the Iraqi Ministry of Transport.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Transport, Ali al-Khalidi, said that the Development Road project is expected to generate approximately 100,000 job opportunities during its first phase.

Plans include the construction of modern stations, industrial zones, and residential areas along the route, developments that could potentially create over a million jobs as the project and its associated facilities expand, according to al-Khalidi.

The Iraqi official explained that 95 percent of the project’s railway designs have been completed, with 92 percent of the highway designs finished, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Extending from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, with both the highway and railway being parallel lines, the first phase of the project is expected to be completed in 2033.

The Development Road’s primary objective is to transport goods from al-Faw Grans Port to Turkey—and onward to Europe—and vice versa.

Work is currently underway to finalize an agreement with Turkey to establish a fund that would finance the project’s implementation by Turkish companies through an oil-for-financing arrangement, according to INA.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

World.title: Norway’s DNO considers exporting Iraqi Kurdistan oil via Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Norwegian oil producer DNO is actively exploring routes through Syria to export its Iraqi Kurdistan crude oil to the Mediterranean.

According to Reuters, the initiative aims to bypass local market constraints and fetch significantly higher international benchmark prices.

DNO has been selling oil from its Tawke and Peshkabir fields to the local market at low prices. Although its domestic sales price increased somewhat to $45 per barrel in October 2026 compared to an average of $38.50 in the third quarter, it is still significantly below global benchmarks.

Due to the Syrian civil war, transport to the Mediterranean through Syria was previously impossible. However, regional logistics are shifting. Significant volumes of southern Iraqi fuel oil and crude are already being transported by tanker trucks directly through Syria for export.

Reflecting past delays in payments from the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), DNO requires international buyers to deposit US dollars into its offshore accounts before any oil is collected.

While trucks would be necessary for short-term movements, long-term solutions would encounter infrastructural obstacles.

Despite prior political support from the United States to study the route, rebuilding a key Iraq-Syria oil pipeline may cost around $15 billion and take years to become fully operational.

DNO is stepping up its drilling operations to increase the gross output from its important Kurdish licenses, which averaged 77,621 barrels of oil per day in the third quarter of 2026.

World.title: Iraq, Syria discuss exporting two million bpd of oil via Baniyas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa discussed on Wednesday the development of economic and security cooperation, particularly the export of Iraqi oil through Baniyas with a capacity up to two million barrels per day.

The discussions took place during the first visit by an Iraqi prime minister to Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime in late 2024. The visit marks a step toward strengthening relations between the two countries, which share a border stretching over 600 kilometers.

The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement that the meeting addressed increasing trade exchange and developing the agricultural sector to achieve food and economic integration, in addition to discussing oil exports via Syria’s Baniyas port.

However, the statement did not mention when the route will start operating at the specified capacity.

Al-Zaidi highlighted initiatives to develop partnerships in the social and economic domains, boost security cooperation, and coordinate stances on regional and global concerns.

The Syrian Presidency said that the extended discussions in Damascus covered approaches to promote security, economic, and commercial cooperation, as well as regional and international developments.

Iraq started earlier exporting limited quantities of oil through the Syrian port of Baniyas—a move prompted by disruptions of maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the conflict in the Middle East.

In July, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to revive the Haditha–Baniyas pipeline. A deal was signed with a consortium of three companies, including US-based Chevron, to carry out the project.

The pipeline was built in 1952, but it was abandoned in 2003 due to damage sustained during the invasion of Iraq by the United States. Its reactivation would provide an outlet for Iraqi oil exports via the Mediterranean Sea.

World.title: Christine Lagarde: unifying ECB chief in turbulent times
World.content:
Frankfurt – Christine Lagarde, who will step down in February 2027 as president of the European Central Bank, has been seen as a unifying leader who headed the institution in turbulent geopolitical times and sought to strengthen it for a more uncertain world.

The veteran French politician’s tenure was also rocky at times; she was criticised for policy missteps, notably failing to lift interest rates fast enough during the post-pandemic inflation surge.

Lagarde, 70, was the first woman to head the ECB when she was nominated in 2019, having previously been the first woman to head the International Monetary Fund.

She had a hard act to follow after Mario Draghi, the Italian economist credited with steering the eurozone through the sovereign debt crisis that began in 2009 with his vow to do “whatever it takes” to preserve the single currency.

Nevertheless, most observers agree that Lagarde’s consensual leadership style unified the central bank’s governing council, which sets interest rates for the 21-nation euro area, and that it has been less riven by disputes than during the Draghi era.

Lagarde “made everyone feel they were part of the same team”, a council member told AFP, speaking on condition of anonymity. “Seven years later, that spirit is still there.”

Highlighting her desire to find a middle ground between the ECB’s “hawks” — who favour rate increases — and “doves” who prefer looser policy, she described herself as an “owl”.

“My ambition is to be this owl that’s often associated with a little bit of wisdom,” she said in 2019. Afterwards she was often seen wearing an owl brooch.

Lagarde did not have an easy start, however.

Just months into her tenure, she faced criticism after saying the ECB was “not here to close spreads” between member states’ borrowing costs, as Italy’s government bond yields surged as the economy was battered by the coronavirus lockdowns.

Following fury in Italy and further sharp rises in borrowing costs, the ECB quickly changed course, announcing a massive pandemic emergency bond-buying programme.

– ‘Madam Inflation’ –

But the central bank’s biggest misstep during her tenure was perhaps its flat-footed response to the inflation surge triggered by the easing of Covid lockdowns and the Ukraine war energy shock, which pushed prices to a record above 10 percent in 2022.

“The ECB was slow to raise rates — probably six months slow,” Andrew Kenningham of Capital Economics told AFP, while acknowledging that other central banks had also not acted quickly enough.

The failure to get to grips with surging prices earned Lagarde the unflattering moniker “Madam Inflation” from Germany’s top-selling tabloid Bild, which also criticised her taste in luxury fashion.

When the ECB did decide to move, however, it moved rapidly.

Policymakers began a historic tightening campaign, lifting its benchmark rate from negative territory in mid-2022 to a record four percent in late 2023.

On the positive side of the ledger, analysts say the central bank has introduced a raft of innovations under Lagarde’s leadership that could help it cope with a more uncertain world.

She has warned that upheavals — like Covid, US tariffs and energy shocks — may be the new normal, and that policymakers must be prepared.

In 2021 she led the ECB’s first strategy review for two decades, which aimed to make policymaking clearer by setting out how it would respond to changes in inflation and the broader economy.

And in 2022 the bank created a crisis-fighting tool, the Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI), that allows the ECB to buy bonds of a eurozone member if yields rise uncontrollably and there is a risk of financial stress spreading.

The tool has never been used, though recently there has been speculation the ECB could step in to help France as its borrowing costs soar amid debt worries.

“The ECB has equipped itself with increasingly flexible tools,” Frederik Ducrozet, head of strategy and macroeconomic research at Pictet Wealth Management, told AFP.

– ‘Rebellious little girl’ –

Away from policy, Lagarde’s time heading the ECB was marked by simmering discontent among some of the central bank’s roughly 5,000 employees in Frankfurt.

A study commissioned by staff representatives in 2024 found that cases of burnout were on the rise, with unions pointing to concerns about favouritism. The ECB responded by saying it took the health and well-being of staff seriously.

Lagarde, a lawyer by training and the daughter of teachers, had a modest upbringing spent mostly in the French port city of Le Havre.

In her autobiography, to be published in early 2027, she says she was a “rebellious little girl”, determined to show that people did not need “the right name” to succeed.

“I have broken a few glass ceilings along the way,” she told Elle magazine this year. “I hope that, thanks to that, other women understand they can too.”

World.title: Iraqi court sentences Azm Alliance leader to 6 years in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court sentenced on Thursday Azm Alliance leader Muthanna al-Samarrai to six years in prison over corruption.

The verdict is part of a sweeping, high-profile anti-corruption campaign known as the “Operation Dawn,” which was initiated by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.

Al-Samarrai was found guilty of profiting from contracts and public works projects, particularly by using his power to mediate illegal deals with significant state-owned refining companies under Iraq’s Ministry of Oil.

Al-Samarrai was sentenced by the court to refund 30 billion Iraqi dinars, or around $20 million, that he had obtained from his dishonest activities.

In late June, Al-Samarrai, a well-known politician and businessman whose Azm Alliance has 15 seats in the Iraqi parliament, was arrested. Additionally, several politicians, oil ministry officials, and political elites were arrested in a police raid on Baghdad’s strongly protected Green Zone.

After former deputy oil minister Adnan al-Jumaili made comprehensive confessions that revealed a widespread network of illicit refinery contracts, the investigations gained momentum.

The case carries considerable political implications, as al-Samarrai leads the second-largest Sunni faction in parliament and is a candidate for the upcoming parliamentary elections.

According to the Iraqi law, al-Samarrai now has 30 days to appeal his verdict before the Court of Cassation.

World.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
World.content:
Jerusalem – Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that made strong gains after an otherwise indecisive election.

National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, a far-right firebrand with a history of attacks on Palestinians, went so far as to encourage Israel “immediately” to order the arrests of Arab party leaders.

Israel was nearing the completion of ballot-counting from Tuesday’s election in which neither Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in the parliament known as the Knesset.

A looming threat on the horizon, meanwhile, was the prospect of a return to war with Iran, alongside Israel’s ally the United States, which is holding its own crucial midterms next week.

Israel’s election saw a soaring performance by Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the country’s creation in 1948, as outrage boiled at calls by ministers such as Ben Gvir to treat the Israeli minority group much as Israel has dealt with Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

The Arab parties together have enough votes to take the opposition bloc over the finish line, but Eisenkot has baulked, after relentless attacks by Netanyahu who warned his right-wing Jewish base that voting for the opposition would put Arabs in power.

Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, a conservative who heads the Central Election Commission, requested an investigation by the Shin Bet security service into allegations that key Arab party Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels for Hamas.

“The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said.

Government officials did not offer evidence to back the allegations.

Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf power.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, for years tacitly supported Qatar funding to Hamas-ruled Gaza, hoping to preserve stability.

That paradigm collapsed on October 7, 2023 when Hamas carried out the deadliest single attack ever on Israel, under Netanyahu’s watch.

– Kingmakers under pressure –

With nearly 93 percent of the vote counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was at 53 seats and the opposition forces led by Eisenkot had 48 — both well under the 61 needed to form a government.

The two main Arab formations were on track for an unprecedented 19 seats.

Some observers quickly said that the allegations would help Netanyahu by making the Arab lawmakers even more toxic to Eisenkot.

Yousef Jabareen, the head of one of them, the leftist Arab-majority Joint List, told AFP on Wednesday that he was willing to cooperate with the opposition to bring down Netanyahu but without joining it in a government.

He said the priority was to end “Netanyahu’s blood-soaked government” but noted that the Arab lawmakers disagreed on plenty with Eisenkot, who has largely backed the destruction of Gaza ordered by Netanyahu after the October 7 attack.

In response to the new allegations, Eisenkot said he was receiving updates and promised “utmost vigilance” against election interference.

“On the other hand, we cannot allow political actors to exploit the situation and influence the timing of the inauguration of the 26th Knesset,” he said.

One of Eisenkot’s right-leaning allies, Avigdor Lieberman, called the allegations “dramatic and unprecedented” and urged a swift investigation.

An Israeli police statement said that they would investigate every complaint about election integrity.

– The great survivor –

Netanyahu, who has led Israel on and off for more than 19 years, is known as a wily political operator.

He also tried on Tuesday to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties were caught with envelopes of cash and encouraging his base to come out in response.

Police said they arrested three suspects but the election commission called it an isolated local case.

Another factor that could play into the formation is an attack on Iran.

Netanyahu has repeatedly threatened to strike Iran, with his ally, US President Donald Trump, signalling he is ready to attack after next Tuesday’s US midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is forecast to lose ground.

Eisenkot has warned the military that Netanyahu has no mandate and that officers must not respond to his “political needs”.

But an attack could raise pressure on Eisenkot to join an emergency unity government, an option he has publicly ruled out, or keep the clock running until Israel can call new elections.

President Isaac Herzog will decide after the publication of the official results which person to task with a first chance of forming a government.

World.title: TotalEnergies profit hits record on high oil prices
World.content:
Paris – French oil and gas giant TotalEnergies said Thursday that its net profit hit a new record in the third quarter as the war in the Middle East pushed up hydrocarbon prices.

Net profit reached $8.3 billion in the period from July to September, up from $5.4 billion in the preceding three months.

“In a high-price environment characterised by historic refining margin levels and a bull gas market, TotalEnergies is once again fully leveraging its integrated business model and its geographic diversification,” chief executive Patrick Pouyanne said in a statement.

The company had already reported a strong rise in its bottom line in the preceding two quarters, similarly driven by soaring oil and gas prices as well as its trading activities.

TotalEnergies said the surge in profits would be reflected in a higher dividend for shareholders.

“The board of directors commended the very good operational performance of all business segments which enabled the company to capture higher market prices,” the company said in its earnings statement.

The group will undertake a new capital increase reserved for employees, “who will benefit from a 20 percent discount on the share price”.

The board confirmed a third interim dividend of 0.90 euros per share for 2026, up 5.9 percent compared to 2025.

TotalEnergies will also proceed with share buybacks for cancellation of $2.5 billion “for the fourth quarter as well as for the first quarter 2027”.

World.title: Most of private equity in health went to west & south: Study
World.content:
A study found that private equity investment in Indiaâs healthcare sector is concentrated in urban hospitals in southern and western states, leaving rural and underserved regions largely overlooked. (AI-generated image)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A mapping of private equity investments in Indiaâs health sector over past 18 years has revealed investments are overwhelmingly in multispecialty hospitals in the urbanised southern and western states, while vast rural and underserved regions attracted little or no investment at all.In the study by Brown Universityâs School of Public Health and Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, which identified 70 private equity (PE) backed acquisitions between Jan 2007 and May 2025, over 73% of the investment was in 45 hospital groups, including 187 multispecialty hospitals and several single ones. Among 16 outpatient care providers targeted, ophthalmology and fertility/reproductive care were the most common ones.According to the study, the investments accelerated after 2020 and peaked in 2023, which witnessed 18 deals. âThis timing mirrors global post-pandemic trends, where healthcare emerged as an attractive investment sector amid favourable financial conditions. During the pandemic, low interest rates and large amounts of available capital (âdry powderâ) made financing inexpensive and widely available, while healthcareâs relatively stable revenues made it more attractive than other economic sectors,â stated the study published in BMC Health Services Research, an open source journal.Karnataka recorded 13 deals, the highest number, followed by 10 each in Maharashtra and Telangana. Gujarat had six deals while Keralam and Haryana saw five each. Northern and eastern states saw minimal or no investment.Four hospital groups that together accounted for one-third of the total deals were Manipal Health Enterprises and Health Care Global Enterprises, both headquartered in Karnataka; and CARE Hospitals and ASG Eye Hospitals.Of the total number of acquisitions, 47 (67.1%) were financed solely by foreign PE firms, including those based in US, Singapore, and Mauritius, while 18 were backed exclusively by Indian investors.Among the 25 observed PE exits, secondary sales to other PE firms were most common (64%) exit strategy. Average holding period among those that exited was 5.1 years, with hospital platforms accounting for over half of these exits.Forty-five hospital groups (64.3%) remained under their original PE ownership.Several of the PE-backed platform deals were initially structured as minority stakes, with ownership expanding gradually over time, a staged pattern of engagement consistent with more cautious, multi-step investment approaches observed elsewhere in Brics markets, noted the study.

World.title: CCPA penalises Justdial, Sunrise Foods for safety, misleading product claims
World.content:
File photo: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties on online business directory Justdial and Sunrise Foods for violations involving consumer safety and misleading product claims.While it slapped a Rs 10 lakh penalty on Justdial for allowing listings of ammonium nitrate, a regulated explosive substance, on its platform without adequate safeguards, a Rs 1 lakh penalty was imposed on Sunrise Foods for marketing its bread as â100% Whole Wheat Breadâ without disclosing its actual whole-wheat content.In an order on Wednesday, CCPA held that Justdialâs platform carried listings of ammonium nitrate without adequate disclosure of sellersâ valid licences issued by Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), verification of buyersâ eligibility and mechanisms to ensure transaction traceability. The listings also lacked appropriate warnings about legal restrictions on the possession and use of the substance.Justdial argued that it was an online directory and information-listing service, not a trading platform and that the listings were old and sourced from public-domain information or user submissions. However, CCPA held that reliance on vendor representations and removal of listings only after complaints or regulatory intervention was insufficient.It directed the company to immediately discontinue listings, advertising and facilitation of access to the product.In a separate order, CCPA penalised Sunrise Foods for its âEveryday 100% Whole Wheat Breadâ. The authority found the product contained only 64% whole wheat, below the prescribed 75% threshold for using the nomenclature âwhole-wheat breadâ. The packaging did not disclose the proportion of whole wheat, potentially misleading consumers about the productâs composition.Sunrise Foods argued that the â100%â claim referred to the wheat flour component being entirely whole-wheat flour rather than refined flour. However, CCPA said the representation created a misleading impression about the productâs composition. It directed the company to discontinue the claim across print, electronic and social media with immediate effect.It directed the company to immediately discontinue misleading s across media and submit a compliance report within 15 days.

World.title: Mandate damages for savings lost in 'digital arrest': SC to RBI
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Convinced of bank personnel's complicity in cases of cyber fraudsters duping people by staging 'digital arrest', SC told Reserve Bank of India that its proposed Nov 30 standard operating procedure (SOP) must mandate every financial institution to indemnify those who lose money kept with banks to digital conmen.

"How do fraudsters and cybercriminals know how much money is kept in which account? Without bank employees sharing this information with fraudsters, there is no possibility of them targeting individual account holders," said a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. It said the SOP, proposed to be released by Nov 30, must mandate banks to immediately intimate an account holder when they come across a high-value transaction on the account, distinct from past transactions and inform police.

SRINAGAR: In a setback to J&K govt, the high court (HC) of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh Thursday struck down the 2010 Water Resources Act, ruling that water usage charges levied on hydropower projects amounted to a tax on electricity generation, a subject beyond the erstwhile state legislatureâs powers.A division bench of Justices Sanjay Dhar and Rajnesh Oswal quashed demand notices issued to 13 independent power producers and restrained J&K govt from imposing any tax on electricity generation under the guise of water usage charges or any other levy.The producers had challenged the law, arguing that charges fixed by Water Resources Regulatory Authority on April 2, 2019, were linked to the height from which water drove turbines rather than the volume consumed, effectively taxing power generation.Govt defended the levy, citing its authority to regulate water storage and use, National Water Policy and the need to conserve J&Kâs water resources.Rejecting its arguments, HC held that the legislation exceeded the erstwhile stateâs legislative competence when enacted. It also dismissed J&K govtâs contention that the lawâs subsequent adoption under Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, had legitimised it.HC observed that a law unconstitutional at the time of enactment could not be validated merely through its subsequent adoption by Parliament.

World.title: Police barged into my office to arrest former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, alleges senior advocate P. Wilson in Madras HC
World.content:
Senior counsel P. Wilson on Thursday (October 29, 2026) complained to the Madras High Court that Central Crime Branch (CCB) police personnel “barged” into his office in Chennai on October 26, 2026 to arrest former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi (DMK) in a case booked on charges of allegedly collecting over ₹400 crore towards ‘party fund’ from more than 177 private school managements in the State.

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, seized of a plea by the former Minister to quash the First Information Report (FIR) registered against him, the senior counsel said, the petitioner was at his office on Nelson Manickam Road at about 3 p.m. on Monday to discuss about the further course of legal action to be taken pursuant to the dismissal of his anticipatory bail petition by the High Court.

“We were discussing at our office regarding further course of legal action. About three vans of 40 policemen came to our office. They blocked the entrance, barged into the office and arrested him. The place of arrest has been shown as my office. This happened in the middle of the consultation Milord, are we living in a police state?” he asked and insisted upon framing of a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).

Denying the claim, State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan and Additional Public Prosecutor (APP) Arun Anbumani told the court the police were conscious of the law that an accused could not be arrested inside an advocate’s office. They asserted that the former Minister was not arrested inside the lawyer’s office. The SPP said, the police were invited into the lawyer’s office after they were waiting outside for about 90 minutes.

Mr. Anbumani said, the former Minister’s counsel-on-record Richardson Wilson had called the policemen inside the office. “It was a ploy. He called the policemen to come inside the office and has the audacity to come and complain to this court,” the APP added. However, Mr. Richardson denied he called the policemen inside and accused the APP of not instructing the SPP properly.

After hearing both sides, Justice Lakshminarayanan pointed out that district judge L.S. Sathyamurthy did not appear to have accepted the argument of the former Minister having been arrested inside the lawyer’s office while remanding him in judicial custody during the intervening night between Monday and Tuesday. Mr. Wilson replied he would challenge the finding given by the district judge.

When the arguments led to a heated exchange between the prosecution and defense counsel, the SPP said: “This is unfortunate. Let him not distort facts. This is what is happening in this case. Personal attacks are happening. We are also lawyers. This (public prosecutor) is not a permanent position. We don’t have any political affiliations. We are only doing our duty.”

Mr. Sathyan said, he had asked the policemen as to how could they enter a lawyer’s office but the instantaneous answer was that they were invited in to the office. “He (the investigating officer in the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Police attached to CCB) said, I have material to show that I was invited into his office. If it is so required, we will place the material before the court.”

Justice Lakshminarayanan asked Mr. Richardson to produce the CCTV footage from his office along with the audio recording since the footage produced on Thursday had only visuals but no audio. The judge thereafter adjourned the hearing on the FIR quash plea to November 10, 2026 since a similar question of law had to be decided in another case related to former Minister E.V. Velu.

World.title: High security, traffic curbs and midnight Metro services for Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi concert
World.content:
The Delhi Police have stepped up security around Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) Stadium ahead of Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert on Friday (October 30, 2026) with around 2,000 private security guards expected to be deployed and vehicle movement likely to be restricted within a 500–metre radius of the venue.

The concert is expected to draw around 70,000 spectators, prompting traffic restrictions and special arrangements by the Delhi Metro to manage the rush.

The South district police have strengthened deployment around the stadium, while organisers have been asked to arrange additional security personnel and parking facilities and coordinate with cab aggregators to manage the influx of concertgoers and prevent traffic congestion.

According to the Delhi Traffic Police advisory, restrictions and diversions may remain in place from 1 p.m. to midnight on Friday (October 30, 2026), with 11 roads around the stadium likely to be affected.

The affected stretches include Bhishm Pitamah Marg, Lodhi Road, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg between the Defence Colony and Lodhi Colony flyovers, Arch Bishop Marg, Fourth Avenue Road, Fifth Avenue Road, internal roads of the CGO Complex and JLN Stadium, the Barapullah flyover between INA and Jangpura Metro stations, Gate No. 2, Dayal Singh College Road and internal roads of Lodhi Colony.

Complaint filed seeking curbs on Diljit Dosanjh’s Delhi show

Traffic diversions may be implemented at eight points, including the Lodhi Road-Dayal Singh College Road T-point, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg near the stadium, the slip road towards Soochna Bhawan, Bhishm Pitamah Marg near the stadium’s red light and the Kushak Nallah bus depot red light. Depending on traffic conditions, vehicles may be diverted towards Lodhi flyover, Arch Bishop Marg, Fourth Avenue Road and Aurobindo Marg.

Parking will not be available to the general public at or around the venue. Limited parking for special invitees will be provided at the Sunheri Nala bus depot and Dayal Singh College parking areas. Taxis, three-wheelers and cabs will not be allowed to park or halt along the roads, with pick-up and drop-off permitted only at designated locations.

Three pick-up and drop-off points have been identified at Arch Bishop Marg, Lal Masjid in Pragati Vihar and the Kushak Nallah bus depot red light. The traffic police have issued route suggestions for concertgoers travelling from different parts of the city and urged motorists to follow the instructions of traffic personnel and diversion signs. Emergency and medical vehicles will be given priority passage.

Metro services extended till midnight

To facilitate the movement of spectators, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) will extend train services on all Metro lines, except the Airport Express Line and Rapid Metro, Gurugram, until midnight on Friday. Additional train trips will be operated across the network, with standby trains kept ready to meet any surge in passenger numbers.

The timings for QR ticket purchases through the Delhi Metro Sarthi mobile application will also be extended by an hour. Additional staff, customer service personnel and customer facilitation agents will be deployed at JLN Stadium Metro station and key interchange stations to guide commuters and regulate passenger movement.

Additional security personnel, door-frame metal detectors and enhanced screening arrangements will also be put in place at JLN Stadium Metro station to ensure orderly movement and security.

The JLN Stadium station on the Violet Line, which runs between Kashmere Gate and Raja Nahar Singh, is the closest Metro station to the venue. Concert-goers using the Violet Line can also alight at Jangpura, while those travelling on the Yellow Line can use INA or Jor Bagh stations and proceed towards the designated access points.

The traffic advisory has recommended that spectators use the Metro to avoid congestion around the stadium. Concertgoers have also been advised to reach the venue using the designated entry gates and pick-up and drop-off points.

The police have urged commuters to avoid affected roads wherever possible, not to park on roads and report unattended objects or suspicious activity to the nearest police personnel.

World.title: Former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen sent to 13 days police custody
World.content:
Kolkata

Former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen was sent to 13 days of police custody on Thursday (October 29). The Trinamool Congress-era minister was arrested on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) in relation to a Durga Puja ticket scam.

“We have got 13 days PC of ex-MIC Indranil Sen till 10th Nov,” a statement from Kunal Agarwal, Additional Commissioner of Police (Crime), said. He was produced at the Bankshall Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) morning.

Police have said that they have found multiple transactions linked to Mr. Sen, which the former minister has not been able to explain. He will be in police custody for further questioning. He had been avoiding the police even after multiple summons.

“The exact amount of cheating and money trail is still being verified. No precise figure can be provided at present. The complaint made is of 34 crore,” police also said.

On Thursday (October 29, 2026), Bharatiya Janata Party workers staged a protest outside Mr. Sen’s house in the Singur area. They also dragged a man with a rope tied around his waist and put a picture of Mr. Sen on his face.

Both the Kolkata Police and the Enforcement Directorate are investigating the former minister for allegations of financial irregularities in the sale of Durga Puja tickets under the organisation MassArt. The organisation is headed by his wife and used to conduct exclusive Durga Puja previews in exchange for expensive tickets.

An FIR at the Bow Bazar Police Station has alleged Mr. Sen and the other members of MassArt had used the Durga Puja’s UNESCO intangible cultural heritage tag for personal gains.

After Mr. Sen’s arrest on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and minister Agnimitra Paul both raised allegations that if Mr. Sen has “stolen money, he shared the proceeds with the former CM Mamata Banerjee.”

“Indranil Sen’s arrest is natural, but will the arrests reach the top of these scams?” senior Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader Sujan Chakraborty asked.

However, Mamata-Trinamool general secretary Abhishek Banerjee said that anyone who has not sold their spine is being put behind bars.

The former Tourism and Culture Minister was denied anticipatory bail by the Calcutta High Court, and Supreme Court judge Dipankar Dutta has recused himself from the bail hearing on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).

Mr. Sen was being questioned for over four hours in the Enforcement Directorate office at the CGO Complex in Salt Lake on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) when Kolkata Police Detective Department and Bidhannagar Police cordoned off the area. He was arrested at around 5.10 p.m., the moment he stepped out of the ED office.

After the regime change in West Bengal, several Mamata Banerjee-era ministers have been arrested. Mr. Sen was the fifth arrest; the first one was Sujit Bose, who was also arrested for a job recruitment scam. Later, ministers Udayan Guha, Ujjal Biswas, and Dilip Mondal were also arrested under allegations of financial irregularities.

World.title: Patrick Stewart, Shakespearean actor turned 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' star, dies at 86
World.content:
Patrick Stewart, who rose from poverty in England to become an accomplished Shakespearean stage actor and then achieved global stardom as the erudite Captain Jean-Luc Picard in TV’s “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” movies, has died at ​the age of 86.

Stewart, knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II for his contributions to drama, died at his home in Los Angeles, according to a statement on his ‌X account. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, ​in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” ⁠it said.

Stewart became an actor at age 18 and gained acclaim on the stage as a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company beginning in the 1960s. But it was not until after he was hired at age 47 for “Star Trek: The Next Generation” - a TV series that ran from 1987 to 1994 as a sequel to ‌the original 1960s “Star Trek” - that he gained mainstream fame, acting into his 80s.

“Make it so,” his character Picard often said, instructing a subordinate to carry out a command, or sometimes deploying the similar catch phrase, “Engage.”

It was a role he had debated even taking ‌after his longtime friend and fellow Shakespearean Ian McKellen advised him to spurn “Star Trek” and remain in theater. Stewart did take the role ‌and became ⁠both a fan favorite and an indispensable part of a lucrative sci-fi franchise, playing Picard not only in 176 episodes over seven ⁠seasons of that series but also in several “Star Trek” films and in the later streaming series “Star Trek:

Picard” that began airing in 2020 when he was 79. “As the seven seasons of TNG (”The Next Generation”) went by, the distinction between Jean-Luc Picard and Patrick Stewart became thinner and thinner, until it was impossible for me to know where he left off and I ​began. So much of what I believed and felt went into ‌that show,” Stewart told the Guardian newspaper in 2022.

Stewart also initially balked at being cast as the wheelchair-using mutant Professor X in the “X-Men” movies, based on the popular Marvel comic book character. “I said, ‘Look, I know this isn’t science fiction, but it’s fantasy, and I’ve done that.’ But they persuaded me that it wouldn’t be like ‘Star Trek,’ so I did it. And yet again I was proved wrong,” Stewart told the Guardian.

He became a ‌critical part of another big-money franchise starting with the first entry “X-Men” in 2000 and followed by several more.

Acting was safe space

Stewart was ​born on July 13, 1940, in the English town of Mirfield in Yorkshire. He was raised in poverty, with a father who he said returned from World War Two an alcoholic who suffered from post-traumatic stress syndrome and physically abused Stewart’s mother. Stewart ⁠recalled putting his body between his father and mother to try to protect her.

As a child, Stewart said, acting became a “safe space” after a schoolteacher introduced him to Shakespeare - specifically “The Merchant of Venice” - during a class when he was 12. He started losing his hair at age 17 and was bald by ‌19. He was embarrassed at the time, but eventually embraced it.

“Star Trek,” created by Gene Roddenberry, presented a hopeful vision of the future, with humankind venturing into the cosmos in spaceships exceeding the speed of light and encountering alien races. The enduring popularity of the original series and the success of spinoff films prompted Roddenberry to create “The Next Generation” sequel series.

The Picard character was the opposite of the swashbuckling and sometimes unintentionally buffoonish Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner, of the original series - envisioned as more cerebral and disciplined, though sometimes coming across as stuffy, humourless, or self-important.

Stewart recalled being a little bit too serious toward his cast mates early on.

“I tell the story of calling a meeting of my principal fellow cast members and telling them that I thought ‌we were not disciplined enough, that we should not be fooling about on the set as much as we were but taking everything seriously,” Stewart told the New Yorker in 2023.

“And ​one of the cast members said, ‘Oh, come on, Patrick, we’ve got to have some fun.’ And I thumped the chair and said, ‘We are not here to have fun ’- which they have never let me forget. They taught me so much about ⁠loosening up and being freer,” Stewart added.

Stewart also felt the series improved as it went along, faulting his own portrayal of Picard in the first two seasons. “I ⁠found it lacking intimacy. It was very authoritative, but there were few other qualities in him,” Stewart said, adding that his work got better in subsequent seasons.

In fact, the finest work for the entire cast may have been the two-part, time-bending series finale.

He became Sir ‌Patrick Stewart when he was knighted by the queen at Buckingham Palace in 2010. He told reporters that his heroes were British actors Laurence Olivier, John Gielgud and Alec Guinness, who also had been knighted, adding that being “in that company is the grandest thing that has professionally happened to me.”

Stewart ​was married three times and had two children. His third marriage, in 2013, was to American musician Sunny Ozell.

World.title: Any plan to restrict sale of liquor in hotel bars and clubs located close to educational institutions? Madras High Court asks Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise
World.content:
The Madras High Court has directed the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise to spell out whether any norms would be put in place for licensing bars inside hotels/clubs located near educational institutions in order to prevent incidents of underage students being offered liquor and ending up in fisticuffs in an inebriated mood.

Justice N. Ramesh issued the direction after expressing shock over a criminal case registered against a 19-year-old college student for having allegedly indulged in a brawl with fellow students when they were consuming liquor at a bar attached to an adjacent hotel reportedly run by the college management.

The judge suo motu impleaded the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise as one of the respondents to an anticipatory bail petition filed by the college student and called for details regarding the licence issued to El Dorado bar at SRM Hotel in Potheri, near Chennai.

He also wanted the Commissioner to explain whether there were any rules, government orders, circulars or any other guidelines governing the grant and renewal of licence in Form F.L.3, and whether any of them prescribe a minimum distance from an educational institution, a students’ hostel or a place of worship.

The Commissioner was further directed to furnish to the court the distance between the bar and the nearest gate/ building/hostel of the educational institution measured along the path a pedestrian would ordinarily take, and whether the premises lies within a municipal area.

The officer was also ordered to state whether the proximity of the educational institution and the number of students studying there was taken into consideration before granting/renewing the FL3 licence to the bar in the hotel and what action would be taken in future.

Justice Ramesh also impleaded the SRM Institute of Science and Technology as another respondent to the petition and directed its Registrar to disclose whether the college management had any connection whatsoever with SRM Hotel and the steps taken by it to prevent students from consuming alcohol.

Taking note that three students who got injured due to a hit with a beer bottle on September 26, 2026 had been treated at SRM Hospital, the judge ordered that the petitioner should not be arrested until further orders provided he cooperates with the investigation and appears for inquiry whenever required.

World.title: M.P. wildlife officials highlight Chambal region’s gun culture as probe into cheetah shooting goes on
World.content:
The wildlife officials in Madhya Pradesh have raised questions about the prevalent gun culture in the Chambal region even as they continue their investigation into the killing of a 19-month-old cheetah cub who was found with five gunshot injuries on October 25. The cub passed away on the morning of October 27 during treatment in Jabalpur.

Speaking to The Hindu, a high-ranking official said that the gun culture has emerged as a “crucial segment” in the probe and that the matter had been brought up with senior police officers in the region. The probe is yet to make a breakthrough.

“It’s a very complex dynamics there with almost everybody owning a gun so we will have to target this culture too going forward. There is need to review the criteria of issuing a gun license in the region and we hope there is some discussion about this at the government level,” the official said requesting anonymity, while calling for a crackdown on the illegal gun manufacturing in the region.

The conversation on gun culture coming up in the probe was confirmed by State’s Chief Wildlife Warden (CWLW) Sameeta Rajora.

Ms. Rajora said that all possible angles, including poaching, revenge killing or self-defence, were being explored in the probe.

On the evening of October 25, a cheetah monitoring team found the cub, which was wearing a radio collar for tracking, in a still position in compartment no. 748 of the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division on the border of Sheopur and Morena districts, about 50 kilometres from Kuno’s boundaries. During treatment in Jabalpur, five firearm metal pellets were recovered from his body, including one from his lung.

The two districts fall under the Chambal region, which was once infamous for its vast ravines and the dacoits hiding in them. Even though the dacoits are a fear of the past now, rivalries, high crime rates, and the tradition of owning a gun continue to thrive in the region. Morena is often in the news for its illegal arms manufacturing.

Officials from the region say a gun can be found in almost every household there.

The probe is being carried out by a State Government-formed special task force (STF) of forest and police officers, while a high-level team constituted by the Union Government also visited the area on October 28.

Sources in Kuno said that various teams had been mapping the area roamed by the cub for 15-20 days before he was shot for leads.

“Our teams have been mapping the area in which the cub roamed for 15-20 days before being shot and, more importantly, where he made the kills. We have also identified various illegal cattle camps in the area because it is believed that he was killed in revenge after he killed someone’s cattle,” an official said.

“So far we have not found any strong evidence indicating a poaching attempt, but it would be premature to conclusively say anything. We are making progress and should make a breakthrough very soon,” the official added.

An official, who is involved with the probe, said that the weapon used in the shooting is “suspected to be a country-made bharmar gun”, a traditional single-shot, muzzle-loading smoothbore firearm that is popular is the rural and forest parts of the region.

“As of now, we believe it to be a bharmar gun based on the pallets and their popularity in the area,” the official said.

The official also added that the monitoring team had already been tracking the KNG22’s movement ever since he wandered off outside the boundaries of Kuno and that contact was made with the cub early in the morning the same day. The cub was found near Morena’s Pahadgarh village, and the surrounding area has dense forests and small hills, he said.

“Including KNG22, we had 14 radio-collared cheetahs that were ranging in the wild, and they are monitored every day with a focus on gathering visual evidences too. Similarly, he was being monitored that day too. Our team spotted him around 3 a.m. and was in sight for about an hour after which it disappeared and we believe it made a kill,” the official said, adding that when his tracker showed him still, the initial assumption is that the animal is resting after eating.

“The concern began when the cub did not move for an unusually long time and the team started following the tacker. Even then the initial suspicion was that he had been attacked by another wild animal like leopard so we went for the rescue and found him with injuries,” the official added.

The Central team held meetings with officials at Kuno as well as from the Sheopur and Morena territorial forest divisions to review the ongoing probe and issue instructions, apart from taking updates on whether it could be a case of poaching.

The Additional Director, WCCB, and a senior wildlife official from Kuno also met the Superintendents of Police of the two districts to improve coordination and “to understand the region’s geography and people’s mindset”, the official added.

World.title: West Bengal government warns of strict action against violations of firecracker norms on Diwali, Chhath
World.content:
Kolkata

The West Bengal government on Thursday (October 29, 2026) announced that it will take strict action against people violating the firecracker norms during Diwali and Chhath Puja. The police have also arrested one man for wrongfully hoarding banned crackers and recovered around 110 kg crackers.

“The accused was arrested from the spot at about 01:45 hrs on 29.10.2026, and the firecrackers were seized in the presence of witnesses following due legal formalities,” a statement from Kolkata Police said on Thursday (October 29, 2026). A suo motu case was registered by a police officer at the Burrabazar Police Station, after which 19-year-old Md. Toufiq was arrested.

The Director General of Police, West Bengal, Siddhi Nath Gupta, also said that people will not be allowed to use sky lanterns without acquiring proper permission from the fire department. “They can be sold, bought, and used, but if you want to use them, acquire permission and follow the due process,” Mr. Gupta said.

They also added that only green crackers will be allowed and that they have multiple methods in place to ensure sellers do not have fake green cracker labels on their products. The Home Secretary, Sanghamitra Ghosh urged that the use of green crackers should also be limited.

Curbing pollution

Meanwhile, Ms. Ghosh urged people to comply with pollution-control regulations for a better environment and said that they have launched an awareness campaign to make people understand that celebrations and festivals can also happen without polluting crackers.

“It is not just about enforcement; it is also a lot about self-awareness. Every single person gets affected by this pollution,” Ms. Ghosh also said.

Ms. Ghosh said the decibel limit was 125 and 90 for sound-emitting and light-emitting crackers, respectively. On Diwali, the time limit for bursting crackers is between 8 and 10 p.m. and on Chhath Puja, from 6 to 8 a.m.

They also added that surveillance and patrolling will be higher during the festival days.

“We will inspect all storage and manufacturing points, and keep a watch on the cracker markets to ensure no violations are made,” Ms. Ghosh added.

World.title: High-speed diesel price crosses Rs400 with Re0.85 increase; no change in petrol rate
World.content:
The government on Thursday increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.85 per litre, leaving that of petrol unchanged at Rs377.91.

Following the revision, HSD will retail at Rs400.67 per litre.

The prices are applicable for Oct 30 (Friday), according to the Petroleum Division’s notification.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

On Tuesday, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy.

The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17 .

For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then.

On Friday, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions.

The same day, senators raised concerns over fuel supply even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: 'Not related to defence': Govt responds to Fazl's remarks about Makkah pact countries' meeting in Tehran
World.content:
Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the meeting was not related to defence. Hence, Asif said his presence was not required, while Naqvi explained the reasons for his participation.

The remarks came after the JUI-F chief questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at the meeting.

The meeting brought together top officials from Iran and member countries of the Makkah Defence Alliance — including Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin.

On Iran’s side, President Masoud Pezeshkian, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi were present. The huddle agreed to “continue their dialogue to bolster cooperation among the four regional nations, including in the areas of regional peace and security”.

On Wednesday, Fazl referred to the development during his address in the National Assembly (NA) and commented: “A defence pact is taking shape in Iran, a meeting is under way (there), and the defence minister is sitting here.”

Amid laughter and desk thumping in the Lower House, he referred to Naqvi’s presence at the Tehran huddle and questioned: “The interior minister is required there as well?”

Then, taking a jibe at Asif, he repeated the defence minister’s phrase that he had used against the PTI.

“There is your respect and stature — koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai (have some shame, show some modesty),” he said, breaking into laughter.

Responding to him in the NA on Thursday, Asif said no defence pact was taking shape in Tehran, nor was the discussion focused on Pakistan’s defence or any related matter.

He said CDF Munir had “assumed a role for Pakistan” following last year’s military conflict with India. That role, he said, was of “peace and dialogue so that peace is established in our region”.

Since then, he noted, Pakistan has signed two defence pacts — the Makkah defence pact and the Badr Memorandum of Understanding.

“I was involved in those pacts as I am the defence minister,” he explained, adding that the meeting in Tehran was “not the defence ministry’s mandate”.

The CDF had gone there “as a messenger of peace and paved the ground” for the huddle, he said, ostensibly referring to Tehran last week.

During that visit, the CDF had proposed the Tehran meeting, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei.

Asif said this was the situation and he was “not needed in Tehran”.

He added that the CDF had played a role in averting a confrontation. “The situation could have deteriorated as far as the Yemen issue is concerned […] There has been some talk and peace may emerge in the coming days or week as far as Saudi Arabia versus Yemen [sic] is concerned.”

Asif advised Fazl to be the bigger person and said his criticism was “misplaced”.

The defence minister further said Pakistan’s and the CDF’s role at the international level should be acknowledged, keeping political differences aside. He said one should at least show some dignity.

‘Not related to defence’

Meanwhile, in the Senate, Naqvi also responded to Fazl’s remarks on his participation in the Tehran meeting. The proceedings were marred by loud exchanges between the interior minister and JUI-F Senator Kamran Murtaza.

Naqvi clarified that he and CDF Munir undertook the visit to “handle the ongoing crisis in Iran”.

On Fazl’s query of why Asif had not gone there, he said, “He (Fazl) did not know that this [trip] was not related to defence.”

Defending his inclusion, the minister said: “I do not go out of my own volition. I have been especially tasked by the prime minister sahib; he has entrusted me with some matters regarding the current crisis of the [Iran] war, because of which I go.”

The independent senator noted that the JUI-F had been commenting on him for many days.

“I personally had heartfelt respect for Maulana Fazlur Rehman, but yesterday when he said I spit on the state, that respect ended,” Naqvi said.

Naqvi said he wanted to ask Fazl and his party’s senators present there just one question and then noted that JUI-F leaders had made very “disgusting statements about institutions” three to four months ago.

This prompted Senator Murtaza to object, saying he could not speak on a personal agenda in the House. Presiding Officer Shahadat Awan also immediately said he was expunging the word “disgusting” from Naqvi’s remarks.

As Murtaza continued shouting, Naqvi said, “You should listen here … You will have to listen.”

The presiding officer noted that Naqvi was a member of the Senate and urged the JUI-F leader to take his seat.

Resuming his remarks, Naqvi said, “Giving people the perception that this was a defence pact; this was not a defence agreement at all.

He added: “For them, the state is like a mother until the day they can squeeze it dry. The state is very good as long as they can extract wealth from the state, and when you do not get a share in the state and the government, then you spit on the state. This is not appropriate anywhere.”

Murtaza again interrupted, objecting to Naqvi’s language, at which the latter replied that the other side had also used similar language a day ago.

As the JUI-F senator continued speaking amid the presiding officer’s calls to halt cross-talk, Naqvi said, “If they criticise, they should garner and keep the courage to take the answer as well. This is no way [to behave] that you go and say whatever you want.”

The interior minister then went on to criticise the JUI-F, alleging that it “used Islam for business and for politics”.

Amid the ruckus, PML-N’s Abid Sher Ali also stood up and responded loudly, prompting State Minister of Interior Tallal Chaudhry and the presiding officer to urge him to take his seat.

Naqvi then addressed PTI’s Ali Zafar and said, “These very people (JUI-F) used to come to us before governor’s rule [was imposed] and say, ‘Impose governor’s rule, rid us of them!’ […] Those who come and sit with you and engage in opposition wanted governor’s rule imposed from their hearts. I will prove this to you.”

Addressing JUI-F, the interior minister said, “Now, you will not get jobs in the state. Now you will not get money from the state, nor will you get tickets from the state.”

He asserted that it was the JUI-F that was “continuously crossing the line” and that they would get a response if they kept doing so.

‘Full of contradictions’

In his remarks in the NA, Asif alleged that Fazl’s past “is full of contradictions”.

“You taunt me with ‘have some shame, show some modesty’, but you should also have some shame and show some modesty. How many perks have you enjoyed over the past 40 years? You have been violating the very principles that you have been highlighting,” the PML-N leader said.

He recalled that Fazl had also offered to mediate with Kabul. “Were you the foreign minister?” he questioned, alleging that the move was aimed at “value addition to his politics and leverage that to extract maximum advantage from the government”.

Asif said Fazl had been in the government with every political party, making an incomplete remark: “When you don’t get a share in the power —”

“When you delete the past from your memory and attack your rivals — at least I don’t have that courage. When I speak, my past is fresh in my mind; that if I say this, whether I would be taunted that we supported General Ziaul Haq’s government,” he went on to say.

The defence minister recalled that Fazl was part of the Musharraf government, had also been an opposition leader in the House and also served as the Kashmir Committee chairperson. He said a person serving as the head of such a committee that raises issues at an international forum should have “impeccable credentials”.

When some lawmakers opposed him in favour of Fazl, he remarked, “The Maulana now needs women’s support. He is unable to find a man.”

He also accused Fazl of “targeting our diplomatic efforts”, saying that the government’s achievement at the global stage had not received the commendation they deserved.

Asif said his advice to the JUI-F would be a line often seen on buses and trucks: “Mehnat kar, hasad na kar (work hard and don’t envy).”

He ended his address, alleging that had Fazl been given some share in the governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the JUI-F chief’s address the previous day would not have been delivered.

“This sideshow that they (JUI-F) are running, I feel that it is unfortunate that our sisters have been forced to defend the men [of JUI-F] while the men are nowhere to be seen,” Asif remarked.

Describing Fazl’s address as “blackmail”, Asif warned against coming into power based on “compromises”.

“Sitting in the opposition would be a more respectable approach, rather than sitting with people who will blackmail you,” he said.

“We as senior parliamentarians should convey to the nation that we will not do group-based politics but politics rooted in the constitution and [..] for the security of the country,” Asif urged, adding that lawmakers should chart a way forward together, rather than “grabbing each other by the collar”.

JUI-F’s Murtaza alleges ‘programme to sling mud’ at Fazl

In remarks after the Senate ruckus, JUI-F’s Murtaza accused the government of staging a “requested programme”.

“I think nizam sahib (Mr System) sent messages and made calls to many people today, and told them to sling mud at Maulana sahib like this,” he said on Geo News’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath’, apparently referring to Naqvi.

Murtaza questioned why Asif “suddenly remembered” to respond to Fazl the next day, rather than using his right of reply “even though he was present” in the NA yesterday.

He went on to object to the interior minister making “personal accusations”, even though he could have simply explained that the prime minister had tasked him with peace efforts.

The JUI-F senator insisted that Fazl’s remarks were not particularly about Pakistan but “if a state starts making its children fight each other”, asking if the ministers were considering that the state was doing so.

Asked what Fazl implied, Murtaza maintained that the JUI-F’s stance was “about every such state” that engaged in such acts.

The senator also claimed that Chaudhry had approached him with an “offer for a certain thing” when he was in the Senate hall.

“Did I reject you or not? 26th Amendment,” Murtaza said, with Chaudhry acknowledging that a “lot of things were being discussed at the time of 26th Amendment” but “not everything should be disclosed”.

Meanwhile, appearing on the same show, the state minister for interior regretted that Fazl, despite being a senior politician and a religious leader, “made martyrs a point of his and discuss it to advance his politics”.

Chaudhry said he had noted immense anger and frustration visible in the JUI-F chief’s demeanour in recent days.

Asked if the government wanted a “clash” with the JUI-F chief, the PML-N leader said, “I think Maulana sahib is deliberately clashing and bringing up such issues, after which no option is left for us other than to respond to it. Today, I have never seen Kamran Murtaza sahib in such a state of anger in my entire life.”

He highlighted that Fazl had questioned “what has this state given us”. “Do you think the state has given you nothing?” he asked.

Electoral reforms committee

In his remarks, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas claimed KP had been “snatched from the people” and reiterated the opposition’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections.

“If even one person’s vote is snatched, it is a crime. It is the responsibility of those conducting elections to protect the vote. Earlier also you laid a crooked brick, and Pakistan broke. On Feb 8, elections were stolen. While stealing elections, where have you reached — you have even stolen Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he claimed.

The opposition leader said no society could progress without law, or function if law existed but without its implementation.

The House also took up a motion moved by Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik for the constitution of a parliamentary electoral reforms committee.

PTI’s Zafar said he could write down entire electoral reforms on paper in an hour. “The issue is implementation. Make such a committee and procedure that the electoral process is actually implemented. Whatever they want to do, only that is approved,” he said.

Barrister Aqeel said the issue could be resolved by sitting together and asked members to bring their proposals.

World.title: Pakistan, Turkiye shall 'continue to champion dialogue, diplomacy' alongside bolstering defences: PM Shehbaz
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday affirmed that Pakistan and Turkiye would continue to push for dialogue and diplomacy while strengthening their defences under the Makkah Defence Agreement.

He made the remarks while addressing an event in Islamabad marking the 103rd national day of Turkiye, with which Pakistan enjoys strong bilateral ties and maintains multi-sectoral cooperation.

The premier said the pact, signed on Aug 7 between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, marked an “important milestone” in cooperation between Islamabad and Ankara.

“It strengthens our collective deterrence and reinforces our shared commitment to regional peace and stability,” PM Shehbaz noted.

“While we strengthen our defences, we shall continue to champion dialogue, diplomacy, respect for international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes.”

The prime minister hailed Turkiye’s diplomatic support during Marka-i-Haq last May, when India initiated unilateral aggression against Pakistan, triggering a four-day conflict between the nuclear-armed neighbours.

“Turkiye stood firmly by our side with unwavering commitment and dedication. This sincere act of solidarity was a profound source of comfort and strength for the people of Pakistan, a gesture that will forever remain etched in our hearts and our memories,” he emphasised.

Additionally, the premier observed that Islamabad and Ankara’s relationship had evolved into a “multifaceted strategic partnership”, spanning political dialogue, defence, trade, culture and people-to-people ties, among other areas.

He stressed that the economic partnership between Pakistan and Turkiye needs to match the heights of the political and strategic bond between both nations.

“In July this year, at the Pakistan-Turkiye business conference in Istanbul, I announced the establishment of the President Tayyip Erdogan Special Economic Zone in Karachi,” PM Shehbaz said.

“Now I invite Turkish businessmen to look at Pakistan with its young population, strategic location and growing economic opportunities. Let us translate the goodwill between our two peoples into joint ventures, shared prosperity and meaningful jobs for our young people.”

During his speech, the prime minister highlighted the longstanding, historic ties that the two countries shared, recalling that during the Khilafat Movement — a campaign to protect the Ottoman Empire after World War I — people donated whatever they could from the subcontinent, including money and jewellery, to support their “Turkish brethren”.

“A century ago, our forefathers sent their love across the seas. Generations later, that love returned to our doorsteps during our darkest times,” he added, referring to humanitarian aid from Turkiye during the 2005 earthquake and the devastating floods of 2010.

PM Shehbaz also highlighted that under Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s instructions, Turkiye established a modern hospital, a school and modern villages for the people of Muzaffargarh after the floods.

“The 100 years between the Khilafat Movement and that moment seemed to close into a single circle,” the premier said, noting that when a massive earthquake rocked Turkiye in February 2023, “the people of Pakistan grieved as if the rubble lay upon our own homes”.

“We stood with our Turkish brothers and sisters, in their hour of sorrow, just as they had stood with us.”

Earlier this week, Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Iran participated in a quadrilateral meeting where Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for “regional unity” and hoped that the presence of other Islamic powers would “further consolidate regional unity and cohesion”.

Earlier this month, both nations signed an agreement to enhance cooperation in combating terrorism, narcotics trafficking and organised crime and agreed to establish a joint working group to strengthen collaboration between their interior ministries.

The decisions were taken during a meeting between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Turkish counterpart Mustafa Çiftçi in Istanbul.

World.title: Pakistan 'overperformer' in innovation, climbs 4 ranks globally in 2026: report
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan rose to 95th place among the 139 economies of the world featured in the ‘Global Innovation Index 2026’ published by the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), it emerged on Thursday.

Advancing in rank from 99th place in 2025, Pakistan also reclaimed its “overperformer” status for the fourth time, a status given to economies identified as performing above expectations for their level of economic development. It also held the status in 2022 and 2024.

The global index report showed that Pakistan performed better in innovation outputs than innovation inputs in 2026. This year, Pakistan ranked 121st in innovation inputs and 72nd in innovation outputs — both higher than last year.

“Innovation overperformance shows that innovation does not follow a straight line from income to results,” the report said.

“The 2026 overperformers show that economies can generate more innovation than expected for their level of development when they build on focused strengths.”

A list of countries that performed above expectations for their level of development in innovation in 2026, according to the Global Innovation Index 2026. — screengrab from WIPO report

WIPO highlighted that Pakistan’s strengths were concentrated in the digital economy, particularly mobile app creation, ICT services exports, high-tech imports, and software spending. It added that the country’s “relatively strong” scientific production and university quality supported a developing digital economy.

In the 2026 index, Pakistan ranked 15th among the 36 lower middle-income group economies and eighth among the 11 economies in central and southern Asia. It did not rank among the top innovation clusters in any specific innovation pillar of the index (including ‘human capital and research’, ‘infrastructure’, etc).

This partial screengrab from WIPO report shows Pakistan ranks 95th overall and does not rank among leading countries in any innovation pillar, in Global Innovation Index 2026.

Pakistan’s GII ranking (2020-2026) showed a rise over the past seven years, ranking 107th in 2020; 99th in 2021; 87th in 2022; 88th in 2023; 91st in 2024; and 99th in 2025.

Meanwhile, Switzerland, Sweden and the United States remained the world’s top three innovation economies, with Switzerland ranking first for a 16th consecutive year. The organisation noted, “In a period of major geopolitical and economic turbulence, the most striking feature about the top of the ranking is its stability.”

According to the report, the leading economies broadly remain the same as in 2025, with no new economy in the top 15 since last year, and Europe once more accounting for the largest share of the group with 14 economies out of 25 innovation leaders. Additionally, the Netherlands moved up to seventh place and Austria to 18th.

“The main signal at the innovation frontier this year is continuity, rather than the emergence of any single new entrant,” the report said.

Five Asian economies were also among the top 25: South Korea and Singapore in fourth and fifth place respectively; China remaining 10th — as the only middle-income economy among the innovation leaders — Japan at 12th and Hong Kong, China in 14th place.

The report highlighted that the presence of Asian economies was now an “established feature of the top ranks, rather than a development unique to this year”.

According to the report, the GII 2026 Innovation Tracker pointed to “continued but slower progress across the innovation cycle”. Most indicators advanced, with notable gains in scientific output, corporate research and development (R&D), battery costs and technology adoption; however, about three-quarters remained below the decade average.

Research effort nonetheless remained at a historic high, it pointed out, with global R&D intensity close to two per cent of GDP.

The WIPO report identified that the near-term environment was more demanding than the previous year: “Global growth of about 3.4pc in 2025 is expected to ease to around 3pc in 2026, held back by higher energy prices and elevated uncertainty, before recovering modestly in 2027.”

It highlighted that AI-related investment remained “the main engine on the upside”, with the largest hyper-scalers set to spend over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure across 2025 and 2026.

“This will be increasingly financed through debt and private credit, meaning a downward revision of expected AI returns could tighten financing conditions well beyond the sector,” it added.

The report noted that emerging economies, including Pakistan, could build on their standout strengths to improve their overall innovation performance.

World.title: Rising interest payments, uplift spending strained Pakistan's fiscal position in early FY27: ministry
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Despite a massive 90 per cent cut in subsidies and higher-than-targeted revenue collection, Pakistan’s fiscal and current account buffers weakened at the beginning of the current fiscal year (FY27) owing to an almost 37pc increase in interest payments coupled with greater development spending.

The “overall fiscal surplus narrowed to 0.8pc of GDP (Rs1.198 trillion), compared with 1.7pc of GDP (Rs2.124tr)” in the corresponding period of FY26, said the Ministry of Finance’s Monthly Economic Update & Outlook report issued on Thursday.
