World.title: Australia's Cape Town desperation evident on another pulsating Test day
World.content:
If there was any doubt how much the Cape Town Test matters to Pat Cummins's Australian team, one only needed to clock the cooing pack of them careening towards Cameron Green and Mitchell Starc an hour into the evening session of day three at Newlands.

The catch Green claimed to send his teammates into raptures was straightforward enough, its genesis and aftermath a little more dramatic.

Proteas opener Marques Ackerman, set fair on 62 and attacking everything Australia threw at him, had tried to limbo away from a Starc bouncer that followed him like a heat-seeking missile. Not quite agile enough with his Matrix manoeuvre, Ackerman faintly edged the ball flush into his faceguard, from which it ballooned into the cordon.

Unsure of the deflection and with his ears still ringing from the ding on his grill, Ackerman walked over to his skipper Temba Bavuma to discuss a review of the umpire's call, perhaps as surprised as the Australians when Travis Head arrived on the scene to inquire after his health.

But, in all the chaos and confusion, the crucial 15 seconds had passed before Ackerman could signal for a review. He had to depart.

It has been that sort of series, really; so many periods of ascendancy abruptly terminated by moments of genius, madness and confusion, and so many subversions of the pattern recognition Test cricket followers can normally rely on to impose a sense of order on what they're looking at.

South Africa finished the so-called moving day at 4-140 and 40 runs ahead. It would have wanted to be further in front. It could easily have been far worse off.

Earlier, in the latter stages of its first innings of 429, Australia probably let an extra 100 runs go begging. It sets up a perfect scenario even for those Australian fans who are not normally night owls: a thrilling finish on Friday night into Saturday morning.

On a pulsating day that produced 243 runs and 10 wickets, there was a second Test century for the recalled Josh Inglis and 80 for Alex Carey, both of whom fell to the off-spin of Simon Harmer.

In a Test featuring plenty of runs, only Josh Inglis has reached triple figures. (Getty Images: Grant Pitcher/Gallo Images)

An obscurity to most Australians before this series, and tipped to be dropped after the first Test, Harmer was in the thick of everything again with four wickets, two catches, a busted finger and plenty of chatter.

Youngster Cooper Connolly, looking entirely at home at Test level, made a patient 29 from 83 deliveries and might have kicked on further with better support from Australia's tail; the loss of 6-59 to finish off Australia's first innings was, as Pat Cummins often phrases such things, not ideal.

Yet it was still a 100-run lead, and early in South Africa's second innings you got the sense the game was about to break right open for an early finish.

In quick succession, Aiden Markram, who has been a thorn in Australia's side, lazily slapped a loose one from Starc into the clutches of Head at mid-off, and David Bedingham, seemingly rattled by a Starc bouncer that cannoned into his chest, holed out with another inexplicable hook.

The Proteas were 2-31, still 69 runs behind, and the hyenas were circling.

Via the counter-attack of Ackerman, then in a slow and steady partnership between Temba Bavuma and Matthew Breetzke, South Africa began its rally. Yet there was one last twist in store with barely 15 minutes left in the day's play.

Having tortured Bavuma for a few hours with his sharp turn out of the footmarks, Nathan Lyon removed the Proteas skipper again, this time a dipping off break that snuck between bat and pad to castle the lunging batsman. Bavuma is not quite to Lyon what Daryll Cullinan once was to Shane Warne, but he is not far off.

Proteas captain Temba Bavuma posed a major threat to Australia. (Getty Images: Grant Pitcher/Gallo Images)

On the matter of hoodoos, much has been made in recent days of Cummins's record-breaking streak without a wicket.

It continued today, despite periods in which the Aussie skipper bowled with genuine pace and guile, although his desperation to break his drought was made clear by one ill-advised review. Even when it is 1.6 metre Bavuma in the firing line, it is always difficult to get an LBW call when it hits above the batsman's knee roll.

In truth, the odd brain fade was perfectly excusable due to the ratcheting up of the atmosphere as this game progressed.

Some testiness and conflict in this series was inevitable, but it has manifested in curious ways. Each team's most vocal player — Marnus Labuschagne for Australia, Matthew Breetzke for the Proteas — has been its worst performed.

Breetzke, in fact, finally started to come good late on day three, and will resume tomorrow believing he is the man to turn the game for his country.

Given the way these two teams have echoed each other's efforts in the past few weeks, perhaps that suggests one last tantalising and slightly mad prospect in the Australian chase: how about Marnus Labuschagne as the last-minute hero?

World.title: Quick hits: Marnus caught in ugly exchange after all-time send off
World.content:
Marnus Labuschagne was involved in an ugly moment of DRS drama after giving a retaliatory send-off, as Temba Bavuma threw his wicket away in the shadows of stumps.

Here are the quick hits from day three of the third Test between Australia and South Africa.

1. DRS drama and Labuschagne's ugly exchange

It was one of the most contentious moments of the series when, midway through the evening session, with South Africa 2-95 and still five runs behind, Mitchell Starc collected Marques Ackerman with a steepling, searing bouncer.

The South African lost his balance as the ball thudded into what looked to be a mixture of helmet and bat before flying to Cam Green behind the wicket.

The Australians went up and so did the umpire's finger.

Undoubtedly dazed from the contact, the batter regained his composure and met with partner Temba Bavuma.

Eventually, a referral was called for, but only as the DRS timer ticked to zero.

Ackerman called for the review as the timer hit zero. (Fox Cricket)

It was touch and go, but the officials deemed Ackerman had taken too long, despite the severity of the hit.

With the South Africans pleading their case to the umpires, the ever-vocal Marnus Labuschagne could be heard giving his own opinion over the stump mic.

"The timer's up, oh no, see you buddy!" Labuschagne said from his position at the other end of the wicket.

Meanwhile, Travis Head had made his way over to the South African camp.

"Heady, what are you doing mate? He's off!" Labuschagne could be heard saying.

Head, hands outstretched towards batter and umpire in what appeared to be a peace offering, turned back towards his team and replied.

"I'm just checking if he's alright," Head said.

Head made his way over to check on Ackerman. (Fox Cricket)

Reluctantly, Ackerman made his from the middle, but spent some time at the boundary in the futile hope of being called back.

Thankfully, the replays showed the ball had collected a thick edge before crashing into visor, meaning Ackerman was doomed to be out for 62 even if the review had been permitted.

The technology showed Ackerman was rightly given out. (Fox Cricket)

Even so, it was an ugly exchange and one unlikely to endear Labuschagne to either his opponents or those watching on.

2. Bloodied Harmer keeps South Africa in the game

Simon Harmer, left, made the breakthrough in the first hour of day three. (AP Photo: Halden Krog)

With an advantage to press home at the beginning of day three, the set Australian pair of Alex Carey and Josh Inglis would have been hoping for at least another full session of batting.

The conditions were perfect, the pitch was flat, and things looked very promising as Inglis reverse-swept his way to a hugely impressive second Test century.

However, neither wicketkeeper-batter would see the other side of the first drinks break, with off spinner Simon Harmer once again doing the damage.

Only moments after ripping a nail and bloodying his fingers while attempting a low catch with his non-bowling hand, Harmer had Inglis caught behind for 102.

Harmer received some treatment on a torn nail before dislodging the two set batters. (Fox Cricket)

It was a brilliant delivery; drifting away, spinning in and kissing the outside edge of the Western Australian's blade.

Four overs later, a similarly exquisite off break had Carey (80) nudging to Aiden Markram at slip, and Harmer, a fingernail down, had dragged his side back into the game.

Australia's tail proceeded to eke out a 100-run first-innings lead, eventually dismissed for 429.

3. Marnus gives it to Bedingham

Labuschagne was in quite a mood on day three.

Before the DRS drama in the evening session, the Queenslander took quite some pleasure in giving it back to Proteas batter David Bedingham.

On day two, Matthew Breetzke had joyously celebrated Labuschagne's five-ball duck by leaping over the pitch and shouting directly at the Australian.

And when Bedingham holed out to Josh Hazlewood during the middle session on day three, Labuschagne responded in similar fashion.

The Queenslander had his chest puffed out as he ran towards the South African, face red and fist pumping, screaming what you can only imagine was something entirely considered and reasonable.

Bedingham was out for 11 and South Africa's second innings was already beginning to teeter at 2-31.

4. A strange moment on the hill

It was an unlikely proposal. (Fox Cricket)

It was a strange morning on the hill.

During the first session, the broadcast cameras found a man holding a sign that read: "Ryan Rickelton, is your mum single?"

The middle-aged gentleman received a good amount of screen time, which he used to blow kisses and adjust his sunglasses in a performance that probably wouldn't have endeared him to anyone in the Rickelton family.

Rickelton, South Africa's wicketkeeper-batter, was stony-faced in response, before pursing his lips and shaking his head solemnly.

The commentators were lost for words at what was an uncomfortable moment for everyone involved — and especially, you'd imagine, for Ryan Rickelton's mother.

5. Bavuma throws it away in the shadows of stumps

Stumps were in sight for Bavuma and Matthew Breetzke.

The South African pair had so diligently rebuilt South Africa's innings after Ackerman's dismissal, and had just eight more balls to survive.

But with shadows lengthening at Newlands and with the pitch offering more and more for the slower bowlers, Nathan Lyon conjured a little bit of magic.

It was the perfect off spinner's delivery; drifting, turning sharply and bowling a swinging Bavuma clean through the gate.

However, it was a wildly inappropriate shot from the usually so-considered Bavuma, and the South African captain couldn't quite believe what had happened.

Bavuma was a picture of regret on his way from the middle. (Fox Cricket)

He grimaced and shook his head as he made is way from the middle for 35, with South Africa finishing the day on 4-140 and just 40 runs in front.

World.title: Wallaby 'incredibly proud' as brother represents Australian Deaf Rugby
World.content:
For as long as he can remember, Wallabies back-rower Charlie Cale has always been able to rely on his older brother Jack.

Growing up in Sydney's northern suburbs, they would often team up together against the eldest of the Cale boys, Sam, in fierce backyard rugby battles.

Even when it came to studying during their school years, Charlie knew Jack was in his corner.

"He helped me with a lot of my schoolwork," Charlie fondly tells ABC Sport.

"There's been a few exams … he's helped me in a lot of ways, actually.

"That's the best thing about Jack. He's always been there for me and anyone else that has needed him.

"He's one of a kind."

Jack's encouragement is repaid by the support he receives from Charlie and Sam, who both keenly follow his career with the Australian Deaf Rugby (ADR) men's squad.

Last Tuesday night in Sydney, Charlie proudly presented Jack, Australia's vice-captain, with his official team tie ahead of the World Deaf Rugby Sevens Championship, which begin in Tokyo this weekend.

Australia's men's and women's squads are among the favourites to emerge triumphant once the tournament concludes on November 3.

Jack Cale (right) pictured with brothers Charlie (centre) and Sam. (Instagram: Tim Cale)

Jack is grateful to have Charlie and Sam's backing as he juggles rugby commitments with his job as a lawyer.

"It's always been really helpful having two brothers to go through a rugby career with," says Jack, who has played for Eastwood (Shute Shield) and Mosman (Subbies) at club level.

"We're always checking in with each other, trying to watch each other's games.

"Charlie, even with the limited time he gets outside of training with Brumbies and Wallabies squads, is always trying to watch our games as well."

Charlie Cale has played six Tests for the Wallabies. (Getty Images: Chris Hyde)

On the international stage

Jack's introduction to deaf rugby came out of the blue.

"In late 2022, I got a phone call from an old coach of mine on a Saturday morning," says Jack, who had played colts and grade rugby in Sydney by this stage.

"He gave me a call and said, 'Mate, there's this deaf rugby trial happening down at Hunters Hill.'

"Of course, I didn't know what he was talking about as I hadn't really heard anything before.

"I went down there and ran around in a bit of a sevens trial, for maybe 20 or 25 minutes.

"I didn't think I'd actually played that well. I didn't touch the ball that much.

"I came off the field and I wasn't sure what to expect."

Jack Cale during his Eastwood playing days. (Instagram: Tim Cale)

A letter arrived in the mail a few months later in early 2023, informing Jack he was selected in the ADR men's squad for the World Deaf Rugby Sevens Championship, which were being held in Córdoba, Argentina in April of that year.

There was one small problem, though.

Jack found out about his selection during the club rugby off-season, meaning he was not exactly at peak fitness.

"I had to get myself fit pretty quickly without any rugby training, which was a bit of a struggle," Jack laughs.

Australia finished runner-up in the men's competition at the 2023 world titles. (Instagram: Australian Deaf Rugby)

Jack worked his way back into shape and seamlessly joined the Australian line-up, which he helped lead in his vice-captaincy role.

They made the final, gallantly losing 20-5 to Wales, while Australia finished third overall in the women's competition.

In Tokyo, the men's squad faces England, Japan, Hong Kong China and Italy in the pool stage, with the top three advancing to the knockout rounds of the tournament.

The Australian women's team were presented with their ties in Sydney on Tuesday night. (Supplied: Alfred Naputo)

Australia is one of six teams in the women's draw, where it plays Fiji, England, Wales, New Zealand and a combined Barbarians team in a single pool.

Each will progress, with the two top-ranked teams moving directly to the semifinals.

Australian squads: Men: Tim Anstey (c), Jack Cale (vc), Anau Takiari, Ben Rogers, Charlie Jeffries, Cruz Lemming, Geofrey Reynolds, Kyle Howlett, Josh Chapman, Josh Doe, Royden Chatfield, Tom Witts, Dave Kearsey (coach) Women: Sydnee Cooke (c), Amy Reid, Ashanti Pennell, Bridie Searle, Bianca Roberts, Cathy Ross, Kari Massey, Khiara McCormick, Olivia Hall, Peta Stephens, Sally Faehrmann, Robbie Pirika (coach)

Having avoided Wales in the men's round-robin matches, Jack considers England to be Australia's main threat in the preliminary phase.

"You've obviously got to go match by match," Jack says.

"It's important to get through the pool stage as well as we can and then the mindset obviously shifts to the knockout stages.

"I'd consider us in the better pool for the opportunity to do that."

Embracing challenges

To participate in World Deaf Rugby tournaments, players must have an average bilateral hearing loss across both ears of at least 40 decibels.

The level of hearing loss varies from player to player in the Australian teams, which illustrates to Jack the importance of non-verbal communication during matches.

"I stepped into this environment where nothing was said on a rugby field," he says.

"It was a bit of a challenge to get used to that.

"But I also really enjoyed that challenge, being able to communicate with some of those guys whose hearing is a lot more affected than mine is."

The Australian men's team at Tuesday night's tie presentation. (Supplied: Alfred Naputo)

As much as Jack loves playing alongside his Australian teammates, he also gets a kick out of facing them in club rugby.

On one such occasion last year, he and Australian captain Tim Anstey opposed each other when Mosman met Newport in the NSW Subbies competition.

"It's pretty awesome playing against someone like that, who you now travel with on international tours," Jack says.

"But it's also surreal finding out that someone you might have been playing rugby against is also partially deaf and had the same struggles as you growing up, and you're now representing your country with them.

"It's pretty cool."

Tim Anstey (left) and Jack Cale after a Subbies match in 2025. (Instagram: Australian Deaf Rugby)

While Jack relishes every chance to represent Australia, spreading the message of inclusivity is just as important to him and everyone involved in deaf rugby.

ADR states its goal is to give every deaf and hard-of-hearing athlete the opportunity to play the game, regardless of their experience level.

"We want to find as many deaf or hard-of-hearing rugby players as we can," Jack says.

"It's really just word of mouth within deaf and hard-of-hearing communities."

Jack's family is also firmly behind the cause.

"I've got a lot of respect for this [ADR] program," says Charlie, who has played six Tests for the Wallabies.

"It gives these guys a platform and opportunity they may have lacked growing up.

"We know how much it means to Jack and therefore it means a lot to us."

Family support

Charlie got up early in the morning to watch Jack play at the world titles in Córdoba three years ago.

But a friendlier time zone will make it easier for him to follow his brother's progress in Tokyo.

"I don't think I've missed a game," Charlie says.

"I've woken up at 2am or 3am. I love watching him play."

Jack Cale (centre) with his parents Tim (left) and Sue. (Instagram: Tim Cale)

As he did in Córdoba, Jack will have his devoted mum and dad, Sue and Tim, barracking from the sidelines in Tokyo.

The Cale parents do everything possible to watch their three sons play rugby.

"I don't think our mother has missed a rugby game of ours in God knows how many years," Jack says.

"Dad is always on the phone, straight after games, checking in with us and seeing how we've gone."

Just as he helped Charlie all those years ago with his schoolwork, Jack knows he can also depend on the support of his family.

"We're incredibly proud of him," Charlie says.

World.title: WBBL season gets underway with Thunder thumping of Renegades
World.content:
Anika Learoyd has carved out a career-best innings as the Sydney Thunder began its WBBL campaign with a convincing six-wicket win over the Melbourne Renegades in the season opener.

Learoyd made 48 off 37 balls after off-spinner Georgia Voll (4-26) did most of the damage in the first match of a double-header at Junction Oval today.

The Melbourne Stars host the Hobart Hurricanes in the night game.

In at first drop, after Voll made 25 off 18, including the Thunder's only six of the match, Learoyd hit nine boundaries and put on 62 with Heather Knight in a match-winning third-wicket partnership.

The pair took 28 runs from the power surge, putting the Thunder within sight of victory.

Knight (29 not out off 22 balls) and Nadine de Klerk (12no off six) finished the job, guiding their team to 4-140 with 18 balls to spare.

Learoyd admitted feeling "really nervous" batting near the top of the order, but will take confidence from starting the season with a strong performance.

Earlier, Voll's four wickets and hand in a run-out were crucial in restricting the Renegades to 9-138 from their 20 overs.

Renegades opener Hayley Matthews gave her side a strong start, blasting 45 from 30 balls before holing out in the deep.

Matthews put on 56 for the first wicket with Courtney Webb (22 from 24), and Georgia Wareham made a handy 23 from 19, but a late-innings collapse ended their chances.

The Renegades lost 5-2 in seven balls through the 17th and 18th overs as Voll wreaked havoc.

AAP

World.title: Late Lyon wicket puts Australia in control of deciding Test
World.content:
The late wicket of Proteas skipper Temba Bavuma has given Australia the upper hand over South Africa on a fascinating third day at Newlands in Cape Town.

Nathan Lyon clean bowled Bavuma with less then five minutes to go before stumps on a wearing pitch, leaving the hosts 4-140, with a lead of just 40 runs.

Josh Inglis scored a century as part of a 185-run fifth wicket partnership with Alex Carey to give Australia a 100-run first innings lead before tea.

South Africa overhauled that deficit before the close, but not before losing three wickets at Mitch Starc (2-29) and Josh Hazlewood (1-37) made early inroads to the Proteas' top order.

Australia resumed on day three with a one run lead and two well-set batters in Carey (51no) and Inglish (85no) in the middle, the pitch wearing but, at that stage offering no genuine assistance to the bowlers.

Carey and Inglis continued their excellent partnership to build Australia's lead, looking entirely untroubled as Inglis bought up his second Test century.

However, moments later Simon Harmer came into the attack and extracted an edge from Inglis's bat to have him out for 102, ending a hugely profitable 185-run partnership.

Carey (80) departed just nine runs later, Harmer again extracting an edge with Aiden Markram taking a good low catch.

Simon Harmer, left, made the breakthrough in the first hour of day three. (AP Photo: Halden Krog)

Cooper Connolly managed the tail, turning down singles as Pat Cummins (bowled by Kagiso Rabada for 0) and Nathan Lyon (caught Harmer off the bowling of Mulder for 1) departed.

But his innings ended when Marco Jansen caught and bowled him for 29, ending the innings with a lead of exactly 100 runs.

In response, Markram (1) was caught by Travis Head driving Starc, and David Bedingham (11) fell to a top edged pull shot off Josh Hazlewood to leave the Proteas 2-31.

Travis Head, second right, caught Aiden Markram dfor just a single run. (AP Photo: Halden Krog)

Marques Ackerman and Temba Bavuma combined for a 64-run partnership before Starc brutally bounced Ackerman out for 62.

Starc delivered a head-hunting bouncer right into the grill of the Proteas opener, knocking him backwards.

A clearly shaken Ackerman wanted to review after conversing with his skipper, but was controversially ruled to have taken too long to ask for it and had to depart.

In the end, the replay showed a fine top edge as Ackerman attempted to get his bat up to protect his face so the decision saved South Africa a review, although Marnus Labuschagne chastising Travis Head for checking on the South African opener's welfare left a sour taste in the mouth.

Temba Bavuma played a watchful innings after tea. (AP Photo: Halden Krog)

Bavuma and Matthew Breetzke built a steady 36-run partnership as the shadows lengthened across the ground.

But Lyon, who was extracting increasingly vicious spin and bounce in the dusty pitch, had one last say before stumps were called to put them in an ideal position heading into day four.

Look back on how all the action unfolded in our live blog.

World.title: Brewers complete underdog story with maiden World Series title
World.content:
The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers, playing in the smallest market in the majors, are World Series champions for the first time.

Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings, rookie Cooper Pratt had two more hits and two runs batted in (RBIs), and the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field.

"It's the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here. I know the city's waited a long, long time for this," Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said.

"We're so happy to bring it home to them. I can't wait to get back there and celebrate."

World Series MVP William Contreras hit an RBI double and Misiorowski allowed just two hits before leaving the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee's dugout for the last three games.

The 22-year-old Pratt set a series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth. Jackson Chourio set a five-game series record with 11 hits.

"This is one of the greatest moments of my life. Oh my gosh. It doesn't even feel real," said Pratt, who made his major league debut in June.

"This is surreal. It only took four months."

The championship comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee the following year. The Brewers' only previous trip to the World Series in 1982 ended in heartbreak when they blew a 3-1 lead in the sixth inning of Game 7 and lost 6-3 to the St. Louis Cardinals.

But this team displayed the toughness and resilience of 67-year-old manager Pat Murphy, who survived a heart attack in 2020 and was the NL Manager of the Year in his first two full seasons at the helm in 2024 and 2025.

"This group of guys right here, the 2026 team, will be remembered forever — and they deserve that because they were a team," Murphy said.

"When you talk about this team, you've got to talk about people who care about each other. They're not worried about their own stats. No-one cares about that. They care about coming together and winning tonight."

AP

World.title: Aussie captain most expensive player at WPL auction
World.content:
Australia captain Sophie Molineux has proved the most expensive buy in India's Women's Premier League auction, and she'll suit up for a UP Warriorz side captained by former national team skipper Meg Lanning.

With many of the world's top players having already been retained for the 2027 edition of the lucrative Indian league, Molineux's signature was the most coveted one still left and the Lucknow-based franchise captured the T20 World Cup-winning skipper for the biggest price, INR 1.1 crore ($A164,000).

The spinning all-rounder won't be leading the team in the January 14-February 7 tournament, though.

Instead, Molineux will be playing under the captaincy of 34-year-old Lanning, the inspirational figure who skippered Australia when she first came into the side, in a T20I in India eight years ago.

Big life changes for WBBL winning duo A lot has changed since Nicola Carey and Elyse Villani lifted the WBBL trophy last year, as the Hobart Hurricanes prepare to defend their title.

Molineux's base price in the auction in Kochi was 50 Lakh ($A75,000) but she eventually went for over twice that price as a bidding battle began between Royal Challengers Bengaluru and the Warriorz.

With their superior budget, UP also snapped up big-hitting all-rounder Grace Harris going for $45,000, meaning that the side will have four Australians in their ranks with Phoebe Litchfield already on board.

Intriguingly, national skipper Molineux has been bought for less than both Lanning and Litchfield and four others among the 14-strong Australian contingent in the league.

The most expensive Australian in the league — each of the five teams has at least one Aussie World Cup winner in its ranks — will be Ash Gardner, captain of the Gujarat Giants, who was retained for $523,000 in a side that also includes four Aussies.

Gardner is the joint most-lucrative retention, alongside Royal Challengers Bengaluru captain Smriti Mandhana and Mumbai Indians' England skipper Nat Sciver-Brunt.

Of the 11 Australians up for grabs in Wednesday's auction, only three were sold.

Heather Graham, Tayla Vlaeminck, Tess Flintoff, Charli Knott, Samantha Bates, Maitlan Brown, Maddie Penna and Milly Illingworth were the ones to miss out.

World.title: Gold Coast Suns AFLW finals feat faces home-ground headache
World.content:
The Gold Coast Suns have earned their place in the AFLW finals — but their reward could be a home final away from home.

After back-to-back seasons near the bottom of the ladder, the Suns have surged into fourth spot with eight wins, booking their first finals appearance since 2023.

A victory over GWS on Sunday would strengthen their grip on a double chance, guaranteeing a home final during the series.

But there's a catch.

Carrara Stadium is unavailable for weeks two, three and four of the finals series, due to Australia's T20 clash with England, leaving the Suns and the AFL searching for an alternative venue.

Springfield, home of Queensland rivals the Brisbane Lions and an hour's drive up the highway, and Southport's Fankhauser Reserve are among the alternatives being considered.

Southport however comes with a significant caveat — any final would need to be played during the day, when November temperatures average around 28 degrees and humidity can hover around 70 per cent.

A spokesperson for the club said it is "working with all stakeholders on home venues for each week of the finals" where Carrara is not available.

"Our playing group and staff have been resolute all season in their efforts to play anywhere, anytime, across eight different venues and we know they'll take that attitude into any scenario that presents throughout the post-season campaign," the spokesperson said.

Despite this, coach Rhyce Shaw said on Tuesday the club is embracing the excitement of a long-awaited finals campaign.

Michael Voss Oval in Springfield is being considered as one option for an alternative venue. (Supplied: Brisbane Lions)

"I took [my son] Henry to swimming the other day and all the staff were getting behind us," Shaw said.

"It is exciting for our footy club … It's been a bit of a tough year all round, but for our girls to pick up the slack a little bit and get going and make finals is really, really cool."

"We've got a big job against the Giants and then we'll think of finals after that."

If the Suns were to fall to GWS on Sunday, there is the potential for them finish as low as seventh on the ladder.

However, a fifth or sixth place finish would mean they would earn a home final next weekend and the ABC can confirm Carrara Stadium would be available in this instance.

Rhyce Shaw, Senior Coach of the Suns, says it's been a "tough year" for the club. (Getty Images: Maya Thompson)

ABC Sport AFLW expert Chyloe Kurdas said regardless of the ladder outcome, the lack of venue certainty is an unwanted distraction.

"I think it is such a valuable home ground advantage [finishing in the top four] but it's also not just that, it's the distraction of this conversation right now that happens in the lead up to," she said.

"It occupies bandwidth and it occupies energy from the playing group and the coaching group and the staff."

Kurdas said not being able to play at Carrara, a venue the side has won their last three games at, would be a missed opportunity.

"I think there's a real sweet spot right now with the number of talented kids that are Gold Coast born and raised … that are now playing at the Suns," Kurdas said.

"Fan engagement is going to be such an important part of this Gold Coast Suns women's team journey … they're so talented."

The Suns have had a 75 per cent increase in AFLW memberships for this season.

A familiar problem

The Suns aren't the only club caught in a scheduling squeeze.

Second-placed Geelong, one win away from securing a top-two finish, also faces a venue clash, with Kardinia Park unavailable next weekend due to the AUSX Supercross Championship.

While, the AFLW Grand Final, should it be played in Melbourne, has already been locked in for Princes Park — with a capacity of 13 thousand that has sold out for the showpiece game within hours in recent seasons.

Docklands Stadium, with a 53,343-capacity is unavailable, with Harry Styles booked across the weekend, despite players calling for a bigger venue.

The Geelong Cats are facing a similar venue problem. (Getty Images: Quinn Rooney)

The Grand Final has also been scheduled for Friday night, November 27, to avoid a clash with the Victorian State Election.

It's a familiar problem that's haunted the competition since it started in 2017.

In the inaugural season, the Brisbane Lions earned the right to host the Grand Final but were forced to play at Carrara, with the Gabba unavailable due to cricket.

Now in its 11th season, the debate continues about where the AFLW competition belongs in the sporting calendar.

The AFL is reportedly considering an earlier start to align the women's season with the end of the men's competition.

"You do your due diligence and you look at where is there likely to be these kind of clashes," Chyloe Kurdas said.

"But ultimately, whenever you choose to play it, you then have to live and die by those decisions."

She says clubs and the AFL must also be prepared to make commercial decisions that put their women's programs first.

" You can't just buy in when it suits you. "

The AFL and Stadiums Queensland were contacted for comment.

Tech.title: Patrick Stewart has died at age 86
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Patrick Stewart, best known for his roles in Star Trek and X-Men, has died at age 86. A message posted to Stewart’s Instagram account says the actor died in his Los Angeles home on Wednesday “following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.”

Born in 1940 in Mirfield, Yorkshire, England, Stewart began his acting career in theater. He eventually landed the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, which ran from 1987 to 1994. Stewart returned as the Star Trek captain in subsequent films, including Star Trek: Generations (1994), Star Trek: First Contact (1996), Star Trek: Insurrection (1998), and Star Trek: Nemesis (2002). Stewart also starred as Professor Charles Xavier in several X-Men movies. He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010.

“His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the message on Instagram says. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.”

Tech.title: Reddit will force everyone to log in
Tech.content:
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Reddit is announcing a huge shift: It’s going to start requiring users to log in.

Right now, you can browse Reddit without having an account, and the site is generally a great resource for crowdsourced information on a whole range of topics. I know I’m not the only person who appends “reddit” to a lot of Google searches to find answers to things written by actual humans instead of robots. But that openness has made it a target for scraping and automated traffic, leading Reddit to file lawsuits over alleged unauthorized access of its data and make product changes like limiting access to “Old Reddit.”

There’s no definitive timeline on when this change will roll out to all users, or how the site will work if you’re logged out. (If I send my friend a link to a thread and they aren’t logged in, what will they see?) To start, Reddit will test the logged-in requirement in “select markets outside the US” in the “coming months,” according to CEO Steve Huffman. “We’ll look at the impact on the user experience, on our business, and on the whole Reddit ecosystem, figure out where the right boundaries are, and go from there.” Reddit has also rebuilt and is rereleasing the Reddit app’s incognito mode.

Huffman claims the login requirement is better for Reddit’s user experience and its ads business and is “more protective of Reddit data.” The “vast majority” of unauthorized Reddit access happens “through our logged-out experiences,” though the company will still strike licensing deals of its data with companies, like the deals it made with OpenAI and Google in 2024. Huffman notes that Reddit does not need to know a logged-in user’s identity — “Honestly, we don’t want to know” — just that the user is logged in at all. And he says that more logged-in users lets the company deliver “more relevant ads.”

“This is a big change for Reddit, where we’ve allowed logged-out access to basically all of Reddit for the last two decades,” Huffman says. “And I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me. But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business.”

Reddit is making this announcement alongside its Q3 2026 earnings, which were released today. Search traffic was “down meaningfully” in Q3, Huffman says in the company’s shareholder letter, with logged-out traffic and web traffic being the most heavily impacted. “During October, we have seen that search traffic has dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week,” Huffman says.

However, Huffman notes that app and logged-in daily active unique users make up “over 80% of the monetization on Reddit,” which he says “speaks to the strength of Reddit as a destination and the impact of our ongoing product work.”

Rivian reported its third quarter earnings of 2026, providing us a closer look at the company’s financial health as it ramps up production of its all-important R2 electric vehicle — which is now, for the first time, outselling all of Rivian’s other EVs.

Rivian said it brought in $2.155 billion in revenue, a 38 percent increase compared to the $1.558 billion in Q3 2025. Of that amount, $1.55 billion came from automotive revenue, which is up 36 percent year over year. Comparatively, the company reported $605 million from software and subscription services, a 45 percent increase year over year. As EV sales slow down, the company is seeking to make more money from its digital products, including the Autonomy Plus package.

Automotive gross profits were on an upward trajectory, a sign that the company’s finances were improving as it delivered more vehicles. Rivian made $176 million in gross profit this quarter, a $152 million improvement compared to the same time last year. The company still lost $80 million in Q3 automotive gross profits, which is much better than the $130 million loss a year ago.

In other words, Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle. (Also, the company continued to sell pollution credits to other carmakers, and also received a tariff refund from the government — all of which was recorded as revenue.)

Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle.

Rivian brought in $256 million in profit in software and services, up $102 million from last year, with a strong 42 percent profit margin. Most of this cash came from licensing their tech to Volkswagen, alongside customer subscriptions for Rivian’s Autonomy Plus driving features. In many ways, Rivian’s tech partnership with Volkswagen and software sales are currently paying the bills, keeping the company profitable overall while it absorbs a lot of heavy upfront costs from launching the R2.

Earlier this month, Rivian reported a record sales quarter, with 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered. That represents an 85 percent year-over-year increase in production and a 45 percent jump in deliveries. (For a direct-to-consumer automaker like Rivian, deliveries serve as a proxy for sales.)

Rivian doesn’t break down sales by model, so we don’t exactly how many R2s have reached customers so far. But the company said that the R2 is now the “best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume,” outselling the R1T and R1S, as well as the Electric Delivery Van (EDV).

“We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter,” Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement, ahead of the company’s earnings call this afternoon. “Customer and media feedback on R2 has been exceptional.”

The R2 was designed from the ground up to be Rivian’s higher-volume, mass-market offering — and by overtaking the company’s more expensive, lower-volume legacy vehicles, it seems to be doing just that. Still, the R2 isn’t bringing in the bulk of the revenue yet, as indicated by Rivian’s use of the phrase “by volume.” Most of the money is still coming from the VW partnership and its software division.

But that could change once Rivian starts shipping the more affordable versions of the R2, like the $55,485 Premium trim (coming in late 2026), the $49,985 Standard Long-Range (early 2027), and the $46,495 Standard (late 2027).

Developing…

Tech.title: GM to pay $220 million to resolve claims it sold driving habits data
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold driver and location information to data brokers, as reported earlier by Reuters. The agreement, which resolves a complaint from a coalition of 36 US attorneys general, requires GM to limit the driving data it collects and obtain “express consent” from drivers before collecting their information.

The allegations surround GM’s now-discontinued Smart Driver program, which collected data about driving habits, including acceleration, braking, and trip length. GM allegedly passed this information to data brokers, enabling insurance companies to purchase the data and raise premiums. The states also accused GM of failing to notify drivers that they were enrolled in its Smart Driver program, and that the carmaker was collecting their data.

“This agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” GM spokesperson Charlotte McCoy said in an emailed statement to The Verge. “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”

This settlement comes just months after GM agreed to pay $12.75 million to settle similar claims in California. Oregon AG Dan Rayfield and Washington AG Nick Brown co-led the states’ case against GM, which also included New York, Florida, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and many others.

“People bought a car, not a tracking device,” Rayfield says in a press release. “GM told drivers this program would help them drive more safely and promised it wouldn’t share their data with insurers without permission. Our investigation found GM sold that data anyway, and some drivers paid for it with higher premiums.”

Update, October 29th: Added a statement from GM.

Tech.title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now
Tech.content:
is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini. The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now.

Google added support for generating and downloading files in Gemini earlier this year, but now you can tweak those files without leaving the Gemini app. Google says you can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text in files to ask Gemini questions or prompt it to make changes to the file, like highlighting a table and asking Gemini to turn it into a graph.

You could already use Gemini to edit files with its integrations in Google’s Workspace apps, like the Gemini bar in Google Docs. Anthropic also launched a feature earlier this year that allows users to generate and edit documents and presentations in Claude chats.

Tech.title: Ikea’s colorful donut-shaped smart lamp is $20 off
Tech.content:
With its playful design, versatility, and relatively affordable price, the Ikea Varmblixt quickly became one of my colleague Jennifer Pattison Tuohy’s new favorite smart light products when she tested it in April. Now, the donut-shaped lamp is on sale for $79.99 ($20 off) through November 11th at Ikea.

Don’t let us tell you where you can or cannot put your Varmblixt. But it’s meant to sit on a table or be mounted on a wall (it can hang from a drilled-in screw, nothing fancy). At just 180 lumens, it isn’t particularly bright, so it’s better suited for use as a bedside lamp or for mood lighting than being tasked to illuminate a room. The newer model lets you cycle through 12 preset colors, including shades of pink, blue, green, and white, as opposed to just orange with the predecessor. The included wireless remote lets you switch between colors, adjust the brightness, and turn the lamp on or off without needing an app or a separate hub (there’s a power button on the lamp itself) . You can also use the remote to control other compatible Ikea lights.

For those who want to embed the Varmblixt into their smart home setup, the lamp supports Matter, allowing it to work with compatible smart home platforms including Apple Home, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa. In addition to letting you control the lights with your voice, this gives you access to hundreds more colors, lets you set lighting schedules and sleep or wake-up routines, and allows you to connect the lamp with motion sensors and other smart lights you may have. You can unlock those features with Ikea’s Dirigera hub, as well, which also offers a feature through its Home Smart app that gradually adjusts the shade of white throughout the day akin to natural daylight.

Tech.title: Apple’s new laptop supports one of the coolest features for color pros
Tech.content:
is a senior reviewer covering TVs and audio. He has over 20 years experience in AV, and has previously been on staff at Digital Trends and Reviewed.

The new MacBook Pro brings with it a bunch of firsts for Apple laptops, the two flashiest being an OLED display and touchscreen functionality. But as an image-accuracy enthusiast, trained calibrator, and resident display expert, what excites me most about the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is the technology it uses to display an accurate picture. It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes. It could be the future for displays.

CMFs, or color-matching functions, mathematically represent how we perceive color, and there are a few different variations. The specification that’s been the standard for years is CIE 1931 (CIE stands for Commission Internationale de l’Éclairage, or International Commission on Illumination). For nearly a century, CIE 1931 has been a reliable calibration target, and most of the reference modes on the new MacBook use it.

But with the development of new display technologies over the past 20 years that have ultra-narrow band spectra — such as OLED, LEDs with KSF phosphors, and quantum dots — CIE 1931’s shortcomings are increasingly apparent. Even when calibrated to the same D65 white point, the same image on an OLED and quantum dot LED can look identical to one person, but different to another because of biological variations in our eyes. We all have small discrepancies in our eyes — such as the sensitivity of the cones in our eyes, which allow us to see color — and those can change as we age. CIE 1931 doesn’t properly handle that and was created based on only 17 test subjects. It’s not ideal in a professional setting where content needs to look the same regardless of the screen technology it’s on or who’s viewing it. Apple CMF 2026 addresses that, so that displays look the same regardless of the technology they use.

Apple first included its new CMF on the Studio Display XDR, which I reviewed earlier this year and found to be an excellent, albeit expensive, monitor for color professionals because of Apple CMF 2026 and the reference color modes. But the fact that this technology is now on a laptop that’s portable and not just a standalone monitor living on a desk is a big help for professionals on the move.

Related The Apple Studio Display XDR is an excellent but expensive pro option

As on the Studio Display XDR, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display has two Apple CMF 2026 reference modes — one for P3 color primaries and one that includes both P3 and Adobe RGB color primaries for more flexibility. Peak brightness with both HDR and SDR content is 2,000 nits (on the XDR monitor peak SDR luminance is up to 1,000 nits), and the True Tone setting automatically adjusts HDR tone mapping, brightness, and white point based on ambient lighting. (An option to disable True Tone is in Displays preferences.)

The MacBook doesn’t require using Apple CMF 2026, as there are 14 more reference color modes that use the CIE 1931 color space — it is still the standard, after all — including DICOM for medical imaging (which is cool, but only useful to those in the medical field). The MacBook also supports Apple Pro Display Calibrator, which includes three calibration methods to adjust the reference color modes, or a custom mode, if necessary. There are options for a full calibration or to fine-tune a calibration with the proper measurement gear, or to visually fine-tune the display.

Color science and display technologies have come a long way since 1931, when the CIE 1931 color space was established. Apple’s development of the Apple CMF 2026 and its standardization efforts — the company is currently working with a CIE technical committee on a proposed standard — is an important step to make sure current display technologies look the same to as many people as possible.

Extending support to the new MacBook expands the user base considerably (let’s face it, more people are buying a touchscreen MacBook, even at $2,900, than a $3,300 professional monitor). And more importantly, it gives professionals that can get the most out of it easier, portable access.

Tech.title: Elon Musk is ‘truly a genius,’ says Vladimir Putin
Tech.content:
In Brief

Russian President Vladimir Putin said that he and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk are in “close contact” about Rassvet, Russia’s answer to Starlink, Musk’s internet satellite service.

“Elon Musk is a genius, truly a genius,” Putin said at the Russia-Africa Summit on Wednesday. “He has already had more than 5,000 such satellites in orbit, while we are only taking the first steps.”

A potential relationship between Putin and Musk could have serious implications. Musk has recently voiced frustration with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, whose country has been fighting a Russian invasion since 2022. After the U.S. eased sanctions on Russia earlier this month, Ukrainian officials became concerned that Ukraine could lose access to Starshield, the military version of Musk’s Starlink network, which Ukrainian forces rely on.

There was some merit to these concerns. For about 10 days earlier this month, Ukrainian drones experienced frequent losses of connectivity. According to the Wall Street Journal, Musk ordered SpaceX to limit Ukraine’s Starlink access, though other reports say the order came from the White House. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine violated Starlink terms of service by using the technology for “offensive drone strikes to kill people.”

Starlink service in Ukraine appears to have since resumed normal operations.

“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk also wrote on X. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”

Tech.title: Amazon reported booming cloud revenue but otherwise missed expectations
Tech.content:
Amazon reported its third-quarter earnings on Thursday and missed analysts’ expectations for both its total revenue and earnings per share. There were other murky numbers in the report that scared investors, too, including how much cash the company is burning through.

But the report did have a big, bright spot: its cloud unit, Amazon Web Services, beat revenue expectations and grew a whopping 39% compared to the year-ago quarter.

Here are the numbers:

Net sales increased 12% to $201.9 billion. But analysts were expecting $202.2 billion, according to FactSet.

Fully diluted earnings per share were $1.89. Analysts were expecting $1.97.

AWS sales reached $45.98 billion. Analysts were expecting $45.29 billion. In addition, Amazon said that AWS operating income grew to $17.8 billion, compared with $11.4 billion in the third quarter of 2025.

But here’s the biggest ouch of the report: Free cash flow fell to a negative of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 months — meaning the company was spending far more cash than it generated. This compares to positive free cash flow of $14.8 billion for the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2025.

The big spending was driven largely by Amazon’s investments in AI, the company said. With one quarter left in its fiscal year, Amazon reiterated that it still expects to end its 2026 with cash capital expenditures of about $220 billion.

To put that in perspective, the company forecast fourth-quarter net sales of between $240 billion and $247 billion. The fourth quarter is typically a retainer’s biggest, thanks to the holiday shopping season. That means Amazon expects to spend almost as much on capital expenditures, largely for AI, over the full year as it expects to bring in from sales in the fourth quarter alone.

Tech.title: GM reaches $220M settlement over selling drivers’ private data
Tech.content:
General Motors will pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers.

As part of the settlement, GM must get drivers’ express consent before it collects or shares their driving and location data — terms that are in line with separate agreements it previously reached with California and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). This settlement does contain a new requirement that GM must have a third party assess the automaker’s compliance with the privacy program it has put in place.

The agreement announced Thursday settles a lawsuit brought by a coalition of attorneys general from 36 states that alleged GM had sold the information to data brokers, which in turn then sold it to insurance providers.

“This agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” GM said in an emailed statement. “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”

The settlement comes more than two years after a New York Times report showed how GM and OnStar collected, used, and sold drivers’ precise geolocation data and driving behavior to third parties, including data brokers LexisNexis and Verisk. The data was collected through GM’s Smart Driver program, a free feature contained within its connected car apps that tracked and rated driving behaviors and seat belt use. Data brokers sold this information to insurance providers, which could affect customers’ rates, the NYT reported at the time.

GM discontinued Smart Driver in 2024, but that didn’t stop legal action. In January, the FTC finalized an order that bans GM and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data. The FTC settlement, as well as the multistate one announced Thursday, also requires GM to be more transparent with its consumers and receive their explicit consent for certain collection.

The company now says it is focused on protecting the privacy of its customers and will no longer sell vehicle information that can be linked to an individual, their vehicle location, or how they drive. However, GM may still disclose anonymized data not tied to an individual with certain partners. GM has also updated the language in its privacy policy and created a consumer-facing Privacy Center.

The settlement and mandated changes to how GM handles customer driving data come as more sensor-laden vehicles equipped with computing power enter the market. Automakers have made large bets on software-centric vehicles that drivers and passengers can interact with and connect with other digital apps such as their calendar, messages, and email.

For instance, GM is adding a personal AI assistant to OnStar, its 30-year-old safety and roadside assistance service. Cameras on the vehicle will be connected to the software to offer live views as well as crash and safety recordings. Users will also be able to use voice to control certain functions on the vehicle, including climate, and ask questions about any specific vehicle feature.

The automaker emphasized its privacy protections when it announced the new assistant during its GM Forward event in October. The company said customers will have the ability to decide what data is shared and that the recordings have time limits and are encrypted. GM said it and OnStar cannot access Connected Camera recordings. Customers will also be able to manage permissions. However, customers who opt not to share their data will likely have limited access to certain features, according to GM.

Tech.title: Fan-fiction site Archive of Our Own could be offline for up to 4 weeks
Tech.content:
In Brief

Archive of our Own (AO3), the popular site where fans publish and read stories about their favorite characters and worlds, has bad news for its community. After going offline for what was supposed to be routine overnight maintenance, the site says it could stay online for almost a whole month.

“We estimate that service restoration for AO3 will take around 2 weeks but it could be up to 4 weeks,” the AO3 status page says. “We are hopeful that we will be able to bring the site back up in a degraded state sooner.”

AO3 is a project of the nonprofit Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), which relies on volunteers and donations to keep the site afloat. The site has such a passionate user base that, within two hours of the announcement, its status page’s posts had garnered millions of views (and much panicked commentary) across social media.

We estimate that service restoration for #AO3 will take around 2 weeks but it could be up to 4 weeks. We are hopeful that we will be able to bring the site back up in a degraded state sooner. Refer to our status page for updates: https://t.co/YAyyoTDOpE https://t.co/PUWaHF9M8L — AO3 Status (@AO3_Status) October 29, 2026

Some fans may suspect this issue is related to last week’s “PHP Armageddon,” when tools from OpenAI and Google Wiz uncovered two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language that runs the behind-the-scenes software of about 70% of the internet. But AO3 is not among that majority. Instead, the site is built on a different framework (a toolkit for running websites), Ruby on Rails, so the outage is unlikely to be related.

OTW and AO3 did not immediately reply to requests for comment. We’ll update this article if we learn more.

Tech.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
Tech.content:
Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.”

The move is designed to protect its data from AI scraping, allowing the company to instead forge lucrative licensing deals with model providers. But just as important, such a shift could help Reddit to increase its revenue even as it faces daily active user declines in its largest market, the U.S.

Overall, Reddit’s global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in Q3 and were down 2% year-over-year.

Image Credits:Reddit

The company is not alone in seeing such declines; the shift to an AI-centered web has impacted most websites and publishers by now, leading to fewer click-throughs, as AI summaries provide answers that don’t require website visits and Google’s traditional “ten blue links” have reduced relevance. (The change is now even impacting Google’s bottom line, its earnings revealed.)

But at Reddit’s scale, the numbers associated with such a decline are enormous. The company said search traffic referrals dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week in October. It warned that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low-double-digit percentage by next quarter. (To play that out: a hypothetical 10% to 12% decline could bring Reddit to roughly 115 million to 117 million daily actives, down from 130.3 million in Q3. That’s a huge drop!)

At the same time, Reddit has gotten significantly better at monetizing its audience even as its growth weakens. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of about $875 million. Net income rose 74% to $283 million. Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847 million while nonadvertising revenue, which includes its AI data-licensing business, grew 35% year-over-year to $48 million.

And despite a 2% year-over-year decline in U.S. daily users, Reddit’s average revenue per daily active user in the U.S. rose 53% to $13.82. Globally, average revenue per daily active user increased 36% year-over-year to $6.87.

Shifting to a logged-in experience could boost those numbers even higher because logged-in users are typically worth more to advertisers.

Unlike the logged-out users who often find their way to the site via search, logged-in users provide more signals about their interests and behaviors, which helps to better target and personalize ads.

Those same signals would also help Reddit provide a more personalized experience to its users, which includes personalized feeds, recommendations of new communities to subscribe to, and pushes to vote, comment, participate, and more. (This also includes pushing recommendations to its new algorithmic “For You” feed, announced yesterday, which will combine posts from communities users belong to alongside other recommendations based on their interests.)

Image Credits:Reddit

Still, a change of this magnitude could be the canary in the coal mine for the open web.

“I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me,” wrote Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman in a post published on Reddit’s site. “But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business,” he said.

The company notes that the shift to the logged-in experience will not be an overnight change; it will first run tests in select markets outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. It doesn’t yet have a timeline for when the change will be rolled out to all its users worldwide. It also acknowledged that access to a logged-out front page is important.

Plus, Reddit pointed out that being logged in doesn’t mean having to give up anonymity, nor will it remove its option to browse anonymously through its “incognito mode” experience, which is being rebuilt.

“There are still plenty of questions that are unanswered, particularly around where the boundaries should be between logged-in and logged-out experiences,” Hoffman wrote. “This is a big evolution for Reddit, and not one we’re taking lightly. But I believe it’s the right next step for the platform and for our future.”

Tech.title: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant
Tech.content:
The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants.

Rivian is now licensing elements of its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group as part of the broader joint venture, according to the company’s third-quarter investor presentation released Thursday.

Rivian didn’t disclose the licensing fees, payment terms, or which Volkswagen vehicles will use the technology. However, the AI assistant, which recently rolled out to Rivian vehicles, could make its Volkswagen debut in the automaker’s low-cost EV called the ID EVERY1. The small four-door hatchback is slated to be the first VW vehicle to use Rivian’s software and electrical architecture under the joint venture established in 2024.

The joint venture between Rivian and VW Group has already expanded once before, at least financially. The companies initially announced a joint venture valued up to $5 billion, but within months VW upped its commitment to invest up to $5.8 billion in Rivian by 2027. The initial tie-up, formalized through an independent company that kicked off in November 2024, focused on bringing Rivian’s electrical architecture and software to Volkswagen’s next generation of vehicles.

Rivian described the expansion to include elements of its AI assistant technology as “a proof point for the extensibility of the platform we’ve built in-house.”

Rivian spent two years developing its AI assistant before showing it off last year. That development work continued longer than expected, with the assistant finally rolling out in May 2026 to its flagship R1S SUV, R1T pickup truck, and in October to its new midsize R2 SUV.

Rivian has big aspirations for its AI assistant, which allows drivers and passengers to interact with the vehicle and control certain functions. Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe told TechCrunch onstage at Disrupt 2026 that the company has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. That capability could eventually allow Rivian vehicles to run AI agents created by other companies, including Anthropic.

The in-house AI assistant program also fits into Rivian’s push to become more vertically integrated — a strategy the company emphasized in its third-quarter earnings report.

“Our relentless focus on vertical integration remains a core competitive differentiator, allowing Rivian to seamlessly unify our hardware and software architecture to deliver significant value to our customers,” the company noted in its investor presentation.

That strategy led to Rivian overhauling its flagship R1T truck and R1S SUV, changing everything from the battery pack and suspension system to the electrical architecture, sensor stack, and software user interface. Its new electric architecture system and compute platform slashed the amount of wiring used and reduced the total number of electronic control units, or computers, used to control the vehicle from 17 different ECUs to seven. That foundation, Rivian argued, would allow it to build vehicles that can handle the computing demands required for advanced software and automated driving.

That technology caught the attention (and money) of VW, which has struggled to offer customers a modern software-centric vehicle found in competitors like Tesla.

Rivian made that vertical-integration case repeatedly in its investor presentation, noting that because it controls the entire technology stack, including compute, sensors, displays, lighting, and sound, “it can roll out rapid, vehicle-wide OTA updates that go well beyond the basics.”

This article was updated to provide the two separate rollout dates for the AI assistant.

Tech.title: The R2 SUV is already Rivian’s best-selling vehicle
Tech.content:
Rivian’s new R2 SUV was its best-selling vehicle in the third quarter, the company said Thursday, marking an auspicious start for the all-important EV.

While Rivian didn’t say exactly how many R2s it sold over the three-month period, the company is confident enough in the pace of sales that it raised its delivery guidance for Wall Street. Rivian had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year. On Thursday, it bumped up that floor to 67,000.

It’s the second time Rivian has raised its delivery guidance this year, and the company is now on track to break a three-year stalemate during which it struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually. The company launched the R2 just in June, but it has made a major bet on scaling production of the lower-cost SUV at a historically quick rate.

The early success of the R2 is also a sign that Rivian is finding new customers despite last year’s loss of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit. The death of that tax credit, along with changes made by the Trump administration to U.S. regulations that supported the growth of EVs, has caused many major automakers to shift their attention back to internal combustion and hybrid vehicles — leaving room in the market for pure-EV companies like Tesla and Rivian.

“In a U.S. automotive marketplace starved for high-quality EV choice, R2 is an attractively priced option for everyday adventures that is resonating with a broad set of consumers and we expect will be a game changer for Rivian’s long-term growth and profitability,” the company said in a letter to shareholders released Thursday.

Rivian revealed earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles in the third quarter and delivered 19,248. That was roughly 45% more than it delivered in the same period last year and a big jump from the 12,613 vehicles built and 12,194 delivered in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was driven in large part by the company launching a second production shift at its factory in Normal, Illinois.

Rivian said Thursday that the R2 was responsible for “much of the gain quarter-over-quarter,” but didn’t go into specifics. The company generated $2.2 billion in revenue in the third quarter and suffered a net loss of $913 million — down from $1.2 billion in the same period last year.

Rivian launched the R2 at a starting price of just under $60,000. A more affordable “premium” trim is supposed to be available later this year that starts at $53,990. Even cheaper versions are slated for 2027, which will be available for as low as $44,990.

Tech.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
Tech.content:
In Brief

Thrive Holdings has acquired physical security company ADT for $10 per share or about $7.6 billion in equity, the companies announced on Thursday. Beyond equity, the total enterprise value of the deal is $15.3 billion, ADT said.

Thrive Holdings is the PE spinout from Josh Kushner’s powerhouse VC firm Thrive Capital. It also counts OpenAI as its partner, as well as an investor. The firm’s mission is to hold other companies long-term, revitalizing them with AI. Currently, Thrive Holdings holds over 75 companies, it says.

As a partner, OpenAI supplies AI models and tech as well as people, otherwise known as forward-deployed engineers, to Thrive’s companies.

Neither ADT nor Thrive announced what new AI-powered security products they will be releasing, but they did tease that the plan was to invest and release new products. “ADT will form the foundation of Thrive Holdings’ smart home security business,” the press release said.

AI-powered physical security is having a moment right now. Apple just entered the field with a new line of smart home and home security products in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. Amazon updated its smart home line, including new AI-powered home cameras. And who knows what the future might bring? Some startups are offering AI dog robots as roving security guards.

Tech.title: What to Know About China’s Top-Secret Spaceplane
Tech.content:
A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military’s X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.

The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.

The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.

Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the Defense Intelligence Agency assessment. A US Space Force official revealed Maxar’s observation at a 2024 conference in South Korea, but the Pentagon did not release the full-resolution image to the public until Monday, when it appeared in an unclassified DIA assessment of threats to the United States in space.

Catch and Release

The DIA report doesn’t reveal much new about what the Chinese spaceplane does in orbit. China has launched four spaceplane missions since 2020, with durations of up to nine months. The fourth mission is in orbit today after launching in February. It is not publicly known whether China has one or more such spaceplanes in its inventory.

The Space Force has two X-37Bs flying in rotation, with the longest of their eight missions to date running two-and-a-half years from launch until landing. US officials have released photos of the X-37B vehicles, published information about their design and dimensions, and disclosed a handful of experiments they have carried into orbit. Most of the X-37B’s activities in space are classified.

Like the X-37B, China’s spaceplane lifts off inside the payload shroud of a conventional rocket, then operates as a satellite once in orbit. The spaceplane flies like a miniature unpiloted version of NASA’s Space Shuttle and reenters the atmosphere for an autonomous land runway landing at the end of each mission. Ground teams then refurbish it for another flight.

Tech.title: Polymarket Halted International Trading After Hackers Drained Accounts
Tech.content:
Trading has resumed on Polymarket’s flagship international platform after a hack that drained money from the wallets of some traders.

A third-party vendor based in the United Kingdom was breached, not the prediction market’s website itself. Law enforcement in the UK have been notified of the incident, the company said. Trading was initially paused while the company investigated for several hours.

On X, prominent traders complained that they had lost money; Blockchain analytics firm Bubblemaps reported that around 700 users appear affected, with approximately $2.7 million stolen. Polymarket declined to comment when WIRED asked how many traders were impacted by the breach and how much money was lost, but said it will refund impacted traders.

The hack did not impact users on Polymarket US, the company’s newer platform for people within the United States. Polymarket runs two separate prediction markets; Polymarket US operates as a federally regulated financial exchange within the country, while the flagship Polymarket is a cryptocurrency-based platform that is banned in the United States and a number of other countries.

This is not the first time that Polymarket traders have experienced security woes. In June 2026, Polymarket experienced another breach, which resulted in over $2 million in losses for impacted traders.

The company has been a lightning rod for controversy since its 2020 launch. In the past few years, it has been the center of several high-profile alleged insider trading incidents resulting in arrests. One case involved a special forces soldier accused of wagering on the capture of Venezuela’s former leader; another involved a Google employee who allegedly used confidential information to make millions. In both cases, the suspects have pleaded not guilty.

Polymarket recently raised $1 billion in August 2026, with a fundraising round led by 1789 Capital, the venture capital firm where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner. It is now valued at $21 billion.

Tech.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
Tech.content:
Earlier this year, sources tell WIRED, a contractor caused a security incident at the Department of Defense by connecting a secure centralized system used by multiple intelligence agencies to their personal account for Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI coding agent. It appears that the agent used by the contractor, who is employed by global consulting firm Accenture, then sent information about the DOD system, including login credentials, to a high-risk third-party website.

The centralized system contains controlled unclassified information (CUI), which is considered sensitive and not to be released to the public without review. CUI can include information about critical infrastructure, nuclear submarine propulsion, and vulnerabilities to chemical and biological terrorism. Additionally, security experts say, access to the system could allow for the exploitation of even more sensitive ones.

“It puts all the data that’s in there at risk,” says a source aware of the incident, who requested anonymity as they were not authorized to speak to the press. If the third-party software was compromised, “there could be somebody out there with the ability to log into a secure environment without anyone knowing. It’s 100 percent a national security threat and could cause irreparable harm.”

A DOD spokesperson tells WIRED that “the Department does not comment on the status of its networks or systems.”

“We take all concerns seriously. These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit. We fully complied with our legal and contractual obligations,” an Accenture spokesperson tells WIRED. When pressed, Accenture didn’t offer clarification on who conducted the investigation, or dispute that had been what could be characterized as an incident.
